## PR-129 — the engine's motion law, byte for byte: 0x54250 read
## end to end (it IS the F/T law, PR-99's algebra confirmed), 0x549f0
## shown to be the "lion near" gate PR-125 inferred, and 0x52790's
## reachability resolved (class method-table slot, one call site).
## (pure RE; no C, no tool change)

- WHY. §7 item 13 and §8 T1 (1) have carried the law question since
  PR-98: PR-99 wrote "the engine loop's steady state is v_eq =
  5*F_eff*s/T" from an earlier partial read, PR-125 inferred a per-
  object "lion near" gate from video alone (the sitting fish/penguins),
  and nobody had read the integrator or its contact method start to
  finish, nor found which object classes can even reach them. That is
  the part of this line that is NEVER blocked on footage, so this unit
  reads the code and answers all three questions from the image bytes
  (`build/leo/leo.elf`, VA = file offset + 0xf000; listing
  `/tmp/opencode/vis/text.asm`, scripts under `/tmp/opencode/pr129/`).
- WHO CALLS THE INTEGRATOR (census2.py, literal-dword scan):
  0x54250 is named by 150 dwords in the data area. 137 of them sit in
  the same shape: 0x543a0 0x28 bytes earlier and 0x549f0 immediately
  after - the standard class method-table slots +0xa0 (control dispatch,
  PR-102/108), +0xc8 (velocity method), +0xcc (contact method). So
  this IS the engine's default motion law, shared by ~137 class
  tables, with 13 more tables (exactly the classes carrying 0x52790,
  see below) referencing the same pair from shifted slots, and exactly
  ONE table replacing +0xc8 with a wrapper thunk: 0x24700 - if
  [obj+0x0] > 1600 and [obj+0x5c] in {1,3,4,0x10} it adds 60 to the
  command block's +0x0 and 30 to its +0x4, then calls 0x54250. The
  only indexed call to the slot is 0x52774 (`call [ecx+0xc8]`,
  ecx = [[obj+0x0]+8]) inside 0x52750; the only indexed call to
  +0xcc are 7 plain sites (0x27e1d, 0x282a1, 0x344c8, 0x4010e,
  0x4110c, 0x41c01, 0x4aeca), each with `edx` = a stack block.
  Only three sites call the integrator by direct address: 0x24731
  (inside the 0x24700 thunk), 0x321fe, 0x33348. The function that
  ends at 0x33348 (starts 0x33310) first adjusts block +0x10 by
  5*[obj+0xf2] when [obj+0x5c] is 3 or 5 (swim / float modes), and
  its address sits in exactly one table right before a 0x549f0 - a
  real per-class velocity method. The function ending at 0x321fe
  scales the object's first dword by /640 and %10 and folds both
  into block +0x10/+0x14 first (640 = the game's screen width, so a
  screen-index effect; interpretation OPEN); its address was not
  found in any table.
- THE COMMAND BLOCK (edx, 0x20+ bytes). One builder is a per-class
  entry that 10 tables hold at (0x52790 - 4): 0x4ff80 - when
  [[obj+0x0]+0x126] is non-zero it writes force words 60,60 into
  block +0x0,+0x4 and drag words 7,7 into +0x8,+0xc ([obj+0x126] is
  the same flag 0x4ffb6 asserts on and 0x50970 branches on, meaning
  unread). 0x52750 instead runs the class's OWN builder through the
  [obj+0x44] vtable: slot +0x2c = 0x52680 fills a stack block from
  the object's live fields [obj+0x48..0x5c] and its indexed record
  table, slot +0x30 adjusts it. Who WRITES [obj+0x48..0x5c] - the
  state-token interpreter - is still unread (PR-130). The block's
  meaning below comes from the integrator's own use of it; which
  authored number lands in which word (F vs direction vs cap) stays
  OPEN until that interpreter is read. PR-99's reading (F at +0x0,
  s = [obj+0xba])
  is kept and marked as such.
- 0x54250 END TO END (all numbers are the code's constants):
  1. Guard: calls class slot +0xbc; if it returns non-zero and the
     block's +0x8 < 20 and [obj+0xb6] bit 2 is clear, raise +0x8 to
     20. So a small authored T (like 0x4ff80's 7) is only honoured
     when that hook says no or the bit is set.
  2. Velocity is kept 100x fixed-point: [obj+0xc2] x, [obj+0xc6] y.
     Drag terms are computed from the PREVIOUS velocity first:
     edi = [obj+0xc2]*T_x/100, esi = [obj+0xc6]*T_y/100 with
     T_x = block+0x8, T_y = block+0xc.
  3. Force step: [obj+0xc2] += (block+0x0*[obj+0xba])/20 +
     [obj+0x6d]*block+0x10; [obj+0xc6] += (block+0x4*[obj+0xbe])/20
     + block+0x14. Integer division by 20 (idiv).
  4. Drag apply: v -= the step-2 term. Then overshoot clamps: if
     v_before_force * v_after_drag < 0, v_x = 0; if
     block+0x14 * v_y_after < 0, v_y = 0. (Drag crossing zero kills
     the axis instead of oscillating it.)
  5. Cap: calls 0x54170 with edx = block+0x18*[obj+0x6d],
     ebx = block+0x1c. 0x54170 is a soft pull-toward-limit: it only
     moves a velocity that is BELOW the limit toward it, in limit-
     size steps, clamped exactly to the limit; a velocity already
     past it is never reduced. So the block carries speed limits too.
  6. Output: [obj+0xca] = [obj+0xc2]/100, [obj+0xce] = [obj+0xc6]/
     100 - the integer px/tick used by the mover.
  Steady state of 2-4 (force = drag): px/tick = D/T with
  D = (block+0x0*[obj+0xba])/20 + [obj+0x6d]*block+0x10. With
  PR-99's reading ([obj+0xba] = s = 10): px/tick = F/(2T) - the same
  5*F*s/T in the register's 100x units, so PR-99's algebra is CONFIRMED
  line by line. At a 20 Hz object tick [CORRECTED IN PR-133: there
  is no separate object tick; the object tick IS the iteration
  clock, so "20 Hz" = the 50 ms edge of PR-109's bracket] that is
  10*F/T px/s = law B; T=40 gives F/80 px/tick = F/4 px/s = law A,
  which is why all 29
  T=40 placed rows (PR-126) cannot separate them and why PR-79's /4
  fit worked. Machine-checked: F=100 T=50 (LONA.05 YETI) -> 1.0
  px/tick = 20 px/s at 20 Hz (law A would say 25); F=75 T=20
  (KADMAR.07 BOSS) -> 1.875 px/tick = 37.5 px/s (law A 18.75);
  F=100 T=40 (ZARIA worm) -> 1.25 px/tick = 25 px/s = PR-99's
  reproduction, exactly.
- 0x549f0 END TO END (the +0xcc contact method - PR-125's gate,
  found): eax = obj, edx = a contact record. It seeds
  [obj+0xba] = [rec+0x0] and [obj+0xbe] = [rec+0x4] (record default
  factors [CORRECTED IN PR-132: that edx is a CALLER-BUILT STACK
  scratch record, not a persistent one, and every read producer of
  its words computes the pair; there is no authored default]),
  then if [obj+0xd2] (the object's CONTACT LIST head) is
  null it keeps those defaults. With a contact it re-computes both
  factors from the contact's fields and the object's own position,
  read through class slot +0x68 - whose standard implementation
  (0x23900, in every table checked) is `add eax,0xd6; ret`, i.e. it
  returns obj+0xd6 as the {x,y} block and never touches edx, which
  is how the flag below survives. For kind 1: flag =
  ([contact+0xc] != [obj+0x6d]), and the contact's x (+0x8) is
  offset by 15 when it is set. The factor is +10 if the contact is
  more than 5 px to the +x side,
  -10 if more than 5 px to the -x side, 0 (and 0x551f0 pops the
  contact - it replaces [obj+0xd2] with [contact+0x0], the list next,
  then runs a "lost contact" hook: [class+0x3c]; non-zero ->
  [obj+0x106] = 1) within the 5 px band. Kind 4 does the same on x
  with an 8 px band and on y ([contact+0x1d]) into [obj+0xbe].
  Kind 2, when x positions match exactly, copies a 16-byte block
  (contact+0x10 -> obj+0x60, 0x49580) and pops the contact. Tail:
  [obj+0xbe] < 0 sets facing [obj+0x71] = +1, > 0 sets -1;
  [obj+0xba]*[obj+0x6d] < 0 sets [obj+0xb6] bit 4 and calls 0x53670;
  [obj+0xa5] gets [rec_arg+0x8].
- THE CONFIRMED MECHANISM behind PR-125's "the sitting fish IS in
  its A_RUN state": the integrator multiplies the state's force word
  by [obj+0xba], and 0x549f0 holds that factor at its record-seeded
  default while [obj+0xd2] is empty or the contact sits inside the
  5/8 px band. A record whose default is 0 (the reading the video
  forced PR-125 to infer) gives force exactly 0 and, with drag,
  steady speed exactly 0 - the object animates in place. The factor
  becomes +/-10 (never any other magnitude) once a contact crosses
  the band, and 10 is exactly the s PR-99's formula needed. This is
  a CODE confirmation: the gate is per-object (the object's own
  contact list), on the force side, and magnitude-gated, exactly as
  inferred.
- HOW 0x52790 IS REACHED, which has blocked every previous attempt
  ("zero call 0x52790 in .text" is true and no longer puzzling): it
  is a CLASS METHOD TABLE entry, slot +0x114, in 15 tables; all 15
  hold it as a fixed unit - (0x52680, provider, 0x52790) - the
  provider being 0x4ff80 x10, 0x2b4d0 x3, 0x61250 x2, and 0x52680
  itself being a command-block-from-the-object's-own-fields builder
  ([obj+0x48..+0x5c]) that runs record-evaluator slot +0x10 on the
  class's indexed record table ([obj+0x2e] + [obj+0x4]*4). ALL 15
  literals sit at slot +0x34 of a vtable a constructor stores into
  [obj+0x44] (assignment sites include 0x1e119, 0x23115, 0x240f6,
  0x26425, 0x264e6, 0x26ef5, 0x2b3c5, 0x2c01d - naming those 15
  classes through their constructors is tractable but not done
  here). And [obj+0x44] is an INTERIOR POINTER INTO the object's
  own method table: measured exactly [class table]+0xe0 for two
  classes (0x99258, 0x9f380 - their class tables hold the same
  triplet at +0x110/+0x114, which is why the literal census saw
  both readings as one), +0xdc for another (class 0x97bc0); the
  delta varies per class. That is the reachability, fully: 0x52750
  (eax = obj, edx = out record; 10 direct call sites 0x23fc8,
  0x264a8, 0x2701d, 0x2c3ad, 0x2df08, 0x31fd8, 0x33c98, 0x3620d,
  0x4fff1, 0x61238) is a MOTION PIPELINE through that very table:
  [ecx+0x2c] = 0x52680 builds the block, [ecx+0x30] = the provider
  adjusts it, [[obj+0x0]+8]+0xc8 = the integrator runs on it,
  [ecx+0x34] = 0x52790 is called with the caller's ORIGINAL edx -
  builder, provider, integrator and merger are ONE pipeline the
  class runs. A second, blunter path exists: 0x50970 (eax = obj,
  edx/ebx = two out-pointers; 7 direct call sites 0x246ed, 0x27245,
  0x2c324, 0x2e6c9, 0x3400d, 0x364c5, 0x61695, plus 4 table slots)
  calls [class+0x104] with the mode word [obj+0x5c] first, and only
  when that returns non-zero AND [obj+0x9d] == 1 does it call
  [class+0x114] with edx = *out1 - that is this merger only for the
  +0xe0-delta classes; in the shifted ones that slot holds other
  content (meaning OPEN). 0x52790 itself: builds an empty
  12-byte candidate list (0x749a0), and merges up to three spatial
  candidate lists into it (0x4bd30 / 0x4b890 / 0x4b870, each called
  on the global engine object ds:0xcef40 with the object's leading
  dword [obj+0x0] and the sign flag [obj+0x12]&0x8000) - gated per
  list on the STATE-TOKEN WIRE BITS the port already names (PR-60's
  comment at ported/ll_play.h +0x12 selectors): [obj+0x13] bit 2 ==
  wire 0x200 == CHECK_LEW -> 0x4bd30 (against Lew); [obj+0x12] bit
  0x40 == CHECK_ANI -> 0x4b890 (the animacje list); [obj+0x12] bit
  0x80 == CHECK_ZW -> 0x4b870 (the zwierzaki list). Note the port's
  numeric names are offsets into the OBJECT RECORD here, not the
  state's - 0x52790 reads [obj+0x12]/[obj+0x13] directly. Then it
  copies the merged list to the out
  record. So: per-class CANDIDATE MERGER, the pipeline tail. Which
  classes those 15 are stays OPEN (the tables carry no names, cls.py
  found none; the constructor sites above are the way to name them)
  - it is the next question, and PR-103's "per-class
  rather than universal" caution is now measured: the MOTION pair is
  universal, the CONTACT merger is not.
- WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DECIDE. It completes the code side of
  §8 T1 (1): the engine law is the F/T integrator (law B), and the
  port's law A is the special case T=40 that every fitted sample sat
  at. What remains genuinely open is (a) the object-tick rate that
  turns px/tick into px/s - every published reproduction in §7
  assumes 20 Hz (PR-99), which is not yet a read fact [CORRECTED
  IN PR-130: the published reproduces do NOT all sit at 20 Hz - the
  jump reading implies 25 ticks/s and the only clock §7 has READ is
  PR-109/110's ~28 ms iteration clock; see the PR-130 record]; (b)
  which
  block word carries the authored F - the writer of the fields
  [obj+0x48..0x5c] that 0x52680 copies is unread; (c) the two
  law-discriminating rows still want the L
  video half (LONA.05 YETI, A 25 vs B 20). With this record's
  arithmetic a future probe has a falsifiable prediction per placed
  row: px/tick = F/(2T), sign from the contact band side.
- EVIDENCE IN /TMP (all under /tmp/opencode/pr129/): tab.py, slot.py
  (the first slot-shape dumps), shapes.py (the 15-table shape test),
  cls.py (class-table neighbourhoods), scan52790.py (the pointer-run
  walk around every 0x52790 literal), census2.py (the final counts:
  150 integrator literals / 137 standard triplets / 15 merger units
  with providers). Disassembly read via /tmp/opencode/vis/text.asm
  from build/leo/leo.elf; no new committed tool this PR.
- GATES. No C, no Makefile, no tool, no `.github/workflows` line:
  this is the docs-only class, so per the standing rule the build
  legs would be no-ops - still run anyway: `make` and `make win`
  silent (C tree unchanged from PR-128), and `make -k verify-all`
  twice (fixtures `DATA=/tmp/opencode/iso_stage/LEO
  HD=/tmp/opencode/hd_files`; fixture-free `DATA=/tmp/opencode/nope
  HD=/tmp/opencode/nope` with named SKIPs) - both
  `ALL TESTS PASSED (linux + windows + llrs)`, rc=0
  (/tmp/opencode/pr129/gates.txt). Only HANDOFF.md and this record
  change. Added doc prose lines all <= 79 columns.
- HANDOFF UPDATED: §7 item 13 gains the PR-129 bullet (law confirmed
  byte for byte; the PR-125 gate CONFIRMED in 0x549f0; 0x52790's
  slot reachability and the 137-vs-15 census); §8 T1 (1) is reworded
  to what is still open (tick rate, F's block word, the YETI video

## PR-130 — the authored F reaches the integrator, byte for byte:
## 0x52680 read in full (its field-copy map is exactly PR-99's F=/
## T=/G= layout), the parser 0x52590 shown to be slot +0x00 of the
## object's own [obj+0x44] method block, and the F/T/G lifecycle
## found; PR-129's clock wording corrected. (pure RE; no C, no tool)

- WHY. PR-129 closed the law and the gate but left "(b) which block
  word carries the authored F - the writer of [obj+0x48..0x5c] that
  0x52680 copies is unread" as the named next question (§7 item 13,
  §8 T1 (1)). It is the last link between the placement files and
  the motion, and PR-99 had already read the parser end - what was
  missing was the middle. Read from build/leo/leo.elf via
  /tmp/opencode/vis/text.asm; scripts under /tmp/opencode/pr130/.
- 0x52680 END TO END (eax = obj, edx = the stack command block; it
  is slot +0x2c of every [obj+0x44] block, the FIRST call 0x52750
  makes): a pure field copy, `mov` pair after `mov` pair -
  block+0x8 = [obj+0x58], block+0xc = [obj+0x5c], block+0x0 =
  [obj+0x50], block+0x4 = [obj+0x54], block+0x10 = [obj+0x48],
  block+0x14 = [obj+0x4c]. THEN it takes the current state record
  `rec = [[obj+0x2e] + [obj+4]*4]` (the indexed record table; its
  evaluator is at [rec+0x4] slot +0x10) and calls that evaluator
  with edx = 1 (registers ecx = block+0x4, ebx = block on entry),
  then 0x45900: zeroes block+0x18 and block+0x1c and calls the
  SAME evaluator with edx = 0, handing it those two addresses in
  ebx/ecx; if [[obj+0x0]+0x95] is non-zero it calls it twice more,
  edx = 3 and edx = 2, against block+0x1c / block+0x18. So the
  force/drag/const words are ONLY copies of the object's own six
  fields, and the limit/target words block+0x18/+0x1c (0x54170's
  soft-pull targets, PR-129 step 5) are written by the row-node
  evaluator - which is exactly PR-99's conclusion that "the header
  F= feeds ONLY the increment channel, 0x54170's target comes from
  the row F/I nodes alone", now from this function's own bytes.
- THE SIX FIELDS' LIFECYCLE (the question PR-129 left):
  1. THE PARSER IS IN THE CLASS'S OWN METHOD BLOCK. 0x52590 - the
     `F=`/`T=`/`G=` clause parser PR-99 read and mapped (`F=` =
     +0x50/+0x54, `T=` = +0x58/+0x5c, `G=` = +0x48/+0x4c, T capped
     at 130) - is a literal in exactly the 15 [obj+0x44] vtables,
     at their slot +0x00 (0x97c9c, 0x99338, ... - all 15). Its
     bytes confirm the mapping from the strings: compares the node
     text against "F"/"T"/"G" (0x92281, 0x9228a, 0x92293) with
     " %i,%i" (0x92283, 0x9228c, 0x92295) parsed by 0x49920 into
     receiver+0x50/+0x54, +0x58/+0x5c, +0x48/+0x4c, and the cap is
     there: `cmp edx,0x82` then `mov [ecx+0x58],0x82` and the same
     for +0x5c (0x525f5..0x52610) - 0x82 = 130, PR-99's number. So
     the authored text reaches the object fields THROUGH the
     object's own vtable, not through some external interpreter.
  2. SPAWN ZEROS IT: 0x524a0 writes 0 into all six fields and THEN
     stores the vtable (`mov [eax+0x44],0xa25d4`); 14 direct call
     sites (0x23110 sits immediately before its `[obj+0x44]` store,
     also 0x26420, 0x2b3c0, 0x2b420, 0x2b480, 0x31f00, 0x36140,
     ...). So a fresh object starts with force 0 / drag 0 / const 0
     until the state text runs the parser; 0x52500 (called once,
     referenced at 0x96425 next to 0x524a0's) instead copies all six
     fields off a template object - spawn-by-cloning carries F/T/G.
- THEREFORE: the authored F= pair IS block+0x0/+0x4 (the force
  words the integrator multiplies by [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe] and
  divides by 20), the authored T= pair IS block+0x8/+0xc (the
  percent-drag words; capped at 130 AT PARSE and raised to >= 20
  at runtime only when the +0.bc guard fires, PR-129 step 1), and
  the authored G= pair IS block+0x10/+0x14 (added every tick,
  scaled by [obj+0x6d]). PR-129's open (b) is CLOSED at the byte
  level, and PR-99's reading of which word is F is CONFIRMED - the
  only link NOT read is which caller feeds the node text to the
  vtable +0x00 call (the port already parses the same `F= f1,f2`
  key textually in ll_level since PR-77/99, so this does not
  change any port number).
- PR-129's CLOCK WORDING, CORRECTED (the house pattern: PR-100
  corrected PR-99's 0x543a1). PR-129 wrote "(a) ... every published
  reproduction in §7 assumes 20 Hz (PR-99)". That is not what §7
  contains, and the distinction now matters:
  1. The only clock this repo has READ is the ITERATION clock
     (PR-109's bracket 22-50 ms; pacer 0x4b0e0 -> 0x4a120/0x1dba0
     holds one iteration to two display frames; the engine's own
     fallback setpoint is 27; PR-110 chose LL_ITER_MS = 28 ms), and
     §7's live text already says the row clock IS that iteration
     clock.
  2. PR-99's published jump reproduction implies 25 ticks/s
     (`v` hundredths of a px/tick, "I 150,-1200" -> (1.5,-12)
     px/tick -> (37.5,-300) px/s = the port's /4 constants), while
     its walk numbers fit 20 Hz only at T=40 with s = 10. The two
     reproduces do NOT sit at one rate.
  3. No read link yet ties the motion pipeline to one call per
     iteration: 0x52750's 10 call sites are per-class entry points
     (e.g. 0x4ffb6: it calls the pipeline on EVERY path, but first
     tests [[obj+0x0]+0x126], [[obj+0x0]+0x50] + [[obj+0x0]+0x5c]
     *4 +0x4 and the global ds:0xcf074, and when all three are zero
     it runs a message branch (string 0x920f3 = "deatd.mod", a
     global buffer at 0xcf068, 0x562c0) - those reads are all
     unread territory).
  What is actually open is therefore the PAIR (iteration rate, s):
  px/s = (5*F*s/T)/100 * rate, with s = [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe]
  seeded by 0x549f0 from the RECORD's own default factors [rec+0]/
  [rec+4] - authored values, never censused. (F=100, T=40,
  s=10, 20 Hz) and (F=100, T=50, s=10, 25 Hz) both give 25 px/s;
  (F=100, T=40, s=5.6, 28 ms) also does. The law is settled; the
  scale is one equation with two unread unknowns, and a census of
  the record default factors plus the iteration-driver read close
  it from data and code without video. The LONA.05 YETI video
  referee (PR-126/128) only discriminates once rate AND s are
  fixed. [CLOSED ON THE s SIDE IN PR-132: the "record default
  factors" are the caller's scratch pair, every producer is read,
  |s| <= 10 with s = +/-10 exactly at full one-axis intent, and
  no authored field can carry s. What remains open is the rate
  alone. [CLOSED IN PR-133: there is no separate object tick - the
  rate is the iteration clock x the passes a record runs per state
  step, at most 1 for the moving families; see the PR-133 record.]]
- WHAT WOULD BREAK THE PORT: nothing today. The port's numbers were
  fitted from video and stay; the record keeps §8 T1 (1)'s test
  honest by re-deriving what the test can decide.
- EVIDENCE IN /TMP (under /tmp/opencode/pr130/): life.py (the
  0x48..0x5c writer/reader/literal census that found 0x524a0 and
  0x52500), strs.py (the F/T/G + " %i,%i" string dump), and the
  disassembly reads of 0x52680/0x52470/0x524a0/0x52500/0x52590/
  0x45900 from /tmp/opencode/vis/text.asm. No new committed tool.
- GATES. No C, no Makefile, no tool, no `.github/workflows` line;
  docs-only class - build legs still run anyway: `make` and
  `make win` silent, `make -k verify-all` twice (fixtures
  `DATA=/tmp/opencode/iso_stage/LEO HD=/tmp/opencode/hd_files`;
  fixture-free `DATA=/tmp/opencode/nope HD=/tmp/opencode/nope`
  with named SKIPs) - both `ALL TESTS PASSED (linux + windows +

- HANDOFF UPDATED: §7 item 13 gains the PR-130 bullet and the

## PR-132 — the s side of the (rate, s) pair is CLOSED: 0x549f0's
"record" is a caller-built stack scratch, every producer of its two
words is read at the byte level, |s| <= 10 with s = +/-10 exactly at
full one-axis intent, and no authored data can carry an s. The open
scale question reduces to the iteration rate alone. (engine read;
no port behaviour change)

- WHY. PR-130 left the motion scale as "one equation with two
  unread unknowns: px/s = (5*F*s/T)/100 * rate" and proposed a
  census of "the record default factors [rec+0]/[rec+4]" (PR-129's
  wording for what 0x549f0 seeds [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe] from). The
  census was run - and the first thing it found is that its own
  premise was wrong: there is no persistent record those two words
  live in. This PR is the proof, from the whole call surface and
  the whole write set of those two fields.

- WRITE CENSUS (grep over ALL of /tmp/opencode/vis/text.asm).
  Writes to [obj+0xba] exist at 8 places and to [obj+0xbe] at 5:
  0x549f9/0x54a08 (the seed), the kind-1 x-band literals 0xa /
  0xfffffff6 / 0x0 (0x54a57/0x54a82/0x54a93), the kind-4 x-band
  same three (0x54ac3/0x54ae7/0x54af3), the kind-4 y-band three
  (0x54b16/0x54b3b/0x54b47) - all inside 0x549f0 - plus 0x54e2e/
  0x54e38, which belong to 0x54e00, a stop/reset helper (called
  at 0x50392 right after the caller copied [obj+0]/[obj+4] to
  [obj+0x14]/[obj+0x18]) that zeroes [obj+0xe2], [obj+0xa5],
  [obj+0xba], [obj+0xbe], [obj+0xc2], [obj+0xc6]: intent factors
  and velocities out, together, in one place. No constructor
  writes them; nothing outside those two functions ever does.
  PR-129's note "probably the same ground/terrain code that
  writes [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe]" is therefore CLOSED the honest
  way: there is no second writer.

- CALL SURFACE (also exhaustive). Exactly 8 entries: one direct
  call (0x50369, inside method 0x50340, which sits at the same
  slot offset in at least 12 method tables - data refs 0x96a2c,
  0x97a3c, 0x97b64, 0x989b8, 0x99000, 0x9a618, 0x9b5a0, 0x9ca24,
  0x9d404, 0x9e200, 0x9f23c, 0x9f60c) and 7 indirect
  `call DWORD PTR [reg+0xcc]` sites (0x27e1d, 0x282a1, 0x344c8,
  0x4010e, 0x4110c, 0x41c01, 0x4aeca; grep shows no other form
  that could dispatch slot +0xcc). 0x549f0 appears 140 times in
  the RW method-table region - it is the COMMON +0.cc handler -
  and +0xcc was verified as the slot at the three independently
  located table bases 0x9a778, 0x99258, 0x9f380. Slot +0xcc is
  polymorphic: the 15 tables carrying PR-129's (0x52680, *,
  0x52790) unit hold 0x54250, 0x55020 x3, 0x23840, 0x2b370,
  0x2b3d0, 0x2c0b0, 0x33310, 0x34160, 0x23b40, 0x617d0 at +0xcc
  instead (the scan's 15th hit, 0xa2dbc, is a false positive: its
  "slots" hold data bytes, 0x6188000/0x06000) - and none of
  those is among the 13 writer addresses above, so a class whose
  +0.cc is not 0x549f0 never seeds the factors: they sit at 0
  (force 0) for such a class, the PR-125 fish case as a general
  rule.

- THE ARGUMENT RECORD, PRODUCER BY PRODUCER (edx = a stack block
  in every case, built at the call site or one frame up):
  1. 0x27d60 (slot +0x14 of class 0x9a778; site 0x27e1d) and its
     twin 0x281ab (site 0x282a1): dx = [obj+0x126] - pos.x,
     dy = [obj+0x12a] - pos.y with pos read through getter slot
     +0x68 (0x23900 = `add eax,0xd6; ret`); computed when
     dx > 0 or dy < 0 (0x27da0-0x27da4), else the pair is 0.
     The values are round(10.0*dx/(|dx|+|dy|)) and
     round(10.0*dy/(|dx|+|dy|)) - FPU `fild/fmul/fdivrp/fistp`
     against the double 10.0 stored at 0x909ef and 0x909f7
     (bytes 00 00 00 00 00 00 24 40, read from the ELF): an
     L1-normalised pursuit direction scaled by 10.
  2. 0x3448d (site 0x344c8): record = {10 * facing, 0, 0} -
     facing read through getter slot +0x70 (0x239f0 =
     `mov eax,[obj+0x6d]; ret`), the 10 made by `lea eax,[eax*4]
     + add eax,edx` then `add eax,eax` (5x then doubled at
     0x400e7-0x400f0 in the twin), and +4/+8 zeroed on the spot.
     Full force, one axis, along the facing.
  3. 0x400ad (site 0x4010e): the same {10 * facing, 0, 0}, plus
     a call through [[obj+0x106] -> [0] -> class]+0x4 with
     edx = the record first (0x400f5-0x40104) - the interest
     target's own class gets a chance to edit the pair before
     +0.cc sees it.
  4. 0x410ee and 0x41b8f (sites 0x4110c, 0x41c01): the record
     is first handed to [[cls]+0xd8] - for 0x9a778 that slot is
     0x27ef0 = `mov eax,1; ret`, a constant-1 tag (found at
     0x9a850 = 0x9a778+0xd8; the bytes at 0x27ef0 mis-disassemble
     inside the objdump linear sweep, so they were re-read from
     the ELF bytes) - and then to +0.cc. Which word of the stack
     record other classes' +0xd8 methods fill is class-specific
     and stays unread beyond 0x9a778.
  5. 0x4ae82: the only site whose receiver is NOT self -
     the object-scanner loop passes a record at [esp+0x1e4] to
     [[ds:0xcef40]+0x394]'s class, i.e. the PLAYER's +0.cc, from
     outside the player (the record's producer sits in the
     scanner's earlier block - not read this PR; it is PR-133
     territory, since the scanner is one of the per-frame
     iteration paths). [NARROWED IN PR-133: the record IS the
     12-byte stack copy the frame loop makes at 0x4ae82-0x4aeaa
     (0x4ab50, [esp+0x1f0] -> [esp+0x1e4]); the fields it
     zeroes at 0x4abe0-0x4abee are filled by the modal blocks
     between - the producer chain is the loop itself.]
  6. 0x50340 (the direct-call method, 12+ tables): if
     [obj+0x106] == 0 it zeroes the record's +0/+4/+8 first (no
     interest target -> zero factors); if [obj+0x11a] == 5 it
     negates +0 (reverse-pursuit flag); then calls 0x549f0
     directly. Which slot the callers use, and who supplies the
     record there, is unread - same PR-133 boundary.
  7. 0x549f0 itself then does its contact work on its OWN terms:
     the kind dispatch reads [edx+4] AFTER edx was reloaded from
     [obj+0xd2] (0x54a02-0x54a1b), so the kind comes from the
     object's contact-list node, not from the argument - the
     argument's +4 only seeds [obj+0xbe] - and the recomputes
     write only 0xa/0xfffffff6/0x0.

- THE BOUND AND WHAT IT DOES TO THE LAW. Every read producer and
  every overwrite emits values with |factor| <= 10: 0, exactly
  +/-10 (facing-driven walk/gallop full force, or a contact past
  the 5/8 px band), or the pursuit scaling
  round(10*d/delta_manhattan) which is strictly smaller on a
  diagonal. So s is not free: s = 10 IS full one-axis intent, and
  PR-99's worm fit (F=100, T=40, s=10 -> 1.25 px/tick) is
  structurally confirmed - the worm walks full force along the
  facing. The PR-125/PR-129 reading of an in-place animator
  survives unchanged (no target -> the caller zeroes the pair ->
  force exactly 0), and the motion scale is now ONE unknown:
  px/s = F/(2T) * rate at full intent, with only the iteration
  rate unread. The PR-129 machine-checked set (YETI 20 px/s at
  20 Hz, BOSS 37.5, worm 25) stands with s = 10 read, not assumed.

- WHY NO DATA CENSUS WAS NEEDED. The claim "no authored field can
  carry s" does not rest on the 777 .MOV files: the write census
  above is exhaustive over the code (PR-130 showed the .MOV
  parser 0x52590 writes only the six live fields [obj+0x48..
  0x5c]), no constructor seeds +0xba/+0xbe, and nothing outside
  0x549f0/0x54e00 writes them. A field the engine never reads
  from memory cannot be authored.

- WHAT STAYS OPEN (named). The rate: the 10 entry sites of
  0x52750 (containing functions 0x23f96, 0x26476, 0x26fd6,
  0x2c35e, 0x2ded0, 0x31fa0, 0x33c66, 0x361c0, 0x4ffb6, 0x61206
  - three referenced from data at 0x9cee4, 0x9d544, 0x9f468),
  their guards, and how often they run per frame-loop iteration;
  the record producers behind 0x4ae82 (the scanner) and behind
  0x50340's callers. That is PR-133, and /tmp/opencode/pr131/
  slots.py already maps the sites and the class-table slots.
  Nothing in this PR changes a port number: the port's motion
  constants stay.

- EVIDENCE IN /TMP. Reads from /tmp/opencode/vis/text.asm; the
  constants and mis-disassembled bytes re-read from
  build/leo/leo.elf bytes (flat map VA = file + 0xf000, the same

  table/slot scan is a python one-off (struct.unpack over the

## PR-133 — W0's rate side closed at byte level: the physics-pipeline
## entries are state-record members, a record run IS a state step, and
## a state step IS one frame-loop iteration (PR-106) - there is no
## separate object tick; + the exhaustive slot-dispatcher census, the
## 0x52750 entry map with every table base alignment named, the record
## tables found in the image with their bound physics sets, and the
## [obj+0x9d] gate on the single +0x114 dispatch. (pure RE; no C, no
## tool change)

- WHY. PR-130/132 left exactly one unread quantity in the motion
  scale: the rate, "how often does 0x52750 / the +0xc8 integrator run
  for a class family" (§7 item 13, §8 T1 (1)). PR-129's
  machine-checked set is px/tick facts (1.0 YETI, 1.875 BOSS, 1.25
  worm) converted to px/s at an ASSUMED 20 Hz; PR-106 measured a
  ~28 ms iteration clock; the two do not multiply out. This unit
  reads the iteration-driver structure end to end and answers it.
  Method notes: every VA was read from raw image bytes with
  /tmp/opencode/dat.py (text.asm's linear sweep is misaligned in
  places - at 0x50970 it starts at 0x5096f, and its output at that
  base hides real dispatches like 0x50bae from any grep). So the
  slot-dispatcher census below is a BYTE census: every `FF /modrm
  80-9F/ disp32` call form in .text. It is exhaustive for the slots
  here: offsets >= 0x90 cannot encode a disp8, so only the disp32
  form exists. And every slot cited names its table-base anchor:
  a base here means the dword where +0x68 = 0x23900 (position
  getter) and +0x70 = 0x239f0 (facing getter), except where marked
  "pair anchor" (+0xc8 = 0x54250 with +0xcc = 0x549f0). The 4-byte-
  shifted slot families PR-105/132 hit are why this rule exists.

- THE BYTE CENSUS OF SLOT DISPATCHERS (complete, .text = file
  0x1000..0x80000, pattern `FF modrm disp32`):
  +0x90: 2 sites - 0x3edaf (inside 0x3ed70, itself a value in 5
    tables 0x9dc10/0x9e2a8/0x9f7c8/0xa1fa4/0xa2068; setup shape,
    unread) and 0x5357d (inside 0x53520, the state-step chain).
  +0xa0: 1 site - 0x52317 (inside a contact walk; +0xa0 = 0x543a0

  +0xc8: 1 site - 0x52774 (inside 0x52750; PR-129's claim CONFIRMED
    exhaustively now, not just by grep of one reg class).
  +0xcc: 7 sites - 0x27e1d, 0x282a1, 0x344c8, 0x4010e, 0x4110c,
    0x41c01, 0x4aeca - PR-132's list, now byte-verified complete.
    0x4010e is inside 0x400b0 = +0x14 of the 0x9f380 family: that
    state step runs its own object's +0xcc once per step before
    tailing 0x550a0 (0x40129). 0x4aeca is the frame loop's player
    +0xcc (PR-106/125); its record is the 12-byte copy the loop
    makes at 0x4ae82-0x4aeaa (`0x4ab50`, [esp+0x1f0] -> [esp+0x1e4]),
    the fields the loop zeroed at 0x4abe0-0x4abee - PR-132's open

  +0xe0: 13 sites - 0x276bc, 0x2775e, 0x277cb, 0x27a2a, 0x27fc0,

  +0xe8: 5 sites - 0x378d4, 0x37a04, 0x41a5d, 0x4aba8 (inside

    not +0xe8 - a sweep artifact, corrected by this census.)
  +0xec: 4 sites - 0x3d7b3, 0x415cd, and the two player paths
    0x4ab97/0x4ac0a (0x4ab97 is inside 0x4ab80, which the frame
    loop calls EVERY iteration at 0x4aedb when [level+0x3a8] == 0:
    0x4ab97 dispatches the player class's +0xec, 0x4aba8 its
    +0xe8; 0x4ac0a is the once-per-level copy).
  +0xf4: 6 sites (0x2838d, 0x2856e, 0x3d833, 0x3d84e, 0x3e52d,
    0x41b06). +0x100: 2 (0x41b6a, 0x50c2a). +0x104: 4 (0x41a7e,
    0x50b34, 0x50b57, 0x50b8d). +0x108: 2 (0x41711, 0x50bbc).
    +0x10c: 1 (0x50c1b). +0x110: 1 (0x50c0c). +0x114: 1 (0x50bae).
    +0x11c: 1 (0x50b49). +0x120: 0.

- THE STATE-STEP CHAIN, CLOSED. PR-106 established: while an object
  is on-camera ([obj+0x2c] flag, written by the draw pass), one
  frame-loop iteration = exactly one pump 0x52b80 = exactly one
  `[[obj+8]+0x14]`. Closed now: the cited +0x14 bodies END in the
  same tail - the worm 0x27d60 at 0x27e25 and 0x400b0 at 0x40129
  both call 0x550a0 (0x550b4), 0x550a0 zeroes [obj+0xe6]/[obj+0xea]
  and calls 0x536f0; 0x536f0 runs [cls+0x8c], 0x49580 twice with
  0x523f0, [cls+0x54], then 0x53520 (0x5373c), and 0x53520
  dispatches `[[obj+8]+0x90]` at 0x5357d. So a class's +0x90 method
  runs exactly once per state step. For the 4 classes holding
  +0x90 = 0x50970 (bases 0x98f34, 0x9d338, 0x9f540, 0xa2218 -
  getter-anchored) that method IS the physics-method sequence:
  0x50970 spans 0x50970..0x50c4c and at 0x50b8d calls +0x104 (early
  exit 0x50c30), gates `cmp [obj+0x9d],1 / jne` at 0x50b9b before
  the only +0x114 call (0x50bae), then +0x108 (0x50bbc) with its
  result compared against [obj+0x9d] and the state index (0x50bc8-
  0x50bda: it indexes the record array [obj+0x50] + [obj+0x5c]*4
  itself), then +0x110 (0x50c0c), +0x10c (0x50c1b), +0x100 (0x50c2a)
  and calls 0x54450 directly (0x50c38). Every other family's +0x90
  is 0x54450 - the record guard (PR-129) - so those run their record
  machinery per state step instead.

- THE RECORDS ARE IN THE IMAGE AND BIND THEIR OWN PHYSICS SETS. The
  record array is exactly what 0x50bda indexes: rec = [[obj+0x50] +
  [obj+0x5c]*4]; 0x53410 (0x54450's tail) hands back [rec+4]
  (PR-132). Found layout, identical in every record surveyed:
  rec+0x00 = a condition stub; rec+0x04 = 0x546a0 (shared, all
  records); and rec+0x18.. holds the physics default set at
  rec+0x1c/+0x20/+0x24 = 0x55020/0x54250/0x549f0 - the SAME triplet
  class tables hold at +0xa0/+0xc8/+0xcc, re-bound per record - plus
  small getters at +0x28.. and class-bound members from +0x2c on.
  Specimen 0x9a820: the record right after the worm class table
  0x9a778; its +0x2c binds 0x27ef0 - which is 0x9a778's own +0xd8
  value, a self-linking pair; its +0x30/+0x34/+0x38 =
  0x3df50/0x3df90 (the PR-129/131 physics-record methods) and
  0x52590 (the F=/T=/G= parser, PR-130). Immediately next,
  0x9a85c = an [obj+0x44] physics-parameter block (PR-130 shape):
  0x52470/0x52680/0x4ff80/0x52790 at +0x28..+0x34, and its +0x8 =
  0x26fd0 = the 0x9a778 +0xec pipeline entry. The condition stubs
  write the record's own bytes: 0x3e060 tests rec+0x7 bit 0x8 into
  [obj+0x116] and calls 0x54860; the worm state-0 stub 0x27e40
  reads the player's position ([0xcef40]+0x394, +0x68 getter), sets
  rec+0x7 |= 0x40 when the player is near and that dword < 0x514,
  and sets rec+0x5 |= 0x1 by sign rules on the [obj+0x126]/
  [obj+0x12a] target deltas. The control-mode machinery
  ([rec+0x12] & 7, jump table 0x54380 - the ll_play.h BY_*
  vocabulary) consumes those bits.

- HOW RECORDS RUN THE PIPELINE. The record-bound members ARE the
  containers of the 13 +0xe0 sites: heads at exact prologues
  (cgraph's heads were padding-after-ret artifacts), and 10 of the
  13 are found as record/class values:
  0x27680 in record 0x997c4's block at +0x2c (form: `call
  [edx+0x3c]` predicate, test, `je`; else dispatch [class+0xe0] at
  0x276bc); 0x27720 (record 0x99bf8 +0x30), 0x27770 (0x99d08
  +0x30), 0x27fa0 (0x998d0 +0x30), 0x28470 (two: 0x9a420 +0x30
  region), 0x30270 (0x9c688 +0x28 region), 0x30410 (0x9c5cc +0x30
  region of the 0x9f380-variant family), 0x3b860 (0xa0520 region),
  0x50c50 (+0x30 of 10 record blocks 0x96a60/0x97a70/0x97b98/
  0x99034/0x9a64c/0x9b5d4/...); the other 3 (the 0x277e0 head,
  and the areas at 0x3d7a1 and 0x4d711) appear nowhere as values -
  named open below. And 3 of the 5 +0xe8 sites sit 14-46 bytes
  after a `call 0x3e060` IN THE SAME stub (0x378b6->0x378d4,
  0x37a04, 0x41a5d): condition evaluation then pipeline run inside
  one record member. The worm's own bound physics members
  (0x3df50/0x3df90) are not 0x52750 callers - they are the
  0x52790-shape block builders (12-dword memset via 0x749a0,
  flag bits, 0x49580 merges from engine subsystems 0x4bd30/0x4b890)
  that the record then integrates through the bound +0x20 = 0x54250.

- THE 0x52750 ENTRY MAP (complete; the 10 entries of PR-129's
  caller scan, heads now exact - cgraph's heads were 2-6 bytes late,
  the true values in the tables were found by +-12-byte scans):
  0x23f90 = table 0x98da4 +0xe0 | 0x26470 = 0x99258 +0xe8 |
  0x26fd0 = 0x9a778 +0xec (the ZARIA worm class) |
  0x2c360 = 0x9b3dc +0x220 | 0x2ded0 = 0x9ce04 +0xe0 |
  0x31fa0 = 0x9d088 +0x4bc (pair anchor only - getter anchor not
  verified for that table, flagged) | 0x33c60 = 0x9e048 +0x214 |
  0x361c0 = 0x9f380 +0xe8 | 0x4ffb0 = 0x97bc0 +0xe4 |
  0x61200 = 0x9fb24 +0xe0. All bases getter-anchored except
  0x9ce04/0x9f380 (pair-anchored, PR-129/132) and the flagged
  0x9d088. The slots land in four shifted families (+0xe0, +0xe4,
  +0xe8, +0xec) - one more instance of the 4-byte view families;
  the record/census method above is what makes them line up.

- THE RATE ANSWER. There is NO object tick separate from the frame
  loop. The only paths by which the integrator can run are:
  (a) a record-bound +0xe0/+0xe8/+0xec member called during a state
  step - i.e. at most one pipeline pass per iteration while
  on-camera (PR-106's cadence), gated by the record's own authored
  condition bits; (b) the 0x50970 classes' physics-method sequence,
  once per state step, with the +0x114 leg gated on [obj+0x9d] == 1
  (0x50b9b); (c) the per-iteration player paths of 0x4ab80 (+0xec
  then +0xe8) and the frame loop's player +0xcc (0x4aeca) - the
  LION base 0x96874 holds 0x50340 at +0xec, so the lion's
  input-apply wrapper runs every iteration (0x50340 -> 0x549f0 at
  0x50369, PR-132); and (d) the three direct 0x54250 callers
  (PR-129). So rate = (iterations/s) x (passes per record per
  state step). The first factor is the measured iteration clock
  (PR-109's bracket 22-50 ms; PR-106's two-retrace design point;
  PR-110's LL_ITER_MS = 28). The second is authored, per record -
  and it is AT MOST 1 for the classes whose record chain runs one
  +0xe0-style member per step. Therefore the "20 Hz" is not a
  second clock: it is the iteration clock at 50 ms, the top edge of
  PR-109's bracket. At 50 ms: YETI F=100/T=50 -> 1.0 px/iter =
  20 px/s and the ZARIA worm F=100/T=40 -> 1.25 px/iter = 25 px/s,
  both matching the published reproduces; at the 28 ms design point
  they would be 35.7 and 44.6 px/s, which the videos refute for the
  worm. The scale equation now has NO unread constant: F and T are
  read (PR-130), s is read and bounded (PR-132), the clock is the
  port's own pacing knob, and the passes-per-state-step count is a
  per-record integer with read mechanism. Marked ESTIMATE: "the
  worm's record runs one pipeline member per state step" - the flag
  semantics ([obj+0x116], [obj+0x9d], the record condition bytes)
  are unread (open item 3 below); the upper bound and the mechanism
  are byte-fact.

- IN-PLACE CORRECTIONS TO EARLIER RECORDS (house pattern):
  PR-129's "At a 20 Hz object tick" is corrected there (no object
  tick; the object tick IS the iteration clock). PR-130's closing
  bracket "What remains open is the rate alone" is closed there.
  PR-132's open item 5 (the 0x4aeca record's producer) is narrowed
  there to the frame loop's 0x4ab50 copy chain. Nothing said about
  0x50340's slot by PR-125/132 was wrong: at the getter-anchored
  base 0x96960 (TLewZaria) it IS +0xcc; at 0x96874 it is +0xec
  (and +0xcc there is 0x549f0) - both now stated with anchors.

- OPEN ITEMS, COUNTED AND NAMED (4): (1) who calls rec+0x0 stubs
  directly - the record-step dispatcher; candidate `call [reg]`
  sites in the 0x1e15f/0x1ea2c region and 0x526e9/0x5272a/0x5273d
  (PR-130's [block+0x10] calls) cover the physics-block evaluator
  path only; (2) 3 of the 13 +0xe0 containers' heads (0x277e0, and
  the areas at 0x3d7a1/0x4d711) are not values anywhere in the
  static image - presumed members of records built at load time;
  (3) the semantics of [obj+0x9d], [obj+0x116] and the record
  condition bytes - which decide the passes-per-state-step count;
  (4) the guards on the entries (the 0x4ff80 family's [obj+0x126]
  branch; 0x2ded0's [rec+4] + ds:0xcf074 branch) and the six
  +0xe4 dispatch sites. The six 0x3ed70 tables' slot and role are
  setup-side and counted with (1).

- WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE PORT: no number moves today. The
  F/T/s constants stand; T1's scale test reduces to a two-factor
  fit - the iteration clock (G-1/G-2 referee windows A t=2-13 /
  A t=55-62 decide it, and one ZARIA worm-speed window decides
  the same clock from the other side) and the passes-per-step
  count, which is bounded by 1 for the families that move.
  ll_level.c's LL_ITER_MS (28) is the knob; 50 ms is testable by
  changing that constant alone.

## PR-134 — G-1's referee windows MEASURED: the pass rate is 15-24/s, so
## the iteration clock is the 50 ms edge of PR-109's bracket and LL_ITER_MS
## = 28 is refuted by two independent law objects (video measurements +
## one new RE script; no behaviour change)

- WHY. PR-133 closed the rate MECHANISM and left the two-factor fit: the

  named referees were PR-131's G-1 windows ("A t=2-13 (spawn->ladder@180,
  landmarks fixed)" and "A t=55-62 (ZWODOSPD@992)") plus "a worm-speed

- UNIT FRAME (PR-131's, re-verified twice here). The R3 A clip

- CAMERA-STATE VERIFICATION, THREE ESTIMATORS, AND WHERE EACH FAILS.

- G-1(b), ANSWERED FROM THE FILE. There is no A_RUN state to "raise":
  ZARIA.01_LEW.ZAR_LEWPL.MOV's own state list is A_WALK, A_DEAD,
  A_DRAP, A_DOSTAL, A_JUMP_S, A_JUMP, A_RZUT, A_ODLOT, A_WPAD, A_KILOF,
  A_KAMIEN, A_JUMP_DOWN, A_FALL_DOWN, A_WSP, A_WSP_LIN, A_TURN,
  A_BORRING, A_TO_BOR, A_BOR_END, A_LOOKUP, A_LOOKDOWN, A_FIGHT, ... -
  no A_RUN anywhere. The player's fast gait IS A_WALK: its `[A_WALK]`
  block is `control=BY_X|FRAME_REV|CHECK_ALL|CH_DIR`, `F=100,0`,
  `T=20,5`, `G=30,350`, `seq=walk`, and its row list is
  `10,6,GEN AC_TIME / 11,6 / 12,6 / 1,6 / ... / 9,6` - twelve poses,
  every one gated by row field 2 = 6. Per PR-100 that field is the
  distance threshold compared against the row accumulator [obj+0xa1],
  which for BY_X is fed the travelled px: the walk cycle advances one
  pose per 6 units travelled, and its airborne poses are the gallop art
  the video shows. Same shape as the worm's A_RUN (9 poses x 4 units =
  36 units per cycle), whose cycle period PR-79 measured at 1.44 s =
  25 units/s, the same constant this PR measures. The port is right
  that FWD drives A_WALK; what the port gets wrong is the rate, below.

- THE CLOCK. Per PR-133 the law is px/iteration = (5*F*s)/(100*T) with
  one state step and one physics pass per iteration for these families,
  so a measured rate divides by that constant to give the iteration
  rate:

  | object (F,T)         | u/iteration | measured u/s | it/s    |
  |----------------------|-------------|--------------|---------|
  | worm LICHA3 (100,40) | 1.25        | <= 30.3      | <= 24.2 |
  | lion A_WALK (100,20) | 2.50        | 38 (cold)    | >= 15.2 |
  | lion A_WALK peak     | 2.50        | <= 75.5      | <= 30.2 |

  The two families overlap at 15-24 iterations/s, and 20/s - the 50 ms
  edge of PR-109's 22-50 ms bracket - sits inside both. The 28 ms
  design point (35.7/s) predicts 44.6 u/s for the worm, above the
  measured bound of 30.3, and 89 u/s for the lion's ground run, above
  the whole [38,76] bracket; to rescue it the records would have to run
  0.35-0.68 passes per state step, which PR-133's chain forbids (the
  state-step chain dispatches the record once per iteration while the
  object is on-camera, and these families pass at most once). The
  airborne 73-110 u/s segment is a bonus data point on the same scale:
  if it were driven by the F=180/T=20 states it would predict 90 u/s at
  50 ms (inside 73-110) and 161 u/s at 28 ms (far outside), but the
  state that plays it is not identified, so it is evidence, not a
  measurement. DECISION: LL_ITER_MS's real-engine counterpart is 50 ms
  with one pass per state step; the port's 28 ms constant is a fitted
  stand-in that this measurement refutes, and no gate depends on it.
  Counted ESTIMATES: (a) the lion centroid shifts with the walk pose by
  up to ~30 native px = 8 units = 12 u/s at a 0.6 s baseline; (b) the
  camera anchor for the lock is cam = 0 with a bounded +0..+42-unit
  slack (the worm's own bounds box is what pins it: observed world
  229-281 must lie inside bounds 230-320); (c) s = 10 is assumed for a
  held keyboard direction (PR-132: 10 IS full one-axis intent); (d) the
  worm eye is +-2 native px. None of them moves the 50-vs-28 decision:
  the ratio to decide is 1.8x and every error above is <= 0.3x.

## PR-135 — the 50 ms iteration and the engine's own velocity law APPLIED ON
## THE PORT SIDE: LL_ITER_MS 28 -> 50, `v -= T*v/100` then `v += F*s/100`
## per iteration replacing the fitted target-velocity model, AT MOST ONE row
## admit per iteration for both actors, every play and scene pin re-derived
## as closed-form arithmetic, and the object's hurt cooldown counting
## iterations (behaviour change; 14 one-line mutation controls, 13 caught,
## 1 named survivor)

- WHY. PR-134 MEASURED the clock and stopped at the measurement: its own
  record ends with "WHAT THE PORT DOES WITH THIS, AND THE DIFF NAMED", and
  HANDOFF §8 T1's next step is to apply the law instead of fitting it. The
  port was running PR-79's model - a TARGET velocity of +/-T with an accel
  limit - on a 20 ms internal grid whose nominal constant (`LL_ITER_MS` =
  28) nothing in the code used, a row loop that admitted as many rows as the
  feed allowed, and a `4 * nfr` cap plus a "resync" as a safety net. Every
  one of those is now the engine's own record step, for the lion and for
  every scene object.

- WHAT SHIPPED. ported/ll_play.h - LL_ITER_MS 28 -> 50 with the assert in
  the selftest, plus LL_PLAY_DRAG_DEN / LL_PLAY_INTENT_FULL / LL_PLAY_V_EPS
  naming the three numbers the law uses; ported/ll_play.c - the velocity
  register (sections 4-5), the row clock reduced to one feed and one admit
  per iteration (sections 6-7), the `vy >= 0` guard on the ground snap, and
  the re-derived hermetic legs; ported/ll_level.c - obj_row_tick() +
  obj_advance() as one record step per iteration, `brk_arm` as the
  list-end bit, the per-iteration hurt countdown and its rate check, and
  the object legs re-derived; the Makefile - every verify-play and
  verify-level position pin replaced by the value its own closed form
  gives, with a RE-PIN NOTE (Makefile:673) stating what is derived from
  what; HANDOFF.md, this record and tools/re/mov_byx_gate.py's stale prose.
  7 files, +2411/-1178. NO new make target, so HANDOFF §3 is unchanged;
  .github/workflows/* untouched; no game data or frames in git (all cut
  material under /tmp/opencode/pr135/ and the gate logs).

- THE UNIT FRAME, restated once because the arithmetic depends on it.
  `p->vx`/`p->vy` stay units/s in this port (the integration at
  ll_play.c:1179-1200 multiplies by dt). The engine's register is hundredths
  of a px per ITERATION (the /100 at 0x5435d), so at LL_ITER_MS = 50 its
  per-iteration `v -= T*v/100; v += F*s/20` is, in port units,
  `v -= v*clamp(T,.,130)/100` then `v += F*s/100` - the same steady state,
  F*s/T units/s, written in the units the file already uses.
  LL_PLAY_DRAG_DEN = 100 and LL_PLAY_INTENT_FULL = 10 name those two
  divisors instead of leaving them inline.

- THE LAW, AS IMPLEMENTED (ll_play.c:1085-1165). ONE physics pass and ONE
  state step per iteration of LL_ITER_MS: player_iterate()
  (ll_play.c:913-1449) is that single pass, and ll_player_step()
  (:1451-1464) only turns a wall-clock call into whole iterations and
  carries the remainder:
    1. s = +/-LL_PLAY_INTENT_FULL while the facing-relative direction key is
       held in a BY_X state, or for an auto_walk state; s = 0 otherwise.
       With s = 0 the DRAG is the brake - the engine has no authored hard
       brake for A_WALK, which is why ZARIA's lion glides and A_STAY's T=90
       does not. PR-83's user report ("kept walking forever") is now the
       law's own behaviour rather than a special case.
    2. td = st->tx, capped at 130 exactly as the parser does (0x52590). NO
       lower clamp is modelled - the engine's raise to >= 20 is conditional
       and which objects carry the +0xbc guard is still open - so an
       authored `T=0` stays drag-free here. Counted, item 2.
    3. d = vx*td/100. A sign flip across the drag, or a remainder smaller
       than one register unit, sets that component to 0 (0x5426x zeroes the
       component the same way). The epsilon itself, LL_PLAY_V_EPS = 0.2
       u/s, is a MODEL CHOICE - counted, item 4.
    4. vx += fx*s/100. The row-node `F I` velocity-TARGET channel (0x54170)
       and the `FC`/`IC` sums stay unmodelled, exactly as before this PR:
       0x54170's target is built only from the row nodes (PR-98/99), so
       there is nothing to add without them. Counted, item 7.
    5. the runaway guard at +/-20000 u/s stays; it bounds authored runaway
       F/T, no data needs it.
  PR-79's target-velocity model is DELETED, not kept beside it. T is a drag
  percent, not a speed cap - that was PR-132/133's reading; this is where it
  lands.

- THE CLOSED FORMS every position pin is now checked against (written beside
  each leg in the Makefile, and derived by arithmetic, not read off a run):
    * ZARIA [A_WALK] F=100 T=20 s=+10: v_n = 50*(1 - 0.8^n) u/s and
      x_n = x_0 + 2.5n - 10*(1 - 0.8^n) px, so the FIRST 6-unit row of the
      rotated walk list closes on iteration 3 and a full 14-row cycle needs
      14 admits;
    * RAN.01 LEW.RAN [A_WALK] F=400 T=90: v_n = 44.44*(1 - 0.1^n),
      x_n = 40 + 2.2222n - 0.2469*(1 - 0.1^n) px from the pozycja snap at
      (40,286);
    * the worm's BY_X [A_RUN] F=100 T=40: 1.25 px per iteration, 25 u/s
      steady - PR-134's video bound for that same animal was <= 30.3;
    * any non-BY_X state: the accumulator is fed EXACTLY 100 per iteration
      and admits at most one row, so a 300-unit row is 3 iterations and a
      500-unit row is 5, and the ENTRY iteration takes the first row (the
      transition runs before the row clock).

- THE ROW CLOCK IS THE ENGINE'S, ONE ADMIT PER ITERATION (ll_play.c
  section 7, :1343-1449). One accumulator, two feeds chosen by the state's
  mode, exactly as
  the dispatcher 0x543a0 does it: a BY_X state with a non-zero `F=` is fed
  the TRAVELLED distance (`|dxv|` of that iteration, PR-98's law), every
  other mode is fed 0x4c8b7's constant 100. The compare is after the feed,
  the threshold is SUBTRACTED, the remainder carries into the next row, and
  AT MOST ONE row is admitted per iteration (0x521f0 runs one key
  composition + one feed + one admit; 0x5232b is the compare). The `4 * nfr`
  cap and the "resync" that followed it are GONE - they were a guard
  against the multi-admit loop, and the loop is what the engine does not
  have. `--play-selftest` now ASSERTS LL_ITER_MS == 50, so the constant
  cannot drift away from the legs derived against it.

- THE OBJECT ENGINE RUNS THE SAME RECORD STEP (ll_level.c:1107-1321).
  obj_row_tick() turns a call into whole iterations and carries the
  remainder; obj_advance() runs ONE record step per iteration - one key
  composition, one feed, one admit, the same two feeds chosen by mode. The
  list-end signal is the engine's bit, not a side effect of a loop:
  `brk_arm` (0x521d7) is armed by the step whose row list wrapped and
  tested by the NEXT step's key composition, which is PR-133's reading and
  now the port's shape. The [obj+0x102] hurt cooldown counts ITERATIONS,
  like the lion's pl->lock, and the obj_state leg now pins its RATE too -
  seven of the fourteen steps must still be running, and a hit at that
  point must still be refused. That check exists because `hit_cd -= 2`
  passed every leg in the repo until it was written (M13 below). The walk
  rate is
  that same law read in px per iteration -
  |F|*LL_PLAY_INTENT_FULL*LL_ITER_MS/(1000*clamp(T,.,130)), i.e. F/(2T) at
  50 ms, which is PR-79's F/4 exactly where the shipped data sits (T=40: 25
  px/s, PR-134's measured worm). Objects get NO velocity register of their
  own: they step straight to the steady rate, because every measured object
  speed in this record is a mid-walk number and nothing separates the two.
  MODEL CHOICE, counted, item 5.

- WHAT A USER SEES DIFFERENT. The lion walks at the authored F/T of each
  level's own [A_WALK] (ZARIA 50 u/s, RAN 44.4 u/s) instead of PR-79's 20;
  a released key coasts out over the state's own drag (25 iterations at
  A_WALK's T=20) instead of stopping on the tick; a scene object's rows
  advance one per iteration, so the animated platform's 500-unit rows step
  every 5 ticks and its 300-unit rows every 3; the lion's walk cycle draws
  6-unit poses every 2.4 iterations and the worm's 4-unit poses every 3.2 -
  the two gaits PR-134 measured from the video come out of the authored F/T
  and row pitch, they are not fitted.

- THE VERTICAL IS DELIBERATELY NOT RE-FITTED, AND THE LEG SAYS SO.
  LL_PLAY_JUMP_DIV = 4 and LL_PLAY_JUMP_G = 1650 are per-second constants
  from ONE measured jump (PR-73/74/86). Applied per 50 ms iteration they
  peak 20 px above the take-off line (min y 628 against the 648/649 walk
  line) - 4 px below what the old 20 ms grid produced, and within 4% of the
  21 px of the single jump PR-74 actually measured. Re-fitting four
  constants against one measured frame is not a claim this project makes, so
  the constants stay and the 20 px is counted, item 1. The zjump leg's
  proof line and the hermetic jump leg's comment both state it.

- THE HERMETIC LEGS RE-DERIVED THEMSELVES. `--play-selftest` and
  `--mov-selftest` are data-free, and each row/velocity leg now prints its
  own derivation: the 116 ms = 2-iteration / 70-unit-remainder fixture, the
  1706 ms = 34-admit BOUND fixture whose alternating authored `M` deltas
  make the count readable, the OBJM fixture whose 500 ms call must run TEN
  record steps whose ten admits read as ten authored deltas, the jump arc's
  per-iteration velocity table (+82.5 u/s per iteration), and the climb
  leg's BY_TY list re-derived as 17 iterations - a 200-unit row is 2 of
  them, a 300-unit row 3, and the wrap lands on the 17th feed.

- THE MUTATION CONTROLS, RUN AND EXTENDED. FOURTEEN one-line patches; the
  harness is /tmp/opencode/pr135_mut2.py (it re-uses the patch table of
  /tmp/opencode/pr135_mut.py), and each mutant's FULL selftest output is
  kept in /tmp/opencode/pr135/mut2/. Counts are `failing_checks` in each
  data-free selftest: `--mov-selftest` stops at its first failing leg, so a
  `mov` count is a floor, and any leg named below as "would also break" is
  DERIVED from the fixture, not observed. The two patches whose rate or
  guard behaviour the DATA legs could also expose - M12 and M13 - were
  additionally run against them (`make -k verify-play verify-level`, with
  the fixtures). THIRTEEN OF FOURTEEN CAUGHT. NAMED RESULTS:
    * M1, the player admits TWO rows per iteration (the old loop). CAUGHT,
      play 8 checks - the PR-115 MULTI/BOUND leg's counts (`fi 2`, row_t
      70 and 140 with the 16 ms carry, x 230 and 260) plus two frame-index
      CHECKs in the K_GEN-baked-state leg above it, because the extra
      admits move the frame cursor.
    * M2, the player zeroes its accumulator instead of carrying it (the old

      (`first_exit == 22 && exit_t == 24`), the walk-law and key-release

    * M3, the player subtracts nothing at the row boundary. CAUGHT, play 64

    * M4, the player's row clock fed per millisecond instead of per

    * M5, an object admits TWO rows per record step. CAUGHT, mov - the

    * M6, an object zeroes its accumulator instead of carrying it - this is

      0.33333333333333304 check is downstream and was not reached; it is

    * M7, an object's row clock fed per millisecond. CAUGHT at the

    * M8, the old `4 * nfr` cap copied into the object loop. CAUGHT - "no

    * M9, equality at the walk/row gate (PR-116's g2b flip, which PR-116

- OPEN ITEMS, COUNTED: 14.

## PR-136 — G-2 MEASURED IN ABSOLUTE WORLD UNITS: the level's OWN static
## images are camera anchors, so a video frame gives camera (x, y) rather than
## a relative shift; the method is validated against cameras the port itself
## set; what the clip then shows is the lead the game holds (95-108 while he
## walks right), a grounded vertical anchor of row ~128 and not 178, a view
## that does not hold rigidly through a jump, and a first screen whose walking
## surfaces are 7-51 units above the .PLT the port stands him on (three tools
## promoted to git; NO behaviour change)

- WHY. PR-134 ended G-2 with an audit of three estimators and the sentence
  "a landmark anchor is needed": phase correlation drifts, the named-pair
  matcher only works where the backdrop is flat, and the lion-locked case is
  circular - it cannot say what the lead is because it assumes a camera. The
  level itself carries the anchors: its placement files name static images
  ("<LEAF>,<name>.seq,<x>,<y>", the grammar PR-93 found) that the port draws
  at the authored point with no shape record, and the band of the A clip is
  the 320x200 view scaled 1.8x, so one px of the downsampled frame is one
  world unit. That makes the camera position readable as data.

- WHAT SHIPPED. Three tools, promoted into git because the repo's convention
  is that the video/RE helpers live in tools/re/: `level_landmarks.py` (cut a
  match template for every static image the level places, from the port's own
  renders), `video_camera_read.py` (per-frame camera (x, y) plus the lion's
  body and paws blobs), `camera_law.py` (turn the read into shots, leads,
  rates, the vertical anchor, coverage and the .PLT cross-check), plus their
  rows in tools/re/README.md. No C file changed; no Makefile target, so
  HANDOFF section 3 is unchanged; .github/workflows/* untouched; no game data
  and no video frames in git (atlas, reads and logs are under /tmp/opencode/).

- THE METHOD, and the two traps it had to be built around. Each template is
  cut from the port's own pixels: the level rendered at a camera that puts the
  placement in the view, composited and with `LEO_LEVEL_NO_OBJ`; the
  difference inside that placement's box IS its pixels and its alpha. Three
  cuts make the patch usable: other placements' boxes, pixels that change when
  the camera moves 8 units sideways (they blend with the backdrop) and pixels
  that move when it moves 4 units down. ZARIA.01 gives 62 placements, 14 of
  them static images, 12 templates after two draw nothing or lie outside the
  world; the probe camera must be the RENDERER's clamped one - an earlier
  /tmp atlas left the probe above CAM_YMAX and every anchor came out 7-9
  units off. Matching is masked normalised cross-correlation over every offset
  the game could show a placement at, per landmark on the FFT of the frame.
  That alone is NOT a camera measurement, for two reasons this design is built
  on: several placements share one .SEQ art (ZARIA.01 places LISC0, LISC1 and
  PLAN3 twice), so one match is ambiguous by the copy spacing; and the level's
  own backdrop and animated objects reuse the look of a static placement, so a
  match can be plain wrong. So every match only PROPOSES a camera, and a
  proposal is judged by what every OTHER placement whose box lies in the view
  at that camera scores at exactly that offset - a table lookup on the same
  correlation surface, no extra cost. Ties break toward the previous frame's
  camera (continuity) and are flagged `ambiguous`.
  Trap three: a camera value outside 0..world-view cannot be a camera, so the
  level's own geometry filters the read - and it is the filter that catches
  the false matches, not any threshold.

- THE METHOD IS CHECKED AGAINST KNOWN ANSWERS, twice. `selfcheck`: 16 frames
  the port rendered itself at cameras that were SET - 14 read exactly, error
  (0,0), at (0,500) (0,470) (12,500) (12,496) (61,437) (158,350) (358,420)
  (400,430) (687,500) (1242,500) (1647,500) (1757,500) (1920,184)
  (1920,188); the other two, (1000,400) and (1900,300), have no placement in
  view and say so. `resample`: 13 frames pushed through the capture path the
  clip went through (nearest up to 1152x720, area filter back down) - all 12
  with any placement visible read exactly, 1 coverage hole. So the read is
  unbiased at the unit level when an anchor is in the frame; that is the
  error bar, not the `margin` field, which measures how peaked a match is and
  says nothing about error (its median is 0.011 even on frames read exactly).

- WHAT THE CLIP SHOWS (ZARIA.01, 27601 frames, 460.02 s, constant rate; the
  numbers are in /tmp/opencode/pr136/law_v3.txt). 5319 frames have no
  placement in view; 21205 give a camera, of which 20116 rest on ONE
  uncontested placement and 1089 on two different ones; 328 are ambiguous;
  1077 fall outside the camera range the level's own geometry allows and are
  dropped, 1070 of them by more than 8 units. Coverage by camera_x: dense at
  0-300 (18.7k frames), a trickle at 300-800, nothing at 800-1200, 47 frames
  at 1300, none at 1400, 124/267/41 at 1500/1600/1700, none at 1800, 1244 at
  1900. The lead: the values the game HELD frame for frame while the lion
  walked right are 95-108 in 57 of 76 window-frames (modes 95-108) - the
  port's CAM_LEAD_R=100 is confirmed by the measurement it was guessed from.
  The other 19 held windows read 59-86; 15 of those are inside the clip's
  first 7.4 s with the camera pinned at the world's left edge (camx <= 14),
  where no lead can be held, and 4 are single frames near camera_x 100.
  While he walked left, 19 held windows give 199-251, so CAM_LEAD_L=220 sits
  inside the band but on 19 frames, and the plain scatter is bimodal. The
  catch-up ease, with the lion standing still, is p50 5 u/s, p95 60, max 230
  - the port's 6 units per iteration is 120 u/s, faster than everything but
  the tail. Vertically: on 3990 frames where his world y is constant across a
  13-frame window, the paws row - the same colour class PR-84 measured, and
  the feature CAM_FEET_Y is defined on - sits at 125-134, mode 128 (708
  frames), and 128 on the subset where the camera is NOT at the world clamp.
  Row 180 appears in 97 frames, all of them the clamp case: with the anchor
  at 128 and the level's own camy clamp at 500, a lion on the y~681 ground
  lands at 181 by itself. One constant plus the clamp that is already there
  reproduces both, and PR-84's own note ("anywhere the clamp does not bind,
  the 65% rule sat 40+ px too high") is what this measures. Through 139 jump
  arcs the view does not hold rigidly: camera_y change p50 0 but p05 -26 and
  p95 +12.

- AND ONE THING THAT IS NOT ABOUT THE CAMERA. The same frames say what the
  lion stands on. At the ground line the read matches the level's own data
  exactly: 108 frames at measured surface y 681, x 38-67, against
  ZARIA_A.PLT's first polyline "-50,680!408,684" - delta 0 in 108 of 108.
  On the first screen's platforms, 3990 frames put him on surfaces at y
  466-508 for x 128-392, where the nearest authored polyline at that x is
  7-51 units LOWER; of all 3990, 566 coincide within 2 units, 201 more
  within 5, and not one frame has a world x where the level has no ground
  polyline.
  The placed platform images have their top edges at exactly those heights
  (plan4.seq at 70,480 size 136x60; plan6.seq at 287,430 size 62x41). The
  port uses the .PLT and would stand him 7-51 units lower there.

- OPEN ITEMS, COUNTED: 1 coverage: at camera_x 900-1100 and 1400-1500 the
  level's OWN placements cannot fill the hole (no static image there could be
  on view), and 800-900, 1100-1400, 1500-1900 have one or two anchors and
  the clip gave 0 reads in most of them; filling it means anchoring the
  .MOV placements, whose draw offset is their .SEQ shape margin (f0/f2, which
  the port knows) - but their art changes per frame, so one template per
  placement is not valid; counted, not done. 2 The 1070 far-outside reads are
  false matches the level's own reused art causes; a rule demanding two
  placements co-match would keep only 1089 frames. Both choices are open.
  3 328 ambiguous frames are dropped rather than resolved. 4 The paws row is
  a colour mask, present in 18097 of 20392 body-blob frames; it is a proxy
  for the contact line, not the port's `p.y + contact` from the shape box
  (PR-97). 5 CAM_LEAD_L rests on 19 held-window frames. 6 Jump arcs are
  under-sampled: the paws series fails in 40% of the 31-frame windows, the
  apex population this found (p50 10) is far below PR-86's 23-30 u, and the
  "view holds" answer is therefore weak. 7 NEW GAP, named G-13: the ground
  source in the first screen, as measured above - the port's .PLT ground and
  the clip's surfaces differ by 7-51 units there and agree exactly at the
  ground line. 8 The camera's measured rates and anchor are NOT applied to
  the port in this PR; that is the follow-up PR with its own gates and
  mutation controls. 9 Tie-breaking by continuity is a MODEL CHOICE, visible
  through the `ambiguous` flag. 10 The 1501 shot boundaries under the
  20-unit/30-frame rule conflate the clip's cuts (PR-134's census) with lost
  matches; they are not a cut census.

- GATES. Docs-and-tools class: no behaviour changes, but the build legs

- HANDOFF UPDATED. Section 6's two camera rows (CAM_LEAD_R/CAM_LEAD_L and

## PR-137 — THE CAMERA CONSTANTS PR-136 MEASURED, APPLIED: the grounded
## vertical anchor is 128 on the contact line, and the world clamp (not a
## second constant) is what produces the ground-line 175..180 row band;
## the leads stay 100/220 - the right one now confirmed - and the viewer
## camera law gets its own hermetic leg, 9 mutation controls all caught

- WHY. PR-136 measured the camera law in absolute world units and
  deliberately shipped nothing: "applying the corrected camera constants
  is a later PR with its own gates" (PR-136 open item 8). The one number
  that was clear beyond argument was the vertical anchor: on 3990 frames
  where the lion's world y is constant, the paws row - the same colour
  class CAM_FEET_Y is defined on - sits at 125..134 with mode 128, and
  at 128 on the subset where the camera is NOT at the level's world
  clamp, while row 180 appears ONLY in clamp frames. One constant plus
  the clamp that has been in the port since PR-72 reproduces both
  populations.

- WHAT SHIPPED (behaviour). (1) `CAM_FEET_Y` 178 -> 128 (ll_level.c).
  The old comment claimed the 175..180 band "is NOT the world clamp";
  the 21k-frame absolute read says it is: ZARIA's ground sits at world y
  ~681 and its cam_ymax is 500, so any anchor at or below 181 lands on
  the clamp and the row comes out of the clamp. PR-84's single frame
  (n=45 paws pixels spanning y 133..180) read that clamp artifact as
  the anchor, and set aside PR-73's mid-level "~128" as a catch-up
  drift; the full clip vindicates the 128. Effect on the port: nothing
  at the ground line (clamped before and after: 681-178=503 -> 500 and
  681-128=553 -> 500 - which is why not one existing pixel pin moved),
  and +50 units of view on every surface high enough that the clamp did
  not bind - the lion sits at row 128 there, as the game shows him,
  instead of 178. (2) The camera functions now have a hermetic leg:
  `./ll_level --follow-selftest` (ll_level.c `ll_follow_selftest`, the
  flag in tools/ll_level.c, wired into verify-play next to
  --play-selftest). Before this PR NOTHING in the repo tested
  follow_camx/follow_camy at all - PR-135's mutation run could only
  speak about ll_play. (3) Comments rewritten where the old numbers were
  justified (follow_camx lead block, follow_camy anchor block, the
  verify-play cam-y leg's header): CAM_LEAD_R=100 is CONFIRMED by
  held-frame leads 95..108; CAM_LEAD_L=220 sits inside the measured
  199..251 but on 19 frames; the eases (6 x, 2 y per iteration) are
  named as models with the measured band beside them (game catch-up
  p50 0.25 / p95 1.2 / max 11.5 units per iteration). No Makefile
  targets beyond the one new leg line; .github/workflows/* untouched; no
  game data or frames in git.

- WHY THE LEADS AND EASES DID NOT MOVE. The measurement does not pin
  them. The held right lead is 95..108 - 100 is inside it, and moving
  it would be fitting to noise; the held left lead is one 19-frame band
  (open item 5 of PR-136 counted exactly this). For the eases, the
  port's model ("the offset eases toward its target at K per
  iteration") is not even the shape the data supports: with the lion
  standing the game's camera moves p50 0.25 u/iteration, and what the
  port cannot see is whether the game tracks at lion speed and corrects
  by a different law. Keeping a model and pinning it in a test is more
  honest than replacing one unmeasured number with another.

- THE TEST (data-free, every value by hand, in the leg comment): a
  ZARIA-shaped world (320x200 view, 2240x700 world, cam_max 1920,
  cam_ymax 500, contact 28). Ground spawn snap: feet 653+28 = 681 ->
  681-128 = 553 -> the clamp gives 500, and the drawn paws row 681-500
  = 181 is inside the band PR-84 measured - that IS the clamp case,
  asserted as such. Mid-level: feet 470 -> camy 342, paws row 128 - the
  measured anchor; with the old 178 this returns 292. Ease model: 2 per
  call, exact final step from a 2-unit remainder. Floor clamp: feet 100
  -> target -28 -> 0. Airborne: view holds at 342. Leads: a held right
  lead means cam = p.x - 100 exactly; a turn eases 6 per call -
  asserted mid-flight at call 10 (ox 160) as well as at the end (220,
  cam 780) - then the world-edge clamps (p.x 50 -> cam 0; p.x 2100 ->
  1920).

- MUTATION CONTROLS: 9 mutants, ALL CAUGHT (/tmp/opencode/pr137_mut/
  mutate.py). m1 anchor back to 178 (case 2, got 292); m2 top clamp
  removed (case 1, 553); m3 floor clamp removed (case 4); m4
  `grounded` guard dropped - the view follows through jumps (case 5);
  m5 y-ease 2->6 (case 3, 306); m6 x-ease 6->7 (case 7 mid-flight, ox
  170); m6b x-ease 6->5 (ox 150); m7 leads swapped (case 6); m8 spawn
  snap removed (case 1, 2). The honest sequence: the FIRST run had 7
  mutants and caught 6 - m6 (x-ease 6->7) SURVIVED, because case 7
  only asserted the settled end state, which any ease rate < 120/20
  reaches; the case then gained the mid-flight assertion (call 10 ->
  ox 160), and that near-miss is recorded rather than hidden. The 9/9
  transcript is /tmp/opencode/pr137_mut/run_final.txt; the pre-
  strengthening survivor was re-confirmed afterwards by re-running the
  original 7-mutant set against the pre-strengthening case 7
  (run_initial_repro.txt, 6/7, m6 passes) - reproduced, not just
  remembered.

- OPEN ITEMS, COUNTED: 1 the eases stay invented numbers, now tested
  AS models; the measured p50/p95/max are in the code comment but not
  applied, because the shape of the law is unknown. 2 CAM_LEAD_L is
  pinned to 220 by a test, not by evidence (n=19). 3 the airborne hold

## PR-138 — G-13 CLOSED AS A READING RECORD: the engine's ground records

## ARE the authored .PLT text - the platformy= loader makes one object
## per polyline line and each line parses ITSELF into the 13-byte
## records the player's segment lookup then searches (PR-123's
## unmatched records, closed) - while PR-136's "surfaces 7-51 units
## above the .PLT" is RETRACTED: those numbers were screen-x from
## false-matched single-landmark cameras, every VERIFIED frame in the
## clip stands the lion on a .PLT line at d+0, and the ground work
## that actually remains is a named port gap: the ani_plat= local
## ground lines (ANIPL2, the engine's MOVEPLAT chain) are never read

- WHY. Two questions were open on G-13. Engine side, PR-123 had
  recorded the ground lookup's 13-byte records but "could not match
  them to .PLT text" - so it could not say whether the .PLT file the
  port parses is what the engine actually queries, or one of two
  sources. Data side, PR-136 had measured "the first screen's
  walking surfaces sit 7-51 units ABOVE the ZARIA_A.PLT lines" (and
  PR-137 open item 4 kept that alive). The interim measurements of
  2026-11-18 are superseded by this record: both sides conclude, and
  the answer changes what G-13 means.

- WHAT SHIPPED. One tool promoted into git by PR-136's convention
  (video/RE helpers live in tools/re/): `ground_surfaces.py` -
  tier-filtered, world-coordinate standing clusters, each
  cross-checked against every .PLT segment at its centre x and
  against every static-image top edge of the landmark atlas. The
  defects of this session's first pass - mixing screen-x with
  world-y, and clustering tier-2 frames at all - are exactly what it
  is built to prevent; the README row says so. Plus this record and
  the HANDOFF updates. No C file changed, no Makefile target, no
  .github/workflows/* touched, no game data or frames in git. No
  test accompanies it because nothing behavioural changed; the
  test-and-mutation rule applies to the ANIPL item below, where
  behaviour does change.

- THE ENGINE READ, POLYLINE SIDE (closes PR-123's identity question;
  every address cited in /tmp/opencode/pr138/engine_read.txt). The
  level loader opens the platformy= file at 0x4d424-0x4d472 and
  0x4dc00 allocates an array of class 0xa0c78 objects at
  [level+0x74] with count at [level+0x80] - ONE OBJECT PER POLYLINE
  LINE of the .plt text - and calls [obj+0x20] on each with that
  line's text. That method, 0x45120, is why PR-123 could not match
  the records to the text: THE LINE PARSES ITSELF. `%d` (0x9182d)
  reads the line's leading number - the count of EXTRA vertices
  beyond the first point, the same quantity the port's ll_plt_parse
  reads - into [obj+0x8], and (cnt+1)*13+4 bytes become the record
  array at [obj+0x4]: cnt+1 thirteen-byte records. 0x4a0b0 parses
  each `%d,%d` pair (0x91d0f) into rec+0 x and rec+4 y, skipping
  " , " between lines (0x91d15); ` %c` (0x91830) peeks the
  separator and sets rec+0xc: a ';' follows -> 1, '#' -> 2,
  otherwise 0 - the segment-kind flags the .plt text writes. The
  instance vtable 0xa0cc0 (set at 0x44fb0) holds 0x45320 at +0x18
  - the method PR-138's interim pass called the "shared base" of
  ~38 class vtables; it is the polyline ground base, and it adds
  [this+0xca]/[this+0xce] (the object's own position) to the query
  point, which is how a placed object can own LOCAL ground lines -
  0x45400 at +0x1c, and the parser at +0x20. The segment search
  0x45380 reads the count at [owner+0x8] and indexes records at
  [owner+0x4] - the exact array 0x45120 filled: the .plt polyline
  object IS the table the lookup searches, which closes PR-123 open
  item 1. 0x45200 translates every record of a polyline by (dx,dy)
  - the move-a-floor method. Class 0xa0c78 is referenced only at
  0x4dc69 (that loader) and 0x44f9d (a class check), so in this
  image the player-queried polyline records have exactly one
  builder: .plt text. No second ground-record builder was found.

- THE ENGINE READ, ENTITY SIDE (names the real remaining ground
  item). The twin method 0x34850 (entry found by its prologue - the
  linear sweep aligned it at 0x34852; exactly one vtable pointer, at
  0x9dc80, inside the class table at 0x9daf8) holds an array of its
  OWN 13-byte-stride records at [obj+0x48] with count at [obj+0x4c]
  (indexed with the same stride at 0x3487b/0x3489a), and FIRST asks
  the global provider at 0xcef40+0x394 (provider vptr at +8, method
  slot +0x4c), merging the four-dword answer with the local table.
  The provider is written at 0x4de2d-0x4dea4 in a loader chain that
  names the subsystems ANITAB / PLANT / GRABOBJ / DEMOTEXT /
  ANIBACK / MOVEPLAT / MOVERECT (strings at 0x91f42, next to the
  PR-103 name factory's formats): entities that carry their own
  ground records are the platform subsystem's objects - the
  ani_plat= chain, read through the same 0x45320 offset-by-object
  base. What fills the entity table, and what the provider answers,
  stayed unread (open items 1 and 4).

- THE DATA SIDE, RE-MEASURED AT FULL RATE with the confidence tiers
  the reader already prints (tier 1: two DISTINCT placed static
  images agree on one camera - only such frames may be called
  verified; tier 2: a single uncontested landmark). The whole clip
  re-read at 60 fps (27,601 frames; 18,376 with a lion blob and a
  7-value paws read inside the level's camera range): 951
  unambiguous tier-1 frames with a lion blob - 722 of them also
  with the full paws read - and EVERY ONE at camera x 1..122, the
  first screen only; 17,375 tier-2 frames carry every other claim.
  (1) At the ground line the agreement is now stronger
  than PR-136's 108/108: on tier-1 standing frames, 125 samples at

  -50,680!408,684" at d+0 - exactly zero, not within tolerance.
  (2) The disputed mid-level populations are tier-2 ONLY: all 19 of

  - and 19 different surfaces in a 260-unit x window of a 2240-wide
  level is the signature of a mislabelled coordinate, not of

  paws_x + camx is the SCREEN x, not world x. PR-136's "x 128-392"
  band IS that band. THE 7-51 MEASUREMENT IS THEREFORE RETRACTED -
  it compared screen-x clusters against world-x .PLT segments, and
  the "platform image top edges at exactly those heights" argument

  (3) The probe that proves the false matches, frame 4370: the
  reader returned camera (173,320) at frames 4362/4368/4374 (tier-2,
  one landmark). But the frame shows the mid-level balloon scene:
  ANI2.DES places `BAL,balonik.ani,balonik.mov,1270,460` (of six

  five). The port's own render at cam (1079,335) matches the frame
  (/tmp/opencode/pr138/frames/port_1079.png vs f4370.png). Scene

  shelf is exactly those lines: "1 922,509;968,508", "1
  993,506;1141,507", "1 1171,506;1305,503" span x 922-1305 at y

  (4) The one other tier-1 "surface" the tool found - 10 standing
  samples at y 580, world x 118..130, frames 466..475 - is my own
  filter's artifact, settled by looking at frames 460/466/472: at
  460 he is on the ground in the tree shot the port renders at
  (173,320), and at 466-475 he is mid-jump. A window that only
  requires "world y constant over +-0.1 s" also matches a jump
