  a jump travels horizontally. (The earlier read's walk/stand
  classifier called it standing while walking; it was wrong.)
  CONCLUSION: for the first screens the data asks for no ground
  source beyond the authored .PLT, and the engine builds no records
  the .PLT text does not write - G-13 as PR-136 framed it is
  dissolved, and with it PR-137 open item 4. The ground-related gap
  that REMAINS is a port gap with a name: ani_plat= files are never
  parsed for ground at all. ANIPL2.DES (ZARIA.01) carries four
  entries, each followed by a .plt-style LOCAL line: KATAPULT@300,
  588 "1 7,45;40,45" with a trailing "-6300,-1350", and
  PALMA@820,435 "1 18,40;80,40", @965,335 and @1010,275
  "1 -80,45;-18,45" - world tops 475/380/320. The engine's entity
  twin above is plausibly their reader (0x45320's add-the-object-
  position is exactly what local lines need); the port's ground
  load (ported/ll_level.c 6721-6756) parses platformy= only, plus
  the .des-as-.plt fallback, and drops ani_plat entirely
  (ll_level.c 4703-4766 count the references). Reading the
  0x34850/MOVEPLAT chain and parsing those local lines, with a test
  and mutation controls, is the successor item - call it G-13's

- OPEN ITEMS, COUNTED: 1 nobody was FOUND that fills the entity-side

## PR-139 — G-5 CLOSED: AN AUTHORED `damage=` HURTS THE LION ONLY THROUGH

## THE OBJECT'S OWN ATTACK WINDOW - the port's unconditional

## contact-damage block is DELETED, the engine's clash gate 0x550c0 is

## ported as a named helper, the window latch is the authored `atc_on`

## directive at last (its apply method 0x45c20), and PR-89's hit

## countdown 14 is corrected to the 0x1e = 30 that the lion's own class

## table installs

- WHY. G-5 is the gap that decides how far the stage can be walked:
  the port has carried, since PR-89, a rule that a lion/object shape
  contact deals damage on first touch - 15 for the worm, 30 by the
  stomp default - and that rule kills a walking lion around x=153-180,
  which is exactly where the stage's first climb sits (G-9's probe was
  blocked by it). The A-clip cannot settle the question either way:
  the 6.35-7.35 s contact shows the push-out, but no HUD is read (the
  lives are G-8), so "did the lion lose life on that bump" is not a
  decidable video claim. The two engine claims underneath the rule had
  never been read either: what `[obj.vt+0x40]` tests (PR-94/96 called
  it an is-enemy predicate) and what a hit RECEIVER does with the
  damage. Both are read now; both change behaviour, so this is a
  behaviour PR with a hand-derived test.

- WHAT SHIPPED. `ported/ll_level.c`: the unconditional contact-damage
  block in `play_collide` is deleted (a comment names what replaced
  it); the object's window block keeps the authored damage and gains
  the engine's clash gate as `clash_suppressed()` (0x550c0);
  `LL_OBJ_HIT_CD` moves 14 -> 30; the `atc_hit` flag is now consumed
  only when a hit lands, so a window cancelled by 0x550c0 stays armed;
  every comment that carried the old reading is rewritten with the
  addresses this PR read. A new `--mov-selftest` case,
  `contact_model_selftest`, pins the law with no game data and no
  video. `Makefile`: the two pinned play legs are re-pinned with an
  in-file RE-PIN NOTE. No `.github/workflows/*` touched, no game data
  or frames in git.

- WHICH ANSWER ENTRY EACH FAMILY INSTALLS (the census that rewrites
  PR-96's wording). Method: the image blob `build/leo/leo.img`
  (sha256 `edf19a129e85efb8...c40e`, byte-identical to the copy the
  disassembly was made from) scanned for four-aligned dword
  occurrences of each method, treated as vtable slots, then each
  candidate checked for an in-image +0xd0 pointer ("N slots, M
  sane"). Answer-A 0x50f80: 15 slots, 15 sane. Answer-B 0x552e0: 78,
  78. The window-bit getter 0x23860 at +0x40: 156, 155 (one
  candidate is not a vtable); the constant-0 getter 0x23c00: 64, 61.
  The face getter 0x239f0 at +0x70: 186, 186. Over the 155 sane
  window-bit tables the +0x9c filter slot is 0x23a40 in 150 and
  0x3d980 in 5. So "every answering family installs 0x50f80"
  (PR-96's shorthand) is FALSE, and it matters: the animals ZARIA
  places are in the answer-B set. The authored `SEP` token compares
  at 0x616a4 (literal 0x9320b) and its constructor 0x62e40 writes
  `[obj+8] = 0x97bc0` at 0x62e59 - a table with +0x40 = 0x23860,
  +0x78 = 0x552e0, +0xd0 = 0x1ecd0, +0xe4 = 0x4ffb0. `LICHA`
  (0x9321c, ctor 0x61890) and `PAJAK` (0x93222, ctor 0x626c0) chain
  into sub-factories that this PR did not resolve - counted below.

- THE ANIMAL ANSWER IS THE WHOLE LAW (0x552e0 -> 0x55230, verbatim).
  0x552e0 needs a real shape meet (`call 0x53ae0` at 0x55308) and the
  `[obj.vt+0x9c]` filter (0x55318), then calls 0x55230 at 0x55328.
  0x55230 (push ecx/esi/edi at 0x55230; the body the disassembler
  enters at 0x55232) has three branches and nothing else:
  (a) 0x55242 reads `[obj.vt+0x44]` - 0x23920, which returns the flag
  word of the object's CURRENT animation row record,
  `[[[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4]+0x12]` - and if it carries 0x80000 it
  calls the other side's `[+0xd0]` with `ecx=0, ebx=0`, i.e. a
  DAMAGE-0 hit (0x55245..0x55257); (b) if the object's window bit is
  set (0x5525d..0x55267) it calls answer-C 0x55130 (0x5526f); (c)
  else if that same row word carries 0x2000 (`test ah,0x20` at
  0x5528b) it reads the LEVEL's global `danger_power`
  (`[ds:0xcef40+0x54]`, 0x55290/0x5529f) and calls the hit with THAT
  as the damage (0x552a2). Answer-A 0x50f80 is the same two laws for
  the 15-table family - its window gate is 0x50ff1 and its DANGER
  branch 0x51011..0x51033, reading the same global at 0x5102d. There
  is no fourth path: an authored `damage=` reaches the lion only
  through (b). The port models exactly (b) plus the (c)-is-nothing
  consequence, and no code for (c): no shipped level authors
  `danger_power` (PR-90 census; the port's own level dump prints
  `danger_power=(not authored)`), and a 0-damage hit is dropped by the
  receiver's own first gate.

- THE WINDOW LATCH, AND THE OPEN ITEM PR-90 LEFT (now closed). The
  bit 0x23860 tests is bit 5 of `[obj+0xb6]`
  (`mov eax,[eax+0xb6]; shl eax,0x1a; shr eax,0x1f`). Its only
  writer found in the image is the action-record applier at 0x45c20
  (the function the disassembler shows from 0x45c22): `and
  [obj+0xb6],~0x20` then `or [obj+0xb6],([rec+8]&1)<<5`
  (0x45c2d..0x45c45). The records it applies are built by the row
  directive parser: 0x4636e matches the literal `atc_on` (0x918f2)
  case-insensitively (0x76a69), allocates 12 bytes (0x46383), writes
  the vtable 0xa10f0 at `[rec+4]` (0x46398) and the flag 1 at
  `[rec+8]` (0x4639f); `atc_off` (0x918f9) is the same record with
  flag 0. 0xa10f0's slot +4 IS 0x45c20, so an authored `ATC_ON` row
  is exactly what opens the window the collision path tests. PR-90's
  open item "no pinned consumer of `atc_on` in the hit path" is
  CLOSED by this. (The authored `lock` directive is the sibling
  record, vtable 0xa10d8, same applier slot -> 0x45c50.)

- ANSWER-C 0x55130, VERBATIM (the hit delivery). At entry eax/ebx are
  the pair; 0x55140 saves `[obj+0xad]` (the energy counter - see
  0x54550 below); 0x55146 asks 0x550c0; on "no suppression" 0x5514f
  ..0x55164 call the RECEIVER's `[+0xd0]` with the deliverer's
  `[deliverer+0xb1]` in `ebx` as the damage; 0x5516a compares the
  saved value with the live one and, only if it DROPPED, sets the ATC
  variant bit (`or bl,0x1` at 0x5518c) instead of the plain one
  (`or dl,0x80` at 0x551ad). Its third argument `ecx` is the CALLER's
  choice: 0 from the animal path (0x5526f), `[obj+0xee]` from
  answer-A (0x50ffd) - open item 13. PR-91's "a landed hit raises
  AC_ENEMY_ATC, a dropped one raises plain AC_ENEMY" - which the port
  has run since PR-91 as an inference - is now machine code.

- THE CLASH GATE 0x550c0 (ported as `clash_suppressed`). 0x550cf
  calls `[toucher.vt+0x40]` on the toucher; a CLOSED window answers
  "no suppression" (0x550d2/0x550d4 -> 0x5511b). Otherwise 0x550db
  takes the toucher's face (`[toucher.vt+0x70]` = 0x239f0), 0x550e6/
  0x550f1 take both positions through the level position getter
  0x52d30 (camera terms are the same function of the same layer, so
  they cancel between the pair), 0x550f6..0x55108 build
  sign(toucher.x - self.x) - `setg` answers 0 for EQUAL x, not +1 -
  0x5510d multiplies by the face and 0x55112..0x55119 answer 1 only
  for a STRICTLY negative product. In answer-C the "toucher" is the
  LION, so an object's window hit is cancelled exactly while the
  lion's own window is open AND he is turned toward the object;
  turned away, at equal x, or with his window closed, it lands.

- THE RECEIVER 0x50ed0, GATES IN ORDER (this is what G-5's "and then
  what" question was). `eax` = receiver, `edx` = deliverer, `ebx` =
  the damage. Drop rules, in the order the code tests them:
  `[receiver+0x11a]` is 6 or 7 (0x50ed7..0x50ee9); the damage is 0
  (0x50eef `test ebx,ebx; je 0x50f76`); `[receiver+0x126] != 0`
  (0x50ef7); the pairing rule - if the RECEIVER's window bit is set
  the deliverer's must be too (0x50f04..0x50f1a). Then it records
  `[receiver+0x10a]` = the deliverer's class token (`[+0xc]`) and
  `[receiver+0x10e]` = its face (0x50f1c..0x50f38), drains the
  `[receiver+0xd2]` chain through 0x551f0, calls 0x502f0 (0x50f54)
  which tests `[obj+0x102]` and drops a repeat hit at 0x50f59, then
  0x50f67 runs `[receiver.vt+0xe4](1)` - and only then 0x54550
  `sub [eax+0xad],ebx` subtracts the energy.

- THE ARM VALUE: 30, NOT 14 (PR-89's constant corrected).
  `[obj.vt+0xe4]` is 0x50300 for 14 of the 15 answer-A tables, and
  0x50300 is `edx ? mov [obj+0x102],0x1e : mov [obj+0x102],edx`
  (0x50300..0x50315) - with the argument 1 that is 0x1e = 30. The
  countdown is then decremented exactly one per record step by 0x50720
  (0x536f0 -> 0x523f0 -> `[.vt+0xa8]`), the rate PR-135 already
  pins. So `LL_OBJ_HIT_CD` = 30. WHERE 14 CAME FROM: `edx ?
  [obj+0x102]=14 : [obj+0x102]=0` at 0x27260/0x27264 is reached from
  exactly one +0xe4 slot in that census, table 0x9a54c - a different
  family, and PR-89 read its constant as the general one. WHICH
  TABLE IS THE LION: the factory 0x1fef2 matches the class-name
  literal "TLewZaria" (0x9078b, next to "TLewZariaB", "TLewEna",
  "TLewKadmar1" - per-level lion classes) and writes `[obj+8] =
  0x96960` at 0x1ff15; 0x96960 has +0x78 = 0x50f80, +0xd0 = 0x50ed0
  and +0xe4 = 0x50300. So the 30 IS the lion's own countdown - the
  port's `pl->lock = 30` (PR-89) is exact - while the same constant
  applied to an OBJECT is a stand-in, because an animal's own
  receiver/arm pair is elsewhere: SEP's 0x97bc0 installs
  0x1ecd0/0x4ffb0, the ZWIERZ base 0x97f64 installs 0x41c30 (which
  calls 0x41180 and then `fild [obj+0x107]` -> `fstp [obj+0x14c]`)
  and 0x41460 (`fild [ebx+0x102]`, an arithmetic use - it never
  WRITES 0x1e). Neither writes 30, and the port keeps 30 there as a
  named model. The other answer-A receiver this PR read, 0x34020
  (table 0x9e134), is the object-side one PR-89 quoted: it dispatches
  on the deliverer's class token against the globals
  `ds:0xcecf0..0xced04` - 0xced00/0xcecf0 substitute
  `[receiver+0xad]*30/100+10` (0x34037/0x3406b: `shl 4`, `sub`,
  `lea [eax+eax*1]` = *30, `idiv 100`, `+10`), 0xcecf8 sets
  `[receiver+0xad] = -1` (0x340a7), the 0xced04 branch (0x340c8/
  0x340db) is PR-89's stomp and takes the fixed `mov ebx,0x1e`
  (0x34103), and the default at 0x340ce jumps to 0x34108 forwarding
  the incoming damage unchanged. So `LL_LION_HIT_DAMAGE = 30` stands
  as the stomp value; what the engine really passes for any hit is
  `[deliverer+0xb1]`.

- `[obj+0xad]` / `[obj+0xb1]`, THE TWO NUMBERS. `[obj+0xad]` is the
  energy counter: 0x54550 is exactly `sub [eax+0xad],ebx`, and the
  answer-C tail compares it before/after (above). `[obj+0xb1]` is the
  deliverer's damage: it has ONE setter in the image, 0x1e540 (`mov
  [eax+0xb1],edx` plus `or dl,0x40` into `[obj+0x66]`), reached
  through the thunks 0x207cf and one table slot (0x96ce8); it is
  zero-initialised at 0x22e48, copied field-for-field by the
  object-construction chains (0x1ed27, 0x24583, 0x28d45, 0x2e2f3,
  0x2fb7f, ...), and hard-coded to 0x14 = 20 for one class at
  0x362d2. That pattern - authored attribute, copied onto instances,
  one default of 20 - matches the shipped `.des` values exactly
  (`damage=10` x6, `damage=15` x2, `damage=20` x2 in the ZARIA.01
  .des texts this PR re-extracted), but the grammar that feeds
  `[obj+0xb1]` from the text was NOT pinned here, so the value the
  port supplies stays a model, counted below.

- WHAT THE PORT DOES NOW (the behaviour that ships). A shape contact
  with a resting animal answers with the push-out and the plain
  AC_ENEMY raise only - no damage at all. Damage flows only while the
  object's own window is open (the authored `atc_on` rows), only if
  the 0x550c0 clash rule does not cancel it, and one landed hit per
  armed episode: `o->atc_hit` is consumed ONLY when the hit lands, so
  a cancelled window stays armed. The window law the pins use:
  LICHA's `A_ATAK` is 8 rows x 400 units with `ATC_ON` on row 4 and
  `ATC_OFF` on row 8, and a forced state admits its first row on the
  NEXT iteration (PR-135), so an A_ATAK forced at tick T opens its
  window at T+16 and closes it at T+32.

- THE TWO RE-PINNED PLAY LEGS (Makefile, with an in-file RE-PIN

## PR-140 — G-9's TRAVERSE PROBE RUNS: THE WALKING LION REACHES AND

## CROSSES THE LADDER COLUMN AT x=180 AT ZERO ENERGY COST, the probe is

## pinned as a new data-backed verify-play leg, the PR-131 "the probe

## was blocked by the worm at x~153" framing is CORRECTED with the

## pre-PR-139 measurement, and the ladder/rope chain is read from the

## authored `.des` + `.MOV` pair end to end except for the answer bits

- WHY. G-9 is the climb/traverse gap: the PR-131 stage audit could not
  run its own traverse probe - "the probe was blocked by the worm at
  x~153 (G-9)" - because the port's then-unconditional contact damage
  drained energy on every bump, and the stage's first climb sits at the
  ladder column x=180 (ANI2.DES places DRABINKA at 180,510). PR-139
  removed that rule, so the probe can finally run. This PR does not
  change behaviour - it runs the probe, measures it, pins it as a
  data-backed regression leg in `verify-play` (the new
  "play traverse probe" target inside the play legs), and records the
  ladder chain it read. Per the PR-138 precedent a reading record needs
  no hand-derived data-free test; here the shipped test IS the
  data-backed leg, and its mutation controls are the named detectors.

- FINDING 1, THE TRAVERSE MEASUREMENT (the leg's own run). Setup:
  `LEO_LEVEL_SECS=12 LEO_PLAY_SOLID=1 LEO_PLAY_SCRIPT="1:FWD"` on
  ZARIA.01 - 300 iterations at the 25/s iteration clock (LL_ITER_MS =
  40, PR-110's pin). Result, all from /tmp/opencode/ly_trv.log: the
  ONLY state ever entered is A_WALK; the lion stands the ladder column
  x=180 at tick 91, x=435 at tick 200, x=685 at tick 300; damage lines
  are ZERO everywhere (`hit by`, `ATTACKS through`, `lion energy` all
  count 0), and no reaction state (A_DRAP / A_DOSTAL / A_FALL_DOWN /
  A_JUMP / A_SITW) ever prints. Both LICHA placements answer the
  contact with the SEMI push-out ALONE: 70 `solid LICHA/licha3.mov
  SEMI` lines spanning ticks 37..135. That costs DELAY, not a stop:
  the walk advances 0.8 units/tick while pressed (ticks 37..90)
  against an unpressed 2.5 units/tick (ticks 136..200) - about 40
  lost iterations across the zone. The first pinned push line is tick
  50, `solid LICHA/licha3.mov SEMI at 179,669 push -2,0 (ret -10)
  lion 157,648`. (The probe was first run at 8 s / 200 ticks,
  /tmp/opencode/pr140_walk.log; the leg pins the 12 s run because it
  also crosses the second worm and the whole second screen band.)

- FINDING 2, THE PR-131 FRAMING CORRECTED (what the old model
  actually did). With the pre-PR-139 source (HEAD~1's
  `ported/ll_level.c`) the SAME script reaches the SAME positions -
  x=180 at tick 91, x=685 at tick 300, still only A_WALK - but takes
  three contact hits: ticks 37, 67, 109, `hit by LICHA/licha3.mov:
  damage 15`, energy 100 -> 85 -> 70 -> 55
  (/tmp/opencode/pr140_mut/log_c1b.txt at 8 s, log_c1_12.txt at
  12 s). So the old model blocked the traverse by ENERGY COST, not by
  a position stop, and this probe configuration does not reproduce
  PR-131's "dies/turns back at the worms" wording as a positional
  fact - that audit claim came from a different, longer probe
  extrapolation. The new leg detects the old model ONLY through its
  damage negatives, and the record says so plainly instead of
  repeating the death claim. The video comparison stays what it was:
  the original crosses that zone in the gallop state (A_RUN), which
  the port has no path into (G-1(b)) - no video claim is made here,
  and the A-clip cuts at 6.35-7.35 and 11.0-11.35 s are never
  integrated across. Tier discipline: every position x >= 180 is
  tier-2 territory (no two static landmarks are co-visible beyond
  camera x 122, PR-136/138), and these numbers are port-vs-port
  regression pins, not video matches.

- FINDING 3, THE LADDER/ROPE CHAIN AS AUTHORED (verbatim, the part
  that is readable today). Placement (ZARIA.01 ANI2.DES lines 6-14):
  `DRABINKA,drab.ani,drab.mov,180,510` followed by its local block
  `1 33,-3` / `23,30;53,160` / `30,50`; `LINA,lina.ani,lina.mov,
  125,292` with `1 0,200` / `23,30;31,200` / `25,49`; and a second
  `LINA,lina.ani,lina.mov,525,525` with no block. The port places all
  three (`obj DRABINKA/drab.mov[mov]: art DRAB.SEQ, 3 state(s), bbox
  42x48 at (180,510)`; `obj LINA/lina.mov[mov]: art LIN.SEQ, 3
  state(s), bbox 24x68 at (125,292)` and `... at (525,525)`) and
  counts the local blocks in its honest census ("10 polyline line(s)
  (moving ground: needs the AC_* signal bus)") - it does not act on
  them. The object scripts (`ZARIA.01_DRABINKA_DRAB.MOV`,
  `ZARIA.01_LINA_LINA.MOV`, identical shape): states A_UP/A_DROP/
  A_DOWN; `[A_UP] control=BY_TIME`, `A_DROP(1)=K_GEN1`, one row
  `1,0,WAIT K_GEN1` - it hangs idle until a K_GEN1 signal; `[A_DROP]`
  unrolls the ladder downward through rows of growing art
  (`sample=6`, drab rows `2,500 3,400,smpauto 4,400 5,300 6,300
  7,200 8,200 9,200 10,200`; lina rows 2..9) with
  `A_DOWN(1)=AC_BREAK_NEXT`; `[A_DOWN]` row `11,0,WAIT K_NEVER` -
  parked, never again. The LION's side (ZARIA.01 LEW.ZAR's script):
  states A_WSP and A_WSP_LIN exist, `control=BY_TY|CHECK_ALL|
  SEQ_REV_Y`, `F=0,100 T=160,50 G=0,0`, `seq=climb` / `seq=climb_r`
  with rows `1,300` then 200-unit rows then `10,300` - the vertical
  feed PR-109 named "direction and meaning unread". The entry/exit
  law is plain text: from A_WALK and from A_DRAP,
  `A_TURN_BACK(1)=K_UP,AC_DRAB_CATCH` (and the AC_LINA_CATCH twin),
  and from A_TURN_BACK `A_WSP(1)=AC_BREAK_NEXT,AC_DRAB`; the air
  entries sit at row 3 of A_JUMP / A_JUMP_S / A_FALL_DOWN as
  `A_WSP(3)=AC_DRAB_CATCH,AC_ONAIR`; letting go is
  `A_FALL_DOWN(1)=!AC_DRAB` (and `!AC_LINA`); going up through the
  edge is `A_PODCIAG(1)=AC_EDGE,K_UP`; down is
  `A_TURN_BACK(1)=AC_DUP,K_DOWN`; the canopy state re-enters through
  `A_SCIAG(1)=AC_BREAK_NEXT`. So the mechanism the stage shows -
  walk under the ladder, hold the up key, climb - needs exactly three
  things the port does not have: the K_UP key condition, the
  AC_DRAB/AC_LINA "there is a rung here" answer bits (and their
  AC_*_CATCH air variants), and the object-side trigger that fires
  K_GEN1 to unroll the ladder. All three are open items, counted
  below; nothing was invented for them.

- FINDING 4, WHAT THE LEG PINS (the shipped test). A new
  "play traverse probe" leg in `verify-play`, placed before the
  render leg, asserting: the DRABINKA placement line above (authored
  position 180,510 with its 3 states); the tick-50 pinned push-out
  line; `test $(grep -c 'solid LICHA/licha3.mov SEMI' ...) -ge 30`
  (the answer-only contact); the position pins tick 91 `pos 180,648`,
  tick 200 `pos 435,648`, tick 300 `pos 685,648` (all `state A_WALK
  ... grounded 1`); NO damage line of any kind; NO reaction state.
  The positions/ticks are the port's own walk law output (PR-135's
  F/T register law), pinned as a regression - not fitted to anything.
  The leg adds no code and touches no `.github/workflows/*`; no game
  data or frames in git.

- OPEN ITEMS COUNTED (8 new; PR-139's 13 carry unchanged). (1) The
  K_UP/K_DOWN key conditions are unimplemented in the port's input
  model (PR-82's keys cover F/B/L/R/jump/attack only), so the
  A_TURN_BACK-with-K_UP entry law cannot run even if the answer bits
  existed. (2) Who RAISES AC_DRAB/AC_LINA and the AC_*_CATCH variants
  is unread - presumably the DRABINKA/LINA objects' own answer entry
  (the +0x78 family PR-139 censused but read only for the animal
  base 0x97bc0); neither DRABINKA's nor LINA's class table was
  located. (3) What fires K_GEN1 (the unroll trigger) is unpinned;
  same for K_NEVER's role (an always-false condition, assumed).
  (4) The A_WSP vertical feed law - BY_TY's `F=0,100 T=160,50` pair,
  SEQ_REV_Y, and the 300/200 row feeding - is still PR-109's
  "vertical feed, meaning unread"; the climb's motion law is
  unknown, so no climb constants are claimed. (5) The local polyline
  blocks (`1 33,-3` / `23,30;53,160` / `30,50` under DRABINKA) are
  exactly G-13's named remainder - the objects' LOCAL ground lines:
  the entity twin 0x34850's table at [obj+0x48]/+0x4c and the
  MOVEPLAT-chain provider are unread (PR-138), and the port only
  counts these lines. (6) No path into A_RUN (G-1(b)) still stands,
  so the traverse cost stays a delay estimate against the port's own
  walk, never a race against the video. (7) The A_WSP_LIN twin's
  per-object differences (seq=climb_r, 8 rows vs 10, different
  bboxes 24x68 vs 42x48, the second unanchored LINA at 525,525) are
  unexplored. (8) Whether the ladder blocks or carries the lion
  (SOLID/SEMI semantics for drab/lina art) is unread - the leg's
  run shows the port's collision path never meets them (the walk
  crosses the column untouched), which is consistent with the shipped
  art's states carrying no SOLID flag, but the engine-side answer was

## PR-141 — DRABINKA'S CLASS TABLE AND ITS ANSWER ENTRY ARE READ: THE

## LADDER ITSELF RAISES AC_DRAB/AC_DRAB_CATCH AT THE TOUCHER (PR-140

## OPEN ITEM 2 CLOSED FOR DRAB), THE LADDER CAN NEVER HAVE AN ATC

## WINDOW, PLAIN `LINA` HAS NO CLASS-NAME TOKEN, AND THE SIGNAL

## VOCABULARY IS RE-DERIVED FROM THE CODE (A READING RECORD - NO CODE

## CHANGE; PR-138 precedent)

- WHY. PR-140's Next item (a): find DRABINKA's and LINA's class
  tables and read their answer entries for who raises
  AC_DRAB/AC_LINA/AC_*_CATCH and what fires K_GEN1. Attribution up
  front, because it matters: the CONDITION VOCABULARY IS NOT NEW -
  PR-88 read the same parser ("the name->bit function is 0x48000",
  the literals 0x919ec..0x91c40, "AC_BLOK 0 ... AC_EV_MAX 68 ->
  3-dword masks", K_ANY/K_NEVER "node ops, not bits"), and the port
  has carried the exact LL_SIG_* enum since PR-88. What this PR adds
  is (i) the first ANSWER ENTRY of a non-animal family read end to
  end, which is where the AC_DRAB signals actually live, and (ii)
  the constructor/factory chain that pins the ladder's class table -
  neither had ever been read, and PR-139's census had left the
  DRABINKA/LINA families unmapped.

- FINDING 1, DRABINKA'S FACTORY AND CLASS TABLE. The literal
  `DRABINKA` is at 0x906ff (between SEP2 and RYBA in the
  class-name region); its factory branch is 0x1f8ac, inside the same
  token chain that names TLewZaria (PR-139). Verbatim
  0x1f8c0..0x1f951: allocate 0xd9 = 217 bytes, base constructor
  0x531f0, then [obj+0xa5]=0, [obj+0xa9]=0, [obj+0xad]=0x97f50 (an
  attribute-table pointer, sibling of the ZWIERZ-base table 0x97f64
  PR-139 named), then [obj+0xb1] = [obj+0xb5] = [obj+0xb9] =
  [obj+0xbd] = 1 — a 1x1 default RECTANGLE in the four dwords the
  answer below reads — then [obj+0xc1]=0x98274 (a data table), and
  finally [obj+0x8] = 0x97cdc, [obj+0xc] = 0x97cd4. Table 0x97cdc:
  +0x40 = 0x23c00, one of the 64 CONSTANT-ZERO window getters
  PR-139 censused — THE LADDER CAN NEVER HAVE AN ATC WINDOW, which
  removes any doubt about whether ladders can hurt through the
  PR-139 path; +0x44 = 0x23920 (standard row-flags getter); +0x78 =
  0x3f1c0 (Finding 2); +0x9c = 0x23a40 (standard filter); +0xd0 =
  0x3e5e0, +0xe4 = 0x53d80 (receiver/arm pair — unread, open item
  6). PLAIN LINA HAS NO TOKEN: the literal `LINA` at 0x910ca has
  zero code references, and the token regions instead name a
  K-prefixed CLIMBABLE FAMILY, 0x910a7..0x910fb: KSOWA, KZABA,
  SZCZURK, SZCZURS, KSMOK, KLINA, KMIOTLA, KDRABINA, KDYBY, KWINDA,
  KBLOK, KGARNEK, KMAG — matching the AC_DRABK bit (11) and
  ZARIA.02's DRABK.MOV. The ZARIA.01 `LINA,lina.mov` placements
  therefore come from some generic construction path (open item 4);
  the BRECT/BICZRECT/WSPRECT tokens at 0x90a40..0x90a4f sit next to
  the RECT bit family — suggestive only, not claimed.

- FINDING 2, THE LADDER'S ANSWER ENTRY 0x3f1c0 IS THE AC_DRAB RAISE
  SITE. Entry: eax = the ladder, edx (kept at [esp+0x34], ebx) =
  the toucher; [self.vt+0x3c] gates ("still active"); the body
  branches on [self+0x5c], the CURRENT ROW INDEX — so the ladder
  answers only from its unroll rows (drab.mov's `2,500` is row 1,
  `3,400,smpauto` is row 2 — exactly the rows A_UP's K_GEN1
  transition admits through A_DROP):
  * row == 1: [toucher.vt+0x4c], then 0x44ec0 on [self+0xa5]; on
    true `or ah,0x40` sets bit 6 of [self+0x66] — the same bit
    0x1e540 sets alongside every authored damage (PR-139 open item
    12), here raised by an object with no damage at all; meaning
    still unread (open item 5).
  * row == 2: the four rectangle dwords [self+0xb1..0xbd] are read
    into a parameter block ([esp+0x10] = the 0x98274 table) and
    probed through 0x49fb0 with edx = 0x46 = 70 — 0x49fb0 is NOT a
    record builder: it is arithmetic (`(t-a)*n`, `idiv 100`,
    halving — 0x49fb6..0x49fd7), a percentage probe of the authored
    rectangle. Its result is answered by the TOUCHER's
    [toucher.vt+0x8](record), and there are three outcomes, two of
    them SIGNAL WRITES:
    - does-not-fit branch A (0x3f237..0x3f24d): the 12 bytes at the
      toucher are memset to 0, the flag byte at [toucher+0xc] is
      written 0, then `or BYTE PTR [toucher+0x1],0x1` — bit 8 =
      AC_EDGE. A ladder the toucher does not fit answers "edge".
    - merge branch (0x3f2bc..0x3f333): build set A with `or dh,0x10`
      at byte 1 = bit 12 = AC_DRAB_CATCH; build set B with
      `or bh,0x4` at byte 1 = bit 10 = AC_DRAB; merge through
      0x49580 (the OR-INTO of the TEventSet family, PR-88/100) and
      copy the result to the toucher — flag byte at [toucher+0xc],
      then `repnz movs` from the toucher's byte +0x0: `repnz` on
      movs STOPS AT THE FIRST ZERO WORD, so a {bit 10, bit 12}
      packet writes word 0 (+ word 1 zeroed) and leaves the bytes
      past it untouched. THE HOLD/CATCH SIGNALS ARE EXACTLY
      AC_DRAB | AC_DRAB_CATCH — PR-140's open item 2 is CLOSED for
      DRAB (and PR-139's "the caller of the +0x78 entries" stays
      open, unchanged).
    - does-not-fit branch B (0x3f33f..0x3f355): `or BYTE PTR
      [toucher+0x1],0x4` — bit 10 = AC_DRAB alone, no CATCH.
  The 13-byte write target (+0x0..+0xb set, flag at +0xc) is the
  same shape PR-92 recorded for answer-A's packet copy and the same
  13-byte shape PR-101 read at [obj+0x60] as the object's identity
  key ("fills a 13-byte key out of the record class, the step, the
  owner and the frame ... ORs into [obj+0x60]"). PR-101's
  "what that key is" is STILL the open mechanism; what is now
  pinned is that a placed ladder's answer writes those 13 bytes on
  the toucher, with bit numbers from PR-88's table (AC_EDGE 8,
  AC_DRAB 10, AC_DRAB_CATCH 12). The row-1/row-2 gate also explains
  drab/lina's `1,0,WAIT K_GEN1` from PR-140: the answer is inert
  until the ladder unrolls — the K_GEN1 RAISER is still unknown
  (open item 3).

- FINDING 3, THE VOCABULARY RE-DERIVED, PLUS WHAT THIS PASS ADDS TO
  PR-88'S. Re-reading the chain 0x48009..0x49541 confirmed PR-88's

## PR-142 — THE KEY/CONDITION MECHANISM IS READ END TO END: THE

## 13-BYTE "KEY" IS THE LIVE SIGNAL SET AT [obj+0x60], 0x47e40 IS A

## SET-OPERATION DISPATCHER (NOT A REGISTRY LOOKUP), AN AUTHORED

## CONDITION IS AN AND-AGAINST-LIVE INSIDE AN ORDERED ROW SCAN - THE

## PORT'S SHIPPED CONDITION MODEL IS CONFIRMED BY THE CODE ITSELF

## (READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE; PR-138/141 precedent)

- WHY. PR-141's Next item (a), and the repo's oldest open
  mechanism: PR-88 read the condition parser and named [obj+0x60]
  "a latching TEventSet"; PR-101 re-read the same composition code
  and described [obj+0x60] as "the object's identity key" looked up
  with 0x47e40 ("null = no match"). PR-141 open items 1 and 2
  asked which is true: is an authored transition condition matched
  by that key lookup, or by an AND against a live set? This PR
  answers it with the code of both consumers of 0x47e40 - and the
  answer reconciles the two readings. No behaviour change ships
  here; what it makes possible is the climb-entry decision
  (PR-143), because the match law the port already implements is
  now the engine's law on the record, not an inference.

- FINDING 1, [obj+0x60] IS THE LIVE SIGNAL SET (13 bytes: 3 dwords
  + flag byte at +0xc) - PR-88's reading, against PR-101's. Read
  the ladder class table 0x97cdc (PR-141) as a plain slot array:
  its +0x10 is 0x53770 and its +0x14 is 0x536f0 - exactly the two
  functions that settle this.
  * 0x53770 = the class's EVENT-RECEIVE entry (slot +0x10): it
    takes a parameter record, requires [rec+0x4]=0x10 and
    [rec+0x8]=0x8138764 (a magic tag), then from
    `movsx cl,[rec+0xc]` (a BIT INDEX from PR-88's table, signed)
    builds a ONE-BIT set and ORs it into [obj+0x60] with 0x49580
    (0x53789..0x537d4). A signal arrives at an object as a record
    whose byte +0xc is a signal-bit index; receiving it SETS that
    bit in the live set. 23 class-table slots carry 0x53770
    (0x96c48..0xa24a8) - the whole object family, DRABINKA's
    table included, receives signals this way.
  * 0x23a60 = the class's "standing bits" provider (slot +0x8c,
    the callee of PR-101's compositor first step): memsets the
    13-byte buffer and returns it - ZERO standing bits. Nothing
    "identifies" a class into [obj+0x60].
  * The rest of PR-101's composition is equally vacuous for this
    family: 0x523f0 fills its 13-byte key through record vt+0x8,
    record vt+0xc, and object slots +0xac/+0xa8 = 0x23930/0x23940
    - BOTH plain `ret` stubs (eax untouched, nothing written) -
    plus object slot +0x10 (the event entry, no-op unless the
    record is a signal). The tag assembler 0x53df0 (slot +0x54)
    assembles [obj+0x89..] and owner-method chains (0x53df2..
    0x53e2b) - contribution unread, open item 5.
  CONCLUSION: [obj+0x60] is fed ONLY by signal events for this
  family. PR-88's TEventSet reading is right; PR-101's
  "identity key" language described composition writes whose
  object-class providers are empty stubs. And PR-100's note that
  0x49580 "is an in-place OR, NOT a lookup" extends to 0x47e40 -
  Finding 2.

- FINDING 2, 0x47e40 IS NOT A LOOKUP - IT IS THE 13-BYTE-SET
  OPERATION DISPATCHER. eax = a record/list, edx = a 13-byte
  CALLER KEY; it dispatches on the caller key's FLAG BYTE at
  edx+0xc through the jump table 0x47e30 = [0x47e63, 0x47edc,
  0x47fb2, 0x47f42] and asserts (error string 0x919ca via 0x49660)
  for flag > 3:
  * flag 0 (0x47e63): copy the key, fall to the epilogue 0x49543,
    RETURN 0.
  * flag 1 (0x47edc): copy the key, call 0x49550(record's own set,
    caller) = the TEventSet AND (verified slot by slot, `and` per
    dword, 0x49552..0x49562), copy the RESULT out, and return
    0x495b0(result) = "is ANY bit set" (OR of the three dwords,
    0x495b2..). THIS is the authored-condition match test.
  * flag 2 (0x47fb2): `repz cmps` of the 12 data bytes -> 1 iff
    EQUAL.
  * flag 3 (0x47f42): the same equality, negated at 0x47fa0..
    (`sete`) -> NEVER-style.
  THE FLAGS ARE AUTHORED TEXT AND THEY DECODE CLEANLY. The clause
  parser 0x47d60 writes the flag byte at [node+0xc] from the
  operator characters (0x47db2..0x47dd0, verbatim): the DEFAULT
  (any separator that is not '*' or '|' or '!', which includes an
  ordinary condition) sets flag 1; '!' (0x21, tested 0x47dce) and
  '*' (0x2a) set flag 2; '|' (0x7c) sets flag 3. The two special
  names work differently: K_ANY (0x48029..0x48048) memsets the
  node then fills set WORD 0..1 |= 0x1f8/0x2 - bits 3,4,7,8,9,10
  and 21 (AC_BREAK_NEXT, AC_BREAK_PREV, AC_ENEMY, AC_EDGE,
  AC_TIME, AC_DRAB, AC_MRECT) - plus a word-1 marker 0x2001f8
  (bit 53 = K_JUMP plus two bits beyond the 69-bit space);
  K_NEVER (0x4806f..0x4807d) leaves the set EMPTY and ORs 0x60
  into set WORD 3 - bits 96/97, where the flag byte lives (its
  +0xc byte), marking the node as the two out-of-space bits. If a
  K_NEVER node carries the default flag 1, an EMPTY set ANDs to
  nothing = NEVER - exactly the name; flag 3 (negated equality)
  is also never-matching. K_ANY with flag 1 would read "any of
  those 7 specific signals is live" - which does not match the
  name either, and flag 0's mode returns 0. The precise runtime
  honour of the two marker encodings is open item 1 - both
  constants and the empty-set/never alignment are stated; no
  semantics is fitted to the names. The '!'/'*' flag-2 nodes
  (real in shipped texts: `A_DRAP(1)=!K_UP`) and their
  complement representation are open item 2.

- FINDING 3, THE ROW-TRANSITION SCAN - THE ANSWER TO THE PR-141
  QUESTION. 0x52000 is a record method (entity-class table slot
  +0x194 - tables like 0x9a6e0, whose +0x18 is 0x521f0): the
  current ROW record keeps a transition list at [rec+0x1a] with
  count [rec+0x22]; the loop 0x52020..0x5204d walks it with stride
  0x15 = 21 bytes. Each transition record is exactly the 13-byte
  authored condition key (what the parser at 0x47d60 builds -
  node masks + flag byte) followed by [rec+0xd] = TARGET STATE and
  [rec+0x11] = TARGET ROW. For each record: `call 0x47e40` with
  the caller key = the object's LIVE STATE (the chain composes it
  via 0x536f0 into [obj+0x60]; in the step path the same merge is
  explicit at 0x52279..0x522bc: caller := authored ([rec+0x1c]) OR
  [entity+0x60]); on no match the loop CONTINUES (`add ebx,0x15`);
  on the first match it copies [rec+0xd] and [rec+0x11] to the
  output pair and stops, and 0x52052..0x52059 hands the result to
  record-class vt+0x4 to apply it. So an authored transition
  condition IS matched by an AND against the live 13-byte set
  inside an ordered scan - the OR-of-ANDs of PR-87's model is the
  SCAN (first match wins, in authored order) and the AND is the
  node mask; the "0x47e40 lookup, null = no match" of PR-101 is
  this boolean read as a pointer. There is no global key registry.
  `A_WSP(3)=AC_DRAB_CATCH,AC_ONAIR` fires exactly when bits 12 AND
  18 are set in the lion's live set - and the port's shipped model
  (comma-AND against `o->sig`, per-name wiring, GEN raising name
  bits - PR-88's selftest in ll_level.c) IS THE ENGINE'S LAW. The
  strongest confirmation the project asked for since PR-87/88,
  recorded as confirmation, not change: no port behaviour touched.

- FINDING 4, THE RECORD-STEP PATH, THE ROW GATE AND THE LATCH.
  0x521f0 is the record class's step method (table +0x18; the same
  table repeats it at +0x1c0/+0x1f8). Its argument is a 0x4c+-byte
  WRAPPER (ebp): [ebp+0x0]=entity, [ebp+0x4]=current record index
  (the [obj+0x5c]/[obj+0x50] pair PR-101/139 read), [ebp+0x1c]=
  the 13-byte authored key, [ebp+0x44]=record array; the entity
  keeps the wrapper back at [entity+0x2e] (0x52472..0x52486 reads
  it the same way). Step: [entity+0x95] := 0 at entry and := 1 on
  ANY completion (0x52217/0x5234a) - a latch whose consumer was not
  read (open item 6); rec = recordarray[index]; rec.vt+0x8 fills
  the record's OWN set; EMPTY (the row-transition records - their
  conditions live in the scan) -> merge caller := authored OR live,
  0x47e40(record array, caller), and on non-zero call the
  target-state handler [record-class vt+0x18] with ebx = 0.
  NON-empty (motion-style records) -> OR rec.vt+0xc into the
  caller in place (0x5230c), then the handler runs UNLESS a second
  gate fails: obj.vt+0xa0([rec+0x10]) vs obj.vt+0xa4 - for the
  object family 0x239c0 (`ret 0`) and 0x239d0 ([obj+0xa1] + the
  global dword at [0xcef40]+0x388, a clock-like accumulator,
  written back into [obj+0xa1]). So `STATE(N)`-style records carry
  an authored threshold [rec+0x10] tested against the object's
  accumulated index/clock - the direction convention and units are
  open item 7, and this is the field where PR-134/135's
  "row feeding" and the record-step path meet. 0x52033 and 0x522e6
  are the ONLY two calls of 0x47e40 in the image: the scan and the
  step path - exactly the two condition consumers the port models.

- WHAT THIS CLOSES. PR-141 item 1 (the 13-byte key/set): CLOSED -
  the live signal set; its only non-vacuous feeders for the object
  family are signal records through the class +0x10 entry; the
  "identity" providers are `ret` stubs. PR-141 item 2 (the
  transition evaluator): CLOSED - Findings 3/4 ARE the evaluator,
  and the port's model is confirmed by the code. PR-141 item 7
  (K_ANY/K_NEVER record words): PARTIAL - both marker encodings
  are now decoded (K_ANY = an empty node filled with bits
  3,4,7,8,9,10,21 plus word-1 marker 0x2001f8; K_NEVER = an
  EMPTY set plus word-3 bits 96/97 - and an empty set under the
  default flag 1 IS "never"); the exact runtime honour of the
  K_ANY marker stays open (item 1). PR-141 item 3 (K_GEN1's
  raiser): MECHANISM FOUND (a signal record with byte +0xc = 54
  through the +0x10 entry), POSTER unknown. PR-101's "identity
  key" wording is superseded (its composition facts stand; the
  interpretation does not). PR-92/94's 13-byte answer packets keep
  their meaning as answer-argument buffers; whether answer bits
  reach a toucher's [obj+0x60] as signal records is open item 3 -
  the concrete next question for AC_DRAB and the lion.

- OPEN ITEMS COUNTED (8 new; PR-139's 13, PR-140's 8 and PR-141's
  7 carry with PR-141 items 1/2 CLOSED). (1) K_ANY: its filled
  node (bits 3,4,7,8,9,10,21, flag 0) and flag 0's mode both read,
  yet flag 0 returns 0 - the always-fires honour is not
  reproduced; who consumes flag-0 nodes, if anyone, is unread.
  (2) '!'/'*' flag-2 (equality) nodes: how a negated condition's
  complement is represented at match time (the port models '!'
  directly; the engine's mechanism is not this dispatcher alone).
  (3) Whether the ladder answer's AC_DRAB/AC_DRAB_CATCH packet
  (PR-141 0x3f1c0) reaches the lion's [obj+0x60] as a signal
  record, and where the lion's scan caller key is composed.
  (4) Who POSTS the type-0x10/magic-0x8138764 signal records (GEN
  frames, answers, collisions - the port raises bits for all three;
  the engine's posting sites are unread). (5) What the 0x523f0/
  0x53df0 per-frame tags ([obj+0x89], owner chains) contribute, if
  anything in the 0..68 space (vacuous for the object family via
  +0xa8/+0xac stubs, not for all classes). (6) [entity+0x95]: set
  1 on every step, cleared at entry - consumer unread. (7) The
  units/convention of the [rec+0x10] threshold vs
  [obj+0xa1]+[0xcef40]+0x388, and its relation to PR-134/135's
  row-feeding numbers. (8) Class +0x10 entries that are NOT
  0x53770 (the LION family was not checked) - receive may differ
  per family.

- MUTATIONS. None: no code and no test changed (reading record,
  PR-138/141 precedent). The honesty mechanism is attribution plus

## PR-143 — THE SIGNAL DELIVERY MACHINERY IS READ: SIGNALS TRAVEL AS

## RECORDS (WHOSE TYPE/INDEX NUMBERS SHARE THE CONDITION INDEX

## SPACE), PUSHED ONTO PER-OBJECT QUEUES AND RAISED INTO THE LIVE

## SET AT [obj+0x60]; THE TRANSITION SCAN IS CALLED WITH A VERBATIM

## COPY OF THE LIVE SET RIGHT AFTER THE LIVE SET IS RECOMPOSED; AND

## THE ROW-SWITCH

## EXECUTOR 0x535a0 IS PINNED (READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE;

## PR-138/141/142 precedent)

- WHY. PR-142's Next item (a): the evaluator is read, but the
  climb still hangs on three routing questions - who POSTS the
  signal records whose receiver 0x53770 PR-142 found, whether the
  ladder answer's AC_DRAB/AC_DRAB_CATCH packet reaches the lion's
  live set, and what feeds the K_* key bits. This PR reads the
  delivery machinery end to end and pins the evaluation trigger and
  the row-switch executor. No behaviour change; every finding is
  quoted from the code of the same image (sha256 edf19a12...).

- FINDING 1, THE SIGNAL-RECORD DELIVERY MACHINERY. Three pieces,
  all read:
  * THE BROADCAST POSTER 0x4bc40 (22 call sites): called with
    eax = the global world object ds:0xcef40, ebx = the SIGNAL BIT
    INDEX (PR-88's table), ecx = a class magic (0x8138764 when the
    broadcast is class-filtered, 0 = unconditional), edx = 0. It
    walks the world's object lists ([0xcef40]+0x58 indexed arrays
    counted at +0x44, 3 list slots, plus the chain at +0x64 with
    links at +0x34), for each object optionally requires
    [obj.vt+0xc]() == the magic, then pushes the signal. THE BIT
    CENSUS AT ALL 22 SITES (the last `mov ebx,imm` before every
    call; all 22 resolved, none dynamic): bit 7 AC_ENEMY x2
    (0x1ec46/0x1ec5f), bit 16 AC_ENEMY_ATC x4 (0x247e7 + the
    three magic-filtered sites 0x2c5e6/0x2c624/0x2c664), bit 18
    AC_ONAIR x5 (0x1f468, 0x3457c, 0x34a71, 0x34a9a, 0x3a20d),
    bit 19 AC_DRECT x3 (0x246dd, 0x324f0, 0x34a48), bit 25
    AC_UP_DUP x7, bit 26 AC_SPOKUJ x1 - NO key bits (35-38/53)
    and NO AC_DRAB(10)/AC_DRAB_CATCH(12) is ever broadcast.
    Example, verbatim 0x2c5b0..0x2c5e6: an object method gated on
    [obj+0x5c]=2 AND global ds:0xcec70==0 posts bit 16 filtered
    by magic 0x8138764.
  * THE PER-OBJECT QUEUE: 0x52b10 allocates a 16-byte node
    (next=0, payload fields at +0x4/+0x8/+0xc) and appends it to
    the singly-linked list rooted at [obj+0x10] (0x52b13..0x52b3f:
    walk to the last node, store); the drain 0x52b52..0x52b7d pops
    each node and calls THE CLASS +0x10 ENTRY per node - the same
    slot PR-142 mapped to 0x53770 for the object family. So the
    queue field [obj+0x10] and the receive method slot +0x10 work
    as a pair. The direct callers of 0x52b10 include the collision
    push path (0x53b70/0x53b9d push kinds 5 and 13, PR-133's
    ported push), and other direct receive calls build payloads
    inline (0x1e931 `call [ebx+0x10]` in the collision family).
    0x52b52 itself has no direct call site - its caller is
    reached through a jump-table/far-pair encoding not present as
    a plain dword (counted, open item 2).
  * THE PAYLOAD TYPE = A NUMBER FROM THE SAME INDEX SPACE: the
    else-branch of the receive entry, 0x52bb0, dispatches
    parameter records on [rec+0x4] with `cmp 0xe / jb, jbe /
    cmp 0x21, je` - types 14, 15 and 33; the 0x21 arm treats type
    33 = AC_KILO (PR-88 index 33) as a MOVE record: it adds
    [rec+0x8]/[rec+0xc] deltas to the object's x/y at [obj+0x0]/
    [obj+0x4] (0x52bbd..0x52bd7) - i.e. signal-record TYPE
    numbers live in the same numbering space as condition bits,
    and an authored signal can carry a motion payload. The
    receiver 0x53770's bit-raise branch requires type 0x10 +
    magic 0x8138764 (PR-142); 0x52bb0 is its dispatcher for
    everything else.
  * A SIGNAL-RECORD RECEIVER EXISTS IN THE COMPOSITION TOO:
    0x523f0 includes obj.vt+0x10 in filling the 13-byte key
    (PR-142), and 0x536f0 processes the CURRENT record via
    0x53770 - a queued/processed signal is raised exactly once
    (the node is consumed by the drain).

- FINDING 2, THE EVALUATION TRIGGER AND THE ROW-SWITCH EXECUTOR.
  0x53520 is called from exactly one place: inside PR-101's
  compositor 0x536f0 at 0x5373c - and its body settles the last
  routing doubt of PR-142:
  * 0x53531..0x53557: it copies 13 bytes VERBATIM FROM
    [obj+0x60] (the live set, flag byte included) into its stack
    buffer, and calls the row-transition scan 0x52000 with that
    copy as the caller key ([ebp+0x50]/[ebp+0x5c] = the record
    array/current index select the record; ecx/ebx = result
    out). So the match test is EXACTLY (the record's own set -
    what the clause parser 0x47d60 filled - AND the live set) !=
    0, with the flag byte honoured as PR-142 read; the "authored
    OR live" merge PR-142 saw at 0x522bc belongs to the record-
    step path only. PR-142 open item 3 (where the scan's caller
    key is composed) is CLOSED: 0x53520, verbatim from [obj+0x60].
  * 0x535a0 (called from 0x5374b, same compositor) IS THE ROW
    SWITCH EXECUTOR: `mov edi,[obj+0x5c]; cmp esi,new; je skip` -
    it fires ONLY when the target record differs from the current;
    on a switch: old record's exit method [record-class vt+0x20],
    [obj+0x9d] := 0, [obj+0x95] := 1 (PR-142's latch: its writer
    here is the row-switch itself - narrow for PR-142 item 6),
    [obj.vt+0xa4] read, new record's entry method
    [record-class vt+0x1c], then [obj+0x5c] := new index. That is
    the engine's row-change law - exit method, entry method, index
    store - the shape the port's row-change models.
  * THE COMPOSITOR SEQUENCE, end to end (0x536f0): raise the
    current signal record into the live set (0x53770 branch), OR
    the standing bits (zero) and the composition, run the
    evaluation (0x53520 -> scan -> first match), then apply (
    0x535a0 row switch), then [vt+0x54] and [vt+0x28]. Signal
    processing and transition evaluation are ONE pass: a signal
    raises a bit and the transitions are tested against the live
    set in the same step.

- FINDING 3, WHERE AC_DRAB AND AC_DRAB_CATCH ACTUALLY COME FROM
  (THE LADDER QUESTION). None of the 22 global broadcasts posts
  bits 10/12 (the census above); and the ladder answer packet
  (PR-141 0x3f1c0) provably does NOT write any [obj+0x60]: its
  result lands in the CALLER's buffer - the answer chain 0x53ae0,
  which is the caller PR-139 hunted: the collision/contact handler
  0x50f80 calls it at 0x50fa9 with ebx = a result buffer on the
  caller's frame; 0x53ae0 copies the answer result (3 dwords +
  flag byte, `movs` x4 at 0x53bdd..0x53be0) there, and 0x50f80
  later ORs that buffer plus AC_ENEMY (bit 7, `or dh,0x80` at
  0x51050) into a local set and copies the 13 bytes to [esp+0x30]
  - the COLLISION CALLER's output (0x51062..0x5107a, PR-92's
  copy). So contact answers feed the collision CALLER, not the
  live set. What posts bits 10/12: direct signal raises at ~40
  sites merging bit-12 masks with 0x49580 (the 0x49580 census),
  and per-object posts with state
  gates - e.g. 0x1f440..0x1f468: an
  object whose [obj.vt+0x3c] gate passes AND whose CURRENT ROW
  INDEX == 9 broadcasts bit 18 (AC_ONAIR) right after setting the
  [obj+0x66] bit-6 flag PR-139/141 keep meeting (an honest
  correction: my first window pass read this site as bit 12; the
  resolved census above is the corrected one). So: the
  signal-posting sites EXIST and are gated on object state and
  row; which of them is the ladder/rope answer to the lion is not
  yet identified - every 0x49580 merge destination was not read
  (counted, open item 1). The KEY FACTS stand: the delivery
  mechanism (Finding 1), the consumption law (Finding 2), the
  negative that the answer packet writes no live-set bit, and the
  bit census of every global broadcaster.

- FINDING 4, THE ANSWER-CHAIN ENTRY GATE (PR-140 item 8's engine
  half). 0x53ae0 (the chain 0x50f80 calls) first reads the
  object's ROW FLAGS via [obj.vt+0x44] (PR-139's row-flags
  getter) at 0x53b18 and runs only `test ah,0x4` - bit 0x4000 =
  the port's LL_CTRL_CHECK_ANI (ll_play.h line 151) - and skips
  the chain when the toucher's row flags carry 0x10000 = the
  port's row-flag ANTI_SOLID analogue (the port's push path
  already reads that bit at 0x10000, ll_level.c 3798). The push
  branch inside (0x53b39..0x53ba9) is PR-133's ported law verbatim
  again (kinds 5 and 13, `idiv 5`, SEMI/CHK_ANI gate `and
  0x40400`). So whether an object answers a contact AT ALL is
  row-flag governed (0x4000), and ZARIA.01's drab/lina art states
  carry no such row flag - the ladder answers nothing today in
  either model, which is consistent with PR-140's run (the walk
  crossed the ladder column untouched). PR-140 open item 8
  ("whether the ladder blocks or carries the lion - the engine-side
  answer was not read") is CLOSED for the read-the-law half: the
  engine's answer entry runs only for rows flagged 0x4000, and
  ZARIA.01's ladder rows are not so flagged.

- WHAT THIS CLOSES. PR-142 open item 3: CLOSED (the scan's caller
  key = verbatim [obj+0x60] copy, 0x53520, invoked right after
  the live-set recompose). PR-142 item 4 (who posts type-0x10
  records): POSTER READ as a mechanism (0x4bc40 + the queue +
  direct calls) WITH the full 22-site bit census; per-site
  semantics are data questions, not mechanism. PR-142 item 6
  ([entity+0x95] latch): NARROWED - the row switch 0x535a0 writes
  1, the record step writes 0/1; consumer still unread. PR-142
  item 8 (non-0x53770 +0x10 entries): the pair [obj+0x10] queue +
  +0x10 receive is uniform for the object family (0x52b52 calls
  the slot, not a fixed address), so per-family differences would
  show in the slot value - the LION's own +0x10 slot was still
  not located (keeps as open item 4). PR-140 item 8: CLOSED for
  the law half (Finding 4). The AC_DRAB-to-the-lion ROUTING stays
  open (item 1) - honestly counted, mechanism found, instance not.

- OPEN ITEMS COUNTED (5 new; the carry: PR-139's 13, PR-140's 8

- MUTATIONS. None: no code and no test changed (reading record,

## PR-144 — THE LION'S OWN OBJECT SIDE IS READ: LewZaria's CLASS

## TABLES (0x96960, +0x78 = THE GENERIC CONTACT HANDLER 0x50f80),

## THE PLAYER'S CLASS-TABLE SWAPPING AT RUNTIME, THE CONTACT-PAIR

## PROBE 0x4bd32 THAT INVOKES BOTH MEMBERS' +0x78 AND AGGREGATES

## THEIR SIGNAL SETS, AND THE COMPLETE CENSUS OF DIRECT WRITES INTO

## LIVE SETS (READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE; PR-138..143

## precedent)

- WHY. PR-143's Next item (a): the delivery mechanism, the
  evaluation trigger and the answer-chain gate are read, but the
  AC_DRAB INSTANCE for the lion is not, and the LION's own +0x10
  receive entry was not located (PR-143 open item 4). This PR
  reads the lion's object side: its class tables, its receive and
  contact entries, and the machinery that invokes both parties'
  contact handlers in one pass - and censuses every direct write
  into a live set in the image. No behaviour change.

- FINDING 1, THE PLAYER CLASS TABLES. The token `LewZaria` is at
  0x9078b (0x9078c with the length byte; the factory branch at
  0x1fef2 was PR-139's), and 0x1ff15/0x1ff1c write
  [obj+0x8] = 0x96960, [obj+0xc] = 0x96958 - the same pair
  pattern as DRABINKA (0x97cdc/0x97cd4, offset by 8: the second
  table is the same table read from its +8, PR-141). The sibling
  tokens LewZariaB (0x90795), LewEna, LewEna2, LewKadmar1/2,
  LewSades, LewRan (0x908b4..0x90fe7) build the per-game player
  classes the same way. THE TABLE 0x96960 (first 0x90 slots):
  +0x10 = 0x1e130 (the lion's OWN receive entry - PR-143 open
  item 4 CLOSED: the slot value differs per family exactly as the
  PR-143 mechanism predicted), +0x1c = 0x50380, +0x74 = 0x50320,
  +0x78 = 0x50f80 (PR-142's contact handler IS the lion's contact
  entry), +0x7c = 0x537f0, +0x80 = 0x501e0, +0x84 = 0x1e0f0,
  +0x8c = 0x504e0, and the standard window (0x23860)/row-flags
  (0x23920) getters. 0x50f80 appears in 15 class tables
  (0x969d8..0xa2290) - the generic contact handler shared by the
  player and many object classes; the ladder's 0x3f1c0 and this
  0x50f80 are the SAME SLOT (+0x78) on the two sides of one
  contact.
  * CLASS SWAPPING: the player's own code WRITES its class-table
    pair at runtime - 0x1ec36/0x1ec3f (inside the branch that
    also broadcasts bit 7, AC_ENEMY, x2 at 0x1ec46/0x1ec5f):
    `[esi+0x8]=0x978dc; [esi+0xc]=0x978d4` - the lion changes
    its whole behaviour class (receive entry included) by state
    (the area is the health/death handling: `cmp
    [obj+0xad],0x64` guards at 0x50df4 too). This is a new engine
    mechanism the port does not model and has no need of - counted
    as open item 3 (0x1ec36..0x1ec3f is the exact range), and it
    explains why the receive-slot
    census found 23 identical 0x53770 slots but the lion has its
    own.

- FINDING 2, THE LION'S RECEIVE ENTRY 0x1e130. It dispatches
  parameter records on [rec+0x4]: type 5 (`jb 0x1e153` arm:
  calls the payload object's [vt+0x0](2) when the payload is
  non-null, bumps a global counter at 0xa94f4, calls 0x44900
  with the world's +0x38c field, then `edx=9; 0x52cc0` - the
  meaning of the 9 unread, item 4), type 0xc (sets
  [obj+0x12a] := 1); types below 5 go to 0x50d60 - the lion's
  FALLBACK receiver - and the tail past 0xc at 0x1e18d also
  reaches 0x50d60 for unlisted types (`jne` at 0x1e144 falls to
  0x1e18d; 0x1e18f). So the lion receives through a
  family-specific front door with its own arms (5, 0xc) plus
  the generic 0x50d60 tail (which itself contains 0x49580
  live-set merges at 0x50ab7/0x50e24 - the Finding 4 census) -
  and the bit-raise branch for the exact type-0x10+magic form
  lives in the shared 0x53770 pattern which the lion's own
  entry does NOT contain: the lion's live-set signal path is
  thus 0x50d60, not 0x53770 (this is the concrete per-family
  difference PR-143 item 4 predicted; its arms' meanings are
  open item 4).

- FINDING 3, THE CONTACT-PAIR PROBE 0x4bd32 - THE CALLER OF THE
  +0x78 ENTRIES. Four sites in the image invoke the +0x78 slot
  (0x4b5be, 0x4bda9, 0x4be09, 0x55421); the one at 0x4bda9 is
  the pair machinery: 0x4bd32 (a 4-register+stack-arg entry:
  eax/edx/ecx + one stack parameter) builds a zeroed 13-byte
  result set, then walks the world chain ([0xcef40]+0x64 ->
  +0x34 links), per object: its [vt+0x60]() gate ("participates"
  - slot meaning unread, open item 5), a filter on [obj+0x24] vs
  a parameter (a kind/layer match; with [esp+0x2c] as an "all"
  override), skipping self, then calls [other.vt+0x78](other,
  self, &result) - the SAME slot whose ladder instance is 0x3f1c0
  and whose lion instance is 0x50f80, so ONE pass gives BOTH
  members of a pair their contact turn against the other - then
  ANY-BIT (0x495b0) on the result; if signals were raised, the
  whole 13-byte result is copied to the caller's output
  ([esp+0x20], the stop-at-zero repnz idiom again, 0x4bdd4..
  0x4bde8). THE 0x50f80 CONTACT-CONSUMER PUZZLE RESOLVES PARTLY:
  PR-142/143's "collision caller's buffer" is this result set -
  the union of both members' answer/contact outputs - handed to
  0x4bd32's CALLER. 0x4bd32 itself has NO direct reference
  anywhere in the image - the exact same situation as the queue
  drain 0x52b52 (PR-143 item 2): the two per-object dispatch
  passes (contact pairs, queue drain) are both entered by means
  this disassembly does not show as a call/jmp/dword - one shared
  mechanism, kept as open item 1, named precisely. The other
  three +0x78 call sites are separate callers: 0x55421 iterates a
  record's item array [edi+0x3c]/[edi+0x40] with a fresh result
  set per item (0x553f1..0x55421), 0x4b5be and 0x4be09 sit in
  the same 0x4b5xx..0x4be0x cluster as the pair walk.

- FINDING 4, THE COMPLETE LIVE-SET WRITE CENSUS. Scanning every
  `call 0x49580` (69 sites) for the `eax = <reg>+0x60` argument
  form gives FOURTEEN sites that OR a mask directly into a live
  set: 0x244a5, 0x244ea, 0x2451e, 0x24552, 0x26738, 0x27f7d,
  0x28bc7, 0x2fbf0, 0x36cf8, 0x3dfbb, 0x50ab7, 0x50e24 (all
  in/near the lion health/contact families - 0x50e24 is guarded
  by `cmp [ecx+0xad],0x64`, the HP byte against 100), 0x537d4
  (the signal-record raise, PR-142/143) and 0x54b84 (the state-
  machine cluster). NOTE: 0x26738 is a SECOND INSTANCE of the
  bit-raise idiom (movsx/shr/idiv 0x20/shl/or + merge at
  0x26704..0x26738, [edi+0x60]) inside a function around 0x266xx
  whose index comes from a call to 0x26670 (0x266f0) instead of
  a record byte - a twin of 0x53770's raise in an unread
  context, counted as part of open item 2, not interpreted. The
  other sites' bit masks were NOT resolved individually (the
  masks are built through register chains, not immediates - open

## PR-145 — THE KEY PROVIDERS AND THE INPUT FEED ARE READ: THE

## STANDING-BITS PROVIDER IS THE GENERIC KEY-FEED 0x54910 (K_LEW/

## K_UP/K_DOWN/K_JUMP), THE OBJECT-SIDE INPUT CONSUMER 0x549f0

## WRITES THE ±10 INTENT FIELDS, AND A CONTACT PAIR SHARES LIVE

## SETS THROUGH THE TARGET FIELD +0xd2 — AND THE PR-143/144

## "UNREFERENCED" PUZZLE PARTLY DISSOLVES (READING RECORD - NO

## CODE CHANGE; PR-138..144 precedent)

- WHY. PR-144's Next items (a) and (b): the entry into the per-
  object dispatch passes, and the K_UP feed - the climb blocker
  list ends there. Both questions turn out to have large answers
  already in the image, one of them partly in this repo's own
  PR-106 record. No behaviour change; every claim quoted from the
  same image (sha256 edf19a12...).

- FINDING 1, THE STANDING-BITS PROVIDER IS THE GENERIC KEY-FEED
  0x54910, AND IT IS NOT ZERO (a correction to PR-142). PR-142
  read the ladder's +0x8c getter 0x23a60 (memset+return zero) and
  generalised "no standing bits". The generalisation is wrong:
  0x54910 is the standing-bits provider at +0x8c in dozens of
  object class tables (dword occurrences 0x96900, 0x96b14,
  0x97064, 0x97148, 0x972e0 ...; for the 0x97bc0 pair PR-139
  named, 0x97c4c = +0x8c exactly; DRABINKA's 0x97cdc overrides
  it with the zero stub - that override, not the rule). Body
  0x54910..0x549e6: it memsets a 13-byte buffer, sets bits, and
  COPIES the buffer to the caller's output (repnz, 0x549cb..
  0x549d8) - and 0x536f0's first step (`call [obj.vt+0x8c]`,
  then 0x49580 OR into [obj+0x60]) consumes exactly that form.
  The bit sources, verbatim:
  * [obj+0xa5] bit 0 -> word 1 byte 0 |= 0x80 = bit 39
    (LL_SIG_K_FIRE); [obj+0xa5] bit 4 -> byte 1 |= 1 = bit 40
    (K_ALT); [obj+0xa5] bit 5 -> byte 2 |= 0x20 = bit 53 =
    K_JUMP. [obj+0xa5/0xa6/0xa7] are AUTHORED per-state flags
    (the port's .des flags - the consumer census at 0x504e0
    below reads 0x1,0x2,0x4,0x8,0x40,0x80 and 0xa6 bits 1,2,
    0x40,0x80, 0xa7 bits 1,2,4 against globals ds:0xcef5c..).
  * [obj+0xba] (the horizontal intent field, Finding 2) != 0 and
    [obj+0xb6] bit 4 (the PR-92/139 OPEN-WINDOW flag):
    `test BYTE PTR [obj+0xb6],0x10; sete al; add al,0x23` ->
    bit index 35 = K_BKWD when the window is CLOSED, 36 = K_FWD
    when OPEN - raised by the divide-by-32 idiom (0x54964..
    0x5499a).
  * [obj+0xbe] (the vertical intent) > 0 -> word 1 byte 0 |=
    0x20 = bit 37 = K_UP (0x5499d..0x549a6); < 0 -> |= 0x40 =
    bit 38 = K_DOWN (0x549ab..0x549b4).
  So authored conditions naming K_UP/K_DOWN/K_JUMP/K_LEW-family
  bits have a concrete engine-side feed - PR-142 open item 5 is
  CLOSED and its "standing bits zero" claim is corrected to the
    DRABINKA-specific override it was measured on.

- FINDING 2, THE INPUT FEED IS NOT A KEYBOARD POLL: THE INTENT
  FIELDS ARE MESSAGE-FED. The consumer 0x549f0 (edx = a record):
  `[obj+0xba] = [rec+0]`; for [rec+4] == 1 it computes from the
  TARGET object [obj+0xd2]: target x via the [vt+0x68] position
  getter (PR-105 assumed it; here it is called), if own x + 8 <
  target x -> 10, if own x - 8 > target x -> -10 (0xf6), else 0
  (0x54a16..0x54a93); for [rec+4] == 4 the same with the raw
  block x (0x54aa2..0x54afd); and 0x54a02..0x54a08 stores the
  block POINTER into [obj+0xd2] (the contact-target field,
  Finding 3) and dispatches on [target+4]. [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe]
  are cleared at 0x54e2e/0x54e38. THE VALUES ARE ±10 - the
  numeric confirmation of PR-139/PR-145's s = 10 held-direction
  estimate (it was a labelled ESTIMATE; here is the engine's own
  constant). In the same consumer, [rec+4] == 9 is gated on the
  global ds:0xcef64 - the ZARIA-region input reader family
  (0x1e350, whose arms read modes 4 and 9 and call the PR-133
  facing flip 0x53670). Per-frame source: the frame loop copies
  a 12-byte block ([esp+0x1f0]->[esp+0x1e4], 0x4ae92..0x4aea0)
  every iteration (PR-106), hands it to the lion through
  [lion.vt+0xcc] (0x4aeca, ZARIA = 0x50340) - and 0x58690
  (PR-106's `mov eax,0xcf400; call 0x58690`) reads [0xcf400]
  as an OBJECT with a mode at +0xb and record arrays at +0xf/+
  +0x2b (0x5869c..0x586ad): the input singleton is an object
  with authored-style records. PR-108 open item 6 (who writes
  [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe]) is CLOSED; PR-106 open item 1 is
  narrowed (the block's reader 0x58690 is an object-side getter,
  its full record format still open).

- FINDING 3, A CONTACT PAIR SHARES ITS LIVE SETS - THE AC_DRAB
  DELIVERY, GENERIC FORM. [obj+0xd2] is the CONTACT-TARGET field
  (the only non-zero writer found is 0x551fc inside 0x551f0 -
  PR-108's field - which pops the contact list head into +0xd2
  and, when it empties with [obj.vt+0x3c] true, sets [obj+0x106]
  = 1; readers: the key provider above, the intent consumer, and
  0x549f0 itself). The merge at 0x54b65..0x54b84: guard the
  current ROW RECORD: `cmp [rec+0x8],0; je skip` and `cmp
  [obj+0x5c],[rec+8]` (the record's row number must equal the
  object's current row), then `edx = [[obj+0xd2]+0x10]; edx +=
  0x10; eax = [obj+0x60]; call 0x49580` - i.e. THE PARTNER'S OWN
  LIVE SET AT [partner+0x60] IS ORed INTO THIS OBJECT'S LIVE SET
  when the authored row record asks (this is the 0x54b84 entry of
  PR-144's census - its context is now read, PR-144 open item 2
  half-CLOSED). This is the generic form of "the ladder's
  AC_DRAB/AC_DRAB_CATCH reaches the lion": the pair pass (PR-144
  0x4bd32) hands both members' answers, and the live-set sharing
  runs through +0xd2 + the row-scoped merge above. Which site
  SETS the lion's +0xd2 per frame is NOT pinned (open item 1).

- FINDING 4, K_GEN1 HAS RAISERS NOW, THREE, ONE PROBABLY THE
  GENERAL ONE. (a) 0x50df4..0x50e24: `cmp [obj+0xad],0x64; jge
  skip` - HP below 100 -> OR byte [buf+0xa] |= 0x40 = bit 54 =
  K_GEN1 into a live set ([esi+0x60]) - and this fragment sits
  inside the 0x50d60 message-receiver family: 0x50df4 is a value
  AT 0x50d20, the base receiver's 13-case jump table (PR-105) -
  so a MESSAGE TYPE raises K_GEN1 when the object is damaged.
  (b) 0x244a5 and 0x24552 (lion health/death family): both post
  bit 54. (c) 0x26670 + the merge at 0x26738: a PRNG helper
  0x76bcc (Borland LCG constants: imul 0x41c64e6d, +0x3039,
  shr 16, and 0x7fff) feeding `*5+1; div 0x7fff` -> quotient 3
  -> 0x36 = 54 (K_GEN1), < 8 -> 0x37 = 55 (K_GEN2), else 0x38 =
  56 (K_GEN3) - a RANDOM K_GEN* poster raised into a live set
  through the divide-by-32 idiom; the containing class is
  unreferenced (open item 2). For the LADDER's `WAIT K_GEN1`
  idle gate, the general law is the same field for every object:
  [obj+0xad] is PR-139/140's HP/damage field (its only setter

  stated as a question, not fitted.

## PR-146 — THE SIGNAL POSTERS ARE A CLOSED SET AND THE CONTACT

## LOOP CLOSES: THE AC_DRAB POSTER IS FOUND (a direct receive call

## of bit 10), THE BROADCAST ARGUMENT FORM IS CORRECTED, THE

## CONTACT ENTRY +0x78 IS THE WRITER OF THE CONTACT LIST, AND A

## FOURTH MIS-ANCHOR (OURS, AND THE DISASSEMBLER'S) IS CAUGHT

## (READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE; PR-138..145 precedent)

- WHY. PR-145's Next item (a) named one gap with three parts: the
  entry into the contact pass, the per-frame setter of the contact
  target [obj+0xd2], and the signal-record poster for AC_DRAB. All
  three are answered here from the same image (sha256 edf19a12...).
  Reading record only; no behaviour change.

- FINDING 1, THE SIGNAL-RECORD BUILDERS ARE A CLOSED SET - SIX.
  Whole-image byte scan for the signal tag immediate 0x8138764
  (PR-142's magic): exactly SEVEN occurrences - six builders and
  the one receiver test (0x53780, `cmp DWORD PTR [edx+0x8],
  0x8138764` inside the +0x10 receive entry 0x53770, PR-142/143).
  The record layout is confirmed by the BUILDER's own stores (see
  Finding 2): +0x0 = queue link, +0x4 = record type, +0x8 = the
  tag, +0xc = the BIT INDEX. The six:
  * 0x287d1..0x2885a - THE AC_DRAB POSTER. A method (entry
    0x287a0, a clean prologue; it occurs as a table dword once,
    at 0x9a068) that gates on the object's [vt+0x3c]() predicate
    (0x287b1), takes a target object from the indexed array
    [[obj+0x30]+0x40] through the getter 0x55760 (`mov eax,
    [eax+0x40]; mov eax,[eax+edx*4]; ret`, index edx = 1 at
    0x287d1/0x287d6), requires its CURRENT record index
    [obj+0x5c] == 0x12 and that record's type <= 0x19 (0x2880b..
    0x28826), builds the record on the stack ([esp]=0 link,
    [esp+4]=0x10 type, [esp+8]=tag, [esp+0xc]=edi=0xa) and calls
    the TARGET'S receive entry DIRECTLY: 0x28846 `mov ebx,[eax+8]`
    (the target's class table), 0x2885a `call DWORD PTR [ebx+
    0x10]`. Bit index 0xa = 10 = LL_SIG_AC_DRAB. No queue.
  * 0x2c5cf..0x2c5e6, 0x2c611..0x2c624, 0x2c651..0x2c664 -
    broadcast form (0x4bc40, Finding 3): bit indexes 0x21 = 33 =
    AC_KOREK, 0x1c = 28 = AC_BECZKA, 0x1b = 27 = AC_SPOKUJ. The
    second is gated on the record index [obj+0x5c] == 1 AND that
    record's type == 1 (0x2c5f9..0x2c60f).
  * 0x2c990..0x2c9aa - a DIRECT queue push into THE LION: 0x2c995
    `mov eax,ds:0xcef40`, 0x2c9a4 `mov eax,[eax+0x394]` (the
    lion object, PR-144's field), then `call 0x52b10` with
    edx=0x10 (type), ebx=tag, ecx=0x15 = 21 = AC_LINA. The
    AC_LINA poster, aimed at the lion's own queue.
  * 0x3eac6..0x3eaf1 - a LOOP over the same [[obj+0x30]+0x40]
    array (the index register increments at 0x3eaf0): for each
    item it calls [[item]+8 +0x10] (0x3eaf1) with a record whose
    +0x8 = tag and +0xc = 0x39 = 57 = K_GEN4 - the first KEY-bit
    signal-record poster found. The record's +0x4 (type) comes
    from a register set in the unread prologue - open item 4.
  NEGATIVE, counted: no builder posts bit 12 (AC_DRAB_CATCH), and
  none posts 22 (AC_LINA_CATCH). Since this set is closed (the
  tag immediate appears nowhere else), bits 12/22 enter a live set
  ONLY through the answer-set paths: the pair union (0x4bd30,
  Finding 4) or the row-guarded partner share (0x54b84, PR-145) -
  which is consistent with PR-141, where DRABINKA's own +0x78
  contact answer entry 0x3f1c0 raises exactly 10 and 12.

- FINDING 2, THE QUEUE-PUSH PRIMITIVE'S ARGUMENT ROLES ARE READ AT
  EXACT BYTES, AND THE LINEAR SWEEP MISALIGNS ITS ENTRY. 0x52b10
  IS a real entry: a byte-exact disassembly at 0x52b10 gives
  `push esi; mov esi,edx` (0x52b10/0x52b11) then the walk of
  [obj+0x10]'s queue, `mov eax,0x10; call 0x5c320` (0x52b22/27 -
  the record allocation), and the stores at 0x52b30..0x52b3c:
  [node+0]=0 (the queue link), [node+4]=esi (the incoming EDX =
  the record TYPE), [node+8]=ebx (the tag), [node+0xc]=ecx (the
  payload = the bit index). The vis/text.asm linear sweep decodes
  0x52b0f one byte early (`mov [esi-0x77],edx` swallowing 0x52b10)
  so its listing shows `salc` at 0x52b12 and no prologue - the
  FOURTH mis-anchor of this series (PR-143's 0x52b50, PR-144's
  0x4bd32, PR-145's 0x52b50 lesson, and now this one) and the
  first caused by the listing itself. The same three-register
  convention (edx = type, ebx = tag, ecx = bit index) is what the
  stack form of Finding 1 writes at +0x4/+0x8/+0xc, and what
  0x53770 tests at +0x8: three independent sites agree.

- FINDING 3, THE BROADCAST ARGUMENT FORM - PR-143 CORRECTED.
  0x4bc40's entry (0x4bc42..0x4bc57, entered by name from 22
  sites): eax = the level/global object (kept at [esp+0x4]),
  EDX = a per-object predicate filter (0x4bcb9: when non-zero,
  `call [[obj]+8 +0xc]` per object and keep only eax == edx),
  EBX = the RECORD TYPE (0x4bcd3 `mov edx,edi` -> 0x52b10's edx),
  ECX = the tag (0x4bcd1 `mov ebx,ebp` -> 0x52b10's ebx), and the
  stack argument = the payload (0x4bcd0 `[esp+0x28]` -> 0x52b10's
  ecx). It walks every object list of the level the same way the
  think pass does (0x4bc92..0x4bcb7) and pushes ONE record into
  each passing object's queue. So PR-143's sentence "22 sites,
  only bits 7/16/18/19/25/26" read the RECORD-TYPE argument as if
  it were a bit index - corrected. The true type census (all 22
  sites, last-writer windows): type 7 x2 (0x1ec46, 0x1ec5f),
  0x10 x4 (0x247e7, 0x2c5e6, 0x2c624, 0x2c664), 0x12 x5 (0x1f468,
  0x3457c, 0x34a71, 0x34a9a, 0x3a20d), 0x13 x3 (0x246dd, 0x324f0,
  0x34a48), 0x19 x7 (0x2f1ef, 0x2f37b, 0x2f398, 0x3b4e6, 0x3b60c,
  0x3c1a8, 0x3c1c5), 0x1a x1 (0x2f512). Of those, only three
  carry the signal tag (Finding 1). Note 0x247e7: a type-0x10
  record pushed WITHOUT the tag (its filter comes from the global
  ds:0xcec0c) - a second, non-signal record kind sharing the type
  number, counted as open item 3. PR-143's conclusions survive
  (no broadcast posts key bits, none posts 10/12) but for the
  stated reason: those numbers were types, and the payload census
  is 33/28/27.

- FINDING 4, THE CONTACT LOOP CLOSES. (a) THE ENTRY WAS A MIS-
  ANCHOR AGAIN: the pair-walk's entry is 0x4bd30, not 0x4bd32
  (0x4bd32 is one instruction in, after `push ebp`). `call
  0x4bd30` exists once, at 0x527cb, inside 0x52790 - PR-130's
  motion-pipeline merger - which also calls the other two list
  paths at 0x527f5 (0x4b890, the animacje list) and 0x5281f
  (0x4b870, the zwierzaki list). 0x4bdf6/0x4bddb are interior/tail
  fragments of the same function (PR-144's "lion-specific half"
  0x4bdf6 is the no-candidates path of 0x4bd30), and 0x4b500/
  0x4b602 are helpers reached only from inside that group (its
  three call sites 0x4b6c0/0x4b87d/0x4b89d are all inside it). So
  PR-144's open item 1 and PR-145's "still genuinely unreferenced"
  list are CLOSED as a false gap: one function group, entered from
  the per-object motion pipeline only. PR-130's own record already
  named 0x4bd30/0x4b890/0x4b870 and their gates; what this PR
  adds is the instruction-level confirmation and the output shape.
  (b) THE GATES, verbatim at 0x527b3/0x527db/0x52805 with the
  same arguments PR-130 recorded: `test BYTE PTR [obj+0x13],0x2`
  -> 0x4bd30 (the Lew list), `test BYTE PTR [obj+0x12],0x40` ->
  0x4b890, `test BYTE PTR [obj+0x12],0x80` -> 0x4b870, each
  called with eax = ds:0xcef40 (the world), ebx = [obj+0x0] and
  ecx = [obj+0x12] & 0x8000. And the merged result is a 13-BYTE
  ANSWER SET, not an object list: each list's result is ORed into
  a local 12-byte set + flag byte (0x527d0/0x527fa/0x5282a ->
  0x49580) and 0x5282f..0x5285x copies 12 bytes + the flag byte
  to the caller's out record. That refines PR-130's "candidate
  list" wording: the merger returns the union of the neighbours'
  contact ANSWERS (the same 13-byte set shape PR-144 described).
  (c) THE CONTACT-LIST SETTER IS THE CONTACT ENTRY ITSELF. Only
  three sites write [obj+0xd2] (0x5415b/0x54e88 = zero, 0x551fc =
  0x551f0's pop). The setter goes through a list-head ADDRESS: at
  0x3d60a a class's +0x78 contact ENTRY takes `lea edx,[edi+0xd2]`
  and calls the append helper (0x53f00 -> 0x53ee0: if the head is
  empty store into it, else 0x53fe0 walks the node links - the
  link is at node+0 - to the tail). The entry is 0x3d440: a
  contact entry with exactly PR-144's +0x78 signature (eax = self
  -> esi, edx = the other -> [esp+0x40], ebx = the result buffer
  -> edi, and it memsets its own 12-byte + flag-byte answer set),
  and class tables 0x96a88 and 0x99e64 hold it at +0x78 (both
  tables independently anchored: their +0x8c is the generic key
  provider 0x54910, and 0x3d440 is at 0x96b00 = 0x96a88+0x78).
  Inside the same entry, 0x3d5f6 writes [obj+0x106] (PR-108's
  field), 0x3d5b6 clears bit 7 of [obj+0x64], 0x3d5fc allocates a
  0x1d-byte node and 0x3d618 appends it to [obj+0xd2]. The entry
  is called with eax = the object being asked, edx = the caller's
  answer buffer, ebx = THE ASKER (0x3d440 keeps the asker in
  edi), which is why the append lands on the asker's list.
  (d) THE NODE CARRIES THE ANSWER SET, AND THAT IS THE CONSUMER
  EDGE. The allocation size 0x1d = 0x10 + 13, and the node
  builder's stores at 0x53f05..0x53f2a (the sweep mis-aligns
  around 0x53eff, so the builder's ENTRY is not pinned - open
  item 1) read: [n+0]=0 (the list link), [n+4]=1 (the kind word,
  Finding 6), [n+8]=<a pointer argument>, [n+0xc]=<a count>, then
  `lea esi,[eax+0x10]` + `mov ebx,0xc` + `mov BYTE PTR [esi+0xc],
  0` + `call 0x749a0` = a 13-byte ZEROED SET at [n+0x10]. So a
  contact node = a 16-byte header + a 13-byte signal set. And the
  merge PR-145 recorded at 0x54b65..0x54b84 is: `mov edx,
  [ebx+0xd2]` (the head node), `add edx,0x10` (&node+0x10 = THE
  STORED ANSWER SET), `lea eax,[ebx+0x60]`, `call 0x49580` - the
  stored answer set is ORed into the object's live set. PR-145's
  formula "[[obj+0xd2]+0x10]+0x10 = [partner+0x60]" is corrected:
  it is the node's payload, not the partner's live set. THE
  DELIVERY, end to end: object A's motion pipeline (0x52750 ->
  0x52790 -> 0x4bd30) gives B's +0x78 entry a turn; B answers
  with a 13-byte set into A's buffer AND appends a node holding
  that answer set to A's contact list at [A+0xd2]; A's contact
  method (the +0xcc entry 0x549f0) reads the head node's kind and
  merges its stored set into [A+0x60] under the guard; A's own
  key provider (the lion's 0x504e0 at 0x5050f, gated on
  [obj+0xa5] bit 1 and [vt+0xf8]()) pops the head through
  0x551f0; the key feed then sees the bits. That is the route by
  which DRABINKA's 0x3f1c0 answer (bits 10/12, PR-141) reaches
  the lion's live set - no signal record needed. PR-145's gap
  CLOSED, and the answer-set consumer question with it.
