## PR-161 — THE ROW-LINE PARSER IS FOUND AND THE ROW MODEL
## CLOSES END TO END: ROW LINES ARE ID+THRESHOLD PAIRS RESOLV
## ING THE ID THROUGH THE NAME POOL INTO 0x18-BYTE WRAPPER
## ENTRIES; THE WALK IS SINGLE-SHOT PER TICK (CALLED VIA THE
## OBJECT-CLASS +0x44 AT 0x53b18) - THE ROW CURSOR HAS NO
## INCREMENTER ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE AND ROWS ADVANCE ONLY BY
## AUTHORED TRANSITION ROW-OUTPUTS; AN UNRESOLVED ROW ID MEANS
## AN EMPTY KEY THAT ALWAYS PASSES THE KEY TEST (THE WAIT
## LAW); THE 21-BYTE LAYOUT TENSION DISSOLVES (TWO DISTINCT
## ARRAYS) AND THE CLASS-TABLE TWO-VIEW TRICK EXPLAINS THE
## PR-159/160 SLOT CONTRADICTIONS (READING; no code, no new
## test - the PR-138..160 precedent; PR-160 items (1)/(2) and
## the PR-159 item-(3) sub-question CLOSE)

- WHY. PR-160's Next named one first read: who turns authored
  row lines into rows[] entries. It was the last unnamed piece
  of the row model, and it also decided three counted questions
  (the walk-arm attribution, the transition-node vs row-entry
  layout tension, and whether a WAIT-style entry re-matches
  every pass).

- FINDING 1, THE PARSE LOOP AND THE ROW BUILDER. The state-
  block parse driver is 0x52b80: for the placement's current
  param entry it calls entry-class verb +0x14 at 0x52b8f, and
  if [entry+0x28] is nonzero runs verb +0x00 with edx=2 (a
  completion pass). The +0x14 verb body is 0x51eb0: it zeroes
  the HIGH WORD of the time_scale dword ([rec+0xc] half - the
  ctor's 1000 survives as the LOW word - consistent with the
  WORD-pair reading from PR-160; the upper half's role stays
  open), clears [rec+0x8]/+0xa (the time= pair slot, so a
  re-parse resets it), then loops its line stream with token
  format 0x9226f ' %[^[=,( ] %*[,=]' (tokens stop at '[', '=',
  ',', '(' or space - ONE loop therefore sees directive lines,
  F/T/G lines, transition lines and row lines). Dispatch: the
  first token is classified by 0x57db0 = sscanf("%ld") - a
  NUMERIC first token takes the row-line path; otherwise the
  line goes to record-class verb +0x00 (0x52590 - the F/T/G
  header handler which itself delegates to the 0x51910 directive
  parser at its 0x5264b tail). THE ROW-LINE PATH: alloc 0x18
  + ctor 0x515e0(entry, [rec+0xe], ds:0xceff4) - i.e. the
  row's FIRST FIELD IS A SEQUENCE ID, resolved by 0x57fd0 =
  strtol(0x76fa3 - the isdigit class-table routine) through the
  pool singleton's LAST RESULT slot ds:0xceff4 - and the entry
  (payload ptr, 0, 0, threshold, 0, class 0xa2638) is APPENDED
  to the rows vector at [rec+0x2e] (vector count at +0x36,
  growth via 0x21e80). The ctor's 0x3e8 argument seen in PR-
  160 is thus the record's CURRENT time_scale - a default for
  the entry - not a constant. CONCLUSION: PR-160's reading of
  's NAME,N' (pool lookup + wrapper + append) was the NAMED
  variant of exactly this builder; plain row lines are the
  ID-keyed variant. ZARIA.01 grounding: its state blocks au-
  thor rows like `1,0,WAIT K_GEN1` / `2,500` - field 1 is the
  sequence ID, field 2 the threshold (PR-101's data law RE-
  VERIFIED STRUCTURALLY); no pool registration by those names
  exists in the extracted texts, so for ZARIA.01 the lookup
  yields NULL payloads (see F2's empty-key law) - the pool
  contents for the full game remain the data-blocked part.

- FINDING 2, THE WALK IS SINGLE-SHOT PER TICK; THE CURSOR HAS
  NO INCREMENTER - THE ROW-ADVANCEMENT LAW IS THE TRANSITION
  LAW. The walk verb 0x521f0 is called from the OBJECT tick at
  0x53b18 via object-verb +0x44 (0x53ae0 region), once per
  frame, and its body has NO LOOP: it reads entry = rows[cursor]
  exactly once, evaluates, and returns. An IMAGE-WIDE census
  finds NO increment form for [rec+0x4] (no `inc DWORD PTR
  [reg+off+0x4]` and no `add ...,0x1` anywhere; the only reg-
  ister-form stores of a +0x4 field are the PR-159 writer-law
  sites plus generic vector code at 0x1cxxx/0x300e6) [SUPER-
  SEDED BY PR-162 F1: the step tail was OUTSIDE every window
  the census read - the helper 0x520c0 continues at 0x5211e
  and steps [rec+4] at 0x521d4-0x521d7, wrapping at 0x521c1-
  0x521c5; the lea+store idiom is why the inc/add greps mis-
  sed]. THERE-
  FORE the law is exact: a state stays on its current row un-
  til a TRANSITION entry fires and its authored row-output
  writes the cursor (0x53616) - rows advance ONLY by authored
  transition row-outputs [CORRECTED BY PR-162 F2: ordinary
  progression is the STEPWISE advance in the helper, reached
  exactly on a THRESHOLD PASS (the paid path calls +0x18 at
  0x52338) - advance-on-threshold-pass, the port's model];
  the row line's own threshold never
  advances anything, it only gates the frame-advance accumu-
  lator [ALSO CORRECTED: the threshold pass IS what triggers
  the step - via the helper].
  The empty-key case CLOSES PR-159 item-(3): the walk's
  key test is an INTERSECTION test (0x495b0 on the merged
  caller-key OR entry-key; merged with 0x49580 = a 13-byte
  dword-wise OR over [0..0xc]) - NO intersection (an empty key
  ALWAYS qualifies) proceeds to the gate arm; an intersection
  keeps the row inert. The row-entry wrapper verb +0xc (0x45870)
  returns the PAYLOAD's key when a payload exists, else a ZERO-
  FILLED 13-byte key: an unresolvable row ID (or a bare
  threshold line) is exactly the WAIT-style always-passing en-
  try, so its [entry+0x10] threshold gates against the mode-
  dispatcher-fed accumulator every tick ([entry+0x10] < [owner
  +0xa1] pays the debt and runs the helper, else holds - PR-
  100/101 verbatim), and every same-state transition MATCH
  (PR-159 F2) still counts toward the AC_TIME roll. The walk's
  arms: the key-merge path (0x52251-0x522f0) copies the CALL-
  ER's key, the OWNER's live set (12B+1B at [owner+0x6c] - the
  PR-145 live-set shape) and a 13-byte block at [rec+0xc] into
  the merge; the gate path runs [[owner]+8]+0xa0] (0x543a0) as
  a pure side-effect call, then the threshold compare, then
  [[rec-class]+0x18] = the 0x520c0 helper, then [[owner]+8]
  +0xa4] and [owner+0x95]=1. PR-159's "iterates entries by
  POINTER chain" framing is CORRECTED here: there is no entry
  chain - the no-INTERSECTION path at 0x522fc re-reads the
  SAME entry's class field [entry+0x4] and re-dispatches its
  +0xc verb with the merged key as the output buffer; the
  walk then ends. With the 0xa2638 table, [entry+0x4] is AL-
  WAYS the class field, which resolves PR-160 item 2's attri-
  bution worry: the arms map exactly as read.

- FINDING 3, THE LAYOUT TENSION DISSOLVES + THE TWO-VIEW
  CLASS-TABLE TRICK. Rows are 4-byte POINTER slots in the vec-
  tor at [rec+0x2e]; transition nodes are 0x15-byte packed
  nodes in the list at [rec+0x1a] - TWO DISTINCT ARRAYS, so
  PR-159 item 1-part / PR-160 item 2's "+0x10 threshold vs
  +0xd/+0x11 out-slots" contradiction never existed: the walk
  reads the WRAPPER's field +0x10 (the authored threshold, one
  of its five dword fields: +0x0 payload, +0x4 class, +0x8/+0xc
  reserved, +0x10 threshold, +0x14), and the applier reads the
  transition node's out-words. Related mechanism now named:
  the param-entry objects and the records SHARE a field layout
  (the 0x48-byte header: same F/T/G channels at +0x48..+0x5c,
  same time slots) and their class tables are the same method
  set at TWO VIEWS: 0xa25d4 (record view: +0x00=F/T/G parser,
  +0x0c=walk, +0x18=helper, +0x1c=ENTER, +0x38=directive par-
  ser) and 0xa260c (entry/param view at -0x28: +0x14=row-line
  builder 0x51eb0, +0x28=record factory 0x518f0, +0x00=parser)
  - the factory at 0x518f0 stores class 0xa260c in created
  records (0x51851), and every earlier "slot +0x1c = ENTER vs
  +0x18 = walk" discrepancy in PR-159/160 notes came from
  mixing the views. The param-entry registration 0x53850 parks
  the name in the pool (0x57990) and stores the result at
  [param+0] and [param+0x89] - PR-159 F3's name-binding now
  has its pool side too.

- FINDING 4, TICK-ADJACENT OBSERVATIONS (recorded, mecha-
  nisms open): the tick 0x53ae0 region runs the walk then
  tests RESULT bits (ah bit 2 / eax bit 16); the walk's return
  at 0x5235c is [esp+0x20] whose last definite write is the

  fires AT PLACEMENT for the initial state (the port's model-
  ling question for a future CODE pass: initial-state AC_TIME
  rolls at spawn).

- OPEN ITEMS COUNTED (4 new + 1 narrowed). (1) The walk re-

## PR-162 — THE ROW CURSOR DOES STEP: PR-161'S NEGATIVE
## CENSUS WAS THE WRONG IDIOM - THE INCREMENTER SITS IN THE
## HELPER VERB'S OWN TAIL (0x520c0 CONTINUES AT 0x5211e; THE
## STEP AT 0x521d4/0x521d7, WRAP+FLAG AT 0x521c1-0x521c5,
## REVERSE VIA 0x521a1-0x521b1), SO PR-107'S CONTEMPORANEOUS
## NOTE WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG AND THE TRUE LAW IS ADVANCE-ON-
## THRESHOLD-PASS (THE PORT'S MODEL, CORROBORATED); THE COM-
## PLETE 21-NAME control= FLAG-WORD MAP IS DECODED VERBATIM
## (+0x12..+0x15) - SEQ_REV_X/Y = 0x10/0x20 EXACTLY AS PR-95
## OBSERVED, AND PR-160's "+0x15 BIT 0x8 = FACE-FLIP" RE-
## SOLVES TO THE ANTI_POCISK FLAG BIT
(READING + LEDGER CORRECTION; no code, no new test - the
PR-138..161 precedent; PR-161 F2's advance sentence and parts
of PR-159/160's cursor phrasing are SUPERSEDED below)

- WHY. The AC_TIME CODE pass was next and fully specced, but
  grounding it in the port's code (ll_level.c's obj_transi-
  tion/obj_row_tick) re-opened an old comment that cited "the
  row stepper 0x520c0 advances [rec+4] (0x521d7) and wraps it
  at the last row (0x521c5)" - exactly what PR-161 had just
  declared impossible. One of the two had to be wrong, so the
  bytes were re-read before writing any code.

- FINDING 1, THE HELPER VERB IS LONGER THAN PR-160/161 READ
  IT: 0x520c0 CONTINUES THROUGH 0x5211e (no prologue - the
  bytes run straight on: 0x52118 `mov [eax+0xa1],edx`, 0x5211e
  `xor eax,eax`, 0x52120 `mov [esp+0xc],eax`...). After the
  payload/creation steps (PR-161 F2) the helper runs THE ROW
  STEP ITSELF:
  (a) SKIP TEST: [esp+0xc]=0, then entry verb +0x10 is called
  with edx=6 (0x52138-0x5213d; the 0xa2638 wrapper forwards
  via 0x458e0 to the payload's +0x10 getter family); if the
  out-parameter comes back 6 (0x52140-0x52145) the helper re-
  turns WITHOUT stepping (the payload mode verb 0x47770 shows
  mode bit 0x4 clears a content record at 0xa0f14 - the candi-
  date reading is sequence exhaustion; open item 3).
  (b) FORWARD STEP: cursor+1 stored (0x521d4 `lea edi,[ecx+1]`
  + 0x521d7); at the LAST row (cursor == [rows-vec+0x8]-1,
  i.e. count-1, 0x521b6-0x521bf) it WRAPS to 0 and ORs value
  4 into DWORD [[rec+0]+0] - [rec+0] is the owner, so that is
  object vtable slot +0x4 (0x23850) - a row-end signal, half-
  read (item 3).
  (c) REVERSE: when cursor==0 it wraps to the LAST index and
  ORs 8 into the same word (0x5219a-0x521a9); otherwise cur-
  sor-1 (0x521ae-0x521b1). Which direction is gated by the
  flag tests at 0x52158/0x52171 - [rec+0x12] bit 0x10 paired
  with [[owner]+8]+0x70](rec) == -1 and bit 0x20 with +0x71
  == -1, XORed with a [owner+0x99]==-1 term (0x52180-0x52193).
  (d) THE COMPLETE control= FLAG MAP (the directive parser's
  chain 0x51b0d-0x51d97, every arm chain-traced): each name
  is compared by 0x76a69, `je <next arm>` skips ITS OWN store
  on mismatch and `jmp 0x51dc3` ends on match - so every store
  belongs to the arm whose name precedes it UNCONDITIONALLY.
  The flag field is a 4-byte window [rec+0x12..+0x15]. Verba-
  tim map: BY_X -> NO FLAG (the first compare at 0x51b49 is
  skipped by its own je - accepted-and-ignored); BY_Y -> BYTE
  +0x12 |0x1; BY_TIME -> |0x2; BY_TX -> |0x3 (BY_Y|BY_TIME: a
  COMPOSITE); BY_TY -> |0x4; FRAME_REV -> |0x8; SEQ_REV_X ->
  |0x10; SEQ_REV_Y -> |0x20; CHECK_ZW -> |0x80; CHECK_ANI ->
  |0x40; CHECK_LN -> BYTE +0x13 |0x1; CHECK_ALL -> WORD +0x12
  |0x1c0 (= +0x12 bits 6,7 + +0x13 bit 6 = CHECK_ANI|CHECK_
  ZW|CHECK_BASE_LN - CHECK_LN (0x100) is NOT in it; "ALL"
  names a specific authored set, not every check bit); CHECK_
  LEW -> +0x13 |0x2; CHECK_BASE_LN ->
  +0x13 |0x40; SOLID -> +0x13 |0x4; CH_DIR -> +0x13 |0x8;
  INV_V -> +0x13 |0x10; DANGER -> +0x13 |0x20; CHECK_ALL_
  PLANE -> +0x13 |0x80; ANTI_SOLID -> BYTE +0x14 |0x1; SOLID2
  -> DWORD +0x12 |0x20400 (= CHECK_ALL_PLANE | SOLID | (+0x14
  bit 0x4 = 0x40000)); SEMI_SOLID -> DWORD |0x40400 (= SOLID
  | (+0x14 bit 0x4)); the +0x14 bit 0x4 has no authored name
  of its own - reached only through the two composites (flag-
  ged); ANTI_POCISK -> BYTE +0x14 |0x8.
  CONFIRMATIONS: SEQ_REV_X/SEQ_REV_Y = 0x10/0x20 EXACTLY as
  PR-95 observed behaviorally, and the reverse gates at 0x52158
  (bit 0x10 + X-position sentinel [[owner]+8]+0x70] == -1) /
  0x52171 (bit 0x20 + +0x71 == -1) pair X-with-X and Y-with-
  Y; PR-160 F5's "bit 0x10 tested at 0x52158" is SEQ_REV_X ✓.
  RE-ATTRIBUTION: PR-160 F5's "+0x15 bit 0x8 = face-flip-on-
  transition (PR-108 corroborated)" - per this map [rec+0x15]
  bit 0x8 is set ONLY by ANTI_POCISK (the anti-projectile
  flag); a face-flip consumer of that bit has NOT been found;
  PR-108's OBSERVED flip behavior stands, its bit attribution
  gets a bracket and a re-derivation lead (item 4). NOTE: the
  port's LL_CTRL_* enum numbering is its own and is NOT this
  word; mapping the port enum to these engine bits (where the
  port even has names the engine lacks, and vice versa) is
  item (1).

- FINDING 2, THE CORRECTED ROW-ADVANCEMENT LAW (supersedes
  the PR-161 F2 sentence and refines PR-159 F1/PR-160 F4):
  the transition applier writes the cursor only from authored
  row-outputs (PR-159's law, UNCHANGED - its writer census
  simply did not class the helper tail as a writer); ORDINARY
  row progression is the STEPWISE advance inside the helper,
  which runs ONLY on a threshold PASS: the walk's gate arm
  pays the debt (acc -= threshold) and calls record verb
  +0x18 = the helper (0x52338), and the helper steps the cur-
  sor at its tail - so a row advances exactly when its thresh-
  old is met, which IS the port's model (obj_row_tick advanc-
  ing o->fi on threshold passes; PR-100/101's measured law
  CORROBORATED structurally end to end. REFINEMENT of PR-161
  F2's arm story: BOTH arms reach the gate - the intersect arm
  at 0x5224b only adds KEY MERGING (the copies + the +0xc re-
  call at 0x522fc feed the caller's merged key, which the tick
  at 0x53b1b consumes); control then runs 0x52251-0x522f0
  STRAIGHT INTO the gate arm - conditions do NOT hold a row
  inert at this level (PR-161's "an intersection keeps the row
  inert" was wrong). Only the PAID path steps. The mode-6
  query at the helper's head can veto even a paid step (ex-
  hausted-sequence semantics, open). Wrap: at the last row the
  cursor
  cycles to 0 with the [owner-vtable+0x4] |= 4 signal; at 0
  going backwards it wraps to the last index with |= 8.
  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE AC_TIME CODE PASS: unchanged (the match
  counter and the ENTER roll spec stand); CONSEQUENCE FOR THE
  LEDGER: PR-161's negative-census sentence, its HANDOFF/bul-
  let echoes and the PR-159 "pure SET-POSITION" refinement note
  are bracketed below; PR-107's ll_level.c comment (0x520d7 ->
  really 0x521d4) needs a one-line address fix in the NEXT
  CODE PR (not touched here).

  0x495b0's test decides only the MERGE bookkeeping, NOT a
  row gate: the no-intersection branch at 0x5224b `je 0x522fc`
  skips ONLY the copy block (which ORs the caller key, the
  owner live set [owner+0x6c] and the [rec+0xc] block into the
  merged key), and BOTH paths then run the identical gate se-
  quence. So every row's threshold gates payment and stepping
  in practice - PR-161's practical WAIT-law conclusion stands,

## PR-165 — THE FLAG-CONSUMER PASS: THE BYTE-TEST CENSUS IS
## EXHAUSTIVE BUT ITS SCOPE WAS WRONG - THE BY_* BITS' ONLY
## CONSUMER IS THE FEED DISPATCHER ITSELF (0x543a0, owner-slot
## +0xa0: mode = [rec+0x12]&7, jump table 0x54380, five named
## feed arms - the port's distance-feed law RE-GROUNDED
## VERBATIM and BY_Y/BY_TY feeds NEW); THE KEY BUILDER IS
## RECORD SLOT +0x08 (0x52750 -> verbs +0x2c/+0x30 + owner
## getter +0xc8 -> flag merge +0x34 = 0x52790, closing PR-162
## item 4's body); THE DERIVED ENTER SLOTS ARE WRAPPERS THAT
## KEEP THE BASE BODY (0x4fef0/0x50040 tail-call 0x52360) AND
## THE POOLS HAVE A NAMED STARTUP REGISTRY (0x4fe02)
(READING + LEDGER CORRECTION; no code, no new test - the
PR-138..164 precedent; PR-162 item (1) is CLOSED as answered,
its port-name DECISION stays open as a new item; PR-162 item
(4)'s 0x52750 body is CLOSED)

- WHY. The Next entry specced exactly this pass: for each
  control= flag bit, find its CONSUMERS - the flag map was
  read verbatim from the parser in PR-162 F1d, but only two
  consumers were known (the SEQ_REV pair at 0x52158/0x52171),
  and the port's LL_CTRL_* enum, the PR-108 flip-bit
  question, and the FRAME_REV name all hung on WHO READS
  THESE BITS. Method: exhaustive scan of text.asm for every
  read of the flag window [rec+0x12..+0x15], byte, word and
  dword forms, then read each consumer body.

- FINDING 1, THE EXHAUSTIVE BYTE-TEST CENSUS (AND ITS
  BLIND SPOT). Every byte-granular TEST of the window in the
  whole image: SEQ_REV_X/Y (+0x12 bits 0x10/0x20) at
  0x52158/0x52171 (the step helper's reverse arm) AND at
  0x52385/0x523a0 (inside ENTER 0x52360 - PR-95's and
  PR-162's row-order reading corroborated a third time);
  CHECK_LEW (+0x13 bit 2, 0x527b3), CHECK_ANI (+0x12 bit
  0x40, 0x527db), CHECK_ZW (+0x12 bit 0x80, 0x52805) inside
  the key builder (F3). The window's only writers: the
  parser chain 0x51c59-0x51d97 (the or-BYTE stores behind the
  PR-162 F1d map) and record-to-record struct copies at
  0x5181a-0x5181d/0x518b3-0x518bd. FRAME_REV (+0x12 bit
  0x8): ZERO consumers in ANY form (the mode mask and eax,7
  excludes it from F2's mode selection) - its port-side
  name stays unjustified. But the byte-test census was the
  wrong IDIOM for the rest: BY_Y/BY_TIME/BY_TY/DANGER/...
  are read in WORD/DWORD forms, and F2 finds the big one.

- FINDING 2, THE FEED DISPATCHER IS THE BY_* CONSUMER - THE
  MODE *IS* THE FLAG BITS. The record step 0x521f0 calls
  `call DWORD [[obj]+8+0xa0]` at 0x52317 (eax = the owner,
  the standard thiscall shape); slot +0xa0 holds 0x543a0
  (raw-dword census: 155 table slots - the owner class
  tables). Body: 0x543a6-0x543ac re-derives the CURRENT
  RECORD with the standard [[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4] idiom
  (PR-164's object-state shape again), then 0x543af loads
  DWORD [rec+0x12], and eax,7, cmp eax,4, ja default,
  jmp cs:[eax*4+0x54380] - a FIVE-ENTRY jump table indexed
  by the LOW THREE FLAG BITS: mode 0 = NO FLAG = BY_X (the
  PR-162 "BY_X -> NO FLAG" reading MECHANISM-CONFIRMED):
  0x543c6 = abs([obj+0xca]) added to [obj+0xa1] - the
  horizontal speed field, PR-98's |v_x| distance feed law
  VERBATIM at the field level; mode 1 = BY_Y (+0x12 bit 1):
  0x543dc = abs([obj+0xce]) -> [obj+0xa1] - the vertical
  twin, NEW (the port has no BY_Y feed); mode 2 = BY_TIME
  (bit 2): 0x543fb reads [[obj+0xa1]+0xc] (accumulator
  DEREFERENCED - see item 1), cmp with the value at +0xc,
  jle into a full sub-record feed; mode 3 = BY_TX composite
  (bits 1+2, exactly PR-162's composite reading): 0x543f2
  guards `cmp [obj+0xba],0; je` default; [THE ARM TEXT WAS A
  ONE-BYTE LISTING MISREAD - CORRECTED BY PR-168 F1: raw
  bytes at 0x543fb = a PLAIN feed of the pool scalar [contai-
  ner+0x388] into [obj+0xa1] (no deref, no compare - the
  `mov eax,[eax+0x388]` mis-split); modes 2/3/4 are BYTE-
  IDENTICAL feeds, 3/4 pre-guarded by the [obj+0xba]/[obj+
  0xbe] zero-tests, and those "guards" are the authored
  MOTION PARAMETERS (PR-98's fields), not control flags -
  see PR-168 F2]; mode 4 = BY_TY (bit 4): 0x5441b guards
  `cmp [obj+0xbe],0; je` default,
  else adds the pool global [ds:0xcef40+0x388] to
  [obj+0xa1] (0x54429-0x5443d) - a CONSTANT per-step rate
  read at runtime (static image value 0; the pool sets it) -
  [PINNED BY PR-168 F1: the rate is a LITERAL 100 - the sole
  writer of [x+0x388] is 0x4c8b7 `mov DWORD [x+0x388],0x64`
  at container init] -
  the engine's steady BY_TY feed, matching PR-105's note
  that BY_TY flows only when the step runs; default (mode
  >=5, i.e. FRAME_REV bit 3 set or any higher bit): no feed
  at all, straight to the shared epilogue. THE CORRECTION:
  the earlier "no consumers" negatives for BY_* were census
  artifacts of byte-test-only scanning. The port's
  DANGER/CH_DIR-based behaviours remain PORT-DERIVED
  semantics: those bits have NO consumer in this dispatcher
  or in any byte test (their only reads are struct copies).

- FINDING 3, THE KEY BUILDER: RECORD SLOT +0x08 = 0x52750
  (PR-162 ITEM 4'S BODY CLOSED). Table word-scan of the
  record tables: 0xa25d4 +0x08 = 0x52750, +0x34 = 0x52790
  (view 0xa260c: +0x08 = 0x559c0, +0x34 = 0x45800 -
  unread, item 6; derived tables 0x97c9c/0x9a894 share the
  same +0x08/+0x34 pair). 0x52750 body: call record verb
  +0x2c (= 0x52680) with a scratch key buffer, call record
  verb +0x30 (= 0x2b4d0), call the owner's second-table
  getter +0xc8, then tail the record verb +0x34 = 0x52790,
  and return the scratch buffer's value - the composition
  PR-162 item 4 named sight-unseen is exactly that.
  0x52790 = THE FLAG-DRIVEN KEY MERGE: tests CHECK_LEW
  (+0x13 bit 2) -> pool query 0x4bd30(ds:0xcef40, owner,
  flag, 0x8000 = the CHECK_ALL_PLANE sub-mode flag, key
  buffer); CHECK_ANI -> 0x4b890 (pool ds:0xa94ec); CHECK_ZW
  -> 0x4b870 (pool ds:0xcef44); each result is ORed into
  the key via 0x49580, a COUNT byte is written at key+0xc,
  and the 13-byte result is copied to the caller (0x52840-
  0x52850 = the same 13-byte key-set shape the pump merges
  at [obj+0x60..0x6c]) [ARGUMENT ROLES + SPLIT CORRECTED BY
  PR-166 F1: the calls pass eax = ds:0xcef40 (the CURRENT
  CONTAINER - the pools are container-attached), ebx = [rec+
  0] = the owner back-pointer, edx = the key buffer, ecx =
  the 0x8000 mask (LEW direct) or the pool INDEX via the
  wrappers; 0x4bd30/CHECK_LEW is NOT a pool query - it walks
  the object's own list at [obj+0x64] and INTERSECTS
  (0x495b0) and COPIES the match out, no OR; only ANI/ZW
  OR-merge]. So CHECK_* rows do not gate inside
  the engine: they ADD POOL-DERIVED KEY BITS - the engine's
  side of the port's keyed-row model. The three query heads
  0x4b870/0x4b890 are one-liners tailing a common 0x4b500
  pool lookup (body open, item 3); 0x4b890's listing start
  is misaligned again (0x4b88f = 51 = push ecx; 0x4bd30's
  prologue proved against its own epilogue at
  0x4bd1d-0x4bd20) - the one-byte trap class, fifth member.

- FINDING 4, THE DERIVED ENTER OVERRIDES ARE WRAPPERS, NOT

## PR-166 — THE POOL CONTENTS ARE READ AND THEY ARE THE
## LEVEL'S OWN PLACED OBJECTS: THE QUERIED POOLS ATTACH TO THE
## CONTAINERS AT LOAD BY THEIR PR-60 SOURCE NAMES (zwierzaki/
## animacje/ani_plat -> ds:0xcef44/0xa94ec/0xa94e8); THE
## QUERY BODIES CLOSE PR-165 ITEM 3 (0x4b500 = class-filtered
## key MERGE over the container's pool chains, 0x4bd30 = the
## object's OWN list with an INTERSECT-and-copy); THE CLASS ID
## SITS AT [obj+0x24]; THE STARTUP REGISTRY IS FULLY
## TRANSCRIBED - 14 TYPE-0x14 POOLS - AND ITS HANDLES ARE
## READ BY NO CODE ANYWHERE (NEGATIVE); THE 14 NAMES RESIST A
## 256-KEY XOR SCAN (STILL OPEN)
(READING + LEDGER CORRECTION; no code, no new test - the
PR-138..165 precedent; PR-165 open item (3) is CLOSED below,
its F3 LEW/ANI/ZW argument list and its F5 class-id sample
are CORRECTED with brackets)

- WHY. PR-165 closed the flag-consumer pass but left the
  engine's biggest un-read subsystem: its pool queries. The
  Next entry specced the read: the query bodies 0x4b500 /
  0x4bd30 and wrapper contracts, the pool-name decode, the
  0x4fe02 registry walk, and how authored rows land in pools
  - the K_GEN1 data-blocker edge.

- FINDING 1, THE QUERY BODIES (PR-165 ITEM 3 CLOSED). The
  key-builder arms at 0x527b3/0x527e1/0x5280b load: eax =
  ds:0xcef40 (the CURRENT CONTAINER - F2), ecx = DWORD
  [rec+0x12..15] AND 0x8000 (the CHECK_ALL_PLANE bit), ebx =
  [rec+0] = the OWNER back-pointer, edx = the 13-byte output
  key buffer. The wrappers 0x4b870 and 0x4b88f (entry 0x4b88f
  - the listing's 0x4b890 is misaligned again, sixth member
  of the class) save edx, PUSH the 0x8000 mask as the stack
  arg that 0x4b500 reads at [esp+0x54], and set ecx to the
  pool INDEX globals ds:0xcef44 (CHECK_ZW) / ds:0xa94ec
  (CHECK_ANI) before tailing 0x4b500; 0x4bd30 (CHECK_LEW)
  is called directly with the mask still in ecx.
  0x4b500 body: poolObj = base + index*4; COUNT at
  [poolObj+0x44]; chain heads at [poolObj+0x58] + 4*idx
  deref, walk via [entry+0x34]; per entry: verb +0x60
  predicate, then CLASS FILTER - accept iff [entry+0x24] ==
  [ebx+0x24] (the OWNER's class id: the class-ID field is
  at [obj+0x24] - CONFIRMED location, supports PR-139's
  class-id dispatches) OR the pushed 0x8000 mask is nonzero
  (so CHECK_ALL_PLANE = the cross-class accept switch, its
  semantics CONFIRMED), and self-match is skipped; verb
  +0x78 then BUILDS that entry's 13-byte key (edx = a local
  buffer, ebx = owner) and 0x49580 OR-merges it; the final
  12 bytes + count byte at +0xc are copied to the caller's
  key buffer (ret 0x4).
  0x4bd30 is NOT a pool-array query: it walks the OWNER's
  own list at [obj+0x64] (PR-105's object list slots), same
  verb +0x60 predicate + class filter with the mask switch
  (at [esp+0x2c] here), but after verb +0x78 builds the
  entry key it runs the PR-162 intersection idiom 0x495b0 -
  and ON A MATCH copies THAT KEY OUT and stops (0x4bdb2-
  0x4bde8: movs dwords + byte, then the output copy). So
  CHECK_LEW = "match against my own list's keys", CHECK_
  ANI/ZW = "OR the class-filtered keys of the level's
  placed objects" - the two shapes PR-165 guessed at are
  now separated exactly.

- FINDING 2, WHAT THE POOLS ARE: THE LOADED CONTAINERS
  THEMSELVES. The level loader at 0x4cd6c-0x4cdca compares
  the container's name ([ebp+0x3a], case-insensitive via
  0x76d20) against the three literals 0x91dda 'zwierzaki',
  0x91de4 'animacje', 0x91ded 'ani_plat' - EXACTLY the
  PR-60 placement source keys - and on a match stores the
  container's pool INDEX field [container+0x40] into
  ds:0xcef44 / 0xa94ec / 0xa94e8 respectively: the ZW pool
  IS the 'zwierzaki' container's object pool, the ANI pool
  the 'animacje' one, the third the 'ani_plat' one. The
  layout claim is INDEPENDENTLY verified at the container's
  own cleanup (0x4ce0a-0x4ce24): [[container]+0x40]*4 +
  container + 0x58 = the same chain-head array zeroed over
  a count at [ebp+0xe2] - the container object IS the pool
  array base, and ds:0xcef40 at query time = the current
  container. So CHECK_* key bits are computed FROM THE
  LEVEL'S OWN PLACED OBJECTS of a source category, filtered
  by the requesting object's class id: the engine-side
  grounding of the port's PR-60 source model is now NAME-
  EXACT. The ani_plat pool's other consumer sits at
  0x4b6ba, inside 0x4b600 - a position/velocity scan
  (reads [obj+0xca]/+0xce speeds, [obj+0xa9]) called from
  0x546d7/0x54719 near the feed dispatcher: the platform-
  ground check lead (item 4).

- FINDING 3, THE STARTUP REGISTRY, FULLY TRANSCRIBED - AND A
  NEGATIVE. All fourteen registrations at 0x4fccd-0x4fee5
  share the shape 0x5c320(eax=0x14) THEN 0x51120(ecx=1,
  ebx=class id, edx=name), storing the returned handle into
  consecutive globals ds:0xcefbc..0xceff0. The full class-id
  sequence (two entries inherit the previous ebx - PR-165's
  sample was head-truncated): 6,6,11,(11),7,3,5,12,2,9,8,
  10,11,(11). The name table is 0x9201c-0x920e4. NEGATIVE:
  NONE of those fourteen handle globals is READ anywhere in
  the image (grep census over all of text.asm) - the
  startup-registered pools have no direct consumer; the
  QUERIED pool handles are the F2 load-time ones. 0x5c320
  itself = generic pool-by-type-id creator (manager via
  0x7521f; type ids 0x14 here, 0xa5 seen in F4); 0x51120 =
  an adapter reading [creator+0xc]/+0x10 and calling the
  pool MANAGER verb +0xd8 at [[ds:0xcef40]+0x394]+0x8. The
  preceding 0x44350 call stores ds:0xcef58 (adjacent slot,
  semantics open, item 5).
  THE NAME DECODE - still open, with evidence: the 14
  strings are referenced ONLY by this registry; a 256-key
  single-byte XOR scan finds NO key making ANY of them

  (upper/lower alternating; 'CxHxUxJxOxZxAx' is all 'x'-

  their first three pairs 'XtXoTm'); decoded lengths would

  pliku levels: %s.') and readable internal class names
  'ANITAB','PLANT','GRABOBJ','DEMOTEXT','ANIBACK','MOVEPLAT',

  'WODOSPAD','ZWIERZ','GRUPA','PICT','POCISK','IDPOCISK',
  'GRABG','GWIAZDKI','NIESP','ZONE','KORONA','SURPRISE',
  'BAL','DNGANI','TRASA','TRASA2','LINA','TABLICA','BERLO'

## PR-168 — THE FEED LAW IS CLOSED END TO END AND THE BY_*
## "ARMS" ARE ONE ARMS: MODES 2/3/4 ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL FEEDS
## OF A CONSTANT 100/TICK ([container+0x388], SET AT CONTAINER
## INIT 0x4c8b7); THE [obj+0xa1]+0xc DEREFERENCE NEVER EXISTED
## - IT WAS THE ONE-BYTE LISTING TRAP SEVENTH INSTANCE; THE
## [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe] GUARDS ARE NOT GUARDS BUT THE STATE'S
## OWN MOTION PARAMETERS, LOADED AT 0x549F0 FROM THE PARAM
## BLOCK [obj+0xd2] AND CONSUMED AS KEY-BIT SIGNS BY THE
## DEFAULT KEY BUILDER 0x54900 - PR-98's PHYSICS FIELDS, THE
## SAME ONES THE PORT ALREADY MODELS
(READING + LEDGER CORRECTION; no code, no new test - the
PR-138..167 precedent; PR-165 open item (1) is CLOSED (with
one new narrow item); PR-166's carried mention of it gets a
close bracket)

- WHY. The Next entry specced the feed-dispatcher arms: the
  BY_TIME arm's [[obj+0xa1]+0xc] dereference, the [obj+0xba]/
  [obj+0xbe] guards in the BY_TX/BY_TY arms, and the
  [container+0x388] BY_TY rate setter. Method: raw-byte dumps
  at the five jump-table targets (the listing offsets were
  already suspect), a writer census for [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe]
  and [x+0x388], and a reader census for the accumulator
  [obj+0xa1].

- FINDING 1, MODES 2/3/4 ARE THE SAME FEED; THE DEREFERENCE
  WAS A LISTING MIRAGE. Raw bytes at the jump-table targets:
  mode 0 0x543c6 = [obj+0xa1] += abs([obj+0xca]) (unchanged
  from PR-165); mode 1 0x543dc = the abs([obj+0xce]) twin
  (unchanged); mode 2 0x543fb = `mov eax,ds:0xcef40; mov
  edi,[obj+0xa1]; mov eax,[eax+0x388]; add edi,eax; mov
  [obj+0xa1],edi` - NO dereference, NO compare: a plain feed
  of the pool scalar, IDENTICAL in form to the old "mode 4";
  mode 3 0x543f2 = the same feed PRE-GUARDED by `cmp [obj+
  0xba],0; je` default; mode 4 0x5441b = the same feed pre-
  guarded by `cmp [obj+0xbe],0; je` default. The apparent
  "[obj+0xa1]+0xc deref, cmp +0xc, jle full-feed" was the
  objdump starting one byte early inside 0x543fb's sequence
  (the `8b 80 88 03 00 00 = mov eax,[eax+0x388]` mis-split
  into a deref + a 0xc compare) - SEVENTH member of the one-
  byte trap class (0x543a0, 0x52360, 0x535a0, 0x4b890,
  0x4bd30, 0x4b88f). THE CORRECTED LAW: BY_TIME = constant
  100/tick feed; BY_TX = the same feed iff [obj+0xba] != 0;
  BY_TY = the same feed iff [obj+0xbe] != 0; mode bits stay
  exactly PR-162's map (bit 0 BY_Y, bit 1 BY_TIME, bit 2
  BY_TY). The rate is set at container init: 0x4c8b7 `mov
  DWORD PTR [x+0x388],0x64` = 100 (PR-166's "runtime-set" is
  now pinned to a literal 100 at load). THE CONSUMER WAS
  ALREADY KNOWN: [obj+0xa1] is read by the record step at
  0x52323 to compute the distance to the row end and WRITTEN
  by the row-step helper at 0x52118 - PR-98/162's accumulator
  model is the engine's, with the dispatcher as its feeder,
  ENTER as its zeroer (PR-167 F4) and the row step as its
  consumer. The law is now CLOSED end to end.

- FINDING 2, THE GUARDS ARE THE STATE'S OWN MOTION
  PARAMETERS - [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe] = PR-98'S PHYSICS FIELDS.
  Writer census (whole image): the ONLY stores are (a) 0x549f9
  /0x54a08: `mov eax,[edx]; mov [obj+0xba],eax; mov eax,
  [edx+0x4]; mov [obj+0xbe],eax` with [obj+0xd2] the state's
  PARAMETER BLOCK (0x54a45 re-reads [obj+0xd2]+0x8 = the row
  parameter array - PR-101/102's shape): the first two row
  parameters load into the object at the key-gate step (F4);
  (b) 0x54a57/0x54a82/0x54a93/0x54ac3/0x54ae7/0x54b16/
  0x54b3b/0x54b47 - literal writes 10/-10/0 inside the
  physics clamp comparisons against the param block (0x54a51
  `add esi,5; cmp [paramblk+8+edx], esi; jle`) = the engine's
  parameter CLAMPING for authored motion; (c) 0x54e2e/0x54e38
  zeroing both. READERS beyond the feed guards: the key-
  provider family 0x54860 (F3) and PR-98's physics reads (the port's
  own model: NEXT_STEPS cites v_x += ... [obj+0xba]/20 + ...
  [obj+0x6d]). So the "guards" are not control flags: they
  are the authored motion pair (the PR-98 velocity params),
  and BY_TX/BY_TY feed only while the object's motion
  parameters are live - the engine's steady rate feed paired
  with authored motion, not a third speed source.

## PR-169 — THE MEMBERSHIP PREDICATE'S FIELD IS AN ACCESSOR:

  distribution; direct reads of the minority bodies; and re-

  the getter was hiding at 0x23b70).

- FINDING 1, THE PREDICATE'S FIELD IS WRITTEN BY A GENERIC
  ACCESSOR. 0x23b70 (base-table family): `mov ebx,eax; mov
  ecx,[obj+0x8]; call DWORD [ecx+0x8]; mov [obj+0x2c],eax` -
  it CALLS the class's verb +0x08 and STORES the product at
  [obj+0x2c]; the predicate 0x23b80 reads exactly that field.
  So membership is not a boolean flag: [obj+0x2c] holds the
  object's class-verb product (the +0x08 verb's result - for
  the base table that verb is 0x23e00, a BOUNDS-CONTAINMENT
  compare of [obj+0]/+4/+8 vs [edx]-fields, re-confirming
  PR-162's rectangle-identity facts), and the pool predicate
  is a NULL-TEST of that product. This narrows PR-167 F2a:
  "membership = word at [obj+0x2c]" stays factually right,
  but the field is a COMPUTED handle, maintained by the 0x23b70
  accessor, not a state flag. (Which flows call 0x23b70: no
  direct calls in the listing - invoked indirectly through the
  verb tables, like every 0x23bxx body; caller census open.)

- FINDING 2, THE CHAIN-INSERT CENSUS, EXHAUSTIVE - AND ITS
  RE-SCOPE. Every store form in the image: the ONLY +0x58
  store is the container's heads-array allocation (0x4cdf8,

- FINDING 3, THE OBSERVABILITY CENSUS (AUTHORED DATA,
  SCRATCH). Control tokens over ZARIA.01's .MOV texts:
  BY_TIME on 114 states, BY_X on 15, BY_TY on 4. The plain-
  BY_TIME bucket's 1128 row lines carry 12 distinct gates:
  0(22), 1(4), 40(3), 75(12), 80(5), 100(62), 120(5), 150(8),
  200(286), 225(6), 300(330), 400(248) - SEVEN of the twelve
  (1/40/75/80/120/150/225) are NOT multiples of the 100-per-
  step feed, and every state that exits mid-row leaves a
  NON-ZERO remainder. So the zeroing is OBSERVABLE on shipped
  data: with a carried remainder the new state's first row
  opens an iteration EARLY; zeroed, it does not. (The FRAME_REV
  buckets are all 100-multiples; BY_X gates are movement units
  {4,5,6,7,15} - the walk path is untouched.) THE PORT'S
  AUDIT: obj_transition and the forced A_DEAD path zero facc/
  xa but did NOT zero row_t - a real divergence on exactly
  these lines. FIX SHIPPED: `o->row_t = 0;` at both applier
  arms with the engine law cited. The port's two-register
  split (row_t for time modes, facc for distance modes) stays
  OBSERVATIONALLY IDENTICAL to the engine's one register: the
  register is fresh at every state entry (F1) and its feed
  source is mode-fixed within one state (0x543a0 dispatch), so
  no within-state carry can cross the two and both-zero-at-
  entry gives the single-register behavior exactly.

## PR-173 — THE KEY IS THE SIGNAL SET: THE 0x919ec NAME BLOCK
## PINS THE WHOLE BIT NUMBERING (73 ENTRIES: 4 NON-BIT NODE-OP
## SPECIALS, THEN EXACTLY 68 SIGNALS IN THE PORT ENUM'S ORDER,
## THEN THE AC_EV_MAX SENTINEL; BIT N = BLOCK INDEX N+4, AND
## THE PORT'S 68-PAIR TOKEN TABLE IS VERIFIED COMPLETE AND
## ERROR-FREE), THE PUMP'S KEY GETTER IS CLASS VERB +0x8c
## (MERGED INTO THE LIVE SET AT 0x536f0), THE MOTION-TO-KEY
## SYNTHESISER IS REACHED THROUGH IT (ENTRY 0x54910 — PR-171'S
## 0x54912 WAS THE LISTING TRAP AGAIN), ITS BITS DECODE TO
## K_BKWD/K_FWD/K_UP/K_DOWN/K_FIRE/K_ALT/K_JUMP — THE ENGINE
## SPEAKS ITS OWN INPUT VOCABULARY BACK TO ITSELF FROM MOTION
## STATE — AND THE 0x600000/0x800000 "CHECK_LN CONSTANTS" ARE
## CLOSED AS LEDGER ARTIFACTS (GIT-PROVEN: THEY ENTER FIRST
## AT PR-166's NEXT, NEVER AT PR-161)
(READING + LEDGER CORRECTION + ONE CODE COMMENT FIX; no
behaviour change — the PR-138..172 precedent; PR-171's
family-B top lead CLOSED IN PART (re-scoped), its literal-

  PR-171 proved 0x600000/0x800000 do not exist as code or data
  and labeled a hex-dump thesis; PR-171 also left "who builds
  keys for the 99 family-B classes: open (new item)" with the
  "0x54912 has zero table slots" triple negative. Method:
  raw-block dump of 0x919ec; a machine bijection against the
  port enum and its token table (tools in the scratch dir);
  the pump 0x536f0 verbatim; slot censuses anchored on the
  PR-167 class-table marker (+0x60 = 0x23b80, 178 tables);

  authored .MOV condition lines; git -S provenance of the two

- FINDING 1, THE NAME BLOCK PINS EVERYTHING (AND PR-88'S
  BOUNDS WERE SHORT). The block is 0x919ec..0x91c68, NOT
  ..0x91c40: 73 NUL-separated entries — AC_K_ANY, K_ANY,
  AC_K_NEVER, K_NEVER FIRST (the four node-op specials PR-88
  found special-cased in the parser: they are IN the block and
  are NOT bits), then EXACTLY 68 signal names AC_BLOK ..
  AC_DISAPPEAR, then the literal string 'AC_EV_MAX' as the
  end sentinel. Law: signal bit N = block index N+4. Machine-
  checked three ways: (a) the port's LL_SIG_* enum (68 + the
  AC_EV_MAX tail entry) matches the 68 names one-for-one IN
  ORDER, zero mismatches; (b) the port's name->enum table in
  ll_play.c holds exactly 68 pairs, complete against the block
  and with zero name/enum mismatches — PR-88's table was
  built by sampling, this is total; (c) every number PR-88
  ever recorded off 0x48000 (AC_BLOK 0, AC_ENEMY 7, AC_TIME
  9, AC_ENEMY_ATC 16, AC_ONAIR 18, K_FWD 36, K_FIRE 39,
  K_JUMP 53, K_GEN1 54, K_GEN2 55) hits its own block name at
  index = bit + 4, and PR-164's applier write [obj+0x61] |= 2
  (live byte 1 bit 1 = bit 9) is AC_TIME at index 13. The
  13-byte key = 3-dword mask + count byte: 0x552e0 stores the
  count at [dst+0xc] then rep-moves the 12 mask bytes
  (0x5533c-0x5534c); 0x49580 ORs 3 dwords (0x49589-0x4959a,
  bounded by lea ecx,[eax+0xc]). So the row-line key, the
  condition-node mask (PR-88's 3-dword folding), the live set
  [obj+0x60] and the built keys are ONE 68-bit vocabulary —
  PR-101's key law and PR-88's condition model are one system.

- FINDING 2, THE PUMP'S KEY GETTER IS CLASS VERB +0x8c AND
  ITS KEY IS MERGED INTO THE LIVE SET BEFORE THE WALK. 0x536f0
  verbatim: lea edx,[esp+0x10] (local); call [[obj+8]+0x8c]
  (0x536fb-0x536ff); lea ebx,[obj+0x60] — THE LIVE SET;
  call 0x49580(eax=live, edx=returned key) — GETTER KEY ORed
  IN (0x5370c); then 0x523f0 walks the CURRENT record's row
  chain and its returned key is merged the same way
  (0x5371c-0x53725) — the explicit site for PR-154's "authored
  rows compose their key through the chain"; then verb +0x54
  (0x53733, PR-164's hook). So transition matching (0x53520
  copying the live key, PR-164) tests against live ∪ self-getter
  ∪ chain-key. PR-157's shorthand "key = the object's OWN
  12-byte live set" is re-grounded: true of the LOOKUP, but
  the pump feeds that set from THREE producers first.

  [CORRECTED BY PR-175 F7a: the pair is the ENERGY field -
  PR-89's counter, not an order: 0x5516a `cmp [self+0xad],
  [other+0xad]`, the greater side builds the AC_ENEMY_ATC
  key, the jle side the always-AC_ENEMY zero key. Item (2)'s
  "ORDER field?" question resolved.]
  greater side builds a key with AC_ENEMY_ATC (bit 16 =
  [key+2]|0x01), the other branch zero-key; tail partial,
  item 2); flags test ah,0x20 = word bit 0x2000 = DANGER
  (PR-162's map) -> the same +0xd0 with [container+0x54];
  ALWAYS merges a local with byte0 |= 0x80 = AC_ENEMY (bit 7 —
  independent PR-88 constant match). So the entry-key language
  is about RELATIONS: contact, push-resistance, danger,
  ordinals — all in the same 68-bit vocabulary.

- FINDING 4, THE SYNTHESISER IS REACHED, AND ITS BITS ARE
  INPUT KEYS. PR-171's "entry 0x54912, zero table slots" was
  the listing trap (11th member) plus a search for the
  mis-parsed value: the bytes at 0x54910-0x54913 are 53 51 56
  57 — the push ebx/ecx/esi/edi prologue PR-171 itself quoted —
  and EVERY class table stores 0x54910 (x115 at +0x8c in the
  anchor census; table values are the entry ground truth).
  Decoding F1's bit map through F1 of THIS record:
  [obj+0xa5] & 0x01 -> [key+4]|0x80 = bit 39 = K_FIRE;
  & 0x10 -> [key+5]|0x01 = bit 40 = K_ALT; & 0x20 ->
  [key+6]|0x20 = bit 53 = K_JUMP; [obj+0xba] != 0 ->
  K_BKWD (35) / K_FWD (36) selected by the [obj+0xb6] bit
  0x10; [obj+0xba] == 0 -> [obj+0xbe] jge -> K_UP (37), jle
  -> K_DOWN (38) — both at rest. The engine TURNS AN OBJECT'S
  MOTION AND ACTION STATE INTO ITS OWN KEY-INPUT VOCABULARY —
  the authored K_* condition tokens are AI-addressable motion
  tests, not only player input. The 0x60/0x80 byte values of
  PR-171's thesis are exactly the synthesizer's idle
  (K_UP|K_DOWN = 0x60 in key+4) and fire-flag (0x80) states.

## PR-175 — THE KEY-FOLLOW-UP INTERLOCK PASS: +0x14 IS THE
## STATE-STEP VERB SLOT, THE 99-TABLE FAMILY IS A DISJOINT
## LINEAGE, +0xac IS A KEY-EXTENSION HOOK, AND [obj+0xad] IS
## THE ENERGY FIELD (READING; no port code, no behaviour
## change; PR-173'S items (1)/(2)/(5) CLOSED or re-scoped with
## call-site evidence, PR-174's +0xac detail CORRECTED)

- WHY. PR-173's Next specced this pass: (a) the +0x8c "TWO
  contracts" - which families' objects run the pump 0x536f0's
  key merge and which carry the boolean 0x23870; (b) the field
  readers - [obj+0xa9], the [obj+0xad] "ordinal pair" in
  0x55130/0x550c0, and [obj+0x75]; and PR-174 had just
  counted +0xac, "the other half of the 0x53612 guard". All
  three interlock through the SAME call-site maps, so they run
  as one docs pass. Method: the slot-table scan over the
  binary (the 178 tables marker-anchored at +0x60 = 0x23b80,
  plus the independent 99-table family found by its +0x78 =
  0x54860 / +0x60 getter shape), the text-section grep recipe
  (`grep -nE "0xa9\]" text.asm` - the bracket form keeps real
  operands and rejects data-region false disassembly), and
  re-reads of 0x550a0/0x55070/0x546a0/0x23920/0x23870/
  0x55130/0x3ed00-0x3ee27. No port file changes: nothing
  shipped moves.

- FINDING 1, +0x14 IS THE PER-OBJECT STATE-STEP VERB SLOT -
  THE PUMP IS REACHED THROUGH IT, AND LION IS PUMPED. Slot
  +0x14 is called at many engine sites (0x129ac, 0x1349d,
  0x2e9ce, 0x3f5ec, 0x3f680, 0x3fb07, 0x4006f, 0x40c56,
  0x425a0, 0x4579c, ...). Across the 178 marker-anchored
  tables its values: 0x550a0 x79, 0x400b0 x45, 0x536f0 x26
  (the pump installed DIRECTLY), 0x23c70 x18, 0x55380 x4,
  singletons 0x41b90/0x410f0/0x249d0. 0x550a0 reads verbatim:
  zero [obj+0xe6], zero [obj+0xea], `call 0x536f0; ret` -
  and 0x550b4 is the ONLY direct `call 0x536f0` in the whole
  text. So the pump set = the tables with 0x550a0 or 0x536f0
  at +0x14 = 105 of 178. LION 0x96960 carries 0x550a0 at
  +0x14: PR-153's "the pump runs every LION tick" HOLDS for
  LION. The 0x23c70 arm (x18) delegates to class verb +0x28
  before the fall-through; 0x400b0 (x45) is the position path
  PR-173 already named.

- FINDING 2, THE 99 FAMILY-B TABLES ARE A DISJOINT LINEAGE -
  PR-173's JOINT PRESENTATION CONFLATED TWO TABLE POPULATIONS.
  Scanning by +0x78 = 0x54860 finds exactly 99 tables; NOT
  ONE of them is in the 178 marker-anchored set: their +0x60
  holds 0x54450 x41 / 0x40030 x26 / 0x3d2c0 x5 / 0x3d940 x4 /
  0x3d200 x3 / 0x1edb0 x2 - never the 0x23b80 marker. Their
  +0x14 is 0x23920 in ALL 99: read verbatim, `push edx; mov
  edx,[eax+0x5c]; mov eax,[eax+0x50]; mov eax,[[eax+edx*4]
  +0x12]; pop edx; ret` - the CURRENT record's control-flags
  word ([rec+0x12], the same word 0x546c5 tests bit 0x40 and
  the stepper reads for [rec+0xc]) returned as the step verb.
  These classes have NO pump, no walk verb, no key verb at
  +0x14 - they are the passive class lineages (their +0x8c =
  0x23870 is consistent with that). PR-173 F3's "The 99
  family-B tables ... The slot has TWO contracts" mixed the
  two populations; the real separation is between LINEAGES,
  not one slot's contracts.

- FINDING 3, THE +0x8c SLOT HAS EXACTLY TWO CALL SITES, AND
  NEITHER USES THE BOOLEAN'S VALUE. Grep over the text
  section: `call DWORD PTR [+0x8c]` occurs at 0x536ff (inside
  the pump 0x536f0, the merge pinned verbatim by PR-173 F2)
  and 0x3ee18. The 0x3ee18 path (enclosing function spanning
  0x3ed00-0x3ee27; boundary partially read, 0x3eff2 calls
  0x3ed40): builds a 13-byte key via the ctor 0x749a0, sets
  `or BYTE [key+ebp],0x4` - bit 2 = AC_BREAK_NEXT (PR-173
  F1's numbering) - merges it into the OWNER's live set
  ([[ecx+0x3c]+0x60], 0x49580), then calls the CHILD's +0x8c
  with edx = the class table (a clobbered argument: the body
  at 0x23870/0x54910 reads only eax = the object). The
  return value at BOTH sites is discarded (0x536ff: the getter
  writes its buffer through edx = &[obj+0x60]; 0x3ee18: `add
  esp,0x3c` follows). So 0x23870's boolean answer feeds NO
  caller at those slots - the "two contracts" framing
  dissolves into the lineage separation of F2.

- FINDING 4, +0xac IS A KEY-EXTENSION HOOK, NOT A ROW VERB -
  PR-174'S DETAIL CORRECTED. Slot +0xac is called at exactly
  two sites: the applier's state-change arm (0x535f7, always
  after ENTER) and the same-state arm (0x5361c-0x53620) ONLY
  on a row-changing write. At both, ebx = &[obj+0x60] has
  been loaded at 0x535ad and survives, so edx = &the LIVE KEY
  SET at entry - PR-174's "edx = the row value" was WRONG.
  The slot values co-vary with +0x14 exactly: (0x550a0,
  0x546a0) x79, (0x400b0, 0x546a0) x45, (0x536f0, 0x23930 =
  a bare `ret` - the EMPTY extension) x26, (0x23c70, 0x52a00)
  x10. Meaning: whenever the engine changes state or re-seeks
  a row, it calls the class's key-extension verb on the live
  set. 0x546a0 (x130) partially read: test [obj+0xb6],0x2 ->
  0x54804 arm; else read the record's +0x12 word, test ah,
  0x40 -> 0x4b600 (PR-165's pool query, which reads [obj+
  +0xa9] at 0x4b64f!) -> 0x49580 merge into live; then RMW/
  zero of [obj+0xa9] at 0x5477b-0x547f0. Full body: carried.

- FINDING 5, THE PUMP-105 SLOT MAP AND A HOOK DISJOINTNESS.

- FINDING 7, THE FIELD READS: [obj+0xad] IS THE ENERGY FIELD;

  (a) PR-173 F3's "ordinal pair" RESOLVES to ENERGY:

## PR-176 — THE CONTROLLER GETTER READ WHOLE: +0x8c WRAPS
## THE MOTION SYNTH AND ADDS THE K_F1-12 SIGNAL BITS FROM A
## PRIORITY CHAIN; THE TWELVE CONTROLLER CLASSES ARE THE
## STAGE LIONS AND THEIR DEATH-MODULE DOUBLES (PURCHAWA AND
## CAMEL IDENTIFIED; READING, NO PORT CODE, NO BEHAVIOUR
## CHANGE)

- WHY. PR-175's Next named this pass: read 0x504e0 whole and
  its callee 0x551f0; identify the twelve tables carrying the
  0x504e0 getter with the LION controller shape; then update
  the KADMAR camel reachability item. Method: verbatim disas-
 sembly of 0x504e0-0x5071b and 0x551f0-0x55228; the name-
  string region 0x90700-0x91400 decoded from the binary; two
  factory-chain parsers (a class-name literal feeds `call
  0x76a69`, and the MATCH branch's block is the one that
  follows the compare - pinned by the Zaria exemplar at
  0x1fef4/0x1ff15 - NEVER nearest-neighbour matching); the
  jump table at 0x504b0 read as data; the signal vocabulary
  from PR-173 F5's name block cross-checked against the
  port's LL_SIG_* enum. Docs only: nothing shipped moves.

- FINDING 1, 0x504e0 WHOLE: THE CONTROLLER +0x8c GETTER IS A
  WRAPPER - SIGNAL-ORDINAL KEY PLUS THE 0x54910 MOTION KEY.
  Entry: eax = self, edx = the caller's key buffer (saved at
  [esp+0x30]); first gate: class verb +0xf8 nonzero AND
  [obj+0xd2] != 0 AND bit 0x2 of [obj+0xa5] -> call 0x551f0
  (F2). Then a PRIORITY CHAIN, ten legs read to the last:
  ([obj+0xa5],0x40; ds:0xcef5c)->ordinal 0; ([obj+0xa5],
  0x80; 0xcef60)->1; ([obj+0xa6],0x01; 0xcef64)->2; ([obj+
  0xa6],0x02; 0xcef68)->3; ([obj+0xa6],0x40; 0xcef6c)->4;
  ([obj+0xa6],0x80; 0xcef70)->5; ([obj+0xa7],0x01; 0xcef74)
  ->6; ([obj+0xa7],0x02; 0xcef78)->7; ([obj+0xa7],0x04;
  0xcef7c)->8; ([obj+0xa7],0x08; 0xcef80)->9 - each leg
  requires BOTH the object bit and the global word non-zero,
  and writes the winner into [obj+0xee] (0x50634: build a
  ZERO 12+count key via 0x749a0; `cmp [obj+0xee],0xb; ja
  skip; jmp cs:[eax*4+0x504b0]` - the 12-entry table reads
  0x5065b,0x50662,...,0x506a8: case k ORs bit (41+k) (cases
  0-6 set [key+5] bits 1-7, cases 7-11 [key+6] bits 1-4)).
  Bits 41..52 in PR-173 F5's block vocabulary are exactly
  K_F1..K_F12 - and the port's LL_SIG_* enum puts K_F1 at 41
  through K_F12 at 52: EXACT match, a new independent confir-
  mation of the name block from the getter's own jump table.
  Tail: the local key is copied to [esp+0x20], then 0x54910
  - PR-173's MOTION SYNTHESIZER - is called (eax = self,
  edx = [esp+0x10]); `call 0x49580` merges THAT key into the
  caller's saved buffer [esp+0x30], and the merged set (with
  its count byte) is copied back over the caller's buffer.
  So the controller getter = signal-ordinal key OR motion key,
  delivered through the standard +0x8c buffer contract the
  pump 0x536f0 already reads. The chain writes only ordinals
  0..9: cases 10/11 (K_F11/K_F12) are unreachable from this
  chain - counted (open).

- FINDING 2, 0x551f0 WHOLE: A QUEUE-NODE CONSUMER. 0x551f0-
  0x55228: edx = self; unlink the first node - `mov eax,
  [obj+0xd2]; ebx=[[obj+0xd2]]; [obj+0xd2]=ebx`; `call
  0x5c370` (release); if the queue is now empty AND class
  verb +0x3c returns true, set [obj+0x106] = 1. Together
  with PR-175's 0x550a0 (which zeros [obj+0xe6]/[obj+0xea]
  at EVERY state step) and this getter's [obj+0xee], fields
  0xd2/0xe6/0xea/0xee form a controller signal-event queue
  block (head at 0xd2; 0xe6/0xea per-step-cleared pair;
  0xee current ordinal). Producers of queue entries: open,
  counted; the +0xf8 and +0x3c verbs and the [obj+0x106]
  flag: open, counted.

- FINDING 3, THE TWELVE IDENTIFIED: STAGE LIONS AND THEIR

- The DEFERRED Windows gate proved end to end for the first time:

- FOUR BUGS, all mine, all found by running it, each with its
  measured signature (the lesson is in the last one):
  1. buildx with a registry cache on a FRESH GHCR package:
     `importing cache manifest from ...:buildcache` -> `failed to
     fetch anonymous token: 403 Forbidden`. A new package is private,
     and the cache ref cannot exist on its first run. Fixed by
     dropping buildx and the cache for plain `docker build`/`push`
     (auth through the daemon), plus `concurrency: ci-image` after
     the push trigger and a manual dispatch raced on the same tag.
  2. a plain YAML scalar: `run: echo ... docker login ... \` folded
     to a literal backslash-argument -> `docker: 'docker login'
     requires at most 1 argument`. Every run in those files is a
     block scalar now; grepped for the pattern - no other hits.
  3. `permissions: contents: read` with no `packages: read`, and
     `container:` with no credentials: a private GHCR pull that the
     token cannot see answers **404 `... :ci: not found`, not 403**,
     so the text pointed at a missing image and I debugged the
     builder twice while it was fine. Both files now carry
     packages:read + explicit credentials (github.actor /
     secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN), with a comment saying so.
  4. THE REAL ONE: taking `Provision SDL2 for the Windows target` out
     of ci.yml broke the LINUX gate, because the mixed legs declare
     .exe targets as MAKE PREREQUISITES - Makefile:1744 is
     `verify-menu: ll_cutscene ll_cutscene.exe`, and
     verify-skip/-music/-pcm/-help/-cmake name 1-7 .exe each; only
     verify-win's set was purely its own. So make cross-builds a
     Windows binary whether or not the leg then prints its SKIP. The
     ruling defers Windows TESTING, not Windows BUILDING wherever a
     prerequisite asks for it. Failure text (run 44536198608):
     `ported/ll_audio.h:38: fatal error: SDL2/SDL.h: No such file or
     directory`, same at `ported/ll_view.h:41`, then
     `make: *** [Makefile:78: ll_cutscene.exe] Error 1`.
     Reproduced LOCALLY before pushing the fix this time: all 18 TUs
     of $(SRC) (read out of make's own database) with the same flags
     -> SDL_WIN=/nonexistent gives those two fatal errors verbatim;
     with the pinned tarball, 0 errors and 0 warnings.

## OWNER (2026-11-19) — SUITE SPEED, SECOND ROUND: the oracle decodes ONCE,
## two redundant chain replays are gone, one kept ON PURPOSE (no port
## code, no tool changed - no frame can move)

- py-refs: ONE decode pass for both oracle frames. The rule used to run
  the whole file twice to get one frame each. Measured here: 6.43s for
  the pair vs 3.21s for `--only 1020,1520`, and the frames are the same
  bytes either way (sha256 f01020 1e56724734d76d7b..., f01520
  50a7f40a459fd34e... - both methods, compared before the edit).
  tools/is_decode.py already accepted a comma list and names its output
  f<frame>.ppm, so no tool change was needed; the two consumer paths
  (c_py = decode midpoint, py_last = ESC-skip end) are kept by placing
  the second frame, so every leg stays byte-for-byte as it was.
- The duplicate audit, done properly this time. All 71 chain runs in the
  Makefile were parsed and grouped by (exact command line INCLUDING
  positional args) + (state-affecting env), ignoring the dump-output
  variables because they are observers. Result: exactly THREE duplicate
  groups, not the "11 single-shot uses" I estimated earlier - most of
  those differ in LEO_MENU_KEY / _SEL / _PICK, so there was nothing to
  merge. Two were merged, one kept (below).
- Why merging the frame dumps is safe - proven, not assumed. The two
  hooks (single-shot `LEO_MENU_PPM`+TICK at ported/ll_menu.c:1288 and
  sequence `LEO_MENU_PPM_DIR`+MAX at :1305) call the same ppm_fb on the
  same composed buffer in the same loop iteration. Measured on BOTH
  targets: sequence frame == single-shot frame at the same tick (t2
  14c5ef3b..., t8 e41b61fd...), cross-target equality holds in all four
  combinations including mixed hooks, and t2 != t8 WITHIN one run, which
  is exactly what those two assertions claim. Side fact worth keeping:
  frame content is TICK-deterministic, not wall-clock - a sequence run
  does nine extra file writes per pass and still matches byte for byte.
  That is the evidence any future non-real-time pacing mode would need;
  it is NOT applied, because the clock / A-V-sync / row-clock legs
  assert real-time behaviour and that is an owner decision.
- MERGED: verify-menu (same chain, tick 2 and tick 8) and verify-win
  (same chain under wine, tick 2 and tick 8) each now run ONCE with the
  sequence hook. MEASURED PRICE of what that actually removes: one
  native chain run = 1.1s, one wine chain run = 1.4s. Honest sizing:
  my earlier framing implied ~10s; the real saving is ~2.5s per full
  local run. Kept because it is free and removes a cold wine start -
  but it is NOT the big lever, and the numbers here replace the ones
  I quoted earlier today.
- NOT merged, deliberately: verify-level runs `./ll_level $(DATA)
  ZARIA.01` twice with identical state, into two logs. That is ~2s of
  the suite, and two independent processes producing an identical
  placement listing is the ONLY check anywhere that ll_level's scene
  listing is reproducible run to run (the other determinism oracles are
  linux-vs-wine fnv parity in verify-mod and C-vs-python agreement,
  neither of which covers it). The second run now carries a comment
  saying it is deliberate, so it is not "optimised" away later.
- CORRECTION to what I wrote earlier today, twice over. (a)
  "verify-mod produces zero verdicts in 0.2s and needs MOD records
  staged" is wrong - the leg pulls the records itself, and run here it
  took 4.5s and printed three cross-target verdicts (MOD
  TUNGA/RAN/ENA2: parse+render linux == wine (fnv=...)). (b) The cause
  was my own grep, and it invalidates the shortcut I put in HANDOFF
  s3: counting `(ok)` lines UNDERCOUNTS, because verdict wording is
  per-leg (MOD lines, "byte-exact", "== python reference"). s3 now says
  to gate on rc FIRST (authoritative: make -k returns non-zero if any
  leg failed) and then on the verdict-line SET.
- Makefile comment convention, learned the hard way: a tab-indented
  `#` INSIDE a recipe is a recipe line, so make ECHOES it into the log;
  this file's own convention is a column-0 `#` between recipe lines
  (already used, e.g. above the LEO_OBJ_ALL leg), which make treats as
  a comment. My 30 comment lines were re-indented to match; `make -n
  verify-all | grep -cE '^\s*#'` now finds none of mine. The two
  pre-existing echoed lines at Makefile:1369-1370 (verify-play) were
  left alone: different leg, not this round.
- GATES for this round. (1) COVERAGE A/B against the previous Makefile
  (HEAD copy, run with `make -f Makefile.head`, same commands, same
  fixtures): 108 distinct verdict lines before, 108 after, sets
  IDENTICAL, both halves rc=0 - no assertion, pin, SKIP text or wording
  was lost. (2) Full fixture-backed run: Linux half parallel rc=0
  40.8s; verify-win rc=0 144.7s; verify-mod 3 of 3 fnv verdicts;
  fixture-free parallel rc=0 2.7s with 21 named SKIPs. (3) A rebuild
  after touching every ported source: rc=0, 0 warnings, 0 errors
  (`make win` skipped per ruling 8). (4) MUTATION: breaking the oracle
  itself (`make verify-skip PYREF=/bin/true`) fails loudly and
  instantly - `make: *** [Makefile:98: py-refs]`, rc=2 - and with the
  real oracle restored verify-skip passes byte-exact again. Removing the
  PLACED frame is not a mutation: py-refs is a PHONY prerequisite of
  every leg that reads those frames, so make rebuilds it - which is the
  actual safety property: an oracle frame cannot reach a comparison
  stale.
- NOT claimed: verify-win measured 164.8s earlier today (inside the
  full-suite per-leg pass) and 143-145s standalone now. Only 1.4s of
  that gap is this change; the rest is variance in a leg built out of
  real-time segments and cold wine starts, and the per-leg CSV numbers
  were single samples. Do not bank it.
- NEXT, as a measurement rather than a guess: break verify-menu down per
  RUN (12 runs, 19.8s) to find what actually dominates - a chain run to
  tick 8 is only 1.1s, so the cost is spread across the other runs and
  their dwell/`--skip-at` segments, which are part of what those legs

  owner.
- Files: Makefile (py-refs, the two merged pairs, the deliberate-

## PR-177 — THE +0x78 SLOT IS THE RELATIONSHIP-KEY PROVIDER:
## ALL NINE SHARED PROVIDERS READ WHOLE, THE CENSUS CORRECTED
## TO 9-SHARED+56-SINGLETON, THE FAMILY CLASSIFIED, AND THE
## GENERATED SIGNALS OF ZARIA.01 (K_GEN1, AC_ENEMY, AC_
## ENEMY_ATC, AC_BLOK) NOW HAVE THEIR ENGINE MECHANISM NAMED
## (READING, NO PORT CODE, NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE)

- WHY. PR-176's Next named this pass. Method: dword censuses
  over the data segment (marker 0x23b80 at +0x60 = the 178;
  value 0x54860 at +0x78 = the 99 - sets DISJOINT, ledger
  numbers reproduced EXACTLY); the +0x78 slot's call sites
  found by exhaustive xref (exactly FOUR); objdump ranges
  (-D -b binary --adjust-vma=0x10000 --start/stop-address on
  /tmp/opencode/text.bin) because the linear text.asm
  DESYNCS over the provider cluster - stated so future PRs
  do not re-trip; every shared provider value read end to
  end; the named lead singleton 0x28af0 read whole; the
  authored ZARIA.01 .MOV texts grepped for the signal
  tokens. Docs only: nothing shipped moves.

- FINDING 1, THE +0x78 CONTRACT AND ITS FOUR CALL SITES.
  +0x78 = a per-class KEY PROVIDER for the RELATION
  between self and a context object: eax = self, ebx = ctx,
  ecx = aux; the result is delivered by filling the
  caller's buffer (edx) or by returning a key-buffer
  pointer;
  callers merge via the standard 0x49580. Call sites,
  exhaustive: (a) 0x4b5be inside the walk function entered
  at 0x4b500 - walks pool chains ([x+0x58] table / [x+0x34]
  chain), FILTERS candidates by their +0x60 verb truth and
  an ID compare ([x+0x24] == [ctx+0x24]), skips self, calls
  each match's +0x78 (edx = local key), merges all answers
  via 0x49580 (0x4b5c5); the caller buffer is [esp+0x30]
  (saved at 0x4b50a) and the merged key is delivered
  through that epilogue at 0x4b5cc+ (its exact copy shape
  not re-read - counted); (b) 0x4bda9 and (c) 0x4be09
  inside one walk
  function entered at 0x4bd30 - chain walk via [x+0x64],
  same +0x60 + id filter, plus a GLOBAL FALLBACK: manager
  ds:0xcef40's [+0x394] object's +0x78 is called when the
  walk finds nothing (0x4bdf6-0x4be16); 0x4bd30 is CALLED
  AT 0x527cb FROM THE BASE CLASS +0x8c GETTER 0x52750
  (PR-173 F4's base getter), gated by `[rec+0x12] & 0x8000`
  (the record control-flags word from PR-159/160 - NEW
  fact: the base getter's relation-merge arm is
  flag-gated), result merged via 0x49580 at 0x527d6;
  (d) 0x55421 inside 0x553e0 (below). A FIFTH consumer is
  NOT a +0x78 call but the same pool machinery's bounds
  half: 0x4b430 (called from the LION +0xac verb 0x546a0
  at 0x546f0/0x54732): builds a rectangle from ctx's
  bounds pair [ctx+0xca]/[ctx+0xce] plus half-extents from
  0x534e0 (descriptor carrying table 0x98274), tests the
  entries of the [obj+0x70] array ([obj+0x7c] count,
  stride 0x14) via 0x45620, and on a hit returns a key
  with BYTE 0 BIT 0 = AC_BLOK (bit 0) - the collision
  signal, at last, has its engine mechanism.

- FINDING 2, CENSUS CORRECTED: PR-173 ITEM (3)'S "~76" IS
  WRONG - INSIDE THE 178 MARKER TABLES THE +0x78 SLOT HAS
  65 DISTINCT VALUES: NINE SHARED spanning 122 tables -
  0x552e0 x65, 0x3df00 x19, 0x50f80 x15, 0x53c90 x10,
  0x3d990 x4, 0x23b10 x3, 0x3d440 x2, 0x553e0 x2, 0x3e500
  x2 - PLUS 56 SINGLETON tables (122+56=178 exactly). The
  99 0x54860 tables are the SEPARATE passive lineage (zero
  overlap, all +0x14 = 0x23920 = "return [rec+0x12] of the
  current record", all +0x8c = 0x23870) - so the item-(3)
  wording "singletons ARE that lineage" conflated two
  populations a third time (bracket). 0x23920 itself read
  whole: `mov edx,[obj+0x5c]; mov eax,[obj+0x50]; mov eax,
  [eax+edx*4]; mov eax,[eax+0x12]` - [obj+0x50] = record
  array, [obj+0x5c] = record index: the law for WHICH
  record the flag word comes from is now pinned.

- FINDING 3, THE FAMILY CLASSIFIED - ALL NINE SHARED
  PROVIDERS READ (shape-first; helpers named):
  (i) ZERO: 0x23b10 (x3) fills a zero key into the caller
  buffer via 0x749a0 and returns it.
  (ii) RELATION MERGES onto the known contact/flag bridge:
  0x552e0 (x65 DOMINANT): gate 0x53ae0(self,ctx) (contact,
  PR-173 F5) && class verb +0x9c; filler 0x55230 (PR-173's
  ANTI_POCISK/DANGER flag->key builder); copy to caller
  buffer, return it. 0x3df00 (x19): same as a prefix - if
  ctx != self AND ctx class verb +0xd8 truthy, reads chain
  entry 2 at &[self+0xee] via 0x45320 - then 0x552e0.
  0x3e500 (x2): if [obj+0x5c]==1 (record #1) AND ctx +0x3c
  AND 0x52eb0(self,ctx) AND ctx verb +0xf4 AND self verb
  +0xd8: SETS [obj+0x66] |= 0x40 DIRECTLY INTO THE LIVE
  SET ([obj+0x60] 13 bytes) = byte 6 bit 6 = BIT 54 =
  K_GEN1 (PR-155/156's raiser, law-confirmed), with the
  0x52cc0 side effect - then 0x552e0.
  (iii) ENEMY/FACING providers (the 0x50f80 x15 = LION's
  own, 0x53c90 x10, 0x3d990 x4): gate 0x53ae0; +0x9c;
  +0x40 truth -> call ctx class verb +0xd0 (facing/
  relation, ebx = [self+0xb1] or manager [+0x54] or 0);
  0x50f80 additionally runs 0x55130 (ecx = [self+0xee])
  when [obj+0x40] verb is true and merges its energy key,
  and calls +0xd0 when [self+0x11a]==7; 0x53c90 calls +0xd0
  again when +0x44 & 0x80000. ALL THREE then OR byte 0 |=
  0x80 = AC_ENEMY (bit 7) into the local key, 0x3d990 ALSO
  byte 2 bit 0 = AC_ENEMY_ATC (bit 16) on its +0x40 arm -

  greater-energy side" reading now REPRODUCED INSIDE THE
  PROVIDERS themselves; +0x44 flag bits 0x20/0x80000 are

  (iv) DECOR-RECT K_GEN1 providers: 0x3d440 (x2): delegates
  to 0x552e0 unless [obj+0x5c]==1, and for record #1 runs
  the ctx +0x3c truth + ctx +0x68 position + point-in-

  the SAME rectangle format as 0x23e00 (PR-176) - with the
  CAMEL class table 0x98278 loaded as an IMMEDIATE
  (0x3d49d); tails 0x3d687/0x3d6ab unread (counted).
  (v) CHILD AGGREGATOR 0x553e0 (x2): builds a zero key,
  loops the [obj+0x3c] COUNT of child pointers at
  [obj+0x40], ORs each child's +0x78 answer (0x55421) -
  NOTE: object FIELDS +0x3c/+0x40 read here as a group
  list (the +0x3c-as-owner reading from PR-175 F7 is about

  story counted). Direct callers (not via the slot):
  0x1eba0 (constructor-region helper: calls it then TESTS

  (vi) THE 99's slot 0x54860 RE-READ whole, PR-171's decay
  law CONFIRMED with exact gates: skip when caller key byte
  [2] & 4; with [rec+0x12] & 0x10 AND key byte[0] & 0x10:
  [obj+0xc6] := -2*[obj+0xc6]/3 (idiv 3); key byte[3] & 2
  or byte[0] & 2 zero it; byte[0] & 1 zeroes [obj+0xc2].

- FINDING 4, THE NAMED LEAD SINGLETON 0x28af0 READ WHOLE
  (of 56): its table is 0x9a36c - a MARKER table (+0x60 =
  0x23b80) with +0x14 = 0x550a0 (the pump step) and
  +0x8c = 0x54910 (the motion getter): a full ACTIVE class,
  not a passive one. Flow: only for record #4 ([obj+0x5c]
  == 4); one-time init 0x28bf0 guarded by [obj+0xf6] (that
  walk touches [obj+0xee]/[obj+0xf2] object links + class

  counted); ctx class +0x3c truth; self +0x68 position;

- FINDING 5, ZARIA.01 GROUNDING - NO PORT GAP. The authored
  ZARIA.01 texts gate rows on exactly these GENERATED
  signals: ZAR_LEW carries AC_ENEMY_ATC/AC_BLOK/AC_RECT/

## PR-179 — LION'S +0xac VERB AND THE MSG HANDLER ARE READ
## AT LAST: THE KEY EXTENSION RAISES THE POOL-QUERY KEYS,
## THE AC_BLOK BOUNDS TEST AND THE ATTACH KEYS AC_DUP (byte
## 0 bit 4) / AC_DUP_CD (byte 1 bit 5); [obj+0xa9] IS THE
## ATTACHED OBJECT AND [obj+0xe6] THE PER-STEP CANDIDATE
## (THE PUMP CLEARS IT); 0x54560 IS THE 87-SITE MSG
## HANDLER WITH ITS FULL ID MAP; AND 0x55070 IS THE +0x54
## PHYSICS HOOK, NOT A +0x8c GETTER (ONE ADDRESS CORRECTED)
## (READING, NO PORT CODE, NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE)

- WHY. PR-178's Next specced this pass - the +0xac body was
  the longest-carried engine item in the ledger (since
  PR-174) and the msg-id arms since PR-175. Method:
  continuous objdump ranges (obj_range.sh; the 0x545x-
  0x548x region is dense with desyncs - stated per site
  below); the elf dword-scan for installs and field sites
  (callscan-style); the PR-88-verified port signal enum
  (ll_play.h LL_SIG_*) to NAME the key bits the verb
  raises (bit N = byte N/8 bit N%8 - the same law as
  PR-155/156/177's raisers). Docs only; nothing shipped
  moves.

- FINDING 1, THE +0xac VERB 0x546a0, BODY READ (the pump's
  key-extension call discipline is PR-176 F4; the +0x78-
  area call sites are PR-177 F1). Entry: eax=obj, edx=ctx
  (the key buffer being extended); prologue sub esp,0x60.
  (a) GATE: test [obj+0xb6] bit 0x2 -> if set, SKIP
  everything except the tail (d). (b) rec = [[obj+
  0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4]; if [rec+0x12] & 0x4000 (the record
  control-flags word again - PR-159/160/177): call 0x4b600
  (mgr 0xcef40, ecx=0, local buffer) -> merge the answer
  into ctx via 0x49580; call 0x4b430 (the bounds test -
  its answer is AC_BLOK per PR-177 F1) -> merge; then
  0x4b7f0 -> merge (0x54746 common). ELSE test [rec+0x12]
  bit 8 (= mode bit 2, mode >= 4 - the SAME word's mode
  field PR-147/178 pinned): if set, the same triple with
  ecx=2 (the 0x4b600 filter arg); if clear, none of them.

  == 0 -> detach path: if [obj+0xa9] != 0, call

  self = the attached, edx = the lion), write [obj+0xa9]
  := 0, call class-table +0xb8. Else if [obj+0xe2] == 2
  AND [obj+0xc6] (the signed v_y) >= 0x58c (1420 raw units
  = 14.2 px/tick-s scaled, a FALLING-PAST gate) -> skip
  the attach; else if [obj+0xa9] == 0: OR BYTE [ctx] |=
  0x10 = KEY BIT 4 = AC_DUP (the port enum, PR-88 law) -
  then attach: [obj+0xa9] := [obj+0xe6] and call
  [[obj+0xe6]+0] (slot 0 = ENTER on the candidate, edx =
  the lion); the [obj+0xa9] != 0 path re-points at the new
  candidate (0x547b6-0x547c6; the 0x54790-0x547b5 window
  is a desync GAP - the re-attach flow is a data-flow
  story, not a CFG proof, counted as an honesty note), and
  after the re-attach, if [obj+0xe2] == 0: OR BYTE
  [ctx+1] |= 0x20 = BIT 13 = AC_DUP_CD. (d) THE TAIL
  (0x54804, reached by ALL paths): x += [obj+0xca]; y +=
  [obj+0xce] + [obj+0xea]; [obj+0xca] := 0; [obj+0xce] :=
  0 - the position commit consumes the SCALED-velocity
  accumulators and the [obj+0xea] step-delta and clears
  them. So the +0xac law is: gate on the mode word and the
  [obj+0xb6] bit, merge the pool-query/bounds keys, run
  the attach state machine raising AC_DUP / AC_DUP_CD on
  candidate transitions, commit motion. THE PORT MATCHES
  ON THE OBSERVED HALF: the AC_DUP-raising overlap model is
  PR-150's ladder-extent model (green on frames), AC_BLOK
  raising is the port's collision model; the candidate/
  attach FIELDS are engine-internal - no port change
  indicated.

## PR-180 — THE FEED-GATE WORD HAS ITS PRODUCER LAW: THE
## +0xcc SLOT IS A SENSOR-WORD CHANNEL FED BY THE CLASS STEP
## DRIVER, AND THE LION'S DRIVER IS READ WHOLE (0x27d60,
## installed at LION-table +0x240: an anchor-delta quadrant
## gate + reciprocal Manhattan ratios, then +0xcc, then the
## pump); THE CANDIDATE [obj+0xe6] IS WIRED BY ADDRESS AT
## LEVEL INIT - ITS STORES ARE NOT STATICALLY VISIBLE
## (READING, NO PORT CODE, NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE)

  (1) (what fills [obj+0xe6] every step). Method: the byte
  callscans (rel-call + ModRM ff /2) for the seven
  [r+0xcc] sites; continuous objdump ranges (obj_range.sh;
  desync windows at 0x27d80-0x27d95 and 0x5455f flagged
  where they touch a claim); decoding the float constants
  from the elf (struct '<d'); the [obj+0xe6] operand-site

- FINDING 1, THE LION'S GATE-WORD DRIVER, WHOLE (closes
  PR-178 item (1)'s core). The [r+0xcc] site 0x27e1d sits
  in a method entered at 0x27d60 - installed at LION table
  0x9a54c's +0x240 (dword-ref scan; the +0xcc slot of all
  15 LION tables is 0x50340, PR-178). Its law, byte-exact:
  (i) dX := [obj+0x126] - x, dY := [obj+0x12a] - y, x/y
  read through the class +0x68 position getter - the
  ANCHOR pair [obj+0x126/0x12a] has a setter helper in
  the same function's head (0x27d40: `add ecx,0x126; mov
  [ecx+4],edx` writes the y-anchor). (ii) QUADRANT GATE:
  compute only if (dX > 0) OR (dY < 0); else the 2-dword
  buffer is ZEROed. (iii) THE WORD: buf0 = round((|dX| +
  |dY|) / (10*|dX|)), buf1 = round((|dX| + |dY|) /
  (10*|dY|)) - fild/fmul qword ds:0x909ef / ds:0x909f7
  (both decode to double 10.0)/fdivrp/fistp under the
  helper 0x75d96. (iv) call [class+0xcc] (0x50340 ->
  0x549f0: window re-decide per PR-178 F4), THEN CALL THE
  PUMP 0x550a0 (0x27e25) - the driver runs the sensor
  word IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the step, exactly the position
  the law needs. So the mode-2/4 gate scalars start as
  RECIPROCAL MANHATTAN RATIOS against an anchor: e.g.
  buf1 = 0 whenever |dX| < 9*|dY| (the integer division
  floors) - the pure-vertical case feeds ZERO until a
  window re-decide (kind-1/4, PR-178 F4) overrides. WHY
  this parametrization matches climb behaviour is NOT
  claimed (counted); the port's intent-proxy (PR-148) is
  neither confirmed nor contradicted by it. HONESTY: the
  dispatch INTO 0x27d60 (slot +0x240) is not statically
  resolvable - no rel-caller, no `call [r+0x240]`, no
  dword-access of +0x240 anywhere in text (byte scans; the
  only +0x240 mentions are `lea` scans at 0x49e89/0x49ec0
  over table ranges, a different config walk) - a computed
  dispatch or an initialization-time call; counted.

## PR-182 — THE 'MSG' SURFACE IS THE EVENT SYSTEM: EVERY
## OBJECT HAS A QUEUE AT +0x10 DRAINED THROUGH ITS CLASS
## SLOT +0x10 BEFORE ITS STEP VERB; THE 0x54560 ID-MAP IS
## ONE CONSUMER IMPLEMENTATION (73/87 INSTALLS AT +0x10);
## THE GENERIC SENDER IS THE NAMED BROADCAST 0x4bc40,
## WHOSE id-16 EVENTS RAISE KEY BITS BY NUMBER INTO
## [obj+0x60] - THE ENGINE'S SIGNAL-RAISING MECHANISM
## (READING, NO PORT CODE, NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE)

- WHY. PR-181's Next specced the msg-sender pass ("who
  puts ids 2/6/13/27 on the wire"). Method: the byte
  scan for stores of the id dwords (a negative: only TWO
  literal id-stores in all of text - 0x53f62 id 2 and an
  unrelated 0x7b5c1), the rel-call scan from the one
  literal builder outward, and the slot histogram of the
  87 consumer installs. events_evidence.py re-runs every
  count. Desync entry traps again at 0x49872/0x52b52
  (push-edx entries), flagged. Docs only; nothing shipped
  moves.

- FINDING 1, THE EVENT ARCHITECTURE (byte-exact, whole):
  every object has a QUEUE HEADER at [obj+0x10]; a node
  is 16 bytes (allocator 0x5c320 with the size in eax at
  0x52b22): node+0 = next, node+4 = ID, node+8 = SENDER
  identity, node+0xc = argument. APPEND: 0x52b10(obj,
  edx=id, ebx=sender, ecx=arg) links it at the queue tail
  - 66 direct call sites, all argument-driven (the scan
  for `mov eax,imm` within 14 bytes: 0 of 66 - ids and
  args always come from the calling function's
  parameters). DRAIN: 0x52b50 walks the queue calling
  `call [class+0x10]`(node) per node (eax=obj) and
  frees via 0x5c370. PUMP POSITION: 0x52b80 = drain,
  then `call [class+0x14]` - the PR-176 step verb (the
  LION's +0x14 = 0x550a0, the pump of PR-179 F3!) - then
  if [obj+0x28] != 0, `call [class+0x00]`; 6 direct
  call sites (0x4aed6, 0x4baed, 0x4bb12, 0x55398,
  0x55696, 0x556af). So the per-step order is EVENTS-
  THEN-VERB: incoming events are consumed by the class
  consumer slot BEFORE the step runs - and the PR-179
  finding that the pump CLEARS the candidate every step
  now has its full frame: events arrive, the consumer and
  the selector re-decide, the verb acts.
  THE CONSUMER SLOT IS +0x10: the 0x54560 install
  histogram over the 178-table windows: {'0x10': 73, 14
  odd singletons - the usual window-overlap artifacts}.
  The LION tables do NOT use 0x54560: their +0x10 =
  0x1e130 (the 0x1e3a0/0x1e570 provider-cluster family -
  a consumer inside the provider code). 0x52bb0 is the
  non-16 fall-through consumer helper (9 call sites
  incl. 0x537dd, 0x55729; handles ids < 0xE and 0x21
  arms - body not read further, counted).

- FINDING 2, THE GENERIC SENDER: THE NAMED BROADCAST
  0x4bc40 (22 direct callers - the provider clusters
  0x1ecx/0x24xxx/0x2fxxx/0x32xxx/0x34xxx/0x3axxx/
  0x3bxxx/0x3c1xx + the camel inits 0x2c5e6/0x2c624/
  0x2c664). Law: walk the level's object list (array
  [[mgr 0xcef40]+0x58] with count [mgr+0x44], chain
  through node +0x34; then a second chain from [mgr+
  0x64]); per object, optional identity FILTER via
  `call [class+0x0c]` (the identity/name getter - 186
  call sites of that slot across text); enqueue via
  0x52b10 a node with ID=0x10, SENDER=the caller's
  identity, ARG=the pushed immediate (0x4bd13 site; the
  second form 0x4bd30 walks only the [obj+0x64] chain
  with slot +0x0c filter and id 0xc). THE id-16
  CONSUMER: 0x53770 (PR-179 F2's 'generic 0x53770') IS
  THIS HANDLER: if node id == 0x10 and node+8 == the
  constant 0x8138764: take the signal NUMBER from node+
  0xc, compute word = N>>5, bit = N&31, OR it into the
  live KEY set at [obj+0x60] (0x537cb-0x537d2 - the SAME
  set the pump merges into, PR-17x/PR-176 F4), then call
  the merge 0x49580 (0x537d4 - PR-176 F4's merge
  helper); else fall through 0x52bb0. So RAISING AN AC_*
  SIGNAL IN THE ENGINE = SET BIT N: the bit numbering is
  identical to the port's PR-88-verified enum, and the
  broadcast's ARGUMENT IS THE SIGNAL NUMBER - the name-
  index = KEY bit number law. THE MAGIC 0x8138764 is the
  SENDER IDENTITY of these raises: it occurs at exactly
  FOUR sites in text (0x2c5e1, 0x2c613, 0x2c653 - the
  three small methods just before the 0x2c670 camel-
  placement method of PR-181 - and 0x3eacf inside a
  provider cluster). THE THREE CAMEL SITES ARE AUTHORED
  SEMANTICS: 0x2c5e0-ish raises ARG 0x1c (= 28 =
  AC_BECZKA, the barrel signal) guarded by [rec index 1]+
  4 == 1; 0x2c630 raises 0x1b (= 27 = AC_BUTLA, the
  bottle signal) guarded by [obj+0x5c]==1 AND [rec+4]==
  0xa; [CORRECTED BY PR-183 F3 (byte-exact): the site-
  to-bit map is 0x2c5b0 (magic 0x2c5e1) pushes 0x21 =
  33 = AC_KOREK (guard [obj+0x5c]==2 + ONE-SHOT flag
  ds:0xcec70), 0x2c5f0 (0x2c613) pushes 0x1c =
  AC_BECZKA ([[obj+0x50]+4]+4 == 1), 0x2c630 (0x2c653)
  pushes 0x1b = AC_BUTLA ([[obj+0x50]+16]+4 == 0xa);
  and the broadcast is TOKEN-FILTERED (ecx = the target
  family's runtime token, PR-183 F3).] i.e. the camel-
  family classes RAISE the bottle/
  barrel interaction signals when their record hits those
  arms - and those ARE the signals the authored ZAR_LEW
  states listen for (PR-15x read A_WSP(3)=AC_DRAB_CATCH,
  AC_ONAIR style lists; AC_BUTLA/AC_BECZKA are in the
  port's key model - ll_play.c raises them per PR-88/
  PR-9x). 0x3eacf raises 0x39 = 57 = K_GEN4 (the K_*
  general-signal family, PR-17x's bit 54 = K_GEN1) -
  that provider's intent counted. THE MSG-SENDER QUESTION
  IS ANSWERED AT THE
  ARCHITECTURE LEVEL: senders = 66 enqueue sites + the
  0x4bc40 broadcast (id-16 named raises); consumers =
  class slot +0x10 per family; the id 2/6/13/27 map is
  ONE consumer implementation used by non-LION classes
  (73 installs). Whether the port needs anything from
  this: the port's signal model already raises the same
  numbered bits (PR-88 law) and its per-step order
  (read state -> collide -> move) matches events-before-
  verb; no shipped behaviour is contradicted - no port
  change.

- FINDING 3, THE LITERAL id-2 BUILDER 0x53f50 (the only
  literal msg-id store): builds an id-2 'msg' at an
  external buffer ([+0]=0, [+4]=2, [+8]=payload ecx),
  copies a 13-byte block from [edx+0xc] (a node-shaped
  trailer), then 0x53fb0 tests bit 2 in [x+4] and [msg+
  4] and on a match calls 0x5c370 - which is NOT a msg
  delivery: it is the queue/list REMOVAL on the global
  registry ds:0xcf2c8/0xcf2cc/0xcf2d0 (pop last, walk
  the +0x8/+0x0 chain, unlink) - so 0x53f50 (one caller,
  0x3d66d in a provider cluster) + 0x53fb0 = a
  node-append/remove dance around a provider; full
  reading counted.
