- FINDING 3, THE IDENTITY LAW AND THE CORRECTED RAISES.
  ALL 178 marker class tables implement +0x0c as the ONE
  instruction `mov eax, ds:<tok>; ret` (178/178!) - the
  identity getter returns a per-family GLOBAL TOKEN; the
  top tokens: ds:0xceec8 x30, 0xcee78 x11, 0xcf050/54 x11
  each, 0xcee64 x7... (census). Tokens are INITIALIZED at
  level setup in runs of `call 0x44350; mov ds:<tok>,eax`
  pairs (7 pairs in the 0x1dfc0-0x1e006 window alone,
  0x3d119-0x3d137 a second run); 0x44350 (bytes, 17 B) =
  `return ds:0xa90ac++` - a FRESH-TOKEN COUNTER. So the
  magic 0x8138764 IS NOT A HARD-CODED IDENTITY - it is a
  RUNTIME TOKEN VALUE (a counter value the level-init
  stored into one family's token global); what the 4
  magic-sites hard-code is an ASSUMPTION that the counter
  reaches 0x8138764 for the target family (its meaning
  counted: which family owns that token needs the init
  order - traced runs are 0x1dfcf/0x3d119 and others,
  full order counted). [CORRECTED BY PR-184 F2: NOT a
  runtime token - the 135 init pairs start from a counter
  with STATIC VALUE 1 (ds:0xa90ac), so tokens are small
  ints 2..136, and 0x8138764 appears NOWHERE as data - it
  is the CONSTANT NAMED-RAISE STAMP; the owner-family
  question dissolves.] THE 0x4bc40 CONTRACT IS NOW EXACT:
  the caller passes ebx = ID, ecx = TARGET TOKEN (the
  filter compares each walked object's `call [class+
  0x0c]()` against it - 0x4bd02-0x4bd07), pushed arg =
  ARG; the enqueued node gets +4=ID, +8=the CALLER's
  identity (edx), +0xc=ARG. [CORRECTED BY PR-184 F2 by
  the bytes (0x4bc46-0x4bc50): the FILTER argument is
  EDX (0 = NO filter; senders pass token globals, e.g.
  0x1ec46 loads ds:0xcebd4), EBX = ID, ECX = STAMP (goes
  to node+8 via ebp), push = ARG.] THE THREE CAMEL RAISES ARE
  NOW CORRECTED (bracket): 0x2c5b0 (magic 0x2c5e1)
  pushes 0x21 = 33 = AC_KOREK (guard: [obj+0x5c] == 2
  AND a ONE-SHOT flag ds:0xcec70 = 0, set to 1 first -

  28 = AC_BECZKA (guard [obj+0x5c] == 1 AND record
  [[obj+0x50]+1*4]+4 == 1); 0x2c630 (0x2c653) pushes
  0x1b = 27 = AC_BUTLA (guard: call 0x54860, [obj+0x5c]
  == 1 AND record [[obj+0x50]+4*4]+4 == 0xa) - CORK,
  BARREL, BOTTLE: the exact authored props of the camel
  scenes ([obj+0x5c] = the PR-17x camel MODE field; [rec
  +4] = a record kind field, counted). 0x53770's gate
  `cmp [node+8], 0x8138764` then RAISES bit node+0xc
  only for objects of the target family = the NAMED-RAISE
  DISPATCH IS TOKEN-FILTERED BROADCAST. [CORRECTED BY PR-
  184 F2: the camel trio pass edx=0 -> NO filter - the
  raise reaches EVERY object in both chains, and the magic

  family message); consistent with the PR-15x per-object

  port raises the same numbered bits (PR-88 law) directly

  counter) has static value 1 IN THE IMAGE and no other

  nowhere as data (the only occurrences remain the 4 code
  immediates) - PR-183 F3's 'the magic is a runtime token,
  owner family open' is CORRECTED: 0x8138764 is a
  CONSTANT PROTOCOL STAMP. The 0x4bc40 contract, corrected
  against the bytes (0x4bc46-0x4bc50): the caller's EDX ->
  [esp+0x14] = the IDENTITY FILTER (0 = NO FILTER, the
  walk passes every object; non-zero = compared against
  `call [class+0x0c]()` at 0x4bd02-0x4bd07 - senders load
  token globals, e.g. 0x1ec46 loads ds:0xcebd4), the
  caller's EBX = ID, the caller's ECX = STAMP (becomes
  node+8 via ebp), stack push = ARG. So the camel trio
  (edx=0!) broadcast UNFILTERED to every object in both
  chains, and 0x53770's `cmp [node+8], 0x8138764` gate is
  a STAMP DISCRIMINATOR (system-named-raise vs targeted
  family messages) - NOT a family filter. PR-183 F3's
  'raises only for objects of the target family' is
  CORRECTED: the named raises reach ALL objects (every
  object ORs the bit into its own live set - consistent
  with the per-object signal listening of PR-15x reads).

- FINDING 1, THE 15TH CONTROLLER CLASS IS THE KADMAR-STAGE
  LION (PR-186 item (7) CLOSED; PR-176 item (1) PART-
  CLOSED - TLewKadmar1 WAS THE UNRESOLVED ONE). Table
  0x9a54c/0x9a544 (pair stores at 0x2703e/0x27045) has
  the full controller shape: +0x14 = 0x550a0 (the standard
  message pump), +0x90 = 0x27170 signal verb, +0xcc = the
  SAME input wrapper 0x50340 as the fourteen, +0x0 = a
  create-dispatcher 0x27420 (`test cl,0x4`: bit clear ->
  stores [obj+0x8/0xc] := 0x9a54c/0x9a544, edx := 1, call
  0x50180 (the 0x50162-sibling gate site), bit2 of cl ->
  0x5c370; bit set -> edx := 0x99500 (a sibling class,
  its +0x8c is the PR-184-wrapped 0x3dcb0), 0x74bc0/
  0x74be0); the push-string block at the dispatcher holds
  'Blad przy rzucie patrz zrodla kad-1/2/3' (Kadmar throw
  source error strings). Its fresh-object factory 0x27030
  has EXACTLY ONE caller, 0x29b1d, inside the gate 0x29b00
  = the second compare form PR-176 suspected: `mov edx,
  0x90aae` ('TLewKadmar1') `call 0x76a69` (match) THEN
  `mov eax,0x12c; call 0x5c320` (record-type presence in
  the 0xa92d4 registry - the PR-176/186 law re-confirmed:
  0x5c320 = registry probe) THEN create; 0x27030 itself
  calls the PR-1xx allocator 0x500b0, sets WORD [obj+
  0x12a] := 0, the class pair, and [obj+0xf6] := 1500
  (0x5dc - the 0x45200 record-array count authored per-
  stage exactly like TLewZariaB's 10000). Immediately
  BEFORE the factory in the same code block, 0x26ff4
  loads 'kadmdead.mod' through the 0xcf068 module loader
  0x562e0 and then sets [[0xcef40]+0x394]+0x106 := 1 -
  the tracked player's input RE-ARM (the PR-104/106 law).
  So 0x9a54c IS TLewKadmar1's controller class, created
  as a SEPARATE object when the 0x12c record (the death-
  module registration) is present; the death-double model
  in PR-176 F3 pairs .mod names with classes but the
  Kadmar case shows the create-a-new-object form - and
  the OTHER class-switch mechanism is the reclass site
  0x2bfc2: it rewrites an EXISTING object in place -
  [obj+0x12a] := -1, [obj+0x12e] := 1, [obj+0x8/0xc] :=
  0x9b4d4/0x9b4cc (the TLewKadmar2 pair, PR-176 F3). THE
  GETTER IS THE ONLY DECORATED ONE: 0x27280 = `call
  0x504e0` (the standard ten-leg chain) then, IF
  [obj+0xee] >= 3, `[obj+0xee] := movsx(WORD [obj+
  0x12a]) + 2` - the PR-186 flag word DOUBLES AS THE KEY
  ORDINAL when the chain reaches >= 3: [obj+0x12a] >= 8
  makes [obj+0xee] >= 10, so this is the second writer
  that can reach the K_F11/K_F12 jump-table cases (PR-176
  item (2) EXTENDED; the PR-185 F3 wrapper 0x613d0 stays
  the first); the getter also CLEARS key byte bit 0x10
  always and SETS it when [obj+0xee] == 6 (the 12-byte
  result copy follows). Field-width nuance: 0x27030 writes
  [obj+0x12a] as a WORD, 0x2bfc2/0x2419d as dwords - the
  flag field is dword-sized read as a word here (counted
  semantics question). INPUT-GATE RULE CONFIRMED GENERAL:
  the 0x50340 wrapper's [obj+0x106] zero-gate and mode-5
  negate are the SAME code for this fifteenth class - the
  gate is not ZARIA-specific. PORT NOTE: KADMAR is not
  ZARIA.01; no port change; the flag/ordinal doubling is
  engine-side bookkeeping the port does not emulate.

- FINDING 2, THE [obj+0xc] PAIR-STORE IS AN ALIAS, NOT A
  HEADER (PR-186 item (9) CLOSED AS A NON-LAW; PR-186 F1
  CORRECTED). For every class sampled (0x96960, 0x97970,
  0x9a54c, 0x9b4d4, 0x988ec, 0x9d338) the dwords at
  base-8/base-4 are ordinary method pointers of THAT SAME
  class (e.g. 0x96960-8 = 0x20480/0x20440, its own slot
  neighbours; 0x9a54c-8 = 0x2b0b0/0x2b0a0), and the class
  marker 0x23b80 sits at base+0x60 in all of them - there
  is NO header structure before the table. The universal
  factory pattern [obj+0x8] := T, [obj+0xc] := T-8 stores
  two pointers 8 bytes apart INTO ONE flat array: the
  second handle just shifts the slot window by -8 (slots
  at [obj+0xc+0x14] = T+0xc). AND NOTHING DISPATCHES
  THROUGH IT: a modrm scan (mod=01 disp8 and mod=02
  disp32 forms) found ZERO sites where a loaded [obj+0xc]
  value is used for a call-through; every apparent hit
  (0x1e3d0, 0x1ee5a, 0x1efac, 0x3e9e6, 0x52bd0) is a
  3-dword object-field copy block (`mov eax,[edx+4/8/c]`)
  whose following `call [edx+X]` hits the SHARED CAMEL-
  family method tables (the edx := 0x98274 pattern, PR-176
  F4) - the [reg+0xc] field there is an object's third
  coordinate/velocity dword, a multi-role trap. So the
  pair is an addressing alias; WHY the runtime keeps the
  second handle is unobserved (counted item (4)). CORREC-
  TION (1 bracket): PR-186 F1 said the flag block is
  'SHARED ACROSS THE LIFE/DEATH CLASS PAIR of one object'
  because 0x988ec's id-29 arm calls 0x32130 (0x9d338's
  handler). PR-187 F1/F2 show 0x988ec (looser.mod, ZARIA
  death registration) and 0x9d338 (ran1.mod, RAN death
  registration) differ in 20 slots and sit in different
  provider clusters (0x241xx vs 0x31fxx) - SAME-ROLE
  CLASSES OF DIFFERENT STAGES, not one object's life/
  death pair. Flags are PER-OBJECT; cross-class flag
  behaviour happens (a) through SHARED HANDLER CODE
  (0x24170 calling 0x32130 as a helper - 0x2bff0/0x270d0
  and 0x988ec/0x9d338 pairings show the same helper-
  sharing pattern across stage families) and (b) through
  RECLASS SITES like 0x2bfc2 that rewrite [obj+0x8/0xc]
  in place - the death-latch reading survives ONLY for
  such switched objects.

- FINDING 3, THE HARDWARE BOTTOM IS RAW PORT I/O (PR-186
  item (4) CLOSED TO THE HW LEVEL; PR-106 item (1)
  ANSWERED IN KIND). Boot: 0x4d769 `mov eax,0xcf400;
  call 0x58560`; 0x58560 = 0x582d0 THEN 0x58130(dev+0x33)
  (exactly those two calls, no other callers anywhere).
  0x582d0 = the KEYBOARD LAYER 0xcde70 init: flush loop
  `while 0x1c4d0(0xcde70) != 0` (0x1c4d0 compares scan-
  code queues ds:0x96364/0x96368 through the xlat table
  ds:0x9636c), then 0x1c490 = memset(0xcde70+0xa, 0,
  0x80 dwords) + memset(+0x20a) + zero(+0x40a) - A 128-
  entry KEY-STATE TABLE with translation, the classic PC
  BIOS-style scancode layer. 0x58130 = JOYSTICK PRESENCE:
  two timed probes via 0x1ded4 with axis masks {1,2} then
  {4,8}, `cmp [esp],0x3fff` timeout test -> [sub+0x14]/
  [sub+0x18] = 2-/4-axis flags, [sub+0x10] = present. THE
  PORT READERS: 0x1ded4 = `push ebp; mov ebp,esp; in
  eax,0x50` (8253 counter 0 as the clock), push regs,
  `mov dx,0x201` (PPI 8255 port), init both outputs to
  0x3fff, `out dx,al` (fire the one-shots), `cli`, loop
  `in al,dx` waiting for each masked axis bit (masks from
  [ebp+0x10]/[ebp+0x14]) counting ticks up to 0x3fff,
  `sti` - THE CLASSIC PC GAME-PORT AXIS TIMING (capacitor
  recharge counted against PIT counter 0); 0x1df34 =
  `push edx; mov dx,0x201; in al,dx; pop edx; ret` =
  the BUTTON/level byte read. This is RAW x86 port I/O -
  a capture from HARDWARE, not a recording system. WHO
  FILLS THE SAMPLE RINGS: the device-manager open/enumer-
  ate body (0x585e2 gated [[dev]+0xb]==1, running to
  ~0x5878d): per driver it calls the record ctor 0x582f0
  - zeroes [drv+0/4/8] (THE EXACT TRIPLET 0x58690 later
  copies), then probes device presence `call 0x1c550(
  0xcde70, code)` for codes 0x13b, 0x202..0x2xx and sets
  bits [drv+0x8/0x9] - the 0xcde70 registry knows which
  devices exist; then 0x58010(dev+0x33) opens the joystick
  sub-record, and 0x57fe0 DEDUPLICATES the block against
  the LAST record: match -> `inc [rec+0xc]` (0x5872b -
  THE RUN LENGTH the playback walk takes mod); diffe-
  rence -> growth when full (0x225a0) + a 16-byte append
  at count+1 (`add edi,edx; mov [esi+8],idx+1; 4x movs`
  at 0x58778-0x5877b). [CORRECTED BY PR-188 F1: EVERY
  site quoted in this paragraph - 0x582f0/0x58010/
  0x57fe0/0x5872b/0x58778 - sits in 0x58690's legs (its
  prologue is at 0x58690); 0x585e2 is the separate
  enumerate entry and does NOT run to ~0x5878d; the
  'per-driver sample ring' is the record ARRAY at
  dev+0xf, not [[drv]+0]; and the real chain is PORT ->
  0x58690's state!=2 leg (0x58010 fills the block) ->
  the state==1 leg records it -> state==2 replays.] So
  the chain is: PORT
  I/O (0x1ded4/0x1df34) -> 0x580xx/0x581xx sample methods
  -> 0x57fe0 pull -> per-driver sample ring -> 0x58690
  frame read -> [esp+0x1f0]/[esp+0x1e4] -> the +0xcc
  INPUT-APPLY chain. REMAINDER (counted): NOTHING in the
  whole image references 0x585e2 or the other device
  methods as data (aligned-dword scan: zero; 0x58580's
  only hit 0xa2bc0 is unaligned raw bytes) and 0x585e2
  has zero relative callers - the open/poll entry is
  computed-dispatch or externally entered; who sets the
  [dev+0xb] state transitions (0->1->2) is the item.
  PORT VERDICT UNCHANGED: the port's SDL-keyboard ->
  ll_play_keys channel lands at the same key-bit layer;
  the engine reads JOYSTICK axes as analogue timings and
  BUTTONS from port 0x201 plus the scancode table -
  HANDOFF input-model note now says 'hardware capture'
  explicitly. The third sample dword naming (PR-186 item
  (8)) stays (axis-timing words vs buttons, mapping
  untraced).

## walk [dev+0x2b]/[dev+0x2f] mod [rec+0xc]); THE DEMO-
## START LAW: level start 0x4d890 builds a demo-record
## NAME ('%s\%s' + '%d' + 0x4a910), opens it through the

## (0x57a00 x3, edx=1) and sets [level+0x3ac] := 1, which

- FINDING 1, THE INPUT STATE MACHINE: CAPTURE, RECORD,
  PLAYBACK (PR-106 item (1) CLOSED; PR-187 F3 ATTRIBUTION
  CORRECTED). The frame call `mov eax,0xcf400; call
  0x58690` is a THREE-LEG state machine on [dev+0xb]
  (0x5869c loads the state, 0x586a2 `cmp edx,2`):
  (a) state != 2 (0x586e4): zero the block's flag dword
  (`mov [ebx+8],0`), call 0x582f0(dev,block) - the PR-
  187-F3 zero + 0x1c550 presence-probe chain - then
  `lea eax,[dev+0x33]; call 0x58010`: THE LIVE PORT READ
  (0x58010 body): with calibration words [sub+0x10]/
  [sub+0x14] nonzero it calls 0x1df34 (buttons: bits
  0x10/0x20 -> OR [block+8],0x1/0x20; second form
  [sub+0x18]: bits 0x40/0x80) and 0x1ded4 (axis one-
  shot timings), then converts: raw < [sub+0x00] ->
  [block] := -0x14, raw > [sub+0x04] -> +0x14 (y the
  same on [sub+0x08]/[sub+0x0c]) - THE +/-20 STEP MODEL
  (PR-145 F1's 'the input path's constant is 20' re-
  confirmed at the producer). (b) state == 1 (the leg
  continues, 0x586fc `cmp [ecx+0xb],1`): RECORDING.
  0x57fe0(dev-block, last-record) DEDUPLICATES: on a
  match, `inc [rec+0xc]` (0x5872b) - INPUT RECORDS ARE
  RUN-LENGTH COMPRESSED, [rec+0xc] is the repeat count,
  NOT a stride as PR-106 guessed; on a difference it
  appends: 16-byte temp {dx,dy,flags,run=1}, capacity
  check [count]==[cap] -> 0x225a0 growth, then
  `[esi+8]=count+1` + 4x movs at 0x58778-0x5877b. The
  record array struct is at dev+0xf: {[0]=ptr, [8]=count,
  0xc=cap}. (c) state == 2 (0x586a7): DEMO PLAYBACK -
  12 bytes copied from record[[dev+0x2b]] (3x movs),
  then [dev+0x2f] walks +1, wrapping against the CURRENT
  record's [rec+0xc] run-length, advancing [dev+0x2b]:
  THE PLAYBACK UNCOMPRESSES THE RLE. (d) tail 0x5877c
  (Finding 3). DEMO AUTHORING/START: level start 0x4d890
  (guard ds:0xcf074 zero): 0x4a910 builds the demo-record
  NAME with format strings 0x91f19 '\\', 0x91f1c '%s',
  0x91f27 '%d' (stage-dir + sub-name + index); 0x57a70
  resolves the record; 0x56250 = `add eax,0x2c; call
  0x57990` (register into the 0xcf068 subsystem table) +
  0x56150 + 0x55e00(open); then 0x57a00(x,1) x3 probes
  the three sub-records and 0x4d8fd sets [level+0x3ac]
  := 1. THE FRAME LOOP PUMPS IT: 0x4ae6e `call 0x4a9f0`
  -> 0x4aa07 `call 0x56360(edx=10)` + 0x4aa11 `call
  0x561a0` then zeroes [level+0x3ac] (0x4aa16); 0x561a0
  iterates the registry entries at [[0xcf068]+0x48]
  [CORRECTED BY PR-189 F2: the 0x561a0 pump vector is
  {ptr @ [[0xcf068]+0x44], count @ +0x4c} - the count
  slot is +0x4c, NOT +0x48; the entry walk and the
  `[[entry.vt]+0x0](edx=2)` handler call stand as
  stated.] and calls [entry.vt+0x0] with edx=2. So
  PR-106's 'input-
  record playback' IS the game's DEMO SYSTEM, end to end.
  CORRECTION (3 brackets, PR-186 F3 / PR-187 F3 / PR-187
  F4): the capture/record sequence 0x582f0 -> 0x58010 ->
  0x57fe0 runs in 0x58690's legs, NOT in 0x585e2; 0x585e2

  0x49b20 list-builder over the driver array + driver

  [dev+0xb] WRITE CENSUS (settled): a full modrm scan of

- FINDING 3, THE QUERY-CODE TAIL: KEY-STATE PROBE + A
  DEAD LEG (PR-187 item (6) HALF-CLOSED). 0x58690's tail

  IS `xor eax,eax; ret` (3 bytes): THE 0x808 LEG IS DEAD
  CODE in the engine itself. Then `mov edx,9; mov eax,
  0xcde70; call 0x1c530` -> TEST -> `or BYTE [block+8],8`
  (0x587a0). 0x1c530 body: `test dh,0x2` (release bit of
  the code arg) -> remap via table [edx*4+0xce284] ->
  `and edx,0x7f` -> `mov eax,[eax+edx*4+0xa]`: CODE 9 =
  RAW KEY-DOWN QUERY over the 0xcde70+0xa 128-entry KEY-
  STATE TABLE (the PR-187 F3 memset'd table - format now
  pinned: one DWORD per scancode, break-bit stripped via
  the 0xce284 remap). So [block+8] bit 8 = 'any key
  down' at frame end; the 0x1c550 device-code map and
  xlat 0x9636c stay (item (8)).

- FINDING 6, THE +0x100 VERB IS PAIR/CONTACT/CARRY (NEW

- FINDING 1, THE LEVEL LOOP IS ONE FUNCTION AND ITS EXIT
  CODES ARE THE CONTRACT (PR-147 item (2) CLOSED). The
  'loop entry 0x4ae53' is an ARM, not a function: the whole
  region 0x4abd0-0x4ae81 is ONE function (prologue 0x4abd0
  'push ebx ecx edx esi edi ebp; sub esp,0x22c', ecx :=
  manager; ret at 0x4ae81). Prologue: zeroes the 12-byte
  input block at [esp+0x1f0..0x1fb], calls [[mgr+0x394].vt+
  0x54] (player init), [[player.vt]+0xec]/[+0xe8], then
  0x576e0(camera,[player vt+0xe8 result],[+0xec] result) =
  THE CAMERA FOLLOW (Finding 3). LOOP HEAD 0x4ac3b: (a) if
  [[player.vt]+0x116] != 0 -> ebx := 3 jump to exit; (b) if
  [mgr+0x4] != 0 -> ebx := 1; (c) 0x58690(ds:0xcf400, the
  block at [esp+0x1f0]) SAMPLES INPUT EVERY ITERATION;
  (d) 0x4ac76 frame gate: [mgr+0x3a0] != 0 jumps to
  0x4ae82; [0x3b0] one-shot consumed (0x4a8f0, [[x.vt]+8],
  := 0, then 0x4a8c0); (e) THREE HOTKEY LEGS test the
  sampled block bytes: [esp+0x1f9] bit 0x20 -> clear + a
  loop of 0x4a8f0 / 0x5e030 / 0x4a910 / 0x60930 / 0x57a00
  x2 / 0x603b0 / 0x60960 / 0x4a8c0 (re-loops while the
  stream API returns nonzero); [esp+0x1f8] bit 0x04 ->
  0x5e100 / 0x609c0 / 0x57a00 x2 / 0x603b0 / 0x60820;
  [esp+0x1f8] bit 0x08 -> 0x5e0c0 + the same stream family
  and THEN the full end-of-frame leg. These are the game's
  file/stream hotkeys (save/load-style; exact semantics
  counted). END-OF-FRAME 0x4ae82 (a LABEL inside the
  function - the frame gate and the bit-0x08 leg both jump
  to it): ds:0xa94f0 == 0 -> ebx := 2 (0x4ae8b) jump to
  exit; else the input-push chain (PR-189 F4 unchanged:
  0x4ab50 12-byte COPY of the block to [esp+0x1e4],
  0x222d0, 0x4b970, 0x4ba90, [[player.vt]+0xcc](edx = the
  copied block), 0x52b80, 0x4ab80 (its [mgr+0x3a8] == 0
  gate -> [player vt+0xec]/[+0xe8] + 0x57600 = APPLY THE
  CAMERA SCROLL)); then 0x563d0(0xcf068) = the per-frame
  registry SERVICE (walks ds:0xcf064 + the [table+0x24]
  count), 0x4af10 = the plan-script step (Finding 3),
  0x4b0e0 = 0x4a120(0xcef30) + 0x1cfe5, `inc ds:0xcef3c`
  THE FRAME COUNTER, then jmp 0x4ac3b. EXIT TAIL 0x4ae53
  (all four exits): 0x1cfd0 + 0x1dba0 + 0x1cfe5 (stop
  input devices), 0x4a160(0xcef30, mgr), 0x4a9f0 = THE
  DEMO PUMP runs once at level END (its caller census is
  now EXACTLY 2: 0x4a857 level-start (PR-188 F1) + this
  0x4ae6e), eax := ebx, epilogue, ret. THE CALLER (0x5d251,
  sole E8 ref): the level-runner block registers a registry
  entry ('%s\%s'-style name at 0x9262e/0x9262f + the
  0x96200/0x961fc descriptor via 0x57990 + 0x4a4c0 +
  0x57a00(1) + [[x].vt+0x28]), calls the loop, then
  STORES THE RESULT: [ebp-0xc] := the exit CODE (1/2/3/4)
  and [ebp-0x8] := [mgr+0x4] = THE EXIT WORD - then
  0x5b8f0(0xcf1a8), 0x55d20(0xcf068) close, 0x1cc10/
  0x56380 registry-result, the manager teardown
  [[[mgr]+0x3e6].vt+0x4](edx=2), ds:0xcef40 := 0 and
  0x1c490 (the key-state layer reset). So: THE FRAME LOOP
  RETURNS WHY THE LEVEL ENDED (3 = the player's +0x116 flag
  set, 1 = the [mgr+0x4] quit request, 2 = the stage index
  ds:0xa94f0 zeroed, 4 = the hotkey path finished) AND THE
  WORLD LEAVES AN EXIT WORD IN [mgr+0x4] - both flow into
  the caller's result record. Frame helpers: 0x4a8f0 =
  MESSAGE-END (0x74be0([obj]) then [obj] := 0) - called at
  every hotkey leg + the one-shot leg; 0x4a8c0 = 0x4a8f0 +
  [[ds:0xcef14 first entry].vt+0x28] + 0x76a64 with
  comparator fn 0x2f9b8 (test [x+0xf2]==1, state 3,
  [[x].vt+0x70] cmp) -> result stored at [edx] = the end-
  of-frame LIST REFRESH; 0x4a910 = STREAM-OPENER: opens the
  record stream at [obj+0x28] with the DEFAULT descriptor
  pair {0x96200, 0x961fc} via 0x5c680. ds:0xcef3c = the
  frame counter (9th global read in this ledger family).

- FINDING 2, THE PLAN INTERPRETER REPLAYS THE WHOLE SCRIPT
  EVERY CALL (PR-190 CORRECTED), AND THE 'A' LEG IS INDEXED
  (PR-189/190's 'spawn request' REFRAMED). 0x4af10 end-to-end:
  the cursor `ebp := [[mgr+0x30]]` is read ONCE, then every
  arm ends with `cmp BYTE [ebp],0; jne 0x4b076` - the loop
  walks the WHOLE script to its NUL per call, and the cursor
  is NEVER written back: WHOLE-IMAGE CENSUS finds ZERO stores
  to [reg+0x30] in every disp form (mod-10 and mod-01 and the
  two lea forms; only 0x5f119 = an unrelated stream ctor's own
  `lea ecx,[eax+0x30]` + [obj+0x38]=0x98278). THE PLAN IS
  THEREFORE A PER-FRAME SCRIPT EXECUTED TOP TO BOTTOM EVERY
  FRAME (its handlers must be idempotent; per-object state
  machines carry the progress). Dispatch: `mov al,[ebp]` ->
  0x76e98 = THE CANONICAL TOUPPER (cmp 0x61/0x7a, sub 0x20),
  so the alphabet 'A','B','L','T' matches EITHER CASE (the
  PR-190 heading's 'ONLY' needs that note). 'A'-arm 0x4afb1:
  gate [mgr+0x3a0]==0, k := the [esp+0x8] local (0 at each
  call's start, +1 per 'A'), call 0x4b360(mgr, k). THE
  0x4b360 BODY READ: loop the THREE vector headers ecx=mgr,
  mgr+4, mgr+8; if k < [ecx+0x44] (a COUNT) take
  obj = [[ecx+0x58] + k*4] (an ARRAY), walk the [node+0x34]
  chain, per node call [[node.vt]+0x60] and where it returns
  non-zero call [[node.vt]+0x74]. So the k-th 'A' in the
  script = TICK THE k-th AUTHORED OBJECT (the three vectors
  = the level's authored-object groups, the same lists
  0x4b0f0 tests membership in) - NOT a spawn: 0x4b360 has no
  allocation and no list insert; its +0x60/+0x74 verbs are
  exactly the 'L'-leg verbs. 0x4b2f0 (the 'L' leg) = the
  same tick over the [mgr+0x64] entity chain. The 'B' arm
  0x4b008 reads [esp+0x4] = &[mgr+0x3ce] (set at 0x4af36):
  if [[mgr+0x3ce]+8] != 0: target := 0x4a170() =
  `ds:0xcef2c + ds:0xcf0e8 + 0x190` (the grid row bases +
  0x190 = the CENTER-CELL getter), then 0x49bd0(eax =
  [mgr+0x3b4], edx = [[mgr+0x3ce]], ecx = target) - a
  8-byte-stride WORD-record reader: it reads WORD ds:0xcef1a,
  calls [[obj+6] vptr verb +0x74] (0x749a0, args 0xfa00/0xff)
  and copies records into the GLOBALS ds:0xcef18/0xcef1c (the
  same plan-argument globals the object verbs read); the
  guard [mgr+0x3d6] & 0xffff gates the leg. Else 0x448c0
  ([mgr+0x38c]): after 0x44660 it branches on [obj+0x50/54/
  58] into 0x44710/0x447a0/0x44810 = the 0x44xxx plan-data
  class's step legs. AUTHORSHIP: [mgr+0x3b4] is built at
  LEVEL LOAD 0x4d56f-0x4d587 (0x49e40 ctor; its file opened
  at 0x4d58c via 0x4a910 from the level-load name block) and
  [mgr+0x38c] at 0x4d620-0x4d638 (a 0x44xxx-class object via

  pinned: 0x5d233, the first instruction of PR-190's
  level-runner block, immediately before the loop call

## PR-193 — THE STAGE-DRIVER LAYER AND THE EXIT-CODE CONTRACT ARE
## READ END TO END: 13 PER-STAGE WRAPPERS AROUND ONE DRIVER 0x5d170,
## THE ONLY CALL SITE OF THE LEVEL LOOP, AND A QUEUE RUNNER THAT OPENS
## status.leo (RECORD; THREE INHERITED LABELS RETRACTED, WITH THE
## BYTE PROOF)

- WHY. PR-192's Next named the .IS/ANIMACJE formats and the 'levels'
  chain. The reading went a different way once the stage-name strings
  were followed, and the result is the layer ABOVE the level loop -
  who starts a stage, who ends it, and what the exit code means - so
  that is what this record ships. Everything below was measured on THIS
  machine after /tmp/opencode was swept: `tools/re/make_text_asm.sh`
  over `build/leo/leo.elf` (text.bin: VA = file offset + 0x10000)
  is the ONLY disassembler used here, and the fixture side is the repo's own
  `LL.iso` re-staged per the recipe in NEXT_STEPS ("Workspace note").
  The check script is /tmp/opencode/pr193/pr193_facts.py (out:
  pr193_facts.out); every FACT line below is reproducible with it.

- FINDING 1, THE 13 PER-STAGE WRAPPERS AND THE STAGE LIST. `call
  0x5d170` has EXACTLY 14 sites: 0x5d3b0, 0x5d420, 0x5d490, 0x5d500,
  0x5d570, 0x5d5e0, 0x5d650, 0x5d6c0, 0x5d730, 0x5d7a0, 0x5d891,
  0x5d8c9, 0x5d940 and 0x5eb11. The first thirteen are one-per-stage
  wrappers of the same shape (`mov esi,eax` = the stage object,
  `mov ebx,<name>`, `mov edx,esp` = the result pair on the stack,
  `call 0x5d170`), and the name immediates spell, in this order,
  zaria1, zaria2, ena1, ena2, lona, sades, kadmar1, kadmar2, ran,
  kara, junction (0x92631..0x9269b block; the walk-back scan
  recovered 11 of the 13 loads verbatim, the tunga1/tunga2 pair is
  the same block - counted as a scan gap, not as a different list).
  THE 14TH CALLER IS NOT A STAGE: 0x5eb08-0x5eb11 is
  `mov edx,0x9; mov eax,ecx; mov DWORD PTR ds:0xa94f0,edx;
  mov edx,esp; call 0x5d170` - it sets the PR-188 bounded stage index
  to 9 and passes no name. So THE ENGINE'S OWN STAGE ORDER IS
  ZARIA1, ZARIA2, ENA1, ENA2, LONA, SADES, KADMAR1, KADMAR2, RAN,
  KARA, JUNCTION, TUNGA1, TUNGA2 = 13 stages, ZARIA.01 first -
  the port roadmap, straight from the bytes, and the first time the
  engine's stage list is written down.

- FINDING 2, THE DRIVER 0x5d170 (the whole level-start/level-run
  sequence, one function): prologue 0x5d170-0x5d18b; the 0xcf1a8 and
  0xcf068 object reset/save legs (0x5b860, 0x5b9e0, 0x5cdd0, 0x1cc10,
  0x56380, 0x55cf0); the by-name lookup leg 0x5d1f0-0x5d245
  (`mov eax,0x3ea; call 0x5c320` then `call 0x57990` = PR-188's
  named-entry ctor, with edx = the STAGE NAME from the wrapper, then
  `mov ebx,0x961fc` + `call 0x4a4c0` = the by-name finder, then
  `call 0x57a00` release); then 0x5d245-0x5d249
  `mov eax,[edi]; mov edx,[eax]; call DWORD PTR [edx+0x28]` = the
  stage object's CLASS-TABLE verb +0x28; then 0x5d24c-0x5d251
  `mov eax,ds:0xcef40` + `call 0x4abd0` - THE ONLY CALL SITE OF THE
  LEVEL LOOP IN THE WHOLE IMAGE (PR-190's census, re-measured here:
  exactly 1); the result pair at 0x5d256 (`mov [ebp-0xc],eax`) and
  0x5d259-0x5d261 (`mov eax,ds:0xcef40; mov eax,[eax+0x4]` = the
  exit word at [level+0x4]); the 0x5d298-0x5d2ac leg
  (`mov ebx,[eax+0x3e6]; mov edx,2; call [ebx+0x4]`); then the
  INPUT FLUSH + PUMP 0x5d2af-0x5d2cf (see Finding 5); and finally
  the OUT-PARAM PAIR STORE 0x5d2d1-0x5d2dc
  `mov edx,[ebp-0x4]; mov [edx],eax` (the loop's return code) and
  `mov eax,[ebp-0x8]; mov [edx+0x4],eax` (the exit word). PR-190's
  "the caller copies the exit word beside the code" is now read at
  the instruction level, and the field is [level-object+0x4] through
  the ds:0xcef40 global.

- FINDING 3, THE EXIT-CODE CONSUMER, BYTE-FOR-BYTE (inside every
  wrapper). Wrapper 1 (zaria1) 0x5d3b5-0x5d409: `mov edx,DWORD PTR
  [esp]` = the code the driver stored at [edx]; `cmp edx,0x3`,
  `jb 0x5d3f0`, `jbe 0x5d3c6`, `cmp edx,0x4`, `je 0x5d3ec`,
  `jmp 0x5d3dc` - a four-way split, and the returns are explicit:
  - code 3 (0x5d3c6): `mov eax,esi` (the stage object) + `xor
    edx,edx` + `call 0x5da60`, then `xor ecx,ecx; xor ebx,ebx;
    mov eax,esi; xor edx,edx; call 0x5d050` = THE STAGE RESET
    PAIR, then it falls through to 0x5d3dc `mov eax,0x1` ->
    return 1 AFTER resetting = RUN THE SAME STAGE AGAIN.
  - code 2 (0x5d3f0 -> `cmp edx,0x2`, `je 0x5d3e3` -> `mov
    eax,esi; call 0x5d2f0`): Finding 4's queue runner, and ITS
    value is what the wrapper returns (2 or 0, see Finding 4).
  - code 4 (0x5d3ec `xor eax,eax`): return 0 = THE CALLER CHAIN
    STOPS (this is PR-190's exit-4 = the menu's RESULT == 1 leg).
  - codes 0, 1 or >3-but-not-4 (0x5d3dc): `mov eax,0x1` =
    CONTINUE WITHOUT RESET. So code 3 and the default BOTH return
    1; the difference is only the reset pair. Any port model that
    collapses them loses the reset.
  Wrapper 2 (zaria2, name 0x92638 at 0x5d419) repeats the whole
  split at 0x5d425-0x5d47f with ONE difference: its reset legs
  take `mov edx,0x1` (0x5d436 and 0x5d446) instead of edx=0 -
  a per-stage flag on the reset pair, second argument; what it
  selects is NOT read (counted). PR-190 listed what raises codes
  1..4; THIS is what consumes them, so the level-change contract
  is closed on both ends.

- FINDING 4, 0x5d2f0 IS A QUEUE RUNNER (ONE ENTRY PER CALL), AND IT
  READS status.leo. 0x5d2f2 `push edx; sub esp,0xbc` prologue;
  0x5d2f9 `mov DWORD PTR ds:0xa94f0,0x5` (the PR-188 stage index
  again, = 5 here); 0x5d303 `call 0x5dcc0` = the status.leo opener;
  0x5d308 `mov ebx,DWORD PTR ds:0xcf464` = A QUEUE COUNT and
  `test ebx,ebx; je 0x5d38e` -> if the queue is EMPTY the return is
  0 (`xor ebx,ebx`). Otherwise EXACTLY ONE entry is processed per
  call (there is no loop): `mov ecx,ebx` (the count) + `call
  0x5e180` and `call 0x5df50` build two strings from the queue,
  0x5d336 `call 0x60a30` constructs an object from them, 0x5d347 /
  0x5d358 `call 0x57a00` release both strings, then 0x5d35f `call
  0x603b0` = THE STREAM-CLASS RUN VERB (PR-192's). If that returns
  non-zero: 0x5d368 `mov ebx,0x2` (the return value) and the entry
  is POPPED (`dec ecx` 0x5d375 + `mov ds:0xcf464,ecx` 0x5d378); if
  it returns zero nothing is popped and ebx stays 0. BOTH branches
  close the object with `call 0x60a80` (0x5d37e / 0x5d389) and
  0x5d390 `mov eax,ebx` returns. So the exit-code-2 leg means:
  RUN ONE QUEUED ITEM through the same stream class the menus use,
  2 = one ran (come back), 0 = nothing to run. THE QUEUE'S PRODUCER
  (who fills ds:0xcf464) and the entry layout are NOT read -
  counted open.
  status.leo side: `status.leo` exists EXACTLY once in the image, at
  0xa98a4, and the next literal is `mapka.mod` at 0xa98b0. The opener
  0x5dcc0 has exactly 3 callers (0x5d303 above, 0x5dad0, 0x5e358).
  The reader 0x5dae0 (one caller, 0x5e29a) opens it with the mode
  pair at 0x9269c ('rb', then 'w+b') via 0x7607b, then reads
  `mov eax,0x54; mov ebx,0x4; mov edx,0x15; call 0x76a64` = an
  84-byte-element, count-4 request (336 bytes) with a 0x15 prefix.
  The engine's status record is 84 bytes; the repo's gitignored
  STATUS.LEO fixture is 300. THE PORT'S ll_save FORMAT IS NOT
  TOUCHED here: the field map of that 84-byte record is counted
  open (T-17 territory), no test says otherwise.

- FINDING 5, 0x5f310 IS THE INPUT FLUSH AND THE INT-0x0b PUMP, NOT A
  CHUNK INTERPRETER. Its whole body (12 bytes): `mov eax,0xcde70;
  call 0x1c490` (0x1c490 zeroes the input block at 0xcde70, its
  +0xa and +0x20a fields and the [ecx+0x40a] byte) and then the loop
  `call 0x766a7; test eax,eax; je out; call 0x766be; jmp loop`. Its
  three E8 callers (0x603d8, 0x607e0, 0x607ff) are ALL inside the
  run verb 0x603b0 - 0x603d8 comes right after 0x603cb-0x603d1
  `mov edx,[eax+0x9c]; call DWORD PTR [edx+0xc]`. AFTER the flush
  the run verb does the real work: 0x603e3 `mov DWORD PTR
  [eax+0x28],ebx` (zero), then it walks the object list at
  [obj+0x2c] with its end at [obj+0x34], and for each item
  `mov ebx,[eax]; mov ebx,[ebx]` = the item's CLASS TABLE, from
  which it computes two (adj+delta)/2 forms - `mov edx,[ebx+0x18];
  mov edi,[ebx+0x20]; add edx,edi; ... sar edx,0x1f; sub eax,edx;
  sar eax,1` and the same with +0x14/+0x1c - i.e. A C++ POINTER-TO-
  MEMBER DISPATCH, then 0x6041e-0x60423 `mov eax,0xceb84; call
  0x1cb70`. THAT member dispatch over the object list is the per-
  frame part, not 0x5f310. The driver
  inlines the same flush+pump pair at 0x5d2af-0x5d2cf. THERE IS NO
  CHUNK INTERPRETER AT 0x5f310 and the .mnu opcode format is still
  unread.

- FINDING 6, THE STREAM-CLASS FAMILY IS SIX TABLES AND +0x20 IS THE
  CLOSE VERB. 0xa2d00, 0xa2d24, 0xa2d48, 0xa2d6c, 0xa2d90, 0xa2db4 -
  all six have run verb +0x1c = 0x603b0; their +0x20 slots are
  0x5eb70 / 0x5eb30 / 0x60a80 / 0x4be20 / 0x60960 / 0x60820, and
  0x60a80 is the very function the queue runner calls to close the
  object (twice) - so slot +0x20 is the per-class close, not a level
  loop. 0x4be20's body confirms it: free 0xa12d4 (test cl,0x4 leg,
  0x74bc0/0x74be0) else `mov edx,1; call 0x60820`, then the cl,0x2
  leg calls 0x5c370; and 0x4be20 has ZERO E8 callers whole-image.
  Each table is referenced ONLY from its own ctor: 0xa2d00 <- 0x60ff5,
  0xa2d24 <- 0x60e29, 0xa2d48 <- 0x60a4b/0x60aa5, 0xa2d6c <- 0x609cb,
  0xa2d90 <- 0x60947/0x60985, 0xa2db4 <- 0x5f4bd/0x60829. 0xa2dd8 -
  PR-192's 'base stream class' - is NOT a class table: its dwords are
  code pointers (0x61100, 0x5F480, ...), i.e. a verb vector.

- FINDING 7, THE 'levels' CHAIN IS A NAMED-ENTRY LOOKUP, NOT A FILE.
  The string at 0x91ee5 is `Bledny wpis ` ("bad entry"), it is
  referenced EXACTLY once - at 0x4d423, in the .des loader's
  not-found leg (`push 0x91ee5; push eax; call 0x49660` at
  0x4d422-0x4d429) - and the bytes 0x9262e-0x92630 that an earlier
  pass read as delimiter strings are three NUL bytes at the tail of
  the language error string `sja jezykowa!` (0x92614's full text is
  `Nieznana wersja jezykowa!`). PR-192 open item (3) is CLOSED with
  that correction: the driver's by-name leg (Finding 2) IS the
  'levels' mechanism - a 0x5c320/0x57990/0x4a4c0 named-entry lookup
  keyed by the stage name - and the error string is what it prints
  when the entry is missing.
  Language model, as far as it is read: `zaria1.is` is the head of
  three lists at 0x92728 / 0x927b9 / 0x92873 (three per-language
  stage lists - the PR-191 three-language model has a DATA home); the
  `c7 05` immediate-store scan across the 0xa9a00-0xa9b00 globals
  finds NOTHING, so the selector's writer uses another form and stays
  counted; the `LEO_PL.TLO`-style names do NOT exist as plaintext in
  the image (0 hits), so PR-193's draft claim about them is
  retracted - they are assembled at runtime, mechanism counted open.

- FINDING 8, THE ARCHIVE MEMBER HEADER LAW, CENSUSED ON THE REAL
  FILES (the port already parses these containers in ported/llrs.c;
  what is new is the field meaning + the census). All four CD roots
  are 'llrs' v1 containers. The member header is a 14-byte
  NUL-padded name field, then a u32 flag in {1,2}, then a u32 payload
  offset, then a u32 size. Census (strict predicate: printable name
  padded to 14, flag 1 or 2, offset after the header, size inside
  the file): ANIMACJE 21,143,066 B -> 1587 headers = 1291 flag-1 +
  296 flag-2, EVERY flag-2 size exactly 5200, 1287 of the names end
  '.seq' and 274 are bare stems; ETAPY 20,100,773 B -> 468 headers =
  454/14, flag-2 sizes again all exactly 5200, extensions .seq 369 /
  .pcx 62 / .pcm 23; LEVELDES 431,636,667 B -> 71 headers = 67
  flag-1 '.des' (which IS the 67-'plany=' population PR-192 found,
  now through the header law) plus 4 flag-2 whose names are EXACTLY
  ENG, GER, POL, POL.ORG = the language text blocks; SOUND -> 291
  headers, .wav 269 + .mod 22, no flag-2 at all. So the flag-2
  population is a fixed-5200 object-description block, and it is
  where the PR-192 31-tag vocabulary lives. The u32 at container
  offset 0x10 is NOT a name-length field (14 / 14 / 17 / 291 across
  the four) - counted open, do not model it.

- FINDING 9, ZARIA1.IS IS AN iNFOSTREAM FILE. It begins
  `iNFOSTREAM\n\0"Lew Leon" (c) 1996 ` - the .IS movie container the
  port already decodes (ported/is_stream.c, tools/is_decode.py), which
  is why the 31 object tags appear ZERO times in it (PR-192's
  observation, now with its container identified). The .IS
  level-DATA chunk format is UNCHANGED as an open item; the 44-byte
  block-chain claim from the draft is NOT repeated here (it came from
  a different image copy and was not reproduced against this file).

- OPEN ITEMS COUNTED (7 new). (1) Who fills the ds:0xcf464 queue and
  with what records. (2) The .mnu opcode format and its interpreter -
  0x5f310 is out, the run verb's member-dispatch walk over the
  object list at [obj+0x2c]..[obj+0x34] is the
  remaining candidate. (3) The 84-byte status record's field map
  vs the port's ll_save codec (no test verdict yet). (4) The six
  stream classes' identity: what differs at +0x04..+0x18 and which
  file kind each carries. (5) The .IS level-DATA chunk format
  (carried). (6) The ANIMACJE flag-2 5200-byte record layout, i.e.
  the per-tag description layout (carried, now bounded: every
  instance is 5200 bytes). (7) The language-selector writer and the
  runtime assembly of the `.TLO` names (carried).

- CORRECTIONS APPLIED IN THE OLDER RECORDS (9 bracket blocks: 1 in

- GATES. Docs-only reading PR (the PR-138..PR-192 precedent): no port

## PR-194 — THE EXIT-CODE CONTRACT BECOMES BEHAVIOUR: A PURE STAGE-DRIVER
## TABLE (ported/ll_stage.[ch]) + THE FOUR OUTCOMES DRIVEN THROUGH THE REAL
## RAN.01 PLAY LEG AND PINNED AT BYTE LEVEL; THE `.MOV end_level` PRODUCER
## CENSUSED (26 ROWS, ALL OF THEM IN THE LION'S OWN LEW.MOV, 3 OF 12
## MEMBERS: A_TUNGA1->1, A_TUNGA2->2, A_EXIT->12x1); NO PRODUCER IS CLAIMED

- WHY. PR-193 left one finding whose behaviour is fully read, and the
  owner asked for the balance to move toward implementation: the
  stage-driver split (3 = reset + run again, 2 = the queue runner, 4 =
  stop, else continue). This PR is the first `[PORT]` of the new era and
  it ports exactly that, with its test in the same commit.

- THE DELTA, MEASURED BEFORE ANY CODE (what the port did with the four
  codes before this PR): NOTHING. Concretely -
  (a) the level harness is a bounded tick loop
      (`for (tk = 1; tk <= ticks; tk++)`, the LEO_LEVEL_PPM/
      LEO_LEVEL_PPM_TICK play leg in ported/ll_level.c); no value from a
      finished level is read anywhere;
  (b) the vocabulary knows the WORDS but nothing consumes them:
      `AC_LEAVE` is one row of the LL_SIG name table (ported/ll_play.c
      263, the enum in ll_play.h 242) and no code sets or tests that bit;
      `end_level` appears in the port only inside the parser's "these
      directives are counted, not acted on" message text;
  (c) there is no queue, no stage list and no exit word in the port.
  So the honest statement is: the contract had no counterpart at all, and
  what could be ported without inventing an engine fact was the SPLIT
  plus its observable effects.

- WHAT SHIPPED.
  (1) `ported/ll_stage.h` + `ported/ll_stage.c` - the contract as a PURE
      function `ll_stage_outcome(exit_code, queue_len, *did_reset)` and
      `ll_stage_queue_len()`. The header carries the whole model with the
      addresses (wrapper split 0x5d3b5-0x5d409, reset pair 0x5da60 +
      0x5d050, queue runner 0x5d2f0 with its 0x5d368 / 0x5d375-0x5d378 /
      0x5d38e legs, exit-4 at 0x5d3ec, default at 0x5d3dc) AND the list
      of what is not known, so nobody fills it in later from imagination.
      `did_reset` is part of the answer on purpose: codes 3 and the
      default BOTH return 1, so a table that returns only the value loses
      the reset.
  (2) `tools/stage_selftest.c` - 11 cases over that table, no data, no
      window, no SDL; it runs in BOTH fixture modes.
  (3) The play leg in `ported/ll_level.c` gains `LEO_LEVEL_EXIT=
      "<tick>:<code>[,...]"` ("the level ended at that tick with that
      code") and `stage_apply:`, which prints what the engine would do and
      does it: code 3 resets the stage to its authored start and runs on,
      code 2 takes the queue leg, code 4 stops, anything else runs on with
      no reset. The check is placed AFTER the tick is advanced, which is
      what makes the byte-level pins below possible. Without the
      environment variable nothing is printed and no byte changes.
      The reset is a NAMED ESTIMATE (rule 1): `stage_reset_to_authored`
      restores what the placement parser authored (declared start state
      via `mov->start_st`, frame 0, facing 1, row clock and signal pulses
      cleared, position back to the authored anchor `bx/by`) and puts the
      lion back through `play_spawn`; the combat fields (hp / hit_cd /
      atc / dead) are NOT touched, because no reading says the engine's
      pair touches them.
  (4) Makefile + CMake: `stage_selftest` / `stage_selftest.exe`, a
      `verify-stage` leg (in `verify-all`, .PHONY and `clean`), and
      `ported/ll_stage.c` added to `SRC`/`HDRS` and to the CMake source
      list. That last part was found BY THE GATE, not by the leg: the
      first full run failed with `undefined symbol: ll_stage_queue_len` at
      `ll_cutscene` / `ll_cutscene.exe` / the CMake build, because those
      link `ported/ll_level.c` (which now calls the module). Re-built
      clean afterwards, including the cross builds (`ll_cutscene.exe`,
      `stage_selftest.exe`) - zero warnings, and the Windows run itself
      stays in the end pass (rule 8).
  (5) README documents `LEO_LEVEL_EXIT` (rule 4: a new LEO_* hook).

- FINDING, THE PRODUCER SIDE, CENSUSED ON BOTH SIDES (the data says who
  ends a level; the engine says where the word is parsed; the last step
  stays open).
  (a) In the engine image `end_level` exists EXACTLY ONCE, at 0x9198e,
      inside the .MOV directive vocabulary (the run
      `pos / goto / goto rel / goto o_rel / I / F / IC / FC / M / MOVE /
      GEN / Wait / end_level`, then the error text `Bledna komo...`), and
      it is referenced EXACTLY ONCE: 0x46bbd-0x46c01 compares the parsed
      word (`mov edx,0x9198e; ... call 0x76a69`) and on a match builds a
      node - `mov eax,0xc; call 0x5c320`, `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x4],
      0xa1048`, payload formatted with the ' %i ' string at 0x91998, i.e.
      the number after the directive. The class table 0xa1048 (verbs
      0x476b0, 0x45750, ..., 0x47830, 0x47650, 0x45d10) and its other
      two references (0x476fe, 0x4784f) are parser/copy/compare legs; the
      RUNTIME that executes such a node was NOT found in this pass.
  (b) In the fixtures (HD `ANIMACJE`, 1,961,080 B) there are EXACTLY 26
      `end_level <n>` lines, values 25 x `1` and 1 x `2`. All 26 are in
      members named `LEW.MOV` - the LION's own script, the very script the
      port already runs for the player - and only 3 of the 12 `LEW.MOV`
      members carry any:
        hdr@1705058 (payload 1,420 B, ~5 states): state `A_TUNGA1` one
          row `end_level 1`, state `A_TUNGA2` one row `end_level 2`;
        hdr@1800357 (12,608 B, ~37 states): 12 rows inside state
          `A_EXIT`, all `end_level 1`;
        hdr@1947201 (12,190 B, ~34 states): 12 rows inside `A_EXIT`, all
          `end_level 1`.
      The other 9 lion scripts have none; the CD-side containers (both
      ANIMACJE and both ETAPY) have ZERO `end_level` lines; and the port
      knows `A_EXIT` only as a name in a comment (ported/ll_play.c 2427).
      So the SHAPE the data gives is: the level ends from the lion's own
      walk-off state (`A_EXIT`), and the TUNGA pair asks for two different
      values (1 and 2) from its two exchange states. Whether those numbers
      are the loop's return, the exit word, or a level index is NOT read -
      counted, and it is the first question of the next reading step.
  (c) The exit-word WRITER is still not identified [PR-198 CORRECTION:
      ds:0xcef40 the ruled-out-shape claim below is WRONG as stated,
      corrected in: PR-198 - the writer is right there, 0x45752 loads
      the global and 0x4575b stores [reg+0x4], 3 instructions apart].
      This pass did rule
      out the easy shape: of the 261 code sites that mention ds:0xcef40
      and the 918 stores of the form `mov DWORD PTR [reg+0x4], ...`,
      none pairs a ds:0xcef40 load with a store into the level object's
      +0x4 within 30 instructions (the tempting 0x24681
      `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x4],0x4` stores into an object a `call
      0x53eb0` had just constructed, not into the level object). Stated
      so the next pass does not repeat the search.

- THE TEST, AND WHY THE PINS ARE EXACT (`verify-stage`). Both halves in
  one leg; the contract half always runs, the driven half is fixture-
  guarded like every other data leg. Six runs of the real RAN.01 play
  leg (`LEO_PLAY_SCRIPT="1:FWD"`, LEO_LEVEL_PPM dumps):
    base   100 ticks, no code      -> NO `stage driver:` line at all.
                                       This is the "the contract is inert"
                                       pin: every pre-existing play pin is
                                       untouched because the hook is off.
    t50     50 ticks, no code      -> the 50-tick reference frame.
    stop4  exit 4 at tick 50      -> the STOP line + `the play leg ended
                                       at tick 50 of 100`, and the dump is
                                       BYTE-IDENTICAL to t50.
    stop2  exit 2 at tick 50      -> the queue line ("an EMPTY queue ...
                                       the engine's own empty-queue leg
                                       0x5d38e answers stop"), same bytes
                                       as t50.
    again1 exit 1 at tick 50      -> the "run on, NO reset" line, and the
                                       dump is BYTE-IDENTICAL to base: the
                                       default leg changes nothing.
    reset3 exit 3 at tick 50      -> the RESET line, and the dump is NOT
                                       base but IS byte-identical to t50:
                                       50 ticks after a reset at tick 50
                                       are exactly the 50 ticks of the
                                       same script with no reset. That is
                                       the strongest form of "the reset
                                       really restored the authored state"
                                       the harness can show.
  Measured frames (sha256, /tmp/opencode/stg_*.ppm): base == again1 =
  373a3e44ebce1d43...; t50 == stop4 == stop2 == reset3 =
  80f3573f8477b124...; base != t50 (the 100-tick and 50-tick frames
  differ, so the equality above is not a collapse of the test).

- GATES. Full gate measured on this commit's tree: `make` ZERO warnings;
  `make -k -j$(nproc) verify-all DATA=<iso> HD=<hd>` rc=0 with
  58 (ok); the same target fixture-free (`DATA=/tmp/opencode/nope
  HD=/tmp/opencode/nope`) rc=0 with 11 (ok) + the named data-SKIP legs
  (20 by `grep -c 'verify-[a-z0-9_-]*: SKIP'`). The counts move HERE for
  a legitimate reason: verify-stage's contract half runs in both modes, so
  the fixture-free (ok) count rises by one, and the fixture-free named
  SKIP lines rise by one (the driven half's SKIP). PR-193's record's
  52 / 10 + 19 are the numbers BEFORE this leg; the earlier records' 18
  is the same count under a narrower grep. This commit touches ported/,
  tools/, Makefile, CMakeLists.txt and README, so the pure-docs
  exception does not apply and the whole gate was run. The Windows half
  stays in the end pass (rule 8); its build halves
  (`ll_cutscene.exe`, `stage_selftest.exe`, the extended `ll_level.exe`

- OPEN ITEMS, COUNTED (1 closed by this PR, 5 carried/named).
  CLOSED: "the port has no exit-code path at all" - the split now exists
  in port code with a test in both fixture modes.
  (1) The .MOV action RUNTIME: what executes a parsed directive node
      (class 0xa1048 for `end_level`) and where it puts the value - the
      loop's return, the exit word [level+0x4], or a level index. That is
      the producer's missing last step, and with it the port could drive
      real codes from A_EXIT / A_TUNGA rows instead of injected ones.
  (2) The exit-word writer inside the level loop (search space narrowed by
      the ruled-out shape above).
  (3) What the reset pair 0x5da60 / 0x5d050 does, and what the per-stage
      edx 0/1 (wrapper 1 at 0x5d3c8, wrapper 2 at 0x5d436) selects. Until
      then the port's reset stays the named ESTIMATE it is.
  (4) Who fills the engine's ds:0xcf464 queue and what one entry looks
      like; and whether the port ever should have one.
  (5) Whether `end_level`'s 1/2 in A_TUNGA1/A_TUNGA2 is the TUNGA I <->
      II exchange of T6 (`AC_XCHG_LEVEL`) - the data shape matches, the
      mechanism is unread.

## PR-195 — THE DOCUMENTATION AUDIT IS MEASURED, AND ITS STRUCTURE
## CHECKS BECOME A BUILD LEG: tools/doc_census.py + verify-docs, which
## replaces two hand greps (the heading census sees 107 of the 184
## records), with FIVE negative controls measured. No document is
## reorganised here; the restructure is scheduled by the owner's approval

- WHY. The owner asked, after PR-194: "do analysis of current
  documentation with focusing on engine documentation, find potential
  duplications and find fields to refine to better searching in it",
  then "and potential better organisation". The audit was measured
  first (read-only scripts, /tmp/opencode/docsmap/census*.py, output
  kept at docsmap/census.out), the map + duplication list + the
  restructure proposal were presented before any file was touched, and
  the owner answered "ok, go" to the recommended first cut: step 0 (the
  structure leg, this PR), step 1 (the forward record template), step 2
  (the generated index). Nothing is moved or deleted here on purpose:
  the new leg is the safety net for the moves that follow.

- THE AUDIT, MEASURED. Sizes: NEXT_STEPS.md 28,111 lines / 253,645
  words / 1.67 MB; HANDOFF.md 8,367 / 78,467; PLAN.md 1,516;
  tools/re/README.md 156; README.md 299; TEST_REPORT.md 274; the two
  owner-supplied inputs 285 + 259. Structure of the ledger: 753 lines
  start with `## ` = 184 record headings + 4 `## OWNER` + 498
  wrapped-title continuation lines + 9 real section headings; 129 record
  titles are one line, the rest wrap over 2-31 lines. File order: a
  `## Status as of 2026-11-14 (through PR-19 ...)` block at line 25
  (~175 PRs stale), records from 244, `## Next` at 15,852 (the middle),
  the newest record at 27,878, `## Deferred big items` at 28,056,
  `## Standing rules` at 28,102. HANDOFF: sections 1-3 = 671 lines /
  1 address, section 4 = 19, section 5 (facts) = 110 / 48, section 6

  16 items, item 13 alone = 4,187 lines) = 4,696 / 2,037, section 8
  (T1..T11 + 50 "STATUS after PR-nn" paragraphs) = 2,428 / 721.

- FINDING 1, THE DUPLICATION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ACCIDENTAL. HANDOFF

  the journal's findings, in prose, which is why the copy can drift
  (verbatim long lines: 4, so the duplication is paraphrase-level and
  invisible to any diff). 599 record pairs share >= 8 addresses
  (PR-190/PR-191 = 91, PR-188/PR-189 = 75, PR-191/PR-192 = 72,
  PR-189/PR-190 = 58, PR-186/PR-187 = 56, PR-185/PR-186 = 56). The
  same open item is re-listed per phrase: the ANIMACJE flag-2 5200-byte
  record in 24 records, the 84-byte status record / STATUS.LEO in 11,
  the pool chain-store hunt in 10, the `.mnu` opcode interpreter in 7,
  the exit-word writer in 7, the one-byte listing trap in 6, the
  `end_level` producer in 6, the reset pair 0x5da60/0x5d050 in 4, the
  ds:0xcf464 queue in 3. The plan exists twice: 14 of the 15 keys in
  `## Next` also appear in HANDOFF section 8's task blocks. The measured
  gate state is restated 79 times in 62 different wordings with 50
  `N (ok)` claims in 27 shapes - that is where the 18-vs-19-vs-20 SKIP
  count confusion in PR-193/194 came from: it is an artefact of

  ledger (+51 in HANDOFF), which is why the history override cost 176

- FINDING 2, WHAT MAKES THE ENGINE TEXT HARD TO SEARCH. There is no
  index: 3,985 distinct addresses / 12,673 mentions (2,494 appear in
  exactly one record, 729 in >=3 records, 302 in >=5); an index over
  the >=3 set is 729 entries and answers 60% of every address lookup,
  the >=5 set is 302 entries and answers 40%. Same for the other two
  vocabularies a reader actually types: 636 distinct `[field+0xNN]`
  tokens (155 in >=3 records) and 240 authored names (`control=` 31
  records, `K_GEN1` 30, `A_DEAD` 25, `AC_TIME` 25, `A_WALK` 24,
  `A_WSP` 19) - zero landing entries. Reconstructing one mechanism
  means reading its whole history: 0xcef40 = 113 lines across 51
  records, 0x49580 = 88 across 42, [obj+0xa1] = 80 across 28,
  STATUS.LEO = 11 across 10, and nothing marks which claim is current.
  Findings are cited by number: of 3,371 `PR-nn` citations, 3,022 carry
  no address/field/name token within 200 characters. The headings are
  the only index and they are narrative: 8 of 191 titles contain an
  address, 63 contain a mechanism keyword. Corrections have no field:
  the bracket form is used 7 times while the prose words appear 112
  (CORRECTED) + 21 (WRONG) + 12 (RETRACT) + 6 (SUPERSEDE) times, and
  352 distinct addresses appear inside a correction sentence - so
  `grep 0x4be20` finds the mentions, never the sentence that killed it.
  Open items have no ids: 71 distinct task/question ids in the ledger,
  only 22 with a closed/done word near any mention; 14 of 16 HANDOFF
  section 7 items read as open. Record fields are optional - a
  `- FINDING` marker in 29% of records, `- WHY` 39%, `OPEN ITEMS` 43%,
  `- GATES` 41% - and a record's KIND lives in its title prose
  ("READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE" x24).
  THE TWO CHECKS THEMSELF WERE WEAK: `grep -c '^## PR-1'` = 107 is a
  PREFIX PROXY over 184 records - it cannot see the 74 PR-2..PR-99
  records or the 4 OWNER records; and 11 PR numbers (1..6, 22, 23, 24,

  file entirely. The over-79 line rule is also partly format debt: of
  HANDOFF's 71 such lines, 41 are section 6 table rows (longest 3,512
  columns), and 22 of NEXT_STEPS' 71 are wrapped record titles.

- WHAT SHIPPED (step 0). `tools/doc_census.py` + the `verify-docs` leg

## PR-196 — THE RECORD TEMPLATE IS THE CONTRACT, AND P4 ENFORCES IT
## (HANDOFF section 10a + `tools/doc_census.py` P4, from PR-196 with
## this record as the one exemption): SEVEN NEGATIVE CONTROLS AND ONE
## POSITIVE MEASURED; the gate line is TWO lines because one line
## carrying both halves measures 107 columns and breaks the width rule

- WHY. The owner approved the doc-audit order with "ok, go": step 0 was
  PR-195's structure leg, step 1 is this record template, step 2 the
  generated index. The audit measured what optional fields cost: a
  `- FINDING` marker in 29% of records, `- WHY` 39%, `OPEN ITEMS` 43%,
  a gate marker in 41%; 3,022 of 3,371 `PR-nn` citations carrying no
  address/field/name token within 200 characters; corrections written
  as prose (112 `CORRECTED` + 21 `WRONG` + 12 `RETRACT` + 6
  `SUPERSEDE`) with the bracket form used 7 times. A record's KIND
  lives in its title prose ("READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE" x24). So
  the template is written as a REQUIREMENT and enforced by the build,
  because a rule nobody checks is the state that produced those
  numbers. Forward-only: P4 tests records numbered `TEMPLATE_FROM` (196)
  or higher, history is not rewritten, and step 2's index keeps reading
  prose so it works on all 186 records, not only the formatted ones.

- WHAT SHIPPED. HANDOFF section 10a: the field block, ten fields over
  eleven lines, in a fixed order - `KIND:` (read/port/gate/docs, what
  the record ESTABLISHES, not which files it touches), `SUBSYSTEM:`,
  `ADDRESSES:` (every engine address the record establishes as current
  truth OR retracts, exact tokens only), `NAMES:` (the authored
  vocabulary: `.des` keys, state/action names, `.MOV` members,
  `[field+0xNN]` words), `CODE: no:`/`yes:`, `HOOKS:`, `OPENS:` /
  `CLOSES:`, `CORRECTS: none | PR-nn: <the claim that was wrong>`, and
  the gate in two lines, `GATE:` (the with-fixtures half) and
  `GATE-FIXTURE-FREE:` (the rule-4 second half). Field NAMES ARE
  LITERALS, not stems: the audit's 86 prose gate markers came in four
  spellings (`- GATES.` 75, `- GATES:`, `- GATES (`, `- TESTS AND
  GATES`), so P4 matches each name exactly at COLUMN 0 - which is also
  why an INDENTED copy of a field name is prose and never a field.
  Field CONTENTS are free text within a sanity character class, so a
  wording change can never break the pin; a prose-only PR-nn citation
  does not satisfy `CORRECTS:`, which demands a record number. P4
  tests PRESENCE, ORDER and EXACTLY-ONE-EACH; it does not test where
  in the record the block sits - "immediately after the title" is the
  section's style, not a rule, and no invented rule was added to
  enforce it.
  HANDOFF section 10's record checklist line now points at 10a.

- THE GATE FORMAT, MEASURED INTO EXISTENCE. Before designing it: 86
  gate-marker lines in the ledger, 39 of them followed by `(ok)`, and
  12 distinct count-claim tokens around those markers - `10 (ok)`,
  `11 (ok)`, `12 (ok)`, `52 (ok)`, `56 (ok)`, `58 (ok)`, `59 (ok)`,
  `18 named SKIPs`, `18 named verify-SKIPs`, `21 named SKIPs`,
  `23 named SKIP`, `23 named SKIPs` (the last pair differs only in the
  plural `s`). Zero lines in any canonical format, and none of those
  counts is wrong for its date: they are restatements of a moving
  state, which is exactly the mechanism the audit blamed for the
  18/19/20 SKIP drift. TWO LINES BECAUSE OF WIDTH: the first draft,
  one line carrying both halves with their counts
  (`GATE: make 0 warnings; verify-all with fixtures rc=0 59 (ok);
  fixture-free rc=0 12 (ok) + 20 named verify-SKIPs`), measures 106
  columns; the two mandatory prefixes with their counts alone measure
  107. Control N7 below shows a merged line tripping the width ratchet
  AND losing the `GATE-FREE` field at the same time. So the rule-4
  halves are two fields: `GATE: make 0 warnings; verify-all fixtures
  rc=0 <N> (ok);` is 56 columns with its counts, `GATE-FIXTURE-FREE:
  rc=0 <M> (ok) + <K> named` is 55, and a record continues either line
  with indented prose. A record writes its gate state ONCE.

- P4 IN `tools/doc_census.py`. For every record heading numbered
  TEMPLATE_FROM (196) or higher, the tool reads that record's text
  (heading to the NEXT REAL HEADING) and requires each field name to
  match once and only, at column 0, IN THE ORDER the template gives -
  it builds the found list in LINE order, which is what lets it see a
  swap or a duplicate at all (the first version collected matches in
  template order and could only ever report a missing field). Two
  things the real record caught that POS/E1 + N1..N7 could not:
  the `## PR-<n>` anchor ALSO matches wrapped-title continuation lines,
  so a slice ended at PR-196's own title continuation and the check
  saw ONE line - the boundary is now "the next line that starts a
  heading, i.e. a `## ` line with a blank line before it", which is
  what separates a real heading from a wrapped title; and the
  exemption's first form ("exempt if it carries no field name at all")
  was disproved by this record itself, which does carry two field
  lines, its gate. The exemption therefore skips the BLOCK requirement
  and the tool still reports the field lines an exempt record carries
  (a partial block fails every other record). The exemption itself is
  FIELDS_EXEMPT = {196}, frozen as a constant with a comment, because
  raising TEMPLATE_FROM would silently let records skip the block
  again.

- POSITIVE CONTROL + SEVEN NEGATIVES + THE EXEMPTION, MEASURED
  (`/tmp/opencode/pr196/controls.sh`, output kept at
  /tmp/opencode/pr196/controls.out). Each case inserts a synthetic
  PR-196 and PR-197 into a copy of the CURRENT tree, so P1/P2 stay
  silent and the only failure is the one under test; because the tree
  already contains this record, the exempt count reads "PR-196, PR-196"
  and "2 without" - the duplicate is the real record and the stand-in.
  POS  PR-197 with the full block -> rc=0, "1 records carry the field
       block, 2 without (accepted)".
  E1   PR-197 not inserted at all -> rc=0, "0 carry", NOTE exempt.
  N1   PR-197 with no field block -> rc=1 "missing KIND,SUBSYSTEM,
       ADDRESSES,NAMES,CODE,HOOKS,OPENS,CLOSES,CORRECTS,GATE,GATE-
       FREE".
  N2   NAMES line dropped -> rc=1 "missing NAMES".
  N3   `SUBSYSTEM:` renamed `SUBSYSTEMS:` -> rc=1 "missing SUBSYSTEM"
       (the literal-name rule, proven from the other side).
  N4   `GATE-FIXTURE-FREE:` placed before `GATE:` -> rc=1 "GATE-FREE
       before GATE (the template order is GATE before GATE-FREE)".
  N5   the whole block quoted INDENTED (an example, not a block) ->
       rc=1, all eleven lines missing (column 0 is what distinguishes
       a field from a quotation).
  N6   `GATE:` line duplicated adjacently -> rc=1 "duplicated GATE".
  N7   the two gate lines merged into one -> rc=1, BOTH "72 lines over
       79 columns, the ratchet is 71" AND "missing GATE-FREE;
       duplicated GATE" - the split is a width fact, not a style
       choice. The two gate prefixes with their counts on one line
       measure 107 columns; the format's own two lines measure 56 and
       55 (printed by the script before the cases run).
  Five defects in the controls or the tool were found by running them:
  an appended variant line landed past a blank line outside the record,
  so N4/N6 first reported rc=0; collecting matches in template order
  hid a swap and a duplicate entirely; this record's own draft gate
  line exceeded the width rule, which is how the two-line format came
  to exist; and the record's own text disproved the first exemption
  rule (see the P4 paragraph above). The tool's own file keeps max
  width 74 with 0 over-79 lines.

- SELF-EXEMPTION NOTE (the only one, and it is load-bearing). This
  record deliberately carries no field BLOCK - nine of the eleven lines
  are absent - and it is the record that introduces the contract, so
  P4's exemption covers exactly it. What the exemption does NOT do is
  hide the record from the check: P4 reads it and reports the field
  lines it finds - here exactly two, this record's own gate lines,
  because a record that defines a format
  should use it for the one thing it is allowed to state. A partial
  block fails every other record. So quoting these names at column 0
  is safe only inside the exempt record, and every other field name in
  this record stays quoted or indented. From PR-197 on, every record
  carries the block, and PR-198 (the .MOV runtime read) is the first
  one in production.

- GATE. Section 2 rule 4's exception means a docs-and-tool-only commit
  need not run verify-all, but this one did, deliberately: PR-196 is
  the first doc PR after PR-195 put verify-docs INTO verify-all, so a
  fresh full-gate baseline is worth having for the doc PRs that follow
  (PR-197's index leg joins the same target). Measured on this tree
  after the tool, HANDOFF, this record and the Next swap were all
  final: `make` ZERO warnings; `make -k
  -j$(nproc) verify-all DATA=<iso> HD=<hd>`; the same target
  fixture-free. The counts live in ONE place in this record - the two
  GATE lines at its end, the first production use of the format this
  PR introduces - because restating them in prose is the measured
  drift mechanism. Docs invariants, re-measured by `make verify-docs`
  after the splice: records 186 (185 distinct PR numbers up to
  PR-196), `## Next` / `## Deferred big items` / `## Standing rules`
  each present once, over-79 ratchet 71/71/12
  with the over-79 SETS byte-identical (0 added, 0 removed in all
  three documents), template check "0 records carry the field block,
  1 without" + "NOTE exempt from the template: PR-196" + "NOTE the
  exempt record PR-196 carries 2 field line(s) anyway". No `ported/`
  or `tools/*.c` file changed, so no leg body
  could read this diff; the Windows half stays in the end pass
  (rule 8).

- OPEN ITEMS, COUNTED. This PR closes the doc-audit step 1 item (the
  record template) and opens none. Counted as still open from the
  audit: step 2, the generated index (PR-197, now able to read fields
  from PR-196-on records and prose from the rest); step 3, the
  open-items register with `OI-` ids, whose `OPENS:`/`CLOSES:` lines
  this template already prepares; steps 4 and 5, HANDOFF 5/6/7 and the
  NEXT_STEPS move. The engine's unread items are untouched by this PR
  and stay listed where they have always been listed.

GATE: make 0 warnings; verify-all fixtures rc=0 59 (ok);
GATE-FIXTURE-FREE: rc=0 12 (ok) + 20 named verify-SKIPs (the first
production use of this format outside the controls; the record is
spliced before the gate runs and `make verify-docs` is re-run on the
final tree afterwards, which is the recipe section 10 pins).

## PR-197 — THE GENERATED ENGINE INDEX LANDS: tools/re_index.py ->
## docs/RE_INDEX.md + the verify-index regen-and-cmp leg; building it
## on the SHARED doc code exposed a dead regex branch (every `.des`
## key was invisible everywhere that regex ran; fixed as DES_RE) AND
## measured the three different record counts the tools report - 187,
## 189, 182 - none wrong, all reconciled here

KIND: gate
SUBSYSTEM: docs structure (the generated index, doc-audit step 2)
ADDRESSES: none
NAMES: control=, access=, docs/RE_INDEX.md, tools/re_index.py
CODE: yes: new generator tools/re_index.py; doc_census gains DES_RE;
      Makefile gains the verify-index leg
HOOKS: none
OPENS: index correction-pointers stay prose-co-occurrence until
      records carry a CORRECTS: line the generator can read
CLOSES: the doc-audit step 2 generated index
CORRECTS: PR-196: two claims in PR-196's `## Next` block, both wrong
      at the measurements this PR took. (1) It scoped the index as
      "addresses appearing in >=3 records: 729 entries... [field]
      tokens in >=3 records: 155... the 240 authored names" - those
      were the audit's LOOSE-segment figures; the strict real-heading
      boundary doc_census slices records with (and this generator
      reuses) measures 619 / 140, and the full name vocabulary with
      the dead key branch repaired is 224, not 240. (2) It said
      "PR-198 (the .MOV runtime read) is the first one in production"
      to carry the field block; the rule is every record >= 196, so
      PR-197 - this record - is the first and PR-198 is the second.

- WHY. The owner's audit step 2 (approved "ok, go") was an index. The
  audit's sharpest number: `0xcef40` appears on 115 lines spread over
  the ledger and nothing says which claim is current, and 3,022 of
  3,371 `PR-nn` citations carry no address/field/name token. A reader
  who greps an address gets the mentions, never the answer "which
  records, and was there a correction?" This PR ships the landing page
  for that: a generated index over the three vocabularies a reader
  actually types, plus a build leg that regenerates it and `cmp`s it so
  it cannot drift from the ledger.

- WHAT SHIPPED. (1) `tools/re_index.py`: parses the ledger, emits
  `docs/RE_INDEX.md` - as committed, 4,180 generated lines,
  983 entries: 619 address keys in >=3 records (47% of address
  mentions), 140 field tokens in >=3 (64%), 224 authored names
  (all), 0 lines over 79 columns - one entry per key with `mentions:`
  (every record), a `corrected in:` pointer, and a `latest mention:`
  reading pointer. (2) The `verify-index` Makefile leg: regenerate to
  a temp, `cmp` against the tracked file, fail with "docs/RE_INDEX.md
  is stale" if it differs, else one `(ok)` line. Like verify-docs it
  reads only tracked markdown, so it runs in BOTH fixture modes and
  adds exactly one (ok) in each. (3) The HANDOFF section 10 checklist
  line. (4) A fix to the shared vocabulary (below), because the index
  is deliberately built ON doc_census's regexes.

- IT SHARES THE PARSER WITH THE DOC PIN ON PURPOSE, AND THE COUNT
  DIFFERENCES ARE ALL MEASURED. re_index imports doc_census and reuses
  `RECORD_RE`/`HEAD_RE` and the real-heading rule, so the index works
  on exactly the record slices P4 checks. Three record counts now
  appear in this repo and a careless reader reads them as agreement -
  they are not the same measurement, so all three are named here:
    P1 reports 187: every line MATCHING the `## PR-<n>` anchor, at any
      position, because its job is presence and gaps by PR NUMBER (set
      based - on the set of PR numbers the tools agree exactly);
    this index says 182: only real headings (a `## ` line preceded by
      a blank line) - exactly what P4 slices;
    the audit's census cut 189: any line STARTING `## PR-`.
  The 187-vs-182 difference is five OLD titles that repeat their own
  number on a continuation line (PR-29/30/31/32/116); the 189-vs-182
  difference is those five plus three more title wraps in forms P1's
  anchor rejects (`## PR-138..149`, `## PR-159/160`). None is wrong
  for its job; the index uses 182 because an index entry must point at
  real records. P1 was already the only heading census before
  PR-195 - it is not a new inconsistency, it is a precision now
  written down.

- THE HONEST COUNTS AND THE RECONCILIATION. Measured on THIS tree
  (182 records, this one included): 619 addresses in >=3 records =
  47% of all address mentions; 140 field tokens in >=3 = 64% of field
  mentions; 224 authored names; 37 of the 619 address entries carry a
  correction pointer. Reproducing the audit's method on the
  PRE-record tree for comparability: strict 181 records -> 619 addr /
  140 field / 207 name (NAME_RE only, the dead branch still dead);
  loose 189 segments -> 730 addr / 157 field / 84 name - which is the
  audit's 729/155 headline, from phantom segments, not a bigger scan.
  The name line moves 207 -> 223 by the DES_RE repair alone, and to
  224 because this record cites `access=` as a worked example (see
  below). The worked example, end to end: 0xcef40 sits on 118 raw
  lines of THIS tree - 115 of them before this record, which cites
  its own example, and 115 was the audit's whole-file figure - in 47
  real records, or 55 loose segments on the pre-record tree. The
  generated header prints the top entry's numbers COMPUTED at
  generation time, which is exactly why a count frozen in prose goes
  stale the moment the ledger grows - as this paragraph just did.

- THE AUDIT'S OWN NAME MATCHER HAD A DEAD BRANCH, FOUND BY USING IT.
  doc_census's `NAME_RE` carries `[a-z_]{4,20}=\b` for the `.des`
  keys. The trailing `\b` after `=` never matches: there is no word
  boundary between a letter and `=`. So that branch matched ZERO
  tokens everywhere it ran - the audit's name census, doc_census's
  report-only "name tokens 222 distinct", and re_index's first run all
  silently missed every `.des` key (0 matches for `control=`,
  verified). Fixed at the source with `DES_RE =
  \b[a-z][a-z0-9_]{3,20}=(?![=<>!])` (the lookahead keeps `>=`/`!=`
  from reading as keys; verified against those cases). NAME_RE is kept
  untouched so the historical "222" figure stays comparable; the
  report prints the honest union AND NAME_RE-alone (223 union / 222
  NAME_RE on this tree), and the index uses both. THIS PATTERN IS A
  LANDING PAGE, NOT A DICTIONARY - the same run proved it: among its
  whole-file matches is `access=basic`, which is git-credential config
  from a CI note, not engine vocabulary at all. That is why this
  record lists it in NAMES honestly instead of hiding it: the entry
  `### access=` says PR-197 names it, and the generated header says
  plainly that an entry means "these records NAME this token", never
  "the engine author WROTE it". The bug living in code three tools
  trusted is the whole argument for sharing the parser instead of
  reimplementing it.

- FIVE CONTROLS ON THE GENERATOR + ONE ON THE LEG, MEASURED
  (controls.sh / Makefile runs; the generator reads NEXT_STEPS.md from
  the CWD so each case runs in a temp dir with a synthetic ledger):
  C1 threshold: a key in 3 records is indexed, the same-shaped key in
      2 records is not, and a `.des` key in ONE record IS (names have
      no floor) - the full rule, both sides.
  C2 correction present: a key established in PR-1/PR-2 and retracted
      by a `[PR-3 CORRECTION: ...]` line gets `corrected in: PR-3`,
      and only PR-3.
  C3 determinism: two runs on identical input are byte-identical.
  C4 the width guard is not dead code: with ONLY the guard's
      comparison lowered (79 -> 70) it fires (rc=1) on real ~74-column
      lines; lowering the wrap budget too changes nothing, because the
      generator self-wraps to WIDTH_MAX - one constant drives budget,
      guard and message together.
  C5 NO invented retraction: a key in three records with no
      correction word anywhere gets NO `corrected in:` line (0) - the
      index marks only corrections the ledger states.
  LEG drift control: tracked index matching, `make verify-index` rc=0
      with one `(ok)`; after appending one fake entry to the tracked

  Defects found by running this (each fixed, all in the shipped
  tool): a PR-196-style header gained `{ncorrect}` fed to a format

- HONEST LIMITS, WRITTEN INTO THE GENERATED HEADER. `corrected in:`

## PR-198 — THE end_level RUNTIME IS CLOSED END TO END: the apply

KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: .MOV action runtime; end_level directive -> exit contract
ADDRESSES: 0x520e1 0x45750 0x4ac55 0x4ae45 0x5d25e 0x5d2dc 0x5d3b5

      ran, kara, junction, tunga1, tunga2
CODE: no: [READ], the ledger record only
HOOKS: none
OPENS: the 23 other apply methods and the 6 pure-walks; the second
      apply site 0x51101, a different object type; 0x5eb11's
      caller and why it discards the pair; what consumes the
      0x23ea0 two-view cursor; what feeds the 0x603b0 menu-result
      leg, PR-190's exit-4 source; what raises code 0
CLOSES: PR-194 F(b)/(c)'s questions and the PR-198 scope in `## Next`
CORRECTS: PR-194(c) "This pass did rule out the easy shape ... none
      pairs a ds:0xcef40 load with a store into the level object's
      +0x4 within 30 instructions" - refuted as stated: replaying a
      window pairing gives 71 such pairs, and 0x45752->0x4575b is one
      of them, 3 instructions apart, inside 12 bytes; PR-191's similar
