intersects, '!', '*', '|', ',', K_ANY, K_NEVER, AC_BREAK_NEXT,
[rec+0x1a], the 21-byte entry, parse_cond, obj_cond_true,
LL_GOP_ANY, OI-078, PR-87, PR-88, PR-100, PR-101, PR-260
CODE: no: no line of `ported/` changes. The two gaps this
record counts - the group grammar, which differs on 7
clauses, and the K_ANY mask, which 41 clauses ask for and
this port never tests - are separate changes with separate
legs and are put on OI-078, not bundled into a read record.
HOOKS: no red leg: nothing in `ported/` moved. What the record
rests on is the byte-level reading below, one whole-image scan
(0x48000 has exactly one caller), and a census over the 777
texts whose script is kept at /tmp/opencode/pr261_census.py.
MEASURED: (a) THE COMPILER. A .MOV state block's transition
line is read at 0x51e07: the target state's NAME is resolved
to its declared index with 0x53440 (PR-216's one-based list),
the text inside the parentheses is captured by the scanf
format at 0x9225c (' ( %[^) ] %*[)] = ') and copied by
0x57fd0, and the condition text after '=' is handed in edx.
0x51e4d then
calls 0x49610, which is a 10-byte thunk sitting in the padding
right after the 21-byte entry initializer 0x495e2:
`call 0x47d50 / mov [eax+0xd], ebx / mov [eax+0x11], ecx /
ret`. 0x47d50 saves the set pointer and calls 0x47d60 - the
clause parser - so the entry IS a TEventSet, exactly the 13
bytes 0x495e2 clears plus the two payload dwords. The finished
21 bytes are pushed into the state record's vector at
[rec+0x1a] (0x51e54 `lea eax,[esi+0x1a]`, the vector's
{data,size,capacity} header, `rep movs` of 5 dwords + 1 byte,
size at +0x8 = the count 0x52000 reads) - PR-101's table.
(b) THE OP BYTE IS AUTHORED. 0x47d60 (eax = the set, edx = the
text) starts by writing 0 to the op byte at +0xc and memsets
the 12 mask bytes (0x47d73, 0x47d77). It then pulls tokens
with 0x57d30 and the format ` %[^, \r\n\t]` (0x919bc) and
looks at the first character: an ordinary name goes to 0x47de0
and 0x48000, which ORs that bit into the SAME mask; a ',' is
answered at 0x47dfd by taking the next token into the same
mask; and the three operator characters write the op byte of
the whole set - '!' at 0x47dd0/0x47dc8 sets 1, '*' at
0x47dc2 sets 2, '|' at 0x47dbc sets 3, and any of them then
falls through to 0x47de0 so the name after it joins the same
mask. There is no second mask and no node list: one mask, one
operation, last operator wins. Since 0x48000 has exactly ONE
caller in the whole image (0x47de5, inside 0x47d60), this
function is the only place a signal name becomes a bit - the
GEN and Wait clause objects of PR-217/218 are its only other
users (0x46b2f, 0x46b9d).
(c) WHAT THE OPERATIONS DO, restated from PR-260 (b) with the
authoring side: op 0 (subset) = every named bit must be in the
live set, so `A,B` means BOTH; op 1 (disjoint) = none of them
may be, so `!A` means A is absent; op 3 (intersects) = at
least one, so `A|B` means EITHER; op 2 (equal) = exactly that
set. 0x52000 uses the entry's own op byte (match's A side)
against the object's composed key, first match wins.
(d) THE DATA, counted over all 777 texts (script named in
HOOKS): 409 texts carry at least one transition clause, 2764
clauses in all, 429 naming two or more signals. 87 clauses use
'!' - and none of them combines it with ',' or '|', so the
per-name reading is unambiguous in every shipped case. 47 use
'|', 40 of them as the single token `K_ANY`; 7 combine '|'
with a ',' list: ENA.03 A_TO_SWIM(1)=|K_JUMP,K_UP (twice),
ENA2 A_WALK(1)=|K_FWD,AC_BREAK_NEXT, KADMAR.07 and ZARIA.02's
two texts A_DRAP(1)=|K_GEN1,AC_BREAK_NEXT, KADMAR2
A_UPADEK(1)=|AC_DUP,AC_TIME. No clause anywhere uses '*', and
none names K_NEVER; K_ANY appears 41 times, 40 with '|' and
once as `!K_ANY` (SADES.06 A_LAY(1)). ZARIA.01's own lion
texts carry 8 `=|K_ANY` rows (A_WALK(x), A_DEAD(33),
A_DRAP(1), A_BORRING(10) in each of ZAR_LEW.MOV and
ZAR_LEWPL.MOV).
(e) WHY `|K_ANY` IS THE PROOF. PR-260 (f) read K_ANY's mask:
signals 35..39 and 53 = K_BKWD, K_FWD, K_UP, K_DOWN, K_FIRE,
K_JUMP - the six keys the input bridge 0x54910 builds from
[obj+0xa5]/[obj+0xb6]/[obj+0xbe]. With the default op 0 that
mask would mean "all six keys at once", which is nonsense as a
row condition; with op 3 it means "any key", which is exactly
what a `A_WALK = |K_ANY` row wants. The authors write the pipe
40 times out of 41 - the corpus itself confirms the operation
table, and `!K_ANY` = "no key pressed" confirms op 1 the same
way.
(f) THE PORT, and the two places it differs. parse_cond
(ll_play.c:398) splits on '|' into AND-groups and ',' into
terms with a per-term neg, and obj_cond_true (ll_level.c:825)
ORs the groups. Case by case that is the same engine law for
every shipped shape except the 7 of (d): bare names are AND
(subset), '!' is neg (disjoint, and no shipped clause mixes it
with a list), a lone '|' is OR (intersects over single-term
groups); only `A,B|C` diverges - the engine asks for ANY of
A, B, C, the port for (A AND B) OR C. The second gap is
bigger: the port records K_ANY as LL_GOP_ANY (ll_play.c:453)
and NOTHING evaluates gop, so all 41 clauses are dead rows,
including ZARIA.01's 8.
OPENS: in order: (i) the signal-set lifetime PR-260 put first
- still first, and now measurable in one leg that carries the
op byte too, since a row's condition and a persistent set
are read by the same 0x47e40 call; (ii) the
K_ANY gap as a FOCUS 1 item: the six keys of PR-260 (f) are
words this port already carries (the intent words of PR-259),
so an "intersects the input key set" leg is writable, and it
would light 8 dead rows in ZARIA.01; (iii) what the entry's
+0x11 really is downstream: the .MOV line compiler stores the
heap copy of the `(...)` text there (0x51e36, 0x49610), while
PR-101 read that slot as a row index, and 0x53815's
`%[^,], %[^,],%d,%d` (0x9229c) is a second reader of the same
4-field shape that was not followed; (iv) the 7 diverging
clauses of (d); (v) the rest of the OI-078 list unchanged.
CLOSES: PR-260's open item (i) - who writes the op byte of a
compiled condition: the clause parser 0x47d60 writes it from
the authored '!', '*' and '|' at 0x47d73/0x47dbc/0x47dc2/
0x47dc8, and the transition entries carry it from there into
the walk 0x52000. It also settles the shape of the test the
port has been standing in for: a condition is ONE mask and ONE
operation, not a tree of nodes.
CORRECTS: PR-88's "'|' starts another node (OR)" and the
"OR-of-AND-groups" grammar PR-87 shipped as the engine's: the
pipe only sets the operation byte of the one mask, and the
engine has no second node; PR-101's "[entry] +0x11 = a row
index" - on the .MOV path the value stored there is the heap
copy of the text captured from the parentheses (0x51e2a-
0x51e43, `mov [eax+0x11], ecx` in 0x49610); and PR-217/218's

the arm pairs of OI-111 item (2), which the table at 0x47e30
sends the other way: op 2 is 0x47fb2 (byte-identical) and
op 3 is 0x47f42 (the AND is NOT empty).

goes to 0x523f0, which builds the 13-byte record key and
0x53725 ORs THAT in too; then `[[obj+8]+0x54]`, then 0x53520,
then 0x535a0. 0x49580 is the OR: `lea ecx,[eax+0xc]` bounds a
three-dword loop `[eax+i] |= [edx+i]`, the raiser this project
counts at 69 callers; 0x495b0 next door is its empty test.
(b) THE PASS AND ITS FILL. 0x53520 copies the live set to the
stack - 0x53536 `add eax,0x60`, 0x5353b `mov [esp+0x10],eax`
keeps that pointer, 0x5353f reads the op byte at +0xc, 0x5354f
`rep movs` moves the three mask dwords - and calls the walker
0x52000 with the copy in edx. That call site, 0x5356b, is the
only one: no rel32 in the image points at 0x52000 from
anywhere else and no data site holds its address, so the walk
PR-261 described has exactly this one user. After it,
0x5357d calls `[[obj+8]+0x90]` - the apply - and with NO
branch between them 0x53583-0x5358e run `mov ebx,0xc / mov
eax,[esp+0x10] / xor edx,edx / call 0x749a0`: memset
(obj+0x60, 0, 12). 0x749a0 spreads the fill byte through edx
(0x749a2-0x749ae), puts the count in ecx and calls 0x77c00,
which byte-fills to an alignment, then dword-fills through
0x77c37 - the image's fill helper, and 0x77c00 has exactly ONE
caller, that one. The no-match path is the same: 0x52000's
loop exit at 0x5204f calls its own +0x4 verb and returns to
0x53583 too. So the mask is lowered after EVERY transition
pass, matched or not.
(c) THE EXTENT IS EXACTLY THE MASK: 12 bytes, signals 0..95.
The op byte at +0xc and the payload dwords at +0xd and +0x11
are left alone - the same 3-dword extent 0x49580 merges,
0x495b0 tests and 0x495e2 zeroes in an entry's ctor.
(d) THE SWITCH DOES NOT CLEAR. 0x535a0 takes
`lea ebx,[obj+0x60]` at 0x535ad only to pass it as edx to
`[[obj+8]+0xac]` - at 0x535f7, and again at 0x53620 on the
arm that keeps the state. No fill, no store. So the port's
state-entry clears (ll_level.c:1020, 1159, 1241) are inert
duplicates of (b): they always run on a mask that (b) has
already emptied. Left as they are; they become a difference
only if a later read finds a raise landing between the pass
and the switch, and that is named in OPENS.
(e) WHY PR-260 MISSED IT: (b)'s writes reach the bytes through
a pointer built by `add eax,0x60` and a CALL, so the method
PR-260 used - scan the image for instructions that write a
`+0x60` displacement, indexed or not - cannot see them. That
scan stays correct about what it did find: there is no
AND-with-complement lowering instruction anywhere in the code.
(f) THE SHIPPED DATA REQUIRES THE LOWERING. ZARIA.01's own
[A_WSP] block ends with `A_FALL_DOWN(1)=!AC_DRAB`, and after
the lion has once held a ladder that row is true again only if
AC_DRAB is lowered when the answer stops raising it. The same
texts carry a self-entry `A_JUMP(11)=AC_DUP`, and [A_WALK]
raises AC_TIME from rows 10, 11, 3, 4, 5 at gate 6 to arm
`A_DRAP(1)=AC_TIME`: with a monotone mask every one of those
rows would be permanent, and 87 `!`-clauses across the corpus
name signals the game expects to see go away.
(g) THE EXPERIMENT, NOT SHIPPED. With EVERY clear
commented out at HEAD except the one that initialises a
fresh object - the player's ll_play.c:1327, the object
step's ll_level.c:1474, the four bus-raise sites 4719,
5339, 5377, 5421 and the three
state-entry sites 1020, 1159, 1241 - the
ZARIA.01 ladder probe still prints every pin this project
holds at 106 and 119 (the A_JUMP positions 189,602 and
189,550, the frames, DRABINKA's and LINA's `takes its
own K_GEN1` lines), but the `asked ladder DRABINKA`
answers for state 2 from 107 through 120 are gone, and
SURPRISE's 117 line with them: a bit that stays set lets an
earlier entry take the iteration. Five selftest lines that
pin one-tick pulses fail under it. That is what a persistent
mask does, and 0x5358e is
what the engine forbids.
OPENS: in order: (i) the K_ANY evaluation gap, OI-114 - now
first, since the lifetime question that sat in front of it is
closed; (ii) 0x54c00, the ground contact PR-259's guard stands
in for; (iii) AC_EDGE / A_PODCIAG at the top of a climb; (iv)
what the entry's +0x11 is downstream and 0x53815's four-field
reader (PR-261 (iii)); (v) the 7 clauses where the group
grammar differs (PR-261 (iv)); (vi) a raise between the pass
and 0x535a0, which is the only way the port's state-entry
clears of (d) could ever matter; (vii) the `[[obj+8]+0x8c]`
and `[[obj+8]+0x90]` slots named in (a)/(b) and the other 67
callers of 0x49580; (viii) the rest of the OI-078 list
unchanged.
CLOSES: PR-261's open item (i), and the two questions PR-260
put before "dropping the clear" in PR-261: there is nothing to
drop - the clear is the engine's, at the same point in the
step - and the AC_TIME / K_GENn / AC_BREAK_NEXT legs a
persistent set would move stay exactly as PR-182, PR-217 and
PR-257 derived them.
CORRECTS: PR-260's centre sentence - "RAISED BITS ARE NEVER
LOWERED ... every write that clears those bytes is an
allocator/ctor path ... the 21-byte clear 0x495e2 has ZERO
references" - the clear is 0x5358e, inside the transition
pass 0x53520, reached from the step 0x536f0 PR-98 had already
mapped; PR-260 read 0x536f0's two merges and stopped one call
short of the fill. It corrects that record's "the per-frame
key assembler 0x536f0 ... zeroes nothing" only in its
consequence: 0x536f0 does not zero, the pass it calls does.
And with it, the OI-078 header that made the end of the
ZARIA.01 climb this port's own deviation: the climb ends at
298 because the engine's own fill empties the mask when
the ask stops answering.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok);
```

## PR-263 — K_ANY IS A MASK, NOT "A KEY IS DOWN": 0x48000
## ANSWERS THE NAME WITH 0x2001f8 IN DWORD 1, AND THIS PORT'S
## ANY-ROWS ACCEPTED FOUR KEYS THAT ARE NOT IN IT
```
KIND: port
SUBSYSTEM: what a `=|K_ANY` / `=!K_ANY` transition row means -
the name resolver's mask operand, the port's two condition
evaluators, and the seven input bits that mask names.
ADDRESSES: 0x48000, 0x48009, 0x48019, 0x48029, 0x48032,
0x48037, 0x4803d, 0x48043, 0x48048, 0x4804f, 0x4806f,
0x48075, 0x4807d,
0x48087, 0x49541, 0x49543, 0x54910, 0x54931, 0x5493a, 0x54948,
0x54956, 0x54964, 0x549a6, 0x549b4, 0x919ec, 0x919f5, 0x919fb,
0x91a06, 0x53705, 0x53725, 0x523f0
NAMES: K_ANY, AC_K_ANY, K_NEVER, LL_SIG_K_ANY_MASK, K_BKWD,
K_FWD, K_UP, K_DOWN, K_FIRE, K_ALT, K_F1..K_F4, 0x2001f8,
0x60, OI-114, OI-078, PR-87, PR-218, PR-260, PR-261, PR-262
CODE: yes: (i) cond_true's `any` (ll_play.c) drops k_f1..k_f4
- the four weapon-selector keys are signals 41..44, bits 9..12
of the same dword, and the engine's constant lacks them;
(ii) obj_cond_true (ll_level.c) gains the K_ANY case it never
had, testing the object's set against LL_SIG_K_ANY_MASK; (iii)
that mask is defined once, in ll_play.h, from the LL_SIG_*
table with the 0x2001f8 provenance in the comment. The
parser's LL_GOP_ANY capture (PR-218) is untouched: it records
WHICH operand a clause names, and this record is what gives
it a meaning.
HOOKS: red first, three checks, all failing at HEAD and all
derived from the constant above and the fixture's own words,
not from this port's output. Play selftest: with a
`A_WALK(1)=|K_ANY` row (ZARIA.01's `[A_TO_BOR] A_DRAP(1)=
|K_ANY` shape) holding K_F2 alone, `q.sti == 0` FAILED - the
port walked; and with `A_LAY(1)=!K_ANY` (SADES.06's shipped
line 210) holding K_F2 alone, `q.sti == 1` FAILED - the port
refused to lie down. Mov selftest: with `[A_RUN]
A_DEAD(1)=|K_ANY` and a row `2,100,GEN K_FWD`, "a `|K_ANY`
row ignored the K_FWD that was in the set (state 0)" FAILED -
that half was dead code for objects. After the change all
three pass, and so does the pair's other half: `|K_ANY` takes
K_JUMP (53), `=!K_ANY` refuses K_ALT (40), and an object's
`GEN K_GEN1` (54) never satisfies an any-row.
MEASURED: (a) THE MASK. 0x48000 (eax = the set, edx = the
name) starts by comparing the token against the two strings at
0x919ec and 0x919f5 = `AC_K_ANY` / `K_ANY` (0x48009, 0x48019,
through the string-compare 0x76a69); if either matches it
memset-s the 12 mask bytes (0x48029-0x48032, the fill 0x749a0
again), reads dword 1, OR-s in the immediate 0x2001f8 and
writes it back (0x48037-0x48048). In this port's signal table
that constant is bits 3,4,5,6,7,8 and 21 of dword 1 = signals
35,36,37,38,39,40,53 = K_BKWD, K_FWD, K_UP, K_DOWN, K_FIRE,
K_ALT, K_JUMP. It then returns 1 (`mov edx,1 / jmp 0x49543`,
and 0x49543 is `mov eax,edx / ret`; the sibling epilogue
0x49541 `xor edx,edx` is the not-found return). So 0x48000
never writes the op byte at +0xc - PR-261's reading that the
clause parser owns that byte stands - and it REPLACES the mask
built so far, which is why no shipped clause mixes K_ANY with
other names.
(b) THE SAME MASK IS THE INPUT SET. 0x54910 builds the record
key the step ORs into [obj+0x60] at 0x53725 (PR-98, PR-262),
and the only bits it ever sets are those seven: [obj+0xa5] bit
0 -> 39, bit 4 -> 40, bit 5 -> 53 (0x54931-0x54956),
[obj+0xba] nonzero with [obj+0xb6] bit 4 -> 36 else 35
(0x54964-0x5499a, the /32 ordinal idiom), [obj+0xbe] negative
-> 37 and positive -> 38 (0x549a6, 0x549b4). The constant at
(a) is that set, bit for bit. K_ANY does not mean "any key";
it names the input-key mask.
(c) K_NEVER, the other half of the resolver. The second name
pair at 0x4804f/0x4805f (`AC_K_NEVER` / `K_NEVER`) takes the
branch at 0x4806f: `mov ah,[ecx+4] / or ah,0x60 / mov
[ecx],ah` - bits 5 and 6 of mask BYTE 4 = signals 37 and 38 =
K_UP, K_DOWN. So an authored K_NEVER is not empty and not a
bit: it is "both direction intents", the pair that a standing
state never holds. PR-218's "an EMPTY data set" was wrong and
PR-261's "(K_UP,K_DOWN)" is what the bytes say; the port's
capture keeps that name distinct (LL_GOP_NEVER) and no model
acts on it yet, which is unchanged here.
(d) THE REACH, counted over the 777 texts. 41 any-clauses sit
in 14 texts - 40 written `=|K_ANY`, one `=!K_ANY` (SADES.06
line 210), four of them in ZARIA.01's own lion text. All of
them sit in blocks of the lion's
shape - [A_ZABLOK], [A_DEAD], [A_TURN_BACK], [A_TO_BOR],
[A_BORRING], [A_WSP]-shaped names - including the only text
not named `*_LEW.*` (KADMAR.07_0_0.MOV, whose blocks are
[A_ZABLOK], [A_DEAD], [A_TURN_BACK], [A_BORRING]). No
object-only text asks for an any-row, so the object half of
this change has no shipped row behind it: it aligns the second
evaluator with the law and is legged in the unit fixture only.
(e) WHAT THE PORT DID, and what that looked like. The lion's
evaluator answered LL_COND_K_ANY with `any` = eleven keys
(ll_play.c, PR-87) - the seven plus k_f1..k_f4 - so on shipped
data an any-row fired on a weapon-selector key the engine's
mask would not have accepted, and its `!K_ANY` mirror refused
one it would have accepted. K_F1..K_F4 are signals 41..44,
bits 9..12 of the same dword, absent from 0x2001f8, and they
are real bits: the resolver takes them through the /32 path at
0x48087, and the data uses them in AND groups
(`A_FIGHT_UP(1)=K_FIRE,K_GEN1,K_F1`, ZARIA.01 line 82). For
scene objects the case simply did not exist: obj_cond_true's
switch fell to `default: v = 0`, so an object any-row could
never match whatever was in its set.
OPENS: in order: (i) OI-114's other half - carrying the
operation byte instead of the group split, which is where the
7 clauses mixing '|' with a ',' list still differ; (ii) the
K_NEVER mask of (c) and any model that would act on it; (iii)
0x54c00, the ground contact PR-259's guard stands in for;
(iv) AC_EDGE / A_PODCIAG at the top of a climb; (v) the
entry's +0x11 downstream and 0x53815's four-field reader
(PR-261 (iii)); (vi) a raise landing between the pass and
0x535a0 (PR-262 (d)); (vii) `[[obj+8]+0x8c]` /
`[[obj+8]+0x90]` and the other 67 callers of 0x49580; (viii)
the rest of the OI-078 list unchanged.
CLOSES: OI-114's item (b) - "test K_ANY as intersects the
input-key mask" - and with it the claim, made in PR-261's
record and in the OI-078 paragraph, that the any-rows are dead
rows. They are not dead on the lion's side; they were ANSWERED
TOO WIDELY, which is a different and smaller bug.
CORRECTS: PR-260's (f) and PR-261's sentence "K_ANY's mask =
signals 35,36,37,38,39,53 ... the six keys ... minus K_ALT":
the constant is 0x2001f8, which includes bit 8 of that dword,
signal 40 = K_ALT - seven keys, and it is exactly the set
0x54910 raises, so the two readings are the same read. It also
corrects PR-261's "nothing evaluates gop, so all 41 clauses
are dead rows": cond_true has answered LL_COND_K_ANY since
PR-87;
what was wrong was its key set, and the dead half was the
object evaluator, which no shipped text reaches.
GATE: make 0 warnings; verify-all fixtures rc=0 67 (ok);
GATE-FIXTURE-FREE: rc=0 13 (ok) + 22 named (the 23rd SKIP line
is the cmake-windows parity check, which names its own reason:
no vendor/SDL2-2.32.10/x86_64-w64-mingw32 prefix in this tree)

## PR-264 — ONE MASK AND ONE OPERATION PER COMPILED
## CONDITION: THE FOUR ARMS OF 0x47e40, AND THE AND-GROUP
## GRAMMAR IS GONE FROM BOTH EVALUATORS
```
KIND: port
SUBSYSTEM: the transition matcher - ll_mov_tr gains the
engine's operation byte, one shared clause-mask builder, and
the four match arms replace PR-87's OR-of-AND-groups in both
the lion's and the object's evaluator.
ADDRESSES: 0x47d60, 0x47d73, 0x47d9f, 0x47da9, 0x47dbc,
0x47dc2, 0x47dc8, 0x47dd0, 0x47dfd, 0x47e30, 0x47e40,
0x47e4b, 0x47e50, 0x47e63, 0x47ec1, 0x47edc, 0x47f35,
0x47f42, 0x47f9b, 0x47fa2, 0x47fb2, 0x47fd8, 0x49550,
0x49559, 0x4956a, 0x49580, 0x495b0, 0x52000, 0x52024,
0x52033, 0x5203a, 0x53520, 0x5356b, 0x536f0, 0x53705,
0x53733, 0xa68b4, 0xa92d4
NAMES: LL_TOP_SUBSET, LL_TOP_NOT, LL_TOP_EXACT, LL_TOP_ANY,
ll_mov_tr.op, ll_mov_tr_mask, live_bits, TEventSet::match,
Bledna operacja, repz cmps, OI-114, OI-115, PR-87, PR-88,
PR-218, PR-260, PR-261, PR-262, PR-263
CODE: yes: (i) ll_mov_tr carries `op`, the operation byte,
written by parse_cond exactly as the engine's clause parser
does - 0x47d73 clears it, '!' writes 1, '*' writes 2, '|'
writes 3, a ',' writes nothing, last write wins; the row-
clause capture passes NULL and keeps only tokens; (ii)
ll_mov_tr_mask (ll_play.c, declared in ll_play.h) composes
the clause mask: each resolved name's bit, K_ANY's REPLACE
(0x48037-0x48048), K_NEVER's union (0x4806f-0x4807d), and
NOTHING for a name in no table (the resolver's not-found
return 0x49541, its value discarded at 0x47de5); (iii)
cond_true (ll_play.c) and obj_cond_true (ll_level.c) answer
the four arms over a COMPOSED live set: live_bits() = the
lion's p->sig plus the facing-relative key bits plus the
broke/ac_time bits (what 0x54910 and the rows put into
[obj+0x60], PR-262/263); the object's o->sig plus the brk
bit; (iv) an empty mask is never taken - PR-88's convention
kept, now written as a named guard. The group numbers and
per-term negs stay in the terms for the row-clause capture;
they mean nothing to a match.
HOOKS: red first, four checks, all failing at HEAD and all
derived from the table at 0x47e30 and the fixture's own
authored words, never from this port's output. Play
selftest, ENA.03's exact line 551 `A_WALK(1)=|K_JUMP,K_UP`:
holding K_UP ALONE, `q.sti == 1` FAILED - the port demanded
both; K_JUMP alone FAILED likewise; the controls (both,
neither) frame it. Mov selftest: an object's
`A_DEAD(1)=|AC_TIME,AC_EDGE` with a `2,100,GEN AC_TIME` row
- "refused the raised AC_TIME alone" FAILED; and
`=!AC_TIME,AC_ONAIR` with only AC_EDGE in the set - the
engine's disjoint arm answers TRUE, the port never took it.
All four green now. Capture pins added: op == 3 for `|`
clauses, op == 1 for `!`, and
ll_mov_tr_mask(`|K_ANY`) == LL_SIG_K_ANY_MASK. PR-263's
K_ANY pair and every earlier grammar leg pass unchanged.
MEASURED: (a) THE MATCH. 0x47e40 (eax = the compiled 21-byte
entry, edx = the set handed to it): `mov al,[eax+0xc] /
cmp al,3 / ja 0x47fd8` then `jmp [eax*4+0x47e30]`
(0x47e4b-0x47e62) - four entries, and the fifth arm builds
the string at 0xa92d4, PR-260's "TEventSet::match :Bledna
operacja". The arms: 0 SUBSET (0x47e63) copies the clause,
ANDs the two sets through the AND method 0x49550 (the dword
loop 0x49559-0x4956a is `and edi,ebx` per dword) and
requires the AND byte-identical to the CLAUSE (`repz cmps`
0x47ec1) - true iff EVERY name in the clause is live;
1 DISJOINT (0x47edc) runs the same AND and hands it to the
empty-test 0x495b0 (call at 0x47f35); 2 EQUAL (0x47fb2)
`repz cmps` of the two sets directly; 3 INTERSECTS (0x47f42)
runs the AND and answers `sete` of 0x495b0 (0x47f9b,
0x47fa2) - NOT empty. PR-260's "0 subset, 1 disjoint, 2
equal, 3 intersects" is the code, not an inference.
(b) THE OP CHAIN, PR-261's reading confirmed with one new
detail: a token whose first char is alphanumeric (the
ctype-table test `test BYTE PTR [edx+0xa68b4],0xc0` at
0x47da9) goes straight to the name path 0x47de0, so an
operator is its OWN token: 0x47dbc writes 3 for '|', 0x47dc2
2 for '*', 0x47dc8/0x47dd0 1 for '!', all jmp 0x47dd2 and
the loop runs on while the delimiter is ',' (0x47dfd) -
every later name folds into the SAME mask under the SAME
byte. There is no second node: PR-87's "engine's own
evidence for OR-of-AND-groups", written into the ll_play.h
enum comment, is wrong; that comment is corrected in place,
and obj_cond_true's PR-88 paragraph with it.
(c) NO GUARD ON THE PATH. The step 0x536f0 merges the two
built sets into [obj+0x60] (0x53705-0x5370c,
0x5371c-0x53725 - the second merge is the row/key builder
0x523f0's) and calls `[obj.vmt+0x54]` at 0x53733 with NO
test of the set; 0x53520 copies the 13 bytes (0x53531-
0x53559) and calls the walk 0x52000 (0x5356b); 0x52000
walks EVERY entry and calls TEventSet::match on each
(0x52024-0x5203a). 0x495b0 appears on this path only INSIDE
match's own arms. So on the path read so far an empty
composed set still asks, and under arm 1 a `!`-clause is
TRUE on a clean step. What is NOT read: which method
[vmt+0x54] is for the .MOV state-record class (0x53520's
address is at no data site, PR-261 counted) and whether it
guards. This port keeps its object-side gate `(o->sig ||
brk1)`; removing it moves shipped rows, so it needs the
method read first - that, and the empty-mask question, are
OI-115.
(d) REACH, recounted over the 777 texts (2764 clauses):
ALL 47 '|' clauses LEAD a comma list; exactly 7 mix '|'
with a ',': ENA.03:551/575 `|K_JUMP,K_UP`, ENA2:213
`|K_FWD,AC_BREAK_NEXT`, KADMAR.07_0_0:660 and ZARIA.02
LEW:119/LEWPL:116 `|K_GEN1,AC_BREAK_NEXT`, KADMAR2:288
`|AC_DUP,AC_TIME`. Those 7 are the ONLY shipped rows whose
reading changes - under the old grammar they ANDed the
comma list, under the engine's they intersect. No clause
combines '!' with ',' (0 of 87), none uses '*', none names
K_NEVER, so the shipped corpus exercises operations 0, 1
and 3, and the '!'-arm difference exists only in fixture
shapes. ZARIA.01 has no mixed clause - its 8 any-rows are
all the single-name `=|K_ANY`, which read identically both
ways. Measured: the whole fixture suite and the ZARIA.01
climb legs are byte-identical, and none of the 7 clauses
is driven anywhere in it.
(e) THE PORT: the match lives once per side; both call
ll_mov_tr_mask. An unresolved name contributes no bit, so a
clause naming only such tokens masks to 0 and is refused by
the guard - the engine's arm 0 would take it vacuously;
that half-ask is recorded, not guessed (no shipped clause
does it).
OPENS: in order: (i) OI-115 (a) - which method
[obj.vmt+0x54] is for the .MOV record class, the only
unread step on the match path, and with it whether the
port's object-side `(o->sig || brk1)` gate may go;
(ii) OI-115 (b), the empty-mask/vacuous subset; (iii) the
top of a climb, AC_EDGE / A_PODCIAG (OI-078's lead);
(iv) the entry's +0x11 downstream and 0x53815's four-field
reader (PR-261 (iii)); (v) a raise landing between the
pass and 0x535a0 (PR-262 (d)); (vi) `[[obj+8]+0x8c]` /
`+0x90]` and the other 67 callers of 0x49580; (vii) the
rest of the OI-078 list unchanged.
CLOSES: OI-114 - item (a) (the operation, carried and
matched) was its only open half, item (b) closed at PR-263;
PR-261's "7 clauses where this port differs" is discharged,
those 7 now read as the engine reads them. The mechanism
row is gone; its unread residue opened as OI-115.
CORRECTS: PR-87's line in the ll_play.h enum comment -
"'|' = separate node = OR ... the engine's own evidence for
PR-87's OR-of-AND-groups reading": there is no second node
and no group semantics in the compiled entry (fixed in
place). PR-88's obj_cond_true paragraph - "'|' starts
another node (OR) - the same OR-of-AND-groups the player
evaluator uses": same correction, replaced by the arms
above. And PR-261's "the corpus writing the pipe 40 times
out of 41 is the data-side proof" - ALL 47 pipes lead a
comma list, which is the same point measured cleanly.

line is the cmake-windows parity check, which names its own
reason: no vendor/SDL2-2.32.10/x86_64-w64-mingw32 prefix
in this tree)

## PR-265 — THE TRANSITION PASS IS UNCONDITIONAL: 0x53520'S
## ONLY CALL SITE IS A DIRECT CALL FROM THE STEP, AND THE
## PORT'S OBJECT-SIDE `(o->sig || brk1)` GATE GOES
```
KIND: port
SUBSYSTEM: the object step's per-iteration transition ask -
the port's guard that skipped the whole pass when nothing was

CODE: no: no line of `ported/` changes. The three gaps this
record counts - the F-family's source, the name of K_FIRE's
raiser, and the twelve control/global tests - each need their
own legs; they go to OI-116, not into a read record.
HOOKS: no red leg: nothing in `ported/` moved. Every claim
below is read from the image (a disassembly of
build/leo/leo.img at adjust-vma 0x10000 plus a byte dump of
its data) or counted over the 777 captured .MOV texts.
MEASURED: (a) WHAT [obj+8] IS. The step keeps the object in
ecx and reads [ecx+8] four times - 0x536f8 (then +0x8c at
0x536ff), 0x5372a (then +0x54 at 0x53733), 0x53750 (+0x54
again at 0x53755), 0x53758 (+0x28 at 0x5375d). [obj+8] is a
PLAIN DATA ARRAY of code pointers, stride 4: read the SEP2
class's table 0x96fd8 as bytes and its entries are
+0x28 -> 0x52a90, +0x2c -> 0x53d80, +0x54 -> 0x55070,
+0x8c -> 0x54910, +0x98 -> 0x23a50, +0xb0 -> 0x544f0. So
the slots the step calls are compile-time data, which is why
PR-265 found no code site storing a function address into
them. Installed at construction, counted 408 sites of the
shape `mov [reg+8],0x9xxxx`; in 312 of them a companion
`mov [reg+0xc],<same table - 8>` follows within 3
instructions - always that same base minus 8 - and in the
other 96 it is not adjacent. The pattern around
one (0x1f872-0x1f8a2): compare a class-name string with
0x76a69 (verified: walks two strings, returns the
difference), `mov eax,0x12c / call 0x5c320` (the allocation
helper: size in eax, calls 0x7521f), `call 0x62e40` (the
base object ctor: calls 0x3ff70, zeroes +0x120/+0x124,
installs 0x97bc0/0x97bb8 and then 0xa348c/0xa3484 at +8/
+0xc), then the override. 138 of the 408 installs name to a
class string that way; they are the level scripts' class
names (ARMATA, BRAMA, KALAMARN, SEP2, ...) and the player's
own (TLewZaria, TLewZariaB, TLewEna2, TLewKadmar2,
TLewKara, TLewJunction, TLewTunga1). The step 0x536f0 has
exactly ONE caller: 0x550b4, inside 0x550a0 (which zeroes
[obj+0xe6]/[obj+0xea] and enters the step); 0x550a0 is the
shared advance-entry, called from 10 sites.
(b) THE +0x8c SLOT IS THE CLASS'S SIGNAL COLLECTOR, and it
differs by class: 0x54910 in 207 of the 408 tables (the
scene-object families), 0x504e0 in the 18 tables of the
TLew* classes. 0x54910 builds a 12-byte set from the object
OWN fields: [obj+0xa5] bit 0x1 -> 35, bit 0x10 -> 40, bit
0x20 -> 53; if [obj+0xba] != 0 then [obj+0xb6] bit 0x10 ?
36 : 35 (`sete al / add al,0x23`, 0x54964-0x5496e); [obj+
0xbe] < 0 -> 37 (0x549a6), > 0 -> 38 (0x549b4). It writes
13 bytes (the 12 bits plus the byte at +0xc) into the
caller's out-param and returns it (0x549c1-0x549db) - the
same 13-byte shape PR-260 read. 0x504e0 (the lion classes)
first calls [[obj+8]+0xf8] and tests it (0x504ee-0x504f9);
then twelve tests of the form (`[obj+0xa5]/[0xa6]/[0xa7]`
bit set AND `ds:0xcef5c..0xcef80` != 0) each store an index
0..11 at [obj+0xee], last match wins (0x50514-0x50631);
then `cmp [obj+0xee],0xb / ja` and `jmp cs:[eax*4+0x504b0]`
(0x5064e-0x50653) into a 12-case table whose entries
0x5065b..0x506a8 OR exactly one bit into a fresh 12-byte
set - index i -> bit 41+i, i.e. K_F1..K_F12; then it calls
0x54910 on the same object (0x506d6) and merges the two
sets with 0x49580 (0x506ee). So a lion step's live set =
the field-derived set UNION at most one F-signal. What the
+0xf8 slot means is NOT read: 0x96fd8's is the advance-entry
0x550a0, TLewZaria's (0x96960) is 0x1e2f0 = `return [obj+
0xee] == 2 || == 3`, and 0x96874's is 0x22f10 = `return ds:
0xceba4`.
(c) THE +0x54 SLOT IS 0x55070 and it holds no guard: its
whole body is three calls - [[tbl]+0xb0] (0x544f0) with
edx = &obj+0xd6, 0x541f0 with edx = &obj+0x89, and [[tbl]+
0x98] (0x23a50) - with no test of [obj+0x60] anywhere
(0x55070-0x5509f). PR-265's finding holds at this level
too: the two calls that bracket the pass and the apply are
themselves unguarded. The +0x2c slot (called at spawn,
0x539cf-0x539d4, with edx = [obj+8]) is 0x53d80: `mov eax,
0x28 / call 0x5c320 / call 0x56620(edx=1) / mov [obj+0x54],
eax` - it FILLS the object's [obj+0x54] field with a
40-byte sub-object. The +0x28 slot 0x52a90 calls [[tbl]+
0x30], compares with ds:0xcf0e4, calls [[tbl]+0x20], negs
and adds 0x17c and clamps to 0xff (0x52a99-0x52ac3): a
frame/index computation, read no further. The other
[[reg+0x8c]] call site in the image is 0x3ee18, inside a
short function that merges a set into [[ecx+0x3c]+0x60] and
returns - not the step.
(d) THE NAME POOL IS IN BIT ORDER, and this port's table
matches it exactly. The resolver is one unrolled chain of 73
strcmp calls through 0x76a69 from 0x48000 to 0x49540: first
0x919ec AC_K_ANY / 0x919f5 K_ANY -> dword 1 |= 0x2001f8
(PR-263's mask), then 0x919fb AC_K_NEVER / 0x91a06 K_NEVER
-> byte 4 |= 0x60, then 69 names from 0x91a0e to 0x91c5e,
each branch storing its OWN hardcoded index - AC_BLOK 0 ...
AC_KOLO 34, K_BKWD 35 ... K_ALT 40, K_F1 41 ... K_F12 52,
K_JUMP 53, K_GEN1 54 ... K_GEN5 58, AC_PLAT_OFF 59 ...
AC_DISAPPEAR 67, AC_EV_MAX 68 (spot-checked: the K_JUMP
branch at 0x49071 stores 0x35; the AC_BREAK_NEXT branch is
0x48121 = entry 2). An unknown token falls through to 0x49541
`xor edx,edx` - no bit set, "not found" - and the K_ANY
branch jumps to 0x49543, past that zeroing, i.e. it reports
"found". The pool order IS the bit order, and it reproduces
every number of this port's LL_SIG_* table (ll_play.h:243-
266, PR-217) name for name: 0..34, 35..40, 41..52, 53,
54..58, 59..67, 68 = AC_EV_MAX. It also shows two spellings
this port does not accept, AC_K_ANY and AC_K_NEVER; counted,
0 shipped clauses use them.
(e) THE F-FAMILY'S REACH, counted over the 777 texts: 199
active condition lines name K_F1..K_F12 (K_F1 111, K_F2 55,
K_F3 14, K_F4 7, K_F6 1, K_F7 1, K_F8 2, K_F10 1, K_F12 7)
in 12 files, and every one of those 12 is a lion text - 10
`*_LEW*` files plus KADMAR.07_0_0's player-shaped block;
ZARIA.01's two lion texts carry 24 each. No scene-object
text names an F-signal, which fits (b): 0x54910, the scene
classes' collector, raises none. This port raises K_F1..K_F4
from the raw F1..F4 keys (ll_play.c:1108-1118) and never
raises K_F5..K_F12, so those 12 name occurrences can never
match here, and the 187 others match from a different input
than the engine's. Recorded as OI-116.
OPENS: in order: (i) the top of a climb, AC_EDGE / A_PODCIAG
(OI-078's lead, unchanged by this record: no climb row names
an F-signal); (ii) OI-116 - the F-family's source: what
[obj+0xa5]/[0xa6]/[0xa7] are and who writes them, what the
twelve globals ds:0xcef5c..0xcef80 hold (one writer is the
indexed store at 0x39df4/0x39e03), and what [obj+0xee]
means; (iii) who raises K_FIRE 39 - 0x54910 does not raise
it, yet ZARIA.01's texts name it 56 times, so a second
writer of [obj+0x60] exists and is un-named; (iv) OI-115
(b), the empty compiled mask; (v) the entry's +0x11
downstream and 0x53815's four-field reader (PR-261 (iii));
(vi) a raise landing between the pass and 0x535a0 (PR-262
(d)); (vii) the rest of the OI-078 list unchanged.
CLOSES: OI-115 (d) - what [obj+8] is (the class behavior
table, installed by the name-comparing factory) and which
methods answer its +0x8c (the collector: 0x54910 generic,
0x504e0 for the lion classes), +0x54 (0x55070, three calls,
no guard), +0x28 (0x52a90) and +0x2c (0x53d80) slots. Also
settles the name question PR-263 left: the bit numbers are
the pool order at 0x91a0e, and this port already agrees with
all 69.
CORRECTS: PR-265 (d)'s wording. It spoke of "the base record
ctors ZERO +0x54 (0x524ba, 0x52548)" while asking about the
step's slots: those two stores zero the +0x54 of the .MOV
STATE-RECORD class (the same ctors store the 0xa25d4 table
at +0x44, PR-101), while the step's calls go through the
SCENE OBJECT's table [[obj+8]+0x8c / +0x54 / +0x28] - two
different +0x54 slots, and the object's own +0x54 is a
heap pointer filled by 0x53d80, not a function. PR-263's
"bit-identical to what input bridge 0x54910 raises": 0x54910
raises six names - 35, 36, 37, 38, 40, 53 - and never 39
K_FIRE, so K_ANY's mask is not that bridge's output; and the
lion's collector is not 0x54910 but 0x504e0, which calls
0x54910 and unions one F-signal onto it.

(d) THE ANSWER VERB AND ITS BLOCKS. 0x3f1c0 (slot +0x78,
called with eax = self, ebx = the asker, edx = the answer
set): state gate [self+0x5c] == 2 (PR-216); P1 (0x3f228-
0x3f24d) = the asker's point in [self+0xc5] -> the answer is
AC_EDGE ALONE; P2 (0x3f256-0x3f2a4) = the point in
[self+0xb1..0xbd] at full extent, FALSE -> inert (0x3f364);
P3 (0x3f2dc-0x3f355) = the point in that block inset to its
middle 70% (n = 0x46 at 0x3f278) -> AC_DRAB|AC_DRAB_CATCH,
else AC_DRAB alone. This port models it as ladder_answer_core
(ll_level.c:5204-5241) with the SAME three steps. The sibling
verb 0x3f390 (held once, at 0xa1e74 - another class) is the
same tree with n = 0x32 (0x3f448) and its own AC_EDGE branch
at 0x3f41d.
(e) THE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: for THIS class both blocks are
constants, so the verb answers NOTHING, in any state, at any
position. [self+0xc5] is (0,0,0,0) from both ctors and is
never written again: the image contains FIVE references to
+0xc5 in all - 0x3f159, 0x3f228, 0x3f3f8 (all `lea`, all
reads, all inside the two verbs) and 0x1f91d / 0x4e88c (the
ctors' own zero-fill). The [obj+0xb1] block is (1,1,1,1) or
(1,1,_,1); its 29 write sites in the image belong to other
classes' ctors and to the per-class parameter parsers - which
do exist and do fill this field region: 0x2e051 sscanf's
` damage = %d` (0x90bad) into [obj+0xb1], and 0x30167/
0x30174/0x30189 parse ` damage` (0x90de8) into [obj+0xb1] and
` up = %d` (0x90df6) into [obj+0xee], the format-string pool
at 0x90b80-0x90e5d being the authored per-class grammar
(`damage`, `energy`, `up`, `fire`, `v_bounds`, `cord`, `dir`,
`ident`, `number`) - but NOT ONE function reachable from
0x97cdc's slots calls the parser 0x49920 (every slot function
scanned, 0x400 bytes each: zero hits). With pt_in_blk
INCLUSIVE, a point lies in (0,0,0,0) or (1,1,1,1) only at
those coordinates, so P1 and P2 are both FALSE for a lion
standing at, say, (213,507): the verb takes the inert exit.
The port's two pinned legs agree in OUTCOME - `play tick 119:
asked ladder DRABINKA/drab.mov at state [23]: ... 213,507 ...
168,517..215,583 -> no` (Makefile:1835) and the mirror at
1874 - but by a different route: the port hands P1/P2 blocks
built from the object's own shape element (the `168,517..
215,583` in the leg text), the engine hands (0,0,0,0) and
(1,1,1,1). That divergence is OI-117.
(f) EVERY RAISER OF AC_EDGE IN THE IMAGE, counted: exactly
six sites set bit 8 of a set. Two are the answer verbs' P1
branches, 0x3f24d and 0x3f41d, dead as shown above. Two are
inside one comparison family that works on the object's own
position fields: 0x27ea3 (`esi = [obj+0x126] - its
counterpart's x`, `test esi,esi / jl` then the or) and
0x2811c (`eax = [obj+0x126] - [that].x`), and the SAME
function raises K_GEN1/K_GEN2 two instructions later -
0x28127 `cmp [obj+0x112],0` / 0x2812a `sete al / add al,0x36`
(54/55). One, 0x3c2d3, ors bit 8 into a stack set after a
rect test against [esi+0x50]. The last, 0x41aa0, is the only
one that raises AC_EDGE INTO ITS OWN OBJECT'S SET - `lea eax,
[ecx+0x60] / or BYTE PTR [eax+1],1` - and it is gated by an
fcmp of two FLOATS, [ecx+0x10b] against [ecx+0x12f]
(0x41a8c-0x41a9b), plus [ecx+0x5c] == 1 at 0x41ab1. None of
the six belongs to the lion's own class table 0x96874 or to
any TLew* table. So the AC_EDGE that ZARIA.01's
`A_PODCIAG(1)=AC_EDGE,K_UP` needs comes from an object the
lion stands on, and which of these owners it is - above all
0x41aa0, the float-gated self-raiser - is the lead now.
OPENS: in order: (i) the owner of 0x41aa0's function and of
the 0x27ea3/0x2811c family (what classes, what [obj+0x10b]/
[obj+0x12f] floats are), matched against the objects ZARIA.01
places at the top of the ladder - this is OI-078's new lead;
(ii) OI-117, the answer verb's blocks: this port feeds P1/P2
from its own element box, the engine's are class-ctor
constants, and no authored parameter fills them for this
class; (iii) OI-116, the F-family and the missing K_FIRE
raiser; (iv) OI-115 (b), the empty compiled mask; (v) the
entry's +0x11 downstream and 0x53815's four-field reader;
(vi) a raise landing between the pass and 0x535a0; (vii) the
rest of the OI-078 list unchanged.
CLOSES: OI-078's "AC_EDGE unmodelled" lead for the ladder:
the engine's ladder never raises AC_EDGE either - its answer
verb is dead by construction - so the port's ladder model is
not the missing piece, and the search moves to the raiser
census at (f).
CORRECTS: PR-266 (c)'s "the step 0x536f0 has exactly ONE
caller, 0x550b4 inside 0x550a0": true of DIRECT calls, but
0x536f0 is also a class verb - it sits at +0x14 of the
0x97cdc family tables, and `call DWORD PTR [reg+0x14]` sites
exist. PR-266 (b)'s two-collector list is incomplete: a third
family (34 tables, this class among them) has +0x8c = 0x23a60,
the empty-set stub, so those objects have no signal collector
at all. And this port's own model note (ll_level.c:5057) is
right that P1 tests [self+0xc5] but never asked what that
block holds: for this class it is four zeros.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok);

MEASURED: (a) THE FACTORY, IN FULL. 357 strcmp branches, 223
that allocate, 218 distinct class names, 197 behavior tables
now named to their class. Each branch: `mov eax,<size>; call
0x5c320`, one initializer, and - in the branch or in that
initializer - `mov [obj+8],<table>` with `[obj+0xc] =
<table>-8`. Most classes share a small set of initializers:
96 branches call 0x53ff0, 39 call 0x531f0 (itself a wrapper
of 0x52860), 27 call 0x52860, 5 of the lion classes call
0x500b0. 0x53ff0 is the DEFAULT initializer: 0x53ff0-0x5402b
zeroes [obj+0xb5], builds the embedded point object described
in (d), and stores the pair 0xa23b8/0xa23b0 at [obj+8] and
[obj+0xc] - so a class that installs no table of its own is
still a working object. The rest have their own (0x1e0a0
TLewZaria -> table 0x96960; 0x62e40 SEP -> 0x97bc0; and a
second default initializer, 0x54030, at 38 call sites, which
calls 0x532c0 and repeats the same point-object stores).
(b) THE +0x18 SLOT IS THE RECORD VERB: it is the only slot in
any table that calls the scanf helper 0x49920 - 82 tables do,
no other slot in any table does - and each one reads its own
class's parameters out of the placed object's authored block:
` damage = %d`, ` bounds = %d, %d`, ` v_bounds = %d, %d`,
` speed`, ` invincible`, ` hit_time`, ` scope`, ` xchg`,
` end_pos = %i , %i` ... The formats live at 0x90b80-0x91d20.
The two the OI-078 lead wanted, ` bounds = %d, %d` (0x3b500)
and ` v_bounds = %d, %d` (0x3b6d0), fill [obj+0x122] and
[obj+0x126] in the +0x18 verbs of PTAKPLAT, TWINDA and
GEJZER - the fields 0x27e40 and 0x27fd0 compare against
another object's position (see (f)).
(c) THE LADDER'S TWO RECTANGLES ARE AUTHORED TEXT, END TO
END. ZARIA.01's own placement text (hd_files/ETAPY, read as
bytes) authors four lines per climbable object:
`DRABINKA,drab.ani,drab.mov,180,510` / `1 33,-3` /
`23,30;53,160` / `30,50`, and the same shape for two LINA
ropes at (125,292) and (525,525). The class's +0x18 verb
(0x3f0f0, held by BOTH 0x97cdc and 0xa1dfc) reads all three:
0x44f10/0x44e90 for the contact-point list; then 0x49f90
with the format at 0x91d00 = `%d,%d;%d,%d , ` into
[obj+0xb1..0xbd] as x0,y0,x1,y1, and 0x3f124-0x3f14b adds
the placement x,y so the column is ABSOLUTE from load and
never follows the object; then 0x4a0b0 with the format at
0x91d0f = `%d,%d` reads the bare pair (a,b) and
0x3f159-0x3f175 writes [obj+0xc5..0xd1] as x0 = x1 = a, y0 =
b-0x50, y1 = b, and 0x4a050 widens it: `n = [obj+0xb9] -
[obj+0xb1] + 1` (the authored column's width plus one),
`half = ((x1-x0) - n) halved with sign`, then x0 += half and
x1 -= half - for x0 = x1 = a and n = 31 that is a-15 .. a+15,
as wide as the authored column and centred on a; and
0x3f187-0x3f1a7 adds the placement x,y to that block as well.
This port parses all three lines (PR-243/PR-246/PR-247) and
its loader prints the same column this arithmetic gives:
`DRABINKA/drab.mov authors an authored rectangle: absolute
(203,540)-(233,670)`.
(d) THE ANSWER VERB ASKS WITH THE ASKER'S LIVE POSITION, AND
WITH THOSE RECTANGLES - AND 144 CLASSES SHARE THE PROTOCOL.
0x3f1c0's three tests, read through: 0x3f222 calls the ASKER's
+0x68 verb - 0x23900, three instructions, `add eax,0xd6; ret`,
and it is the +0x68 verb of 144 of the 204 class tables -
which hands back the asker's own embedded point object at
[obj+0xde]. That object is filled by the engine on every step:
0x54e0a-0x54e17 copies [obj+0x00] and [obj+0x04] (the live
x,y) into [obj+0xd6] and [obj+0xda], and the default
initializers build it: 0x53ff0 zero [obj+0xd6]/[obj+0xda] and
store the shared table 0x98278 at [obj+0xde] (0x54004-0x5400b,
repeated by the other default initializer 0x54030 at
0x5403c-0x54045), and 0x98278's +0x8 verb is 0x23e00. So
0x3f230 asks the asker's point object, through its own +0x8
verb, "are you inside MY [obj+0xc5]": P1 is the asker's live
position inside the edge band. P2 (0x3f256, 0x3f29f) is the
same verb against MY [obj+0xb1] column, and P3
(0x3f283-0x3f2b1) copies that column into a stack object
carrying the table at 0x98274, narrows it with 0x49fb0 at
n = 0x46 = 70 per cent (x only) and asks again. So the
engine's ladder answers with AUTHORED geometry and the asker's
live point; and the port's `ladder_answer_core` already has
exactly that shape (P1 edge, P2 rung, P3 the 70% copy,
`pt_in_blk`, `blk_probe70` = 0x49fb0, and `ask` = `pt_of(
asker)` = the lion's rounded position) - it only builds the
two rectangles from the wrong source: `blk_of_obj` takes the
object's current art bbox.
(e) THE NUMBERS, FOR ZARIA.01. Placement (180,510), pair
(a,b) = (30,50), column 23,30;53,160. The engine's column is
(203,540)-(233,670) - 31 px wide, 130 px tall, the authored
ladder from its top at y 540 to its foot at y 670; its edge
band is x = 30+-15 plus 180 = 195..225 and y = 50-80..50 plus
510 = 480..560, the top of that column and 80 px above it;
its P3 middle is x = 207..229. This port builds both roles
from `blk_of_obj`: the current row's element box positioned at
the object, which for this class is the DRAB.SEQ art shape,
42x48 by the port's own note at ll_level.c:5110. Those are
different rectangles from the engine's on both axes, so an ask
at a given position can answer either way; in game terms the
engine's AC_EDGE is the top of the authored ladder - which is
what the level's own script asks for,
`A_PODCIAG(1)=AC_EDGE,K_UP` and `A_SCIAG(1)=AC_EDGE,K_DOWN`.
The two pinned legs are not moved by any of this: they print
the 0x44ec0 contact-point test (PR-254's ask probe) against
the ASKER's box, not this verb, and both stay `-> no`.
(f) EVERY AC_EDGE RAISER, BY OWNER. Six sites raise bit 8,
each found through the table cell that holds its function:
0x3f1c0 at 0x97cdc+0x78 (DRABINKA), 0x3f390 at 0xa1dfc+0x78
(LINA), 0x3c270 at 0xa0230+0x78 (DRAB - a third ladder-like
class, size 0x64, ctor 0x52860, with its two rectangles

The two +0xa8 raisers compare [obj+0x126]/[obj+0x12a]
against another object's position - the fields the authored

the only two raisers of K_GEN1/K_GEN2 in the image (`sete al

NOSOROG, PAJAK, PALMA, PIANA, POCISK, RYBA, SEP, SPLYW,
SURPRISE, WODA, ZARROW and its lion TLewZaria); none of the
other five owners is among them, so this level's AC_EDGE can

(g) THE TWO LADDER CLASSES ARE NOT ONE. DRABINKA (0x1f8b3)
installs 0x97cdc/0x97cd4; LINA (0x4e81d) allocates the same
0xd9, calls the same 0x531f0, writes the same member table

change ships a failing test: the cam-y leg's NEW pins (the
(c) paragraph below derives them) were written against HEAD

PR-257-leg script run (FWD at 1, JUMP at 100) falls

through the y 682 line; PR-256 measured 668 -> 688 across
the 681 grass at x 127-128.
(b) THE LAW: the engine's ground answer is a shape-box
CONTACT - PR-97's hit test 0x42a70 and push-out 0x42de0,
reached through the element vtable +0x48/+0x50 slots. A
body whose box overlaps a terrain line IS in contact with
it; the engine cannot have a body stand below a line its
box overlapped on the previous position step. The port
queries one point per iteration (PR-135 item 11); at one
point the content of that law is CONTINUITY: the lines
crossed between two iterations are exactly those between
the previous contact line and this one. So the search top
moves from `start - LL_PLAY_STEP` to
`min(start, prev_line) - LL_PLAY_STEP`, where prev_line is
the rounded y + contact recorded at the end of the LAST
iteration (recomputed from the final position: the ground
pass may have snapped y and section 7's `M` delta moved it
again). Below the line the old reach is untouched, so the
RAN-shelf step-up case the old comment names keeps its
exact behaviour.

ground (`1 -50,680!408,684;`) at x 128 reads 681 by the
polyline's own interpolation (680 + 4*(178/458)); PR-97's

contact gives pos y 653; grounded 1 from 70 on; x 122 at
82 is the LICHA SEMI push-out drift, the push-out law
itself unchanged. The negative "no grounded A_DRAP at
70-82" pin becomes positive: grounded 1 across the range.

195,654 grounded 1 by tick 131 and stays - 654 + 28 = 682,
the main-ground line at x 195 interpolated the same way.

MEASURED: (a) THE GRAMMAR. The keyword pool at 0x91901-
0x91945 reads `atc_on atc_off lock lock2 unlock unlock2
ground_on ground_off chdir ldir rdir pos goto gotorel
goto_rel I F IC FC M` - one handler per keyword in the chain
at 0x4640b ff., each reached through a handler-list walk at
0x45df0. A row's third field compiles to a 12-byte command
object {+0x4 = vtable, +0x8 = value}: lock=0xa10d8 val 1,
unlock=0xa10d8 val 0, lock2=0xa10c0 val 1, unlock2=0xa10c0
val 0, ground_on=0xa10a8 val 1, ground_off=0xa10a8 val 0;

## PR-275 — THE SURFACE-TABLE LAYER BEHIND THE ONE-SHOT [obj+0xea]
## SNAP IS READ: 0x45120 PARSES A COUNT+SEPARATOR TABLE TEXT,
## 0x45200 LOCALIZES IT, 0x45380 BRACKETS A POINT BY x, AND
## 0x45320 ATTACHES A PREDICTED-POSITION SNAP TO A TARGET
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the engine's surface-provider family 0x45120 /
0x45200 / 0x45380 / 0x45320 - the producer side of the
[obj+0xe6]/[obj+0xea] channel PR-110 found written, PR-121
found applied in the position step and PR-122 decoded the
gap arithmetic of. Continues PR-121 items 2-3 and PR-122
OPENS 1-2. No `ported/` change.
ADDRESSES: 0x45120, 0x45200, 0x45320, 0x45380, 0x453d0,
0x45400, 0x455a0, 0x541f0, 0x54759, 0x54804, 0x288d0,
0x288e2, 0x380d0, 0x1e512, 0x1e570, 0x1e970, 0x3dd60,
0x76a64, 0x76bb7, 0x49920, 0x4a0b0
NAMES: OI-073, OI-078, A_PODCIAG, A_FG_PACKA_UP,
A_FG_PACKA, [obj+0xa5], [obj+0xa9], [obj+0xee], [obj+0xca],
[obj+0xce], [obj+0xe2], [obj+0xe6], [obj+0xea], kind byte,
surface provider, polyline, snap, ZARIA_A.PLT, PR-110,
PR-121, PR-122, PR-235, PR-272, PR-273, PR-274, ZARIA.01,
ly_climb
CODE: no: no line of `ported/` or of the Makefile changes,
so there is no behaviour for a red leg to catch.
HOOKS: PR-122 OPENS 1 asked "what the 13-byte records are
and which class answers with an index" (0x45380 unread);
PR-121 item 2 asked whether [obj+0xea] is a one-shot
vertical push; PR-274 OPENS (i) asked which mechanism lifts
the lion in A_PODCIAG. This PR reads the producer side and
answers the shape questions; the provider identity for the
climb window stays open and is OPENS (i) here.
MEASURED: (a) 0x45120(table slot, text) is a parser:
`%d` (0x9182d) reads a COUNT into [slot+8]; (count+1)*13+4
bytes come from the pool whose cursor is ds:0xa0c64
(0x76a64/0x76bb7); [slot+4] = the records; per record
i=1..count it parses `' %c'` (0x91830): separator ';'
stores kind byte 1, '#' stores 2, anything else 0, at
record+0xc (0x4519d-0x451be). It never parses coordinates.
(b) THE RECORDS ARE POLYLINE POINTS: {dword x@0, dword y@4,
byte kind@0xc}, stride 13 - the 13 the four `imul ...,0xd`
scale (PR-122) and exactly what 0x455a0 reads (its two
point pairs use +0/+4 only, PR-122's closed form). 0x45200
(slot, dx, dy) adds (dx,dy) to EVERY point (0x45214-0x45225)
- localization; 0x1e521-0x1e52a parses the [obj+0xa5] slot
for an object and immediately localizes its table by that
object's live x,y.
(c) 0x45380(slot, R) is the bracket finder: count 0 -> 0;
R.x outside [rec[0].x, rec[count-1].x] -> 0 (0x45391-
0x453a1); otherwise the index i with rec[i].x <= R.x <
rec[i+1].x (0x453a3-0x453bd). The polyline must be x-
sorted - the bounds test and the walk both assume it.
(d) 0x45320(provider slot, target, kind): 0x541f0(target,
&stack) writes the target's live [obj+0]/[obj+4] to the
stack pair (its continuation tests [obj+0xb6] bit1 and
[vt+0xbc], unread); then R = (x+[target+0xca], y+[target+
0xce]) - the position PREDICTED from this step's deltas,
the same pair the position step 0x54827/0x54829 adds - and
0x45400 runs with that R. So the snap is computed against
WHERE THE BODY IS ABOUT TO BE, not where it is.
(e) 0x45400 EXTENDS PR-122: before the index it rejects
when the provider's FIRST record kind byte exceeds the
kind argument (0x4540f-0x45419); every observed site
passes kind 2 from ebx (0x1e58a, 0x288fe, 0x380f6), so
only unparsed/garbage tables fail that test. The segment
index comes from the TARGET's [vt+0x6c] (0x45434/0x45439),
not from 0x45380 - 0x45380 instead feeds the direct probe
0x453d0, which returns the gap, or 0x7fffffff when the
point is outside the polyline (0x453db-0x453f5; no direct
caller found - the entry lists index it as a slot).
(f) THE STORE AND THE APPLY JOIN: PR-122's stores
([target+0xe6]=provider, [target+0xea]=the <=0 gap,
skipped when the provider equals the target's own
[obj+0xa9] table pointer) and PR-121's apply in the
position step (y += [obj+0xce]+[obj+0xea], then +0xea=0,
0x54804-0x5482d). Since the gap is line-y minus R.y and
is stored only when <= 0, THE LAW IS A ONE-SHOT SNAP UP TO
THE LINE for a body that would come to rest at or below it;
a body above the line is never moved. The 0x54759 guard
block skips the snap when the stored kind is 2 and the
answer word [obj+0xc6] >= 0x58c, and where [obj+0xa9] is 0
it sets flag byte bit 0x10, stores the link there and runs
two virtual calls (0x54785-0x547f0) before applying.
(g) THE GATES AT THE CALL SITES: 0x1e570 requires
[[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4]+4 < 0xd - [obj+0x50] is the
state-record list and [obj+0x5c] the CURRENT STATE INDEX
(new; the same pair reads at 0x380e9); 0x380d0 requires the
target's [vt+0x3c] true AND [target+0x5c] in {0x1f,0x20} =
ZARIA.01 LEW.MOV block indexes 31/32 zero-based =
A_FG_PACKA_UP / A_FG_PACKA (PR-235's order convention),
provider = [obj+0x44]; 0x288e2 sits in the contact region
next to 0x287a0 and gates on the self's [vt+0xd8](other)
before running the snap against the self's own [obj+0xee]
table (0x288d0 parses that slot). Per-class provider slots:
[obj+0xa5] (generic), [obj+0xee], [obj+0x44].
(h) WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE LIFT (INTERPRETATION, flagged
as such): FOCUS-1's A_PODCIAG question - PR-274 pinned the
lion drifting 2 px/t DOWN through the top platform's line
(.plt line `5 98,514;288,520;...` = y 518 at x 212) and
landing on the main ground. Mechanically (f) is the only
engine path found that moves a body UP to a line exactly,
and it needs a provider whose table holds that polyline to
be ATTACHED to the lion while the `lock` window (PR-273's
bit5, rows 1-7) runs. The port has no counterpart: its
landing search only looks DOWNWARD (ll_plt_first_below,
PR-272's sweep), which is why the drift passes 518 and
lands at 682. The provider identity for the climb window is
the question that stands between this reading and a port.
OPENS: in order: (i) which object's table holds the
ZARIA.01 polylines - the ZARIA_A.PLT load path was not
found among the 0x45120 sites, and [obj+0xa5]'s text source
is unread; (ii) who fills the record x/y fields (0x45120
parses count+separators only; 0x3dd60 shows text of the
shape `<count>...` followed by ` F = %d, %d` (0x91446) -
the row F-pair grammar - copying the FIRST point to
[rec+0xfa]/[rec+0xfe], a row/surface link worth reading);
(iii) which classes answer [vt+0x6c] with a segment index
and what [vt+0x3c]/[vt+0xd8] test; (iv) [obj+0xa9]'s two
writers - 0x45120 stores the object's own table there (via

answer-word comparison ([obj+0xc6] vs 0x58c).
CLOSES: none. PR-121 item 2 (is [obj+0xea] a one-shot

## PR-276 — THE TABLE-TEXT GRAMMAR IS THE PLACEMENT/.PLT POLYLINE
## GRAMMAR, AND PR-275'S "NEVER PARSES COORDINATES" IS WRONG:
## 0x4a0b0 IS THE `%d,%d` COORDINATE READER THE 0x45120 LOOP CALLS
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the 0x45120 table-text grammar (0x4a0b0, the
scanner helpers 0x49920/0x498f0), the engine's `platformy`
wiring read, and the localization call 0x1e512 - a correction
to PR-275 (its CORRECTS field). No `ported/` change.
ADDRESSES: 0x4a0b0, 0x45120, 0x1e512, 0x1e5c0, 0x4cf64,
0x49920, 0x498f0, 0x76d20, 0x76a64, 0x76bb7, 0x45200
NAMES: platformy, OI-073, OI-078, ANI2.DES, ANIPL2.DES,
ZARIA_A.PLT, DRABINKA, LINA, KATAPULT, PALMA, KAMIEN,
pr276_gram.py, kind byte, PR-242, PR-243, PR-246, PR-247,
PR-275, PR-102, PR-270, PR-274
CODE: no: no `ported/` or Makefile line changes; a reading
and a grammar replay, no behaviour to catch red.
HOOKS: PR-275 MEASURED (a) said the 0x45120 loop "never
parses coordinates" and its OPENS (ii) asked who fills the
record x/y fields. That is answered and withdrawn: the two
0x4a0b0 calls INSIDE 0x45120 (0x45169 before the loop,
0x45198 in it) do exactly that.
MEASURED: (a) 0x4a0b0(rec, str) is the coordinate reader:
0x49920(str, '%d,%d' at 0x91d0f, rec+0, rec+4) then the
cursor move 0x498f0(str, ' , ' at 0x91d15). With it, one
0x45120 call parses a whole polyline: the `%d` header is the
SEGMENT count, the FIRST point is parsed BEFORE the loop
into rec[0], and each of the count loop passes reads one
prefix char (' %c': ';' -> kind 1, '#' -> kind 2, anything
else 0 at rec_i+0xc) and then that point. The allocation
(count+1)*13+4 at 0x45149-0x45152 is exactly one leading
point plus count points.
(b) GRAMMAR REPLAY against the fixture's own lines
(emulator /tmp/opencode/pr276_gram.py, log
/tmp/opencode/pr276_gram.log, labelled as the disassembled
scanner replayed in python, not machine output): ZARIA.01's
placement polylines parse cleanly under it - KATAPULT
`1 7,45;40,45 ...` -> segment (7,45)-(40,45), PALMA
`1 -80,45;-18,45` -> (-80,45)-(-18,45), and ZARIA_A.PLT's
own lines too: `1 -50,680!408,684;` -> 1 segment with the
'!' point carrying kind 0, and the top-platform line
`5 98,514;...;589,566;` -> 5 segments, 6 points, all kind
1. So the count field equals points-minus-one, the grammar
is ONE LINE at a time, and the .plt file's first line
("45") is the line COUNT for a line-splitting loader, not a
table header.
(c) THE SAME GRAMMAR AS THE PLACEMENT VECTORS: ZARIA.01
ANI2.DES (dumped with tools/re/llrs_cat1) authors
`DRABINKA,drab.ani,drab.mov,180,510` then `1 33,-3`,
`23,30;53,160`, `30,50` - the point list, rectangle and
pair the port already models through PR-242/PR-243/PR-246/
PR-270 (abs 213,507 / column (203,540)-(233,670) / pair
(210,560) - all reproduce). The replay of `1 33,-3` yields
one real point plus an EMPTY second slot: a one-point table
can never be bracketed (0x45380 needs rec[i].x <= R.x with
i < count), so single-contact-point objects are exactly the
non-surface cases. LINA authors `1 0,200` the same way.
(d) THE ENGINE READS `platformy` FOR REAL: the string sits
at 0x91e1e; 0x4cf69/0x4cf6c compares the current wiring key
through 0x76d20 and 0x4cf7d reads the value with ' %s'
(0x91e28) - the machine-side anchor of the port's
platformy= wiring model (ll_level.c's 10774 block), which
was fixture-derived.
(e) LOCALIZE AT LOAD, SHIFT PER STEP: 0x1e512-0x1e52a parses
the [obj+0xa5] slot from text and calls 0x45200 with the
object's live x,y - the table becomes ABSOLUTE at load, the
same law PR-242 measured for the point vectors. A family of
eight 0x45200 sites (0x1e5f8, 0x1e64c, 0x1e6ce, 0x1e733,
0x1e798, 0x1e803, 0x1e896, plus 0x3dccd/0x3deb2) instead
translates a table by pure offsets; 0x1e5c0-0x1e5f8 is read
in full: it takes the CURRENT state record's field +4 and
shifts the [obj+0xa5] table by (0, +1) when that field is
below 7, (0, -1) otherwise. Field +4 is NOT the control
mode word (PR-102: BY_X 0..BY_TY 4 - both this gate and
PR-275's 0x1e585 gate at 13 exceed it), so it is a second,
unread word of the state record.
OPENS: in order: (i) which loader splits the ground .plt
into lines and WHOSE object slot receives each table -
none of the five 0x45120 sites is a level-file loader, so
the ZARIA.01 top-platform provider is still unnamed (this

field +4 identity (gates 7 at 0x1e5dd and 13 at 0x1e585);
(iii) the 0x1e5c0-family (0, +/-1) per-step shift: which
objects run those eight slots and what walks 1 px a step;
(iv) carried from PR-275: the [vt+0x6c] index responder and
the [vt+0x3c]/[vt+0xd8] tests, [obj+0xa9]'s two writers,
the 0x54759 guard's answer-word compare.
CLOSES: none. PR-275 OPENS (ii) is ANSWERED by (a) but the
answer lives here, so PR-275's row keeps its remaining
items.
CORRECTS: PR-275 - MEASURED (a) "It never parses
coordinates" and OPENS (ii) "who fills the record x/y
fields" are withdrawn: 0x4a0b0, called by 0x45120 itself,
reads them (MEASURED (a) here); the count field is the
segment count, not the raw record count.

here; PR-279's "0x4b600 and 0x4b660" are ONE function
(0x4b600-0x4b6cb), not two - the loop body is its tail.
MEASURED: (a) 0x455a0(lo, hi, &point) is the gap
calculator, exactly: quotient = (point.x - lo.x) *
(hi.y - lo.y) / (hi.x - lo.x); returns lo.y + quotient -
point.y = line_y(point.x) - point.y. It is pure: no clamp,
no contact term.
(b) THE CALLER IS THE POSITION STEP. 0x546a0 (the method
PR-275 read around): `test byte [obj+0xb6],2` set - jump
straight to the position update at 0x54804, skipping the
attach entirely. Otherwise it reads the state record's flag
word at [rec+0x12] (PR-59/PR-60's word): bit 0x4000 ->
0x4b600 with the kind cap ecx=0, then 0x4b430 (the
blokady= array query); else bit 0x100 - CHECK_LN, a member
of the game's CHECK_ALL = 0x1c0 - -> 0x4b600 with cap 2,
then 0x4b430; both then 0x4b7f0. 0x54759 then guards the
application (PR-275's kind-2 guard, confirmed).
(c) INSIDE 0x45400 THE TWO PASSES ARE A CROSSING TEST. The
first 0x455a0 pass is against one point and its result is
REJECTED when negative (0x4547d `jl skip`) unless the table
IS the actor's own [actor+0xa9] table (0x45479 `je`); the
second pass is against the other point (one of the two is
the position 0x541f0 returns, the other position +
[obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] - 0x4b600 builds both in one stack
buffer, MEASURED earlier) and must return <= 0, keeping the
MAXIMUM (closest to zero) such gap (0x4549a). So a foreign
ground line is accepted exactly when it is non-negative
against one point and non-positive against the other: the
point crosses the line between the two evaluations, and the
stored [obj+0xea] lands the point ON the line at the
position update. That is a LANDING law, not a general
snap-up: a line ABOVE both points (gap < 0 twice) never
passes the first gate, and a line below both never passes
the second.

finish): during A_PODCIAG the position point sits ABOVE the

every tick and this channel cannot lift him. The port's
ly_climb finish (drift to grounded 654 on main ground at

missing, expect 489" framing is withdrawn as the mechanism.

[obj+0xea] at 0x5481b (the one-shot is the engine's, not
a port convention); x += [obj+0xca]; y += [obj+0xce] +

[obj+0xce] - the velocity words are CONSUMED by the step:
pos += vel, vel := 0, rebuilt each iteration by the
0x54250/0x542cd pass (PR-122/PR-259). So [obj+0xca]/
[obj+0xce] carry nothing but the per-iteration delta -
no contact term lives there.
(b) THE LINK: when the attach produced a table ([obj+0xe6]
non-null at 0x54788): if the actor has no current link
([obj+0xa9]==0) it ORs bit 0x10 into the output byte and
links: [obj+0xa9] = [obj+0xe6], call table vtable +0x0
(0x45230) with edx=object (attach). If a DIFFERENT table
is already linked it calls the old one's +0x4 (0x39d00,
detach) then links and attaches the new (0x547af-0x547c6).
When no attach is live and the actor still holds a table,
0x547d7-0x547fb detaches it and writes [obj+0xa9]=0.
The byte bits: [edi]|0x10 on fresh link, [edi+1]|0x20 when
[obj+0xe2] (the stored kind) is non-zero, [edi+2]|0x04 on

evaluation1 rejected when negative and evaluation2 required
non-positive (PR-280 MEASURED (c)), a fall landing on the
main ground is the only sign combination that passes:
current above the line (gap1 = line - pos > 0), predicted
below (gap2 = line - pos - vy < 0), store gap2; and the
application then gives y_new = pos + vy + (line - pos -
vy) = line EXACTLY: the position point lands ON the line.
The algebra is closed-form and confirms PR-280: a rising
crossing (current below, predicted above) fails the first
gate, so this channel cannot lift anything.

line (682 at x 214), while the port's convention puts it
at line-minus-art-contact (654, PR-97) and draws art
offset up - the two agree on screen (feet on ground) and
differ only in where the origin sits. Every port-pinned
grounded y (ly_climb's 654, ly_cdown's 651) is the port
convention, not an engine-internal number; nothing here
invalidates a leg, since the legs pin what the port draws.

A_PODCIAG words (F=0,0 T=100,100 G=0,0, no row motion
verbs) feed the 0x542cd force law NO pair - the same law
that PR-259 measured for A_WSP's T=(160,50) one px/t

therefore NOT the T channel, NOT the snap channel, and not

## PR-287 — THE `Wait` CLAUSE GATES THE ROW IT CARRIES: STATES
## HOLD THEIR FRAMES, THE LADDER TAKES ITS OWN 2700-UNIT
## DESCENT, AND PR-218'S BRANCH POLARITY IS CORRECTED
```
KIND: port
SUBSYSTEM: the object row walk (obj_advance's admit) and the
row-record model (a new ll_mov_row_gate); the ZARIA.01
ly_climb leg extended. No player-side change.
ADDRESSES: 0x521f0, 0x52229, 0x52235, 0x5223c, 0x495b0,
0x495d5, 0x52241, 0x5224b, 0x52251, 0x5226f, 0x52290,
0x522bc, 0x522e6, 0x47e40, 0x522ed, 0x522ef, 0x522f8,
0x522fc, 0x52303, 0x52329, 0x52334, 0x52338, 0x52354,
0x521c1, 0x521c5, 0x45970, 0x46b62, 0xa11c8, 0x49580,
0x47e63, 0x47edc, 0x4806f, 0x44e70, 0x53626
NAMES: ll_mov_row_gate, LL_GOP_NAME, LL_GOP_NEVER, LL_GOP_ANY,
WAIT K_GEN1, WAIT K_NEVER, WAIT AC_TIME, WAIT AC_DUP, A_UP,
A_DROP, A_DOWN, AC_BREAK_NEXT, K_GEN1, K_NEVER, K_ANY,
obj_rowgate_act_selftest, ly_climb, OI-111, OI-078, OI-073,
PR-217, PR-218, PR-219, PR-224, PR-135, PR-172, PR-286
CODE: yes: ll_mov_row_gate in ll_play.c (declared in
ll_play.h) and one gate test in ll_level.c's obj_advance,
placed BEFORE the row clock test because 0x52235 precedes
0x52329; a new obj_rowgate_act_selftest; a new comment on the
row-record fields; three header comments corrected (below).
HOOKS: no new hook. The leg uses the LEO_PLAY_ASK /
LEO_LEVEL_PPM pair ly_climb already uses.
MEASURED: (a) THE BRANCH, AT THE FLAG LEVEL. The row step
0x521f0 asks the row node's test slot +0x8 at 0x52235, hands
what comes back to 0x495b0 at 0x5223c - three dwords, all
zero answers 1, any one non-zero answers 0 (0x495ba-0x495d5),
so that call is the EMPTY test - and 0x52241-0x5224b is
`test eax,eax; sete al; and eax,0xff; je 0x522fc`. The `je`
is taken exactly when 0x495b0 answered 1: an EMPTY set takes
0x522fc, the path that calls the row's execute slot +0xc
(0x52303), OR-s what it returns into the caller's set (0x5230c)
and runs the row only when its authored threshold is below the
clock (0x52320-0x5232b), clock minus threshold as its budget
(0x52334). Only a NON-empty set falls through to 0x52251: the
caller's key set (0x5226f) and the object's own [obj+0x60]
(0x5229d) are copied, OR-ed by 0x49580 (0x522bc) and matched
against the clause by 0x47e40 at 0x522e6, and the refusal is
`je 0x52354` - the epilogue, past the execute, the clock and
every class verb. PR-218 paired these the other way round, and
that pairing cannot be the shipped game: it would put every
row WITHOUT a clause - all but the 251 the port's own parser
captures - on the zero-budget path with no clock consulted,
so no authored frame duration would be honoured, while the
durations PR-109 and PR-110 measured ON SCREEN sit exactly
there. (b) SO THE CLAUSE GATES. 0x47e40 switches on the
clause's mode byte: 0 (0x47e63) is "the clause is a SUBSET",
so a plain name must be live; 1 (0x47edc) is "shares nothing",
so a `!` name must be down; the no-bit K_NEVER set (0x60 in
data byte 4, 0x4806f-0x4807d) is a subset of nothing the game
raises, so a `WAIT K_NEVER` row NEVER runs - THAT is how a
shipped state holds its last frame for good - and the
tokenless `Wait ;` compiles to an empty set and gates nothing.
Census over the 777 extracted texts, line-anchored: 201 `Wait`
rows carry an explicit `<frame>,<time>,` prefix, 46 in lion
scripts and 155 in object scripts. Of the object rows, the
ones whose authored threshold is non-zero AND whose operand can
be live are `WAIT K_GEN1` at 100/400/1000 (ENA.03_SKALA,
ENA2_DEMOTEXT, TUNGA2.12_DOMEK x2, LONA.05_SKJUMP), `WAIT
AC_TIME` at 300..4600 (LONA.05_FLAGA, ZARIA.01/ZARIA.02
ANIBACK, ZARIA.02_ANIBACK_GLIST, SADES.06's STULB/STULBIA
family) and `WAIT AC_DUP` at 200/300 (LONA.05_PINGWIN,
LONA.05_YETI, KADMAR.07_0_0); every other non-zero-threshold
gated row names K_NEVER, whose number is unreachable anyway.
Three gated rows carry a second directive at all (2 `smpauto`,
1 `rdir`) and none carries `GEN`, so the execute slot the
gated path skips has nothing to raise in any shipped row.
(c) THE ACT: obj_advance now asks ll_mov_row_gate(f, o->sig)
before its clock test - the order the bytes give - and a
refused row admits NO frame, wraps NO list, raises NO signal
and consumes NO clock. (d) THE LADDER'S OWN SCRIPT, END TO
END, in the new selftest (ZARIA.01/DRABINKA/drab.MOV verbatim
but for the `seq=`/`sample=` art keys): A_UP's `1,0,WAIT
K_GEN1` row admits nothing for 6 steps and arms NO list-end
bit - the red leg, because the port admitted a 0-unit row and
wrapped its one-row list on the FIRST step, every step;
raising K_GEN1 then enters A_DROP at its authored entry row
with the clock zeroed (PR-172); the nine rows close after
5,4,4,3,3,2,2,2,2 = 27 iterations, and the last one's admit
wraps the counter to 0 and arms the bit in the SAME step
(0x521c1-0x521c5); the next step's composition takes
`A_DOWN(1)=AC_BREAK_NEXT`, and A_DOWN's `11,0,WAIT K_NEVER`
admits nothing for 12 more steps and never hands a bit to any
transition. (e) THE SAME CHAIN IN THE LEVEL: ly_climb's ask
log now reads the placed ladder at index 1 (A_UP) through tick
103, at index 3 (A_DROP) 104..131 - K_GEN1 live at 104, the
27 row-walk iterations 105..131 - and at the answerable index
2 (A_DOWN) from 132, and the leg pins those four ticks plus
the negative that no tick below 132 reads state 2 (27 such
lines before this PR, 0 after). Every later pin of that leg
is UNCHANGED: the catch at 146/148, A_TURN_BACK at 150,
AC_EDGE at 262, the hold 263..288, the landing at 299 - the
ladder is lowered by 132, a full 14 ticks before the lion
asks it to answer. What this nets for FOCUS 1: the ladder's
descent is now its own authored list, and the answer window
opens 27 iterations later than it did. (f) WHAT THE PORT
STILL DOES NOT DO: the engine's gated path SKIPS the
threshold compare at 0x52329 and runs the row with a ZERO
budget (0x522ef `xor ebx,ebx` then `jmp 0x52338`, against the
plain path's `sub ebx,eax` at 0x52334) - this port still
requires its own clock, so the two readings agree only on rows
whose authored threshold is 0, which is every row of the
ladder chain and NOT the rows named in (b); and the LION's own
row admit in player_iterate does not consult the clause at
all, although ZAR_LEW carries `8,0,WAIT AC_DUP` and
`8,200,WAIT !K_UP` rows. (g) THE SAME GATE ON THE OTHER
OBJECTS OF THIS LEVEL, counted with a throwaway print at the
gate (removed before commit, not a shipped probe): the
16-second ZARIA.01 run now holds EIGHT object rows it used to
run - KAMIEN A_STOP `1,0,WAIT K_GEN1`, DRABINKA A_UP and LINA
A_UP (the same shape), KORONA A_IDLE and POCISK A_WISI `WAIT
K_NEVER`, KATAPULT A_RUN and PALMA A_RUN `WAIT K_GEN1`,
ANIBACK A_RUN row 8 `8,4600,WAIT AC_TIME`. Two of them were
measured changing: a temporary state-change trace prints THREE
`KAMIEN [A_STOP]->[A_GO]` lines in the first ticks of the
pre-fix run and ZERO after it, and LINA.MOV - the ladder's
twin, `[A_UP] 1,0,WAIT K_GEN1`, a nine-row A_DROP, `[A_DOWN]
10,0,WAIT K_NEVER` - walks A_DROP into A_DOWN exactly, twice.
The held K_GEN1 rows are NOT dead ends in this port:
ladder_flag_raise (PR-241) raises K_GEN1 on ANY asked object
whose current state is declared index 1, and KAMIEN1.MOV
declares A_STOP first, so a pair contact starts the stones the
same way it starts the ladder - the probe never touches one in
16 s. ANIBACK's `WAIT AC_TIME` row is the one that stays held
for good: this port's only AC_TIME raiser is the same-state
match counter of PR-163 (0x53626-0x5365c), which an ANIMATED
BACKGROUND never reaches, so its row never admits - a behaviour
change in a level with no leg for it, named here rather than
smoothed. (h) WHY THE ASK STARTS THE ROW: the gate's live set
and PR-241's raise are THE SAME FIELD. The union at 0x52290
copies [obj+0x60], the object's own 12-byte TEventSet, and the
ask's write is `[eax+0x66] |= 0x40` (0x44e70, PR-241) - byte
6, bit 6, i.e. bit 54 of that set, which is exactly
LL_SIG_K_GEN1 (ll_play.h: LL_SIG_K_JUMP = 53, K_GEN1 next).
So the branch that answers the ladder is the branch that lets
its own A_UP row run, one step later, with no extra plumbing in
either direction.
OPENS: in order: (i) the zero-budget admit - an object row
whose clause names a signal that DOES go up (the (b) list:
K_GEN1 / AC_TIME / AC_DUP with a non-zero threshold) admits in
the engine a whole authored duration earlier than this port
lets it; (ii) the player-side gate, and with it the lion's
`WAIT !K_UP` / `!K_DOWN` rows, whose clause names INPUT keys -
the row step matches them against the caller's key set, which
this port composes only inside the transition pass; (iii) the
gate is only as good as the signals: 19 shipped rows gate on
AC_DUP and its producer is still unmodelled (PR-277 OPENS
(i)), so every one of those rows now holds forever by design
of this fix, which is a behaviour change in levels this port
has no leg for; (iv) the (g) pair is now a measured
difference, not only a text reading: the stones of ZARIA.01
stop moving in this port, and what would release them is the
OTHER half of the row step's live set - the row walk 0x520c0
composes the level-global set at 0x98278 (0x520e6-0x520f6)
and the row step matches the clause against THAT union
(0x52251-0x522e6), while this port has no level-wide signal
set at all, so its gates read one object's raised bits only.
Is K_GEN1 in that global set, and who writes it there?
Unread; (v) OI-111 stays open on (i) and (ii) alone.
CLOSES: PR-286 OPENS (ii) - the ladder's chain timings, which
that record left unverified both ways ("the authored A_DROP

CORRECTS: PR-218's reading of 0x5224b (and PR-217's note

[ebx+4]`; 0x520f2 `mov [esp+8],ecx`; 0x520f6 `call [ecx+4]`.
The callee is 0x23ea0 - three instructions, `{ [eax]=edx;
[eax+4]=ebx; ret }` - so what is built at esp is a
three-dword object: two dwords taken from the table the
object's own [obj+0] points at, and the word 0x98278 in the
third slot. (b) WHAT THAT CLASS IS, FROM ITS OWN VERBS. The
image at 0x98274-0x9827c is a run of code addresses (0x23e30,
0x23ed0, 0x23ea0, 0x23e00), and 0x98278 is the base+8 word
of it, the same convention PR-261 named. Its +0x04 verb is
the setter above; its +0x08 verb, 0x23e00, is a
point-in-rectangle test: it reads [eax] against [edx] and
[edx+8] and [eax+4] against [edx+4] and [edx+0xc], rejecting
outside with `jl`/`jg` and answering 1 inside - the inclusive
bounds the port's own column and edge-band legs pin (PR-269,
PR-270); its +0x00 verb 0x23ed0 is a debug/format path over
the static 0x96858. The base ctor 0x53ff0 installs the same
object inside every object: 0x54004-0x5400b writes x = 0,
y = 0 and the class word 0x98278, the second initializer
0x54030 repeats it, and 144 class tables hand the member out
through the +0x68 verb 0x23900 (`add eax,0xd6; ret`) - the
nested point at [obj+0xd6] that OI-118 recorded. (c) SO THE
WALK COMPOSES A POSITION, NOT A SIGNAL. It takes the object's
two coordinates through its [obj+0] table, puts them in a
stack POINT, and hands that to the record verb `[[rec]+0x28]`
at 0x52100; 0x52103-0x5210f then call `[[[obj]]+8]+0x04` with
the same two values in edx/ebx. No 0x49580 - the three-dword

row path are inside the row step itself: 0x522bc, the union
of the caller's argument with the object's own set at
[obj+0x60] that PR-287 gates on, and 0x5230c, the execute
slot's result OR-ed back into the caller's argument. (d) THE

## PR-290 — THE `control=` QUERY BITS ASK NEIGHBOURING OBJECTS

```

SUBSYSTEM: the world query PR-290 named in PR-289: the three
query calls 0x4bd30 / 0x4b890 / 0x4b870 behind the record
class's composition verb 0x52790, the answer verb 0x23920 they

PR-241, PR-287, PR-288, PR-289
CODE: no: a reading, no behaviour to catch red.
HOOKS: PR-289 OPENS (i) named 0x4bd30 / 0x4b890 / 0x4b870 and
the object at [0xcef40] as unread; PR-287 OPENS (iv) and
PR-288 had left the row step's caller argument (0x521f0's
