## PR-312 — THE OBJECTS' PHYSICS STEP: `+0xac` IS A GROUND QUERY,
## AN ATTACH LAW AND A CARRY-AND-SNAP, AND IT RUNS FOR 108 OF THE
## 151 CLASSES - INCLUDING EVERY LION - BUT NOT FOR THE LADDER
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the object class slot +0xac: what its body 0x546a0
does, how often it is installed, and the field triple its result
travels through; the contact-list insert 0x45320/0x45400 that also
fills that triple; and the interpolation it uses. FOCUS 1 asked
what could move a rider whose own state authors no motion: this is
the named mechanism.
ADDRESSES: 0x546a0, 0x54706, 0x54759, 0x54804, 0x45320, 0x45400,
0x45380, 0x453d2, 0x455a0, 0x49580, 0x4b430, 0x4b600, 0x4b7f0,
0x23930, 0x52a00, 0x45120, 0x541f0, 0x98278, 0x96874,
0x96960, 0x96d1c, 0x97cdc, 0x99ff0, 0x1e970, 0x749a0, 0xcef40
NAMES: physics step, ground query, attach, detach, carry, snap,
clearance, contact list, polyline, segment count, flag byte,
control word, AC_ONAIR, AC_DRECT, TLewZaria, TLewZariaB, DRABINKA,
KATAPULT, WSPRECT, OI-078, OI-018, PR-304, PR-305, PR-307,
PR-308, PR-311, ll_plt_first_below, ladder_answer_core
CODE: no: image and class-table reading only; nothing under
`ported/` changed, so no red leg is owed and none was written.
HOOKS: PR-311's OPENS (i) - "what writing a contact-list entry
with mode 2 does, and who reads that list back" - and the FOCUS-1
rule that a mechanism must be read in the engine, not inferred.
MEASURED: (a) WHO RUNS IT. The class slot +0xac holds 0x546a0 in
108 of the 151 factory-census classes, including TLewZaria (its
+0xac cell is 0x96a0c), the lion base class 0x96874, PLATF, WINDA,
SCHODY..4 and the enemies; 24 classes hold the empty stub 0x23930
- the whole ladder family (DRABINKA 0x97cdc, LINA, KDRABINA,
KATAPULT, PALMA, DZWIGNIA) - 5 hold 0x52a00 (the WSPRECT family),
3 hold 0x45120, and one holds 0x45400. So a rider runs this step
and a ladder does not.
(b) ITS SHAPE. `test BYTE [obj+0xb6],0x2; jne 0x54804` - the
queries are skipped when that bit is set, but the carry at 0x54804
still runs. Then the current state record is read through
[[obj+0x50] + [obj+0x5c]*4] and its control word at state+0x12
selects: bit 0x4000 -> call 0x4b600 with ecx = 0 and then 0x4b430;
bit 0x0100 -> 0x4b600 with ecx = 2, then 0x4b430, then 0x4b7f0.
All three are called with eax = ds:0xcef40 (the world object) and
their result is passed to 0x49580, which ORs three dwords into the
12-byte signal set the verb was handed (that is the set shape with
its mode byte at +0xc, PR-296) - so a ground query RAISES SIGNALS.
(c) THE RESULT TRAVELS IN A TRIPLE ON THE OBJECT: [obj+0xe6] = the
surface found, [obj+0xe2] = that surface's flag byte, [obj+0xea] =
the signed clearance, and [obj+0xa9] = the surface currently
attached. The law at 0x54759: no surface found -> if one was
attached, call its class [+0x4] (leave), clear [obj+0xa9], call
the object's own [+0xb8], set flag bit [edi+0x2] |= 4. Surface
found -> if kind == 2 and [obj+0xc6] < 0x58c it is ignored too;
otherwise if nothing is attached set [edi] |= 0x10, store it, call
its class [+0x0] (enter) and the object's [+0xb4]; if a DIFFERENT
one was attached, call the old one's [+0x4] first. Then kind != 0
sets [edi+0x1] |= 0x20.
(d) THE CARRY, 0x54804: pos.x += [obj+0xca]; pos.y += [obj+0xce]
+ [obj+0xea]; then [obj+0xea] and [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] are
zeroed. So a rider is moved by the surface's per-frame delta and
by the clearance to it - the only channel FOCUS 1 had left, and it
is a snap to a polyline, not an authored rise.
(e) HOW A CONTACT LIST BECOMES A SURFACE. The ask verbs pass their
own [obj+0xa5] list, and the insert 0x45320 first asks the object
for its point through 0x541f0 with the {0,0,0x98278} triple
(PR-308's provider pre-seed), adds [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce], then
calls 0x45400, which treats the list as a polyline of 13-byte
records (x at +0, y at +4, flag byte at +0xc): a mode gate on the
FIRST entry's flag byte, then 0x45380 finds the segment whose
x-span contains the point, and 0x455a0 returns (interpolated Y at
that x) - Q.y; the best (nearest non-positive) candidate is
stored in the triple of (c). 0x453d2 returns 0x7fffffff when no
segment covers x. So the catapult's mode 2 (PR-311) is a filter
value on that flag byte, and the flag byte is the same byte the
.PT text reader fills from the point separator (0x451a1 stores 1
for `;`).
OPENS: 0x4b430 / 0x4b600 / 0x4b7f0 first - the three ground queries
against the world object: which polylines of the level they walk,
and how the mode argument and the per-point flag byte filter them.
This is now the direct route to the ZARIA.01 platform line. Second,
what the state control-word bits 0x4000 and 0x0100 are in the
`control=` vocabulary the port parses. Third, the signals the
queries raise - does one of them name AC_ONAIR / AC_DRECT, the two
the level's own exit chain waits for (OI-018)? Fourth, the object's
own [+0xb4]/[+0xb8] verbs and the surface's [+0x0]/[+0x4] class
verbs. Fifth, F1's capture read still stands as plan step one.
CLOSES: the FOCUS-1 question "is there any mechanism left that
moves a rider with no authored motion" - yes, and it is now read
at the level of its fields and arithmetic; and PR-311's OPENS (i).
CORRECTS: PR-305, whose reading of the +0xac cell as "ENTER" is
kept as a measurement (the ladder family really does hold the
empty stub 0x23930 there) but is the wrong role: for 108 of the
151 classes the slot is the per-frame ground/attach/carry step.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no
red leg by the rule PR-245 states, and no suite run. The last full
no-Windows suite run is PR-298's, rc=0 with 69 green verdict lines;
since then only comments in ported/ have changed.

## PR-313 — THE THREE GROUND QUERIES THE PHYSICS STEP CALLS:
## A BLOCKADE PUSH, AN ASK SWEEP, A CEILING TEST - AND THE
## NAMED SIGNALS THEY RAISE, INCLUDING AC_ONAIR
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: 0x4b430, 0x4b600 and 0x4b7f0, the queries PR-312 found
gated by the state control word inside the physics step 0x546a0;
the world arrays they walk; their sibling nearest-object searches
0x4b6d0/0x4b762; and the signal bits the step itself raises, read
against the port's own LL_SIG_* table.
ADDRESSES: 0x546a0, 0x4b430, 0x4b500, 0x4b600, 0x4b6d0, 0x4b762,
0x4b7f0, 0x4b870, 0x45620, 0x534e0, 0x541f0, 0x49580, 0x749a0,
0x44370, 0x44540, 0x98274, 0x98278, 0xcef40, 0xcef44, 0xa94e8,
0x287a0, 0x23930
NAMES: AC_BLOK, AC_DUP, AC_DUP_CD, AC_ONAIR, AC_UP_DUP, AC_DRAB,
blokady, blockade, ceiling, floor, nearest, penetration, push,
ask sweep, world arrays, control word, OI-018, OI-079, OI-078,
PR-312, PR-305, PR-308, LL_SIG_AC_ONAIR, LL_SIG_AC_DUP
CODE: no: machine-code reading; the port's signal enum was READ
as a name table, nothing under `ported/` was changed, so no red
leg is owed.
HOOKS: PR-312's OPENS first item (the three queries), second item
(the control-word bits) and third item (whether they raise
AC_ONAIR / AC_DRECT - the pair ZARIA.01's exit chain waits for,
OI-018).
MEASURED: (a) THE BLOCKADE QUERY 0x4b430. It builds the object's
own RECT (a local rect object of class 0x98274, filled through
0x534e0), adds the pending delta [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] to all four
edges, then walks an array whose base is at [arg+0x70] and whose
count is at [arg+0x7c], stride 0x14, entry x at +0x4, y at +0x8,
length at +0x10, calling 0x45620 per entry. 0x45620 accepts an
entry whose x lies inside the rect's x-span and whose y..y+len
crosses the rect's y-span AND which is more than 1 px from the
farther x edge; on accept it adds (entry.x - that edge) into
[obj+0xca] - a SIDEWAYS PUSH through the same pending-delta field
the carry reads - and returns 1. First match wins. The query then
composes the answer: an EMPTY set if nothing matched, and with the
set's byte 0 OR-ed with 0x1 = signal bit 0 = AC_BLOK if something
did (the name matches the behaviour exactly).
(b) THE ASK SWEEP 0x4b600, the one the control word runs in mode 0
or 2. It takes the object's POINT through the +0xb0 provider
(0x541f0 with the {0,0,0x98278} triple, PR-308), adds the pending
delta, and if a surface is attached at [obj+0xa9] it asks THAT
first, through the surface's class [+0x8] verb with ecx = 2. Then
it walks a second array, base [arg+0x74], count [arg+0x80],
stride 0xc, whose entries hold an object pointer at +0x0, and
calls each entry's class [+0x1c] verb with eax = that object,
edx = the world, ecx = the asking object, ebx = &point. The
collected answer is composed at 0x4b500 with the mode from the
control word and a global from ds:0xa94e8.
(c) THE CEILING/FLOOR SEARCHES 0x4b6d0 and 0x4b762 walk the same
second array and, for every entry, ask it through its class
[+0x14] verb with the object's own [+0x6c] result, keeping the
best: 0x4b6d0 requires a NEGATIVE answer and keeps the largest
(starting at 0x80000001), 0x4b762 requires a POSITIVE one and
keeps the smallest (starting at 0x7fffffff); both write the chosen
entry's address out. 0x4b7f0 is the third query: it walks a THIRD
array, base [arg+0x78], count [arg+0x84], stride 0x14, whose
entry at +0x10 names an object, calls that object's class [+0x4]
verb, and on a non-zero answer composes an empty set with byte 3
OR-ed with 0x2 = signal bit 25 = AC_UP_DUP.
(d) THE SIGNALS ARE NAMED NOW. Matching the byte index and bit
mask against the port's own enum in ported/ll_play.h (AC_BLOK = 0
.. AC_KOLO = 34): the blockade query raises AC_BLOK, and the
physics step of PR-312 raises, on the surface branch, byte 0 mask
0x10 = bit 4 = AC_DUP when it ATTACHES, byte 1 mask 0x20 = bit 13
= AC_DUP_CD when the surface's kind byte is not 0, and byte 2 mask
0x4 = bit 18 = AC_ONAIR when no surface was found at all (or the
attached one was left). So OI-018's AC_ONAIR has a producer and it
is the ground query FAILING: ZARIA.01's exit chain A_DRAP /
A_PRE_JUMP -> A_WPAD waits on AC_ONAIR,AC_DRECT, i.e. on the lion
having no ground under him. And OI-079's AC_DUP producer is the
attach branch of 0x546a0, not a row-tail directive.
(e) THE WSPRECT ANSWER, one site, read only as far as its signal:
its ask verb 0x287a0 ends by clearing the set's mode byte, calling
0x749a0 with ebx = 0xc and OR-ing byte 1 mask 0x4 = bit 10 =
AC_DRAB - the ladder signal, from a RECTANGLE class.
(f) The three arrays are separate from the contact lists of
PR-312: their base/count pairs (+0x70/+0x7c, +0x74/+0x80,
+0x78/+0x84) are written together at 0x44599..0x4460f, a setup
that parses config text through 0x4a0b0 and builds the runtime
arrays in 0x44370 - that producer is named, NOT read here.
OPENS: 0x44370 / 0x44540 - which level-config block becomes which
of the three arrays, and the entry layout of each; then the
+0x1c / +0x14 / +0x8 / +0x4 verbs a queried object answers with
(which is how a ladder or a platform reports itself as ground);
then AC_DRECT, which is NOT raised by any of the three queries
read here; then whether AC_ONAIR's producer being the missing
ground is what the port's LL_PLAY_GRAVITY stand-in replaces.
Fifth, F1's capture read still stands as plan step one.
CLOSES: PR-312's first three opens: the queries are read at the
level of their arrays, their verbs, their arithmetic and their
signals; AC_ONAIR and AC_DUP have named producers (OI-018,
OI-079).
CORRECTS: none. PR-312's reading of the same bits as "0x10
(landed), 0x20 (kind != 0), 4 (airborne)" is unchanged as bytes;
they are now named AC_DUP, AC_DUP_CD and AC_ONAIR.

## PR-316 — PLAN STEP F2 AND F3 ANSWERED AT ONCE: `pos` SETS THE
## POSITION THROUGH THE OBJECT'S CLASS +0x4 VERB, `lock`/`unlock`
## ARE A FLAGGED PAIR, AND `end_level` IS THE WRITER OF
## [world+0x4] - THE LAST OF WHICH OI-046 HAD ALREADY CLOSED
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the .MOV state-directive node classes - the apply of
`pos`, `lock`, `unlock`, `rdir` and `end_level`, which this port
counts and acts on none of - read through the parser's dispatch,
the node classes, and the object verbs they call.
ADDRESSES: 0x466d6, 0x46ef0, 0x45a30, 0x457e0, 0x45c50, 0x54f40,
0x54f90, 0x45a10, 0x45750, 0xa11b0, 0xa10d8, 0xa0f70, 0xa1048,
0xa10f0, 0x91940, 0x91901, 0x9190c, 0x9193b, 0x9198e, 0x23850,
0x23ea0, 0x53df0, 0x55070, 0x5c320, 0x49920, 0x57a00, 0xcef40,
0x96874, 0x96960, 0x97cdc
NAMES: pos, lock, unlock, rdir, ldir, end_level, set position,
locked flag, direction word, level end, node class, apply verb,
A_WPAD, A_WYJSCIE, OI-078, PR-194, PR-198, PR-199, PR-305,
PR-309, PR-312, ll_player_step
CODE: no: machine-code reading only; nothing under `ported/`
changed, so no red leg is owed and none was written.
HOOKS: plan step F2 (the apply of the directives the exit needs)
and F3 (who writes [level+0x4]). PR-309 named the exit chain and
the two `pos` lines; PR-312 named [obj+0xb6] bit 2 as a physics
skip and PR-305 named the class +0x54 cell.
MEASURED: (a) THE DISPATCH. One parser function compares the
directive names and, for each match, allocates a node and stores
its class word, then appends it with 0x57a00. `lock` (the name at
0x91901, compared at 0x46408) allocates 12 bytes and stores
0xa10d8; `rdir` (0x9193b, compared at 0x4668e) allocates 8 bytes
and stores 0xa0f70; `pos` (0x91940, compared at 0x466d6)
allocates 16 bytes, stores 0xa11b0 at [node+0xc] and then calls
0x49920 with the format string at 0x91944 and two output slots at
[node+0x8] and [node+0xc] - the authored `pos 1020,692` pair.
(The end_level node 0xa1048 and its table were read at
PR-198/199.)
(b) THE NODE SHAPE AND THE APPLY SLOT. A node is {link at +0x0,
class word at +0x4, payload at +0x8}. Each node class differs
from its siblings at exactly two slots, +0x4 and +0x1c, and the
+0x4 bodies are the semantic ones (0x45750 end_level, 0x45c50
lock, 0x45a10 rdir, 0x45a30 pos); every one of them first calls
the shared helper 0x457e0, which walks [node+0x0] and calls the
OWNING object's class +0x4 verb - so a directive runs against a
specific object, and that object is reached from the node. That
+0.4-is-the-apply reading is INFERRED from this shape and from
the bodies; the executor's call site in the level loop was not
read, and PR-198/199 point at other verbs of 0xa1048 (0x45d90 as
its sixth), so a [port] step must re-confirm the call site.
(c) `pos` IS A POSITION SETTER. 0x45a30 reads the target object
from the context ([ecx] then [that+0x8] = its class word), takes
edx = [node+0x8] and ebx = [node+0xc], and calls the target's
class +0x4 verb. For the lion classes (0x96874 and TLewZaria
0x96960) that cell is 0x23850, five instructions: `mov [eax],edx`
- [obj+0x0], the x the physics step and the ask protocol both
read - `mov [eax+0x4],ebx`, then `call [class+0x54]`: the
row/animation verb PR-305 named (0x55070 for the lion family,
0x53df0 for the ladder family). So `pos x,y` teleports the object
and refreshes its row - with no carry, no clearance and no
signal: it does not go through the physics step at all. The
DRABINKA class holds a different setter, 0x23ea0.
(d) `lock` AND `unlock` ARE A FLAGGED PAIR. 0x45c50 branches on
[node+0x8] (the authored `lock` / `unlock` argument) to 0x54f40 or
0x54f90. Both first call the class +0xbc verb as a guard and
check [obj+0xb6] bit 1; 0x54f40 proceeds only when that bit is
clear, and at the end sets `or BYTE [obj+0xb6],0x1`; 0x54f90
proceeds only when it is set. In both, the body is the same trio:
the class +0x48 verb, the class +0x50 verb, and then the class
+0x4 verb of the holder read at [[+0x48 result]+0x33]. Note the
neighbouring bit: PR-312 found the physics step skipping its
queries on [obj+0xb6] bit 2 - bit 1 is this authored lock.
(e) `rdir` sets a direction word: its apply 0x45a10 writes
[obj+0x6d] = 1 (the same field 0x545e5 writes from [edx+0x8]).
`ldir` was not opened further than its name at 0x91936.
(f) `end_level`, AND PLAN STEP F3 WAS ALREADY CLOSED. The body
at 0x45750 - the +0x4 slot of the end_level node class 0xa1048 -
loads the world object ds:0xcef40 and stores the node's
[node+0x8] argument into [world+0x4]. This is the same site and
field PR-198 read ("0x45750 -> the exit word at [mgr+0x4]"), so
this confirms OI-046's contract from the node-class side and adds
nothing to it: the plan step F3 that PR-310 wrote was a duplicate
of a CLOSED row. What is new here is only that ZARIA.01's own
lion script has no `end_level` row, so that node never runs for
this level.
OPENS: the port's apply for these five first - the smallest
honest one is `pos`, five instructions with an obvious test: the
authored `pos 1020,692` must put the lion at x 1020, y 692 and
then run the class +0x54 verb. Second, what [world+0x4] drives in
the level loop (F3b). Third, the [obj+0xbc] guard verb and the
+0x48 / +0x50 / +0x33 trio behind lock. Fourth, AC_DRECT, still
unnamed (F4).
CLOSES: plan step F2 for pos/lock/unlock/rdir, and PR-309's "this
port counts pos, lock, unlock, ldir, rdir and goto without acting
on any of them" now has the engine side measured for four of the
six. It also closes plan step F3 as a mis-scope: that question is
OI-046, CLOSED by PR-198/PR-199.
CORRECTS: PR-310 - its plan list item "F3 read what ends THIS
level: the writer of [level+0x4]" restates OI-046, which PR-198
and PR-199 closed and the port implements; the item is replaced in
T5 by the open half, what the exit word drives. PR-305's cell map
is used as measured: its +0x4 object slot is now named the
position setter, and its +0x54 frame/row verb is exactly what the
setter calls after moving.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no
red leg by the rule PR-245 states, and no suite run. The last full
no-Windows suite run is PR-298's, rc=0 with 69 green verdict lines;
since then only comments in ported/ have changed.
```

failing test first") on the reading plan step F2 shipped a turn ago
(PR-316); FOCUS 1, whose authored end is the A_WYJSCIE walk-off
that opens with this directive.
MEASURED: (a) THE CENSUS, RE-MEASURED HERE. Over the 777 extracted
`.MOV` texts the word appears in EXACTLY 4 rows in 3 files, and
BOTH spellings are shipped: `0,0,pos 1020,692` as the third row of
`[A_WYJSCIE]` in ZARIA.01_LEW.ZAR_LEW.MOV and in
ZARIA.01_LEW.ZAR_LEWPL.MOV, `1,250,POS 220,140,GEN K_GEN1` in
RAN.01_LEW.RAN_LEW.MOV `[A_DEAD]` and `15,300,POS 200,140` in its
`[A_DEAD1]`. No shipped row carries an `M` tail beside a `pos`.
(b) THE NODE. The parse arm 0x466d6-0x46718 asks for 0x10 bytes,
runs the node ctor 0x45770, writes the class word 0xa11b0 at
[node+0x4] and reads the pair through 0x49920 with the format at
0x91944 into [node+0x8] (x) and [node+0xc] (y).
(c) THE APPLY AND ITS ARGUMENT CONVENTION. 0x45a30 saves the node
in ebx and the second argument in ecx, calls the shared prologue
0x457e0, then takes the object from that argument: `mov eax,[ecx]`
and `mov esi,[eax+0x8]` - the CLASS WORD of the object the context
carries - and calls `esi+0x4` with edx = [node+0x8] and ebx =
[node+0xc]. For the lion classes 0x96874 and TLewZaria 0x96960
that slot is 0x23850, four instructions: `mov [eax],edx`,
`mov [eax+0x4],ebx`, `call [edx+0x54]` - write [obj+0x0]/[obj+0x4]
and refresh. The DRABINKA class 0x97cdc holds a different setter,
0x23ea0, so the slot is per-class, not one global setter.
(d) THE REFRESH. 0x55070 (the lion class's +0x54) is
`lea edx,[obj+0xd6]; call [class+0xb0]` - the presented-point
provider of the ask path (PR-313) - then `lea edx,[obj+0x89]; call
0x541f0`, then `call [class+0x98]`. So a `pos` re-derives the
point the ground queries use. It does NOT touch the velocity
registers, [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] or any signal: the directive
bypasses the physics step 0x546a0 of PR-312 completely.
(e) THE CHAIN, EXACTLY. 0x457e0 is `ebx = [eax+0x0]` and, if
non-null, `eax = that link; call [[link]+0x4]+0x4` - the PARENT
link's +0x4 with the SAME second argument, not the owner object;
0x45870 (the +0xc verb every one of these classes shares) walks
the same link into its +0xc and, when the link is empty, builds an
empty 12-byte set through 0x749a0 with ebx = 0xc. The list is a
chain in both slots and the object always arrives as the argument.
(f) THE PORT'S APPLY, RED FIRST. The new selftest leg parses the
two shipped shapes in one fixture - the upper-case RAN.01 row with
its trailing `GEN K_GEN1` and the authored `pos 1020,692` - and
then runs the player on a ground line at 692 + the contact offset,
so the authored point is an exactly-grounded point and the physics
pass neither adds nor removes anything there. Derived expectation,
from PR-110's row clock (100 units a feed): the 250-unit first row
holds iterations 0-2, so the pair must appear on iteration 3 and
nowhere before; on iteration 4 (a row with no `pos`) the position
must be unchanged, because it is a set and not a delta; on
iteration 6, where the list wraps and row 0 is admitted again, its
`POS 220,140` must re-apply, because the engine re-runs a row's
chain every time it runs the row. Controls: with the parse arm
disabled 5 checks fail (2 parse + 3 runtime); with only the apply
disabled exactly the 3 runtime checks fail; with both in, the leg
is green and `--mov-selftest` stays green.
(g) WHAT DOES NOT MOVE. The ZARIA.01 level probe is unchanged, and
its "frame directive(s) the model does not act on" count stays 52
before and after: that count covers the PLACEMENT scripts, not the
lion's own `ZAR_LEW`, so the shipped exit row was never in it.
(h) THE EXIT SITS IN A HOLE. Reading `zaria_a.plt` for the
authored point: the terrain across the exit column runs
(953,654) (994,644) (1007,646) (1051,633), then NOTHING until
(1115,662) - a 64 px gap - and the same file authors a catch-all
line (-100,1500)-(3000,1500). The authored `pos 1020,692` is 39
px below the terrain at x 1007 and 59 px below it at x 1051, inside
that gap column: the level drops its lion through the floor it

MEASURED: (a) THE TOOL, AND WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT SEE.
  tools/re/signal_raise_census.py reads the signal names from THIS
  port's own LL_SIG_* enum in ported/ll_play.h (PR-88 verified that
  table 68/68 against the engine's name block), so its output
  cannot drift from the port's bit numbers. It walks every
  instruction row for the two shapes a raise has: bit N lives at
  byte N/8 of a signal set, bit N%8, and a set is reached either
  as an answer buffer (displacement 0x0..0xb, the 12-byte buffer
  0x749a0 builds with ebx=0xc) or as the live field
  [obj+0x60..0x6b]. Over the whole .text it prints 194 candidate
  sites and names each one's enclosing function. Its blind spot is
  stated in the tool and here: it sees writes of a CONSTANT mask
  only, and a bit also arrives by a register merge - PR-313's two
  AC_ONAIR raisers 0x36165/0x2b327 and the set-OR sites
  0x49580/0x53725 are exactly that form, and the census does not
  print them. So "no raiser" from this tool means no
  constant-mask raiser.
  (b) AC_DRECT (bit 19 = byte 2, mask 0x8) HAS EXACTLY TWO such
  raisers in the whole image: 0x40d99 and 0x286ec. Both are class
  +0x78 ASK VERBS of the rectangle family, reached from the ask
  walk 0x4b500 (PR-312/PR-313), and both raise into the ASKER'S
  answer buffer, not into their own live set: the verb calls
  0x749a0 with edx=0, ebx=0xc to build the 12-byte buffer, stores
  0 at [buffer+0xc], then OR-s the bit into it.
  (c) THE `DRECT` CLASS. The placement factory 0x4df10 compares the
  entry line's first field against its name block (0x91f75 'RECT',
  0x91f7a 'DRECT', 0x91f80 'DRECT2', the names loaded by
  0x4e15c and its neighbours) and installs the class table by
  immediate store: RECT 0xa15ac at 0x4e147, DRECT 0xa1638 at
  0x4e1aa, DRECT2 0xa16c4 at 0x4e20d - and the same three again
  from the level-descriptor parser's own factory 0x4ea10 at
  0x4eb9a / 0x4ec6a / 0x4ed3a (0x4ea10 is called from 0x4c8a0, the
  `.des` key parser, at 0x4d7e4/0x4d7f1). The DRECT table: ctor
  0x4ebb0, +0x18 = 0x40c90, +0x78 = 0x40d50 in the cell 0xa16b0.
  The +0x18 verb is the AUTHORED RECTANGLE: 0x40c90 does
  `add eax,0x3c` and calls 0x49f90, which pushes the format at
  0x91d00 - `%d,%d;%d,%d` - into the field parser 0x49920. The
  numbers on the placement line become the box at
  [obj+0x3c..0x49]: x0, y0, x1, y1.
  (d) THE GATE, READ AT 0x40d50. eax = the DRECT instance, ebx =

  asker's class +0x3c verb - PR-303/PR-304's ASKABLE probe -

  geometry object whose own class +0x8 verb, called with

  authored-rectangle class 0x98274 that +0x8 verb is 0x23e00, the
  contain test the port already prints for authored contact
  points: x within [box.x0..box.x1] and y within [box.y0..box.y1].
  Only then bit 19.
  (e) THE SIBLINGS, SAME SHAPE. RECT's verb 0x40cf0 (cell 0xa1624)
  drops gates (1) and (2) and raises AC_RECT (byte 2, mask 0x2) at

  (f) THE DATA, COUNTED WITH COMMITTED TOOLS. tools/re/llrs_tree

NAMES: the class verb +0x10, opcodes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 0xd, 0x1b,
  `MOVE`, `zero`, `chdir`, `ldir`, `rdir`, `[obj+0xc2]`,
  `[obj+0xc6]`, `[obj+0x6d]`, `[obj+0x71]`, `[obj+0xb6]`,
  `[obj+0xa9]`, `[obj+0xd6]`, `[obj+0x5c]`, `[obj+0xfe]`,
  `[obj+0x126]`, `[obj+0x12a]`, AC_DRECT, AC_RECT, AC_DRAB,
  command_post_census.py, signal_raise_census.py
CODE: yes: one new read-only tool, tools/re/command_post_census.py
  (a census of the poster's call sites over the leodb `insn` table),
  and one comment correction in ported/ll_level.c - the PR-225 note
  that called 0x2885a the lion's vtable+0x10; no behaviour change.
HOOKS: none
MEASURED: (a) THE BUS. 0x52b10 is a poster: eax = the object, edx =
  a command opcode, ebx and ecx = two payload ints. It builds a
  4-word message - [msg+0x4] = the opcode, [msg+8] and [msg+0xc] =
  the ints - and calls `[[obj+8]+0x10]`. This is the same message
  layout PR-235 read for the SIGNAL message (0x2883f-0x2885a builds
  type 0x10 with payload 0xa = AC_DRAB and calls the same verb), so
  the signal posts and the object commands are one bus, not two.
  tools/re/command_post_census.py counts the poster's call sites:
  66 of them, with the opcode each one loads - 0x1 x7, 0x2 x5,
  0x5 x7, 0x8 x5, 0xa, 0xb, 0xc, 0xd x4, 0xf x5, 0x10, 0x11,
  0x12 x2, 0x14, 0x15 x4, 0x19 x11, 0x1b x5, 0x1d, 0x1e, 0x21,
  and 2 sites whose opcode is computed. The tool states its
  heuristic (the last `mov edx, ...` in the 48 bytes before the
  call) in its own header.
  (b) THE BASE HANDLER'S MAP. 0x54560 is the +0x10 verb most object
  classes install: 87 dword cells in the image hold it, and every
  one the class-table join locates sits at table+0x10. Reading it
  end to end: opcode 2 ASSIGNS
  `[obj+0xc2]`/`[obj+0xc6]` from the two payload ints (0x54593 /
  0x5459c); opcode 0xd ADDS to both (0x545aa / 0x545bb); opcode 8
  ZEROES both (0x545f4 / 0x545fe); opcode 6 writes `[obj+0x6d]`
  and `[obj+0x71]` (0x545de) - the same field the `rdir` directive
  writes straight out at 0x45a1a (PR-316, through its node class
  0xa0f70's +0x4 verb 0x45a10); which directive posts opcode 6 is
  NOT established here. Opcodes 3 and 4 set bit 2 and bit 3 of
  `[obj+0xb6]` (0x545c6 / 0x545d2) - bit 2 is the physics-skip
  flag of PR-316; opcode 0x1b runs the `[obj+0xa9]` surface
  attach/detach block, which is where PR-318's AC_DUP (0x54785),
  AC_DUP_CD (0x547d1) and candidate AC_ONAIR (0x54800) sites are.
  Every other opcode - including the signal type 0x10 - falls
  through to 0x53770 (0x5463a / 0x54652 / 0x54675 / 0x5468d).
  (c) THE LION IS ON THIS BUS. The LION class 0x96874 has +0x10 =
  0x3d8f0, which handles opcode 5 itself (writes `[obj+0x6d]` and
  sets a bit at `[obj+0x66]`) and chains EVERY other opcode to
  0x54560 at 0x3d906. The other lion table 0x96960 has +0x10 =
  0x1e130, whose unhandled path is 0x50d60 - a second handler with
  its own jump table at 0x50d20 over opcodes 9..0x15 and a special
  case for opcode 1 when `[obj+0x126]` is non-zero. So the pair is
  reachable on the lion through 0x3d8f0, and nothing in the physics
  step of PR-312/313 writes it.
  (d) THE PAIR IS A COMMAND-WRITTEN (x,y) OFFSET. Opcode-2 posters:
  0x1e952, 0x1f3ce, 0x3e03d, 0x3e446, 0x3e840. Opcode-8 posters:
  0x1f3b6, 0x3e01e, 0x3e364, 0x3e424, 0x45a84. Opcode-0xd posters:
  0x1ea65, 0x1eaef, 0x3c3b8, 0x53ba4. The 0x1exxx family is the
  level-geometry path that also instantiates the KILOF_PL family
  (0x1f870, PR-318); the 0x3cxxx/0x3exxx family is the
  contact/attachment code PR-235 walked (its pair loop 0x3eac6);
  0x45a84 sits in a `.MOV` directive apply, 0x45a6f, which
  resolves its target through 0x457e0 and posts opcode 8 with both
  payload ints zero; 0x53ba4 is inside 0x53ae0, the function that
  compares two objects' class +0x44 verbs (the kind word PR-312
  named) and then posts opcode 0xd. Together with the zeroing at
  every state start (0x5042e/0x50438, PR-318), that is the whole
  write set. Its readers are two: the AC_DRECT gate's boolean test
  at 0x40d65, and the point-provider verbs 0x27350 (installed at
  +0xe8, cell 0x9a634, of the class 0x9a54c that the ctors
  0x2703e/0x2743f build) and 0x36732, which return the asker's
  +0x68 provider's point plus `[obj+0xc2] * 15 / 100` plus
  `[obj+0x6d] * 60` plus `[obj+0xfe]`, the first gated on the
  current record index `[obj+0x5c] == 0x12` and the second on
  `0x1f <= [obj+0x5c] <= 0x26` (PR-235's record-index field).
  (e) WHAT `MOVE` MOVES. The name is at 0x91980; the directive
  parser's arm at 0x46a77 allocates 0x10 bytes, installs the node
  class 0xa1078, and parses the pair with the format at 0x91979 (`
  %i,%i`) into node+0x8/node+0xc. The node's apply, 0xa1078+0x04 =
  0x45ce0, resolves the target through the shared 0x457e0 (PR-316)
  and posts OPCODE 1 with the two ints - so `MOVE` is not what
  writes the pair. Opcode 1 on the classes that install 0x28880
  (cell 0x9a000) reads `[obj+0x3c]/[+0x40]/[+0x44]/[+0x48]` - the
  AUTHORED RECTANGLE the RECT-family classes parse their placement
  numbers into (PR-318) - and offsets it by the payload. So the
  authored rectangle of a placed rectangle-class object is movable
  by a script, and that is what `MOVE x,y` does to it.
  (f) THE AC_DRECT GATE IS NOW FULLY READ EXCEPT ITS UNIT QUESTION.
  The asker's +0x68 verb, which PR-318's gate calls, is the point
  provider: for the lion classes the cell (0x96874+0x68 = 0x968dc,
  0x96960+0x68 = 0x969c8) holds 0x23900, which is `add eax,0xd6;
  ret` - a pointer to the PRESENTED POINT of PR-305. So the gate
  is exactly: the lion's presented point lies inside the placed
  DRECT's authored box, AND `[lion+0xc6]` is positive, AND the
  asker is ASKABLE. What OI-119 still owes is which of the
  opcode-2/0xd posters can run against the lion and in what unit -
